FOREWORD
前言
p.6
p.6
I met Dan Koe in between chapters of my life.
我是在人生的章节间隙里遇见丹·科的。
p.6
Everything seemed to be on the right track. Graduating from a top engineering university, landing a software engineering job with decent pay, benefits, and time flexibility, and finally being able to start my adult life. But all the while, something inside me kept wondering when my life would actually begin.
一切看起来都在正轨上。从一所顶尖工科大学毕了业，拿到一份薪水不错、有福利、时间也灵活的软件工程师工作，终于可以开始我的成年生活了。但整个过程中，我内心深处始终有一个声音在问：我的人生到底什么时候才真正开始？
p.6
I always imagined my life would "begin" after I finished college and started my career. But something still felt wrong. I still felt unfulfilled. My emptiness led to an identity crisis, a deep depression, and a search for meaning.
我一直以为，等我念完大学、开始职业生涯，人生就会“开始”。但总觉得哪里不对。我依然感到空虚。这份空虚带来了身份危机、深度抑郁，以及一场对意义的追寻。
p.6
One day, I had the idea of creating internet content based on the psychology, neuroscience, and personal development knowledge I had been gaining over the past 2 years. My mission was to synthesize science-based, self-improvement guides to help people overcome similar problems I've faced That decision led me to Dan.
有一天，我冒出一个念头：把我过去两年积累的心理学、神经科学和个人成长方面的知识，做成互联网内容。我的使命是综合出有科学依据的自我提升指南，帮助人们克服我曾面对的类似问题。正是这个决定，让我遇见了丹。
p.7
Dan was the first person to reach out to me on social media. We were in a networking group chat, and that group chat eventually dissolved as many do, but Dan and I kept in touch. Many people have come and gone from my professional network, but Dan is one of the few I talk to almost every day. I'm proud to call him a mentor, a business partner, and a close friend. I didn't agree with some of Dan's perspectives when I first met him. I came from an engineering background and had been self-educating in cognitive science for a few years. Dan was, in a way, the opposite of me, with perspectives rooted in philosophy and spirituality. I believed the science I had studied was more reliable than the seemingly woo-woo nonsense Dan was interested in.
丹是第一个在社交媒体上主动联系我的人。我们当时在一个人脉群里，那个群后来像很多群一样散掉了，但丹和我一直保持联系。很多人进进出出我的职业圈子，但丹是我几乎每天都会交谈的少数几个人之一。我很自豪能称他为导师、合作伙伴和挚友。刚认识他时，我并不认同丹的一些观点。我出身工程背景，又自学了几年认知科学。从某种意义上说，丹和我正好相反，他的观点扎根于哲学与灵性。那时我认为，我学的科学比丹感兴趣的那套看似玄乎的鬼话更可靠。
p.7
I can't recall a specific disagreement we had, but I do remember at first thinking Dan was just another spirituality bro like the many I had encountered in passing at electronic music concerts. I knew he was exceptionally intelligent and he was skilled at eloquently explaining his perspectives, but a part of me harbored a quiet sense of superiority due to my scientific approach to productivity, fulfillment, and self-actualization. Over time, as I listened to Dan and dipped my toes in the waters of the "other side, " I began to see that what I had learned was not an opposite or necessarily superior perspective, but instead, it was merely a different one. Dan and I had similar goals for both ourselves and our audiences we simply had different ways of going about achieving those goals.
我记不清我们具体为什么事起过争执，但我记得，起初我觉得丹不过是又一个“灵修哥”，就像我在电子音乐演出现场擦肩而过的那些人一样。我知道他聪明得非同寻常，也善于雄辩地阐述自己的观点，但因为我在效率、成就感和自我实现上走的是科学路线，我内心悄悄地藏着一种优越感。随着时间推移，当我听丹说话、把自己的脚尖伸进“另一边”的水里试了试，我开始明白：我学到的并不是一种对立的、或必然更高级的视角，而只是一种不同的视角。丹和我在自身和受众身上有着相似的目标——我们只是实现这些目标的方式不同。
p.7
The major catalyst of this perspective shift came during a conversation we were having along with our mutual friend, Justin C. Scott (who was also deep into philosophy and spirituality). I asked the question that bothered me most: How else could a recommendation be made to another person if it was not proven to be replicable by rigorous studies in the traditional scientific sense?
这种视角转变最大的催化剂，来自一次我们一起和共同的朋友贾斯汀·C·斯科特（他同样深研哲学与灵性）的对话。我问出了那个最困扰我的问题：如果一件事无法被传统科学意义上的严格研究证明可复现，那我们还能凭什么把它推荐给别人？
p.7
The discussion that followed helped me realize that I wasn't a blind fanatic of Science™; I was, instead, an enthusiast of the scientific method, a neverending trial and error, something Dan and I agreed on. Since that
随后的讨论让我意识到，我并不是“科学™”的盲目信徒；我真正热爱的其实是科学方法——一场永无止境的试错。这一点丹和我是共识。自那以后，
p.8
discussion, I've invested time into studying what I thought was the "other side" so that I could become more well-rounded for myself, those close to me, and my online audience.
我开始花时间研究我原本以为的“另一边”，好在对自己、对身边人、对我的线上读者而言，成为一个更完整的人。
p.8
Thanks to Dan's friendship, support, and guidance, I've been able to grow a business that has finally provided a feeling of fulfillment in my life. If I had the book you hold in your hands back then, I would've seen that it was possible years earlier.
多亏丹的友谊、支持和指引，我得以把一门生意做大，它终于给我的生活带来了满足感。如果当年我手里就有你现在拿着的这本书，我会早好几年就看见：这一切是可能的。
p.8
This book is a synthesis of years of Dan's learnings, experiences, and reflections. The first time I read the draft of the book, I was dumbfounded by the simultaneous depth and simplicity of its teachings. I'm not ashamed to admit I needed to read it a second time in its entirety before I felt like I grasped it enough to write this foreword.
这本书凝聚了丹多年的学习、经历与反思。第一次读到手稿时，我被它同时具备的深度与简洁惊得目瞪口呆。我不羞于承认，我整整重读了第二遍，才觉得自己勉强抓得住，可以动笔写这篇前言。
p.8
Here's one of my favorite quotes from this book: "Once you understand the game, you begin completing a series of quests - that form a storyline - to gain experience. As you gain experience, new opportunities become available to you. You unlock dungeons. You can join a guild. You can travel to new locations to complete different quests. In the real world, we often aren't aware of what these opportunities can be, so we choose to remain stagnant, comfortable, and ignorant."
这是书中我最喜欢的一段话之一：“一旦你理解了这场游戏，你就会开始完成一系列任务——它们串成一条故事线——从而获得经验。随着经验累积，新的机会向你敞开。你解锁了副本。你可以加入公会。你可以前往新的地图去完成不同的任务。而在现实世界里，我们往往不知道这些机会能是什么，于是选择原地不动，安逸、无知。”
p.8
This gamification approach speaks to me. As a former video game addict (and current Dungeons & Dragons Dungeon Master), I've enjoyed finding ways to think of my life more like some sort of a game — not to be won, which is impossible, but instead to be explored, enjoyed, and experienced as much as possible in the life we have now.
这种游戏化的思路深得我心。作为一个曾经的电玩成瘾者（以及现在的《龙与地下城》地下城主），我很喜欢把人生想成某种游戏——不是用来通关的（那不可能），而是用来探索、享受、尽可能充分体验的，就在我们此刻拥有的这一生里。
p.8
The book begins by painting a bleak picture of the average person, a picture of the person I was in the chapter of my life before I had the idea of becoming a creator, sharing my ideas, and starting a business. Though it may feel like criticism, this is a necessary wake-up call so that we might be better prepared for the lessons that come next.
这本书开篇先给普通人画了一幅灰暗的画像——那也是我人生的某个章节里的样子，那时的我还没想过成为创作者、分享想法、开始创业。虽然读起来像是在批评，但这记警钟是必要的，好让我们为接下来的课程做好准备。
p.9
Of course, the journey can be difficult. I've found myself battling sleepless nights, food and drink binges, and moments of seemingly hopeless despair. But I've found that, almost always, those challenges arise not because of the nature of the "game," but instead, a lack of clarity about our next move. Many of us feel trapped. We aren't happy, we aren't fulfilled, and we aren't progressing, just like I was a few years ago. This book gives you insights that can take years (or decades) to fully integrate through trial, error, and frustration.
当然，这段旅程可能很艰难。我曾与失眠的夜、暴饮暴食、以及看似无望的沮丧搏斗。但我发现，几乎总是如此：那些挑战的出现，并不是因为“游戏”本身的性质，而是因为我们对下一步该往哪走缺乏清晰。我们许多人都感到被困住了。不快乐、不满足、没有进步，就像几年前的我。这本书给你的洞见，靠试错和挫败可能需要数年（甚至数十年）才能真正内化。
p.9
You may need to read this book multiple times for its lessons to sink in. But that's okay. The greatest books always have something new to offer you each time you return to them. As you read, apply, and reflect, you'll find your perspective changing. You'll begin to find a path that will lead to freedom, happiness, and fulfillment for yourself and those you care about. My friendship with Dan changed my life. The book you're about to read will change yours.
你可能需要反复阅读这本书，其中的道理才会沉淀下来。但没关系。真正伟大的书，每次重读都会有新的东西给你。当你阅读、实践、反思时，你会发现自己的视角在改变。你会开始找到一条路，通向属于你自己和你所关心的人的自由、幸福与满足。我和丹的友谊改变了我的人生。你即将读到的这本书，会改变你的。
p.9
Joey Justice Co-Founder of Kortex & Performance Consultant
乔伊·贾斯提斯（Joey Justice）—— Kortex 联合创始人 & 绩效顾问
INTRODUCTION
导论
p.10
p.10
We are at a pivotal moment in human evolution. Attention spans are shrinking. Bodies are getting softer. Minds are growing weaker. Some pockets are being drained while others are being filled a bit more than usual. Technological advancements are threatening the mindless, comfortable, and mechanical lives of the masses. It's becoming difficult to tell if I'm the crazy one or if everyone else is.
我们正处在人类进化的一个关键时刻。注意力时长在缩短。身体在变软。心智在变弱。有些人的钱包被榨干，另一些人的则比平时被填得更满一些。技术进步正在威胁大众那种无意识、舒适、机械化的生活。我越来越难分辨：到底是我疯了，还是其他所有人都疯了。
p.10
Wake up. Hit snooze 4 times. Stare at your phone. Roll out of bed. Make coffee. Sit in traffic. Eight hours of unfulfilling work. Sit in traffic... again. Argue with your "significant" other. Walk the pet. Watch TV. Pass out. Repeat.
醒来。按四次贪睡。盯着手机。滚下床。煮咖啡。堵在路上。八小时没有成就感的工作。又堵在路上。和你那位“重要的”另一半吵架。遛宠物。看电视。昏睡过去。重复。
p.10
Get offended. Blame everyone but yourself. Tie your self-worth to radical ideologies. Accept everything at face value and question nothing. Expect free handouts for simply existing, no effort. Do what the authorities tell you. Go to school, get a job, retire at the ripe age of whatever it may be, no guarantees, with just the right amount of currency to survive until death. Go through a painful experience. Find the light. Identify with it. Demonize anyone who questions that identity. Avoid the thought of any meaning, love, and consistent presence you had the potential of achieving in your life because that would require you to change.
被冒犯。把责任推给所有人，除了自己。把自我价值绑在激进意识形态上。对一切照单全收，什么都不质疑。因为“存在着”就期待白给的东西，毫不付出。按权威说的做。上学、找工作、在某个“成熟的年纪”退休——没有任何保障，只拿着刚好够活到死的钱。经历一次痛苦。找到那道光。与它认同。把任何质疑这份认同的人妖魔化。回避一切关于意义、爱、以及你本可能拥有的稳定陪伴的念头——因为那会要求你改变。
p.11
What a life. A life I have lived multiple times, each one being shorter than the next. Many people say they enjoy this lifestyle, that they are fine living out the same day like an experimental TV drama. It seems like a peaceful existence, but one that I could never live. The thought of something more would eat me alive.
多么“精彩”的人生。这种人生我活过很多次，每一次都比上一次更短。很多人说他们享受这种生活方式，说他们可以接受像实验性电视剧一样日复一日地重复同一天。这看起来是一种平静的生存状态，但一种我永远无法忍受的生活。那个“也许还有更多”的念头，会把我活活吃掉。
p.11
If the lifestyle illustrated above made you want to jump off a building, good. You picked up the right book. This is for those that hate the thought of ending up like everyone else. This book is for those that feel an internal sense of despair at the thought of an unlived life. This book is for those that know there is something more, but aren't sure what, when, where, why, or how. This book is for those that will not surrender the little sovereignty they have left to the default path that too many people accept and follow without question.
如果上面描绘的生活方式让你想要跳楼——很好。你拿对了书。这本书是写给那些一想到“最终变成和其他人一样”就厌恶的人的。这本书是写给那些一想到“未曾活过的人生”就感到内心绝望的人的。这本书是写给那些知道还有更多，却不知道是什么、何时、何地、为何、如何的人的。这本书是写给那些不愿把仅剩的一点主权，拱手交给那条太多人毫不质疑就接受并跟随的默认路径的人的。
p.11
Who's to blame for this default path? You. We are not going to start this off by acting as if you can't make a conscious personal choice to change who you are, what you do, and how you do it. I do not believe that modern life is the result of bad intentions from government officials, corrupt politicians, mega-rich founders, and the outdated school system. You know, the people whose products fill your house, mind, and allow you to opt out of life's minor inconveniences, but only for a bit.
这条默认路径该怪谁？怪你。我们不会用“你无法有意识地做出个人选择去改变你是谁、你做什么、你怎么做”这样的话来开篇。我不相信现代生活是政府官员、腐败政客、超级富豪创始人和过时教育体制的恶意造成的。你知道的，就是那些产品塞满你的房子和大脑、让你能短暂逃离生活小麻烦的人。
p.11
Instead, I believe we are right where we're supposed to be at this point in civilization. The turning point that separates the lions from the sheep. But this does not mean that the people, organizations, and institutions above do not have a bit too much influence over our daily actions. What's worse is how they can condition a population to think in black and white, when the magic happens in the gray, the unknown.
相反，我相信在文明的这个节点上，我们正处在该在的位置。这是区分狮子与羊群的转折点。但这并不意味着上面那些个人、组织和机构对我们的日常行为没有过多的影响力。更糟的是，他们能把一整个群体调教成非黑即白的思维——而魔法恰恰发生在灰色地带，在未知之中。
p.11
When it comes to the default path, I am here to give you a new perspective, a positive one. I am not proposing that you need to get rid of all electronics, quit all of your "bad" habits, or move out to the woods to live like a monk. Instead, I am here to bring clarity in a time of external chaos, distraction, and opportunity overwhelm. I am here to help you join the rich. The New
说到那条默认路径，我要给你一个新视角，一个积极的视角。我不是建议你扔掉所有电子产品、戒掉所有“坏”习惯、或者搬到林子里像修士一样生活。我是在外部的混乱、干扰与机会过载之中，为你带来清晰。我是来帮你加入富人的行列的。新的
p.12
Rich. The rich that don't care to be rich, and that's why they're rich in more domains than money.
新富（The New Rich）。那些并不在乎变得有钱的富人——正因如此，他们在金钱之外的更多领域里都很富有。
p.12
My biggest fear with writing this book is that I will make it all about me, and less about you. So, for the sake of establishing perspective, I will talk about myself, but not for long.
写这本书时我最大的恐惧，是把它写成关于我，而不是关于你。所以，为了建立视角，我会谈谈自己，但不会讲太久。
p.12
My name is Dan Koe. I started this journey when I was twelve years old. I was gifted with the specific programming that led to me questioning how the world worked. Questioning how I could game the system. Questioning how I could get miles ahead of everyone else with minimal, focused effort. Questioning why everyone lived out their lives unfulfilled, unhappy, overweight, and with an underwhelming amount of energy. Like their life force had been sucked out of them before they had a chance to pursue their gifts like I have mine.
我叫丹·科（Dan Koe）。十二岁那年，我开始了这段旅程。我被赋予了一种特定的“程序”，它让我去追问世界是怎么运转的。追问我要怎样才能玩转这个系统。追问我要怎样才能用最小、最专注的努力，远远走在所有人前面。追问为什么每个人都活得没有成就感、不快乐、超重、精力低得可怜——仿佛他们的生命力在有机会去追求自己的天赋之前，就已被抽干，就像我得以追求我的天赋那样。
p.12
I wanted autonomy above all. I was hyperobservant of my environment and how it impacted those residing in it. Friends. Family. Acquaintances. Colleagues. Grocery store shoppers. Corporate professionals. All of them put off this sense of unease. A subtle projection of their deep internal state of unhappiness. They seemed to let momentary inconveniences turn into lifelong problems.
我最想要的，是自主权。我对周遭环境、以及它如何影响身处其中的人，有着超常的观察力。朋友、家人、熟人、同事、超市里的顾客、企业里的职场人——他们身上都散发着一种不安。那是他们内在深层不快乐状态的微妙投射。他们似乎任由一时的小麻烦变成终身的问题。
p.12
Telling my story is important because it shows that it is just like every other story: it has its ups, downs, lefts, and rights. The point wasn't to eradicate or amplify any emotional direction by force. The point was to become aware of experience as feedback and focus those resources toward the good life. When I was forced to go to church and accept a belief system as law, that was strike 1. Strike 2 was when my peers told me what not to do, but when I questioned their logic, they danced in circles, regurgitating the same statements their parents and teachers had filled their minds with. Religion was the catalyst to my questioning but went on to fuel my pursuit of truth in the immaterial, material, and everything that lies between.
讲述我的故事很重要，因为它和其他所有故事一样：有起、有落、有左、有右。重点从来不是靠蛮力铲除或放大某个情绪方向。重点是意识到“经验即反馈”，并把这些资源聚焦到美好生活上。当我被迫去教堂、把一套信念体系当成法律来接受时，那是第一击。第二击是：同龄人告诉我“不要做什么”，可当我质疑他们的逻辑时，他们却原地打转，重复着父母和老师灌进他们脑子里的那些话。宗教是我质疑的催化剂，后来则成了我追求真理的燃料——无论那真理在非物质界、物质界，还是两者之间的一切。
p.12
At the same time, my parents had picked up a new fitness routine, one of those DVD sets where you work out in front of your TV, and bought the
与此同时，我父母开始了一套新的健身计划，就是那种对着电视练的 DVD 套装，还买了
p.13
required equipment. I would sneak this equipment into my room at night with high hopes of creating the physique of a golden-era bodybuilder. At some point along this journey, probably due to my obsession with fitness self-education, I became aware that the education system wasn't going to save me; that institutionalized education was a necessary evil that we should evolve away from.
配套的器械。夜里我会把器械偷偷搬进自己房间，满怀希望能练出黄金时代健美运动员的身材。在这段旅程的某个节点——大概是因为我对健身自学太上瘾——我意识到教育系统不会拯救我；制度化教育是一种必要的恶，是我们应当逐步进化掉的东西。
p.13
I realized my curiosity and intuition were going to be the source of my potential success. I could not rely on a preset path to make an income doing something I enjoy. Nor could I rely on it to teach me how to live a fulfilling, healthy, or worry-free life. The state of the modern world was the only evidence I needed to see this truth.
我明白，我的好奇心与直觉，将会是我潜在成功的来源。我无法依赖一条预设路径，靠做自己喜欢的事赚钱；也无法依赖它教会我如何过上充实、健康、无忧的生活。现代世界的状况，就是我看到这个真相所需的全部证据。
p.13
It started with being a silent observer. My parents would get home late, tired, ready to bicker at each other while watching the same show over and over until their marriage came to an end. This is not a dig at my parents. I am grateful that they stuck together for as long as they did to provide my sıblings and me with an incredible childhood filled with adventurous vacations and their desire for us to succeed. I admire the people they have become despite their relationship struggles that I will never understand because I didn't, and never will, have access to their state of mind. The point is this: everyone seemed bitter. I understood that the average individual has their struggles, but they never seemed to try to solve the problems that were a detriment to more than their own well-being. Go to school, get a job, let whatever happens in that multi-decade time period happen, and retire in a way where you have no meaningful work to balance the eternal rest you craved for so long. That was the depressing song that played on repeat in the minds of the masses.
一切都始于做一个沉默的观察者。我父母会晚归、疲惫，随时准备互相拌嘴，一边一遍又一遍看同一个节目，直到他们的婚姻走到尽头。这不是在挖苦我父母。我很感激他们坚持了那么久，给我和我的兄弟姐妹一个不可思议的童年——充满冒险的假期，以及他们希望我们成功的愿望。我钦佩他们后来成为的样子，尽管他们的关系有我看不懂的挣扎，因为我未曾、也永远不会拥有他们内心状态的访问权限。重点是：每个人似乎都很苦涩（苦涩）。我理解普通人都有自己的挣扎，但他们似乎从不试图去解决那些损害了不止自己福祉的问题。上学、找份工作、让那几十年里发生什么都随它去，然后以一种“没有任何有意义的工作来平衡你渴望已久的永眠”的方式退休。那就是在多数人脑海里循环播放的、令人抑郁的那首歌。
p.13
Taking matters into my own hands was the process that stemmed from my rebellion. I wanted quick results. If I could learn everything myself, what was stopping me from doing it in a fraction of the time it took compared to taking the conventional path? This is when the power of the digital world made itself apparent to me.
把命运握在自己手里，是从我的叛逆中长出来的做法。我想要快速的结果。如果我能把一切自学到手，那还有什么能阻止我用传统路径所需时间的一小部分做到？就在那时，数字世界的力量在我面前显现了。
p.14
My eyes were glued to my computer screen for weeks, months, and years on end. I'd take breaks, of course, but all I could think about was all of the knowledge I lacked. Especially after feeling cheated by the conventional resources that were supposed to secure my future.
我连着数周、数月、数年，眼睛粘在电脑屏幕上。当然我也会休息，但我满脑子想的都是自己欠缺的知识——尤其是在感到被那些本应保障我未来的传统资源欺骗之后。
p.14
I spent my days absorbing all the information my focus could handle on fitness, finance, attraction, and perspectives of meaning, happiness, and fulfillment. Consciously experimenting with the best teacher I could find my own mind, body, spirit, and business.
我日复一日地吸收我的专注力能承载的一切信息：健身、理财、吸引力，以及关于意义、幸福与成就感的种种视角。有意识地拿我所能找到的最好的老师做实验——那就是我自己的头脑、身体、精神和事业。
p.14
Through countless bouts of trial and error, a decade of compounding returns on focus, and eliminating the possibility of failure from my mind, I have built something I am proud of: a life of meaning, money, and mastery. At the age of twenty-six, I fill my days with activities I enjoy, I have created a sizeable income pursuing my life's work, and I have attained a degree of freedom that other millionaires of the world would die for. Some of them have said this to my face.
经过无数次试错、专注带来的十年复利回报、以及把“失败”这个可能性从脑中彻底删除，我建起了让我引以为傲的东西：一种由意义、金钱与精通构成的生活。二十六岁那年，我每天充满自己喜欢的活动，靠做自己的人生事业赚到了可观的收入，并获得了世界上其他百万富翁愿意为它去死的自由程度。其中有些人当着我的面这么说过。
p.14
This did not come in an instant, of course. It took a decade of failures, minor successes, feeling hopeless and lost, with a nagging voice in the back of my mind whispering, "It's possible ... you don't have to end up like the rest." This self-taught path brought me to success much faster than the traditional route would have, without the money cap.
这当然不是一瞬间到来的。它花了十年：失败、小成功、感到无望与迷失，同时脑海深处有个唠叨的声音低语着：“这是可能的……你不必像其他人那样收场。”这条自学之路让我比传统路线快得多地抵达成功，而且没有收入天花板。
p.14
On many occasions, I have met individuals who are quick to fill in the blanks of my story with theirs. When I mention my lifestyle and associated income, they are quick to favor coping over curiosity. Closing their minds off to the thought of their potential. I'm relieved to inform you that what I've achieved is not the product of an inheritance, nepotism, a wealthy family, random luck, or a benefactor.
很多场合里，我遇到一些人，急着用他们自己的经历去补全我故事里的空白。当我提到自己的生活方式和相关收入时，他们很快倾向于自我安慰而不是好奇，对自身潜能的念头关上心门。我很欣慰地告诉你：我所取得的，不是遗产、裙带关系、富贵家庭、随机运气或某位恩主的产品。
p.14
I'm an average guy that came from a middle-class, single-income family. There is nothing special about what I have accomplished. I am not living in a different reality from the rest of the population. Even if I grew up on the other side of the world, I would still have access to the information, human experience, and mental ability to maneuver my way to this position. It may
我是个来自中产阶级、单份收入家庭的普通人。我所成就的没有任何特别之处。我并没有活在一个和其余人群不同的现实里。就算我在世界的另一端长大，我依然能接触到那些信息、人生经验和心智能力，来把自己挪到这个位置。也许
p.15
have taken more time, yes, but that isn't a valid excuse. There doesn't seem to be a more worthwhile endeavor to dedicate your life to than to see what you are capable of.
会花更多时间，是的，但那不是有效的借口。似乎没有什么事业，比“看看自己到底能做到什么”更值得你投入一生。
p.15
The journey you are about to embark on is not for the faint-hearted. It is not an external journey, but an internal one. Not a material journey, but immaterial. Not a physical journey, but spiritual. If all I had was a socially accepted definition of a beautiful person of the opposite sex, an abundance of American currency, a nice machine on wheels, and an aesthetic form of my physical body, my life would be all looks and no depth. It would mean nothing. It would serve nothing. It would continue existing as nothing of true value.
你即将踏上的这段旅程，不适合怯懦者。它不是一段向外的旅程，而是向内的。不是物质的旅程，而是非物质的。不是肉身的旅程，而是精神的。如果我拥有的只是“一个社会认可的异性美人标准”、大量的美元、一辆好车、以及一副审美上过关的皮囊，那我的人生就只剩下好看，没有深度。它将毫无意义。它将服务不了任何东西。它将仅仅作为“没有任何真正价值之物”继续存在。
p.15
I am writing this book as a map with faint lines. A map to getting paid for doing what you love, traveling the world, and doing whatever you want. A map to mental peace, meaningful pursuits, and fulfilling relationships. A map to becoming a self-sustaining, self-reliant, and sovereign individual. Dualistically free. I want to give you the tools to a better life, let you crash and burn, and watch you create the light at the end of your own tunnel. I cannot make this change for you. I cannot promise you a better life. I cannot make you do these things. I can only give you the lessons I've learned through living unconventionally. It is your job to take these lessons, experience them for yourself, and make your own decisions. Do not by any means outsource your thinking, decision-making, or potential success to these teachings. I will be one of the first to tell you to quadruple your expectations for how long you think it will take. It will take your entire life, because that's the point of it. This is a tool, a guide, an art and should be treated as such.
我把这本书写成一张线条模糊的地图。一张通向“靠做你热爱的事赚钱、环游世界、想干什么就干什么”的地图。一张通向内心平静、有意义的事业、以及圆满关系的地图。一张通向自我维持、自立、主权的个体——二元性地自由——的地图。我想给你过上更好生活的工具，让你自己去撞墙、去燃烧，然后看着你在自己的隧道尽头创造出那道亮光。我无法替你完成这个改变。我无法向你承诺更好的生活。我无法强迫你去做这些事。我只能把我在非主流生活中习得的教训交给你。你的任务是接住这些教训，亲自去体验它们，做出你自己的决定。无论如何，都不要把你思考、决策、以及潜在成功的责任外包给这些教导。我会是第一个告诉你的人：把你预想需要的时间乘以四。它会花掉你整整一生——因为那正是它的意义所在。这是一件工具、一份指南、一门艺术，就应当被如此对待。
A WORLD OF DISTRACTIONS
充满干扰的世界
p.15
p.15
Do you want your time, attention, and life-changing experiences stolen from you? Are you okay with sitting by, being a slave to modern distractions that have been laid out like breadcrumbs, leading to a life of
你愿意让自己的时间、注意力和那些能改变人生的体验被人偷走吗？你甘心坐在一边，当现代干扰的奴隶——它们像面包屑一样被撒在地上，引向一种
p.16
drained pockets, zapped neurochemistry, abysmal energy levels, and the gradual destruction of anything meaningful in your life? Are you okay with continuing the never-ending search for "safe," "secure," and "pleasurable" experiences that leave you with the opposite feelings?
钱包被榨干、神经化学被烧穿、精力水平惨不忍睹、生活中一切有意义之物被逐步摧毁的人生吗？你甘心继续那场永无止境的搜寻——寻找“安全”“稳妥”“愉悦”的体验，结果却带给你完全相反的感受吗？
p.16
This is the life of the modern human. Walking down an undefined path with mouths open, minds off, and shopping carts - physical and digital - filled with doses that should be considered poison. All while playing a character operating on inconducive and unfiltered information, playing the role they've been molded to play.
这就是现代人的生活。走在一条没有定义的路上，张着嘴、关着脑，推着的购物车——实体与数字的——装满了应该被视为毒药的剂量。同时还在扮演一个基于无益且未经筛选的信息运转的角色，演着他们被塑造成的样子。
p.16
As a collective, we are suppressing our choice to improve so we can continue being spoon-fed pleasurable, numbing, and artificial experiences. Some may think that there is a puppet master hiding behind the state of the modern world, conspiring to create hell on Earth. In reality, it is the individual's inability to understand their nature and use it to adapt to the rapid advancements of our time.
作为一个集体，我们压下了“选择变好”的选项，好让自己能继续被喂食那些愉悦、麻痹、人造的体验。有人或许以为，在现代世界的背后藏着一个操纵一切的人，密谋把人间变成地狱。而现实是：个体没有能力理解自己的本性，也就无法用它去适应这个时代的飞速变化。
p.16
The modern world - more so Western society - is designed not by man, but by years of evolution to keep you in chains. A slave to the system. A drooling bag of bones that craves instant gratification, free handouts, and constant stimulation. This is what our psyche craves, and never has it been so available. Mental mastery must become a top priority so that you can adapt to the times.
现代世界——尤其是西方社会——不是由人设计的，而是由多年的演化设计来把你锁在枷锁里的。系统的奴隶。一具流着口水、渴望即时满足、免费施舍和持续刺激的骨肉口袋。这正是我们心智所渴求的，而它从未如此唾手可得。心智的精通必须成为最高优先级，这样你才能适应这个时代。
p.16
Our choices are not our own, and our choices create who we are. The familiarity we have adopted into our lives digs us deeper into the hole of mediocrity. Those that dare challenge this narrative carry the heaviest burden. If you choose to embark on this path, you will be criticized, mocked, and cut off.
我们的选择并不真正属于我们，而我们的选择塑造了我们是谁。我们接纳进生活里的那些熟悉，把我们越挖越深地埋进平庸的坑里。敢于挑战这套叙事的人，背负着最沉重的负担。如果你选择走上这条路，你会被批评、被嘲笑、被孤立。
p.16
Your beliefs will be challenged. Your transformation will be painful. However, this is the only worthwhile path. I am being dramatic here, and there is a reason behind that. Exaggeration is useful to get the essence of the situation across, because that indeed can be more dangerous than my bold
你的信念会受到挑战。你的转变会伴随痛苦。然而，这是唯一值得走的路。我在这里是故意夸张的，而这有原因：夸张有助于传达处境的本质，因为那个本质确实可能比我大胆的
p.17
assumptions. I am going to make mediocrity so repulsive that you have no choice but to use your gift of creation.
假设更危险。我要把平庸变得如此令人作呕，让你除了动用自己创造的天赋之外，别无选择。
p.17
Everywhere you turn, there are distractions that lead you further away from who you are and who you want to become. Processed food is dangled in front of your face like you are a lab rat. People with misaligned goals flood you with invitations to test how important your own are.
你走到哪里，都有干扰把你推离“你是谁”和“你想成为谁”。加工食品在你脸前晃来晃去，就像你是一只实验室老鼠。目标错位的人用邀请把你淹没，来试探你自己的目标到底有多重要。
p.17
Our souls are being sucked out of us from fluorescent-lit cubicles. We have no sense of meaning and little drive to pursue our life's work. We stick to short-term goals just to free up enough space for us to return to the activities that are killing us, not in an absolutely physical manner, but a holistic one. Mind, body, spirit, and business under the lens of your life's work.
我们的灵魂正在荧光灯管的格子间里被抽走。我们没有意义感，也几乎没有动力去追求自己的人生事业。我们抱着短期目标不放，只为了腾出足够的空间，好让我们回到那些正在杀死我们的活动里去——不是绝对生理意义上的杀死，而是整体性的。心智、身体、精神和事业，都摆在“你的人生事业”这面透镜之下。
p.17
My intention is not to paint these things as bad. Bad is relative, and oftentimes these modern "poisons" are useful, necessary, and fun, but not as an eternal day-to-day lifestyle. The ability to moderate is cultivated with experience, but moderation is difficult without awareness, education, and forward progress.
我的本意不是把这些东西涂成“坏”。坏是相对的，而且这些现代“毒药”常常是有用、必要、有趣的——但不能作为一种永恒的日常生活方式。节制的能力靠经验养成，可如果没有觉察、教育和向前推进，节制是很难的。
p.17
Illnesses are being diagnosed within the fifteen-minute time frame you are given to describe your symptoms. Pills are handed out like candy because people don't have the patience to implement simple lifestyle changes. "Trusted" information is paid for, marketed, and perfectly designed to grab your attention, polarize you, and keep you in a state of negativity, even if it is not their intention.
疾病在你被给予的十五分钟里就被诊断完毕。药片像糖一样发下去，因为人们没有耐心去落实简单的生活方式改变。“可信”的信息是花钱买来的、被营销包装的、被精心设计来抓住你注意力、让你极化、并把你留在消极状态里的——即便那并非它们的本意。
p.17
Mainstream advice encourages you to do everything but improve your life. And if they encourage you to do so, it is in the form of attaching to and defending their ideology. Few people are questioning said information or looking where the money isn't flowing. Everybody has access to the internet and the ability to spread their negative opinion like wildfire. We tap into our innate negativity bias, fry our dopamine receptors, and tie ourselves to our lightboxes, straying further from what is. Those that have
主流建议鼓励你做一切，唯独不鼓励你改善生活。就算它们鼓励你改善，形式也是让你依附并捍卫它们的意识形态。很少有人质疑那些信息，或者去看看“钱没往哪儿流”。每个人都有互联网，都有能力像野火一样传播自己的负面看法。我们调动天生的负面偏误，炸坏自己的多巴胺受体，把自己拴在发光盒子上，越来越远离“本来如是”。那些
p.18
the ability to think for themselves quickly realize that they are being manipulated When people hear the word "work," they cower in fear, hoping that the weekend will extend a few days so they can cuddle up on the couch until further notice. When people hear the word "rest," they grab an unhealthy snack, pour some fermented grape juice, and fall into a vegetative state, hoping that they never have to come out The concept of one's "life's work" has been lost by all but those who learn to focus. Everyone has been made to believe that their life is out of their control, that there is a set path to follow that will result in eventual happiness.
有能力独立思考的人，很快就会发现自己正被操纵。当人们听到“工作”这个词，他们畏缩恐惧，盼着周末能多延长几天，好让他们缩在沙发上等待另行通知。当人们听到“休息”这个词，他们抓起一份不健康的零食，倒上一杯发酵的葡萄汁，然后进入一种植物人状态，盼着永远不用出来。“人生事业”这个概念，除了那些学会专注的人，已经被所有人弄丢了。每个人都被灌输：你的人生不受你控制，有一条固定的路要走，走到最后就会得到幸福。
p.18
They think that if they stick it out long enough, they will reach what everyone is searching for: freedom. Even then, the general perception of freedom is to avoid all work, immerse themselves in "rest," and live out their days as if they were fulfilled by creating nothing by their own desire. This is backwards. You cannot understand freedom if you do not conquer what made you a slave.
他们以为，只要熬得够久，就能抵达所有人都在寻找的东西：自由。可即便到了那时，大众对自由的普遍理解也不过是：逃避一切工作，沉浸于“休息”，把剩下的日子过成仿佛“什么都不创造、只凭自己欲望”就能满足。这是反过来的。如果你没有征服那个让你成为奴隶的东西，你就不可能理解自由。
p.18
I do not believe people are miserable. Maybe at times, like everyone else, but I do believe that the majority of people are on a perpetual spectrum of dissatisfaction with their lives. There is a deep, inner voice calling out that is suppressed by a veil of responsibilities, excuses, and perceived uncertainty.
我不认为人们是痛苦的。也许某些时刻会，像所有人一样。但我确实相信，大多数人处在一条对生活不满意的永恒光谱上。内心深处有一个声音在呼喊，却被一层由责任、借口和“感知到的不确定性”织成的帷幕压了下去。
p.18
Due to this, the masses remain unaware of their potential, and I am aware that I cannot save them all. They have not taken that first step into the unknown, and who knows if they ever will. The difference between you and them is this book. If you do not have the awareness of the possibility of a better life, it is impossible for such a future to actualize.
正因如此，大众始终意识不到自己的潜能，而我也清楚，我不可能拯救他们所有人。他们没有迈出进入未知的第一步，谁知道他们会不会迈出。你与他们的区别，就是这本书。如果你连“更好的生活是可能的”这种觉察都没有，那样的未来就不可能成真。
p.18
I am not saying this to destroy all hope you had for a better life. The system may be rigged against you, but that's the thing. With the advancements in technology, medicine, and decentralization, anybody can build wealth,
我说这些，不是为了摧毁你对更好生活的全部希望。这个系统也许是被人做了手脚来对付你，但关键正在于此：随着技术、医学和去中心化的进步，任何人都能积累财富、
p.19
leverage, and an overwhelming sense of satisfaction in life. All they need to do is learn how to focus in this beautiful black hole of distractions. WHY FOCUS?
杠杆，以及一种压倒性的生活满足感。他们需要的只是——学会在这个美丽的干扰黑洞里专注。为什么是专注？
p.19
Humans can process 10-50 bits of information per second with their conscious attention. The what, how, and why behind that information we choose to process will determine our quality of life. That is, what we hold in our attention, how we interpret that information, and why we gave it our attention in the first place is of utmost importance. Focus is attention with intention.
人类有意识的注意力每秒能处理 10–50 比特的信息。我们选择处理什么信息、如何处理、以及为什么处理，决定了我们的生活质量。也就是说：我们把什么放进注意力、我们如何解读那些信息、以及我们最初为何把注意力给了它，至关重要。专注，是带着意图的注意力（Focus is attention with intention）。
p.19
Your mind is a set of complex systems, like a supercomputer. Even though I do not believe this is a metaphor that can explain the full complexity of consciousness, it helps illustrate a point. Like how a computer can slow down when you have too many tasks, tabs, apps, or other programs running, so can your mind. When your attention is split, or your focus is fragmented, suffering increases in potentiality.
你的心智是一组复杂的系统，像一台超级计算机。虽然我不认为这个比喻能解释意识的全部复杂性，但它有助于说明一点。就像电脑在你开着太多任务、标签页、应用或程序时会变慢一样，你的心智也会。当你的注意力被分割、专注被打碎时，痛苦的可能性就上升了。
p.19
When our mind is not engaged with being or doing, we allow random thoughts to register in our awareness. "Random" in this case does not mean half good thoughts and half bad thoughts. For every one good thought, there are a hundred bad ones. When you think of good health, there is one outcome: good health. But when a random negative thought about your heavy heartbeat sneaks in, chaos ensues.
当我们的心智没有投入到“存在”或“行动”中时，我们就会任由随机念头进入觉察。这里的“随机”并不是说一半好念头一半坏念头。每有一个好念头，就有一百个坏念头。当你想到“身体健康”时，只有一个结果：身体健康。但当关于心跳过重的随机负面念头溜进来时，混乱就开始了。
p.19
One thought about your heart can lead to thoughts about heart disease, incorporating a time-consuming exercise routine, and all the food choices you make that splinter into 10 more negative thoughts about the side effects of each. Controlling the information that you hold in your focus is the key to overcoming the anxiety, boredom, stress, and overwhelm that plague today's society.
关于心脏的一个念头，能引向心脏病的念头、引向一套耗时的锻炼计划、以及你做的所有食物选择，而每一个又裂变成十个关于副作用的新负面念头。控制你放进专注里的信息，是克服今日社会流行的焦虑、无聊、压力和不堪重负的关键。
p.19
While the conscious mind can focus on a limited set of thoughts and actions, the unconscious mind can manage eleven million bits of
意识心智能专注于有限的一组念头和行动，而无意识心智每秒能处理一千一百万比特的
p.20
information per second. This includes our habits, reactions, breathing, chewing, walking, and everything else that we don't have to "pay" attention to, because we've practiced those skills.
信息。这包括我们的习惯、反应、呼吸、咀嚼、走路，以及一切我们不必“付”注意力的事——因为我们已经练熟了那些技能。
p.20
While much of our unconscious is a result of our mental programming and centuries of evolution, our conscious mind still plays a large role in forming what information our unconscious mind can manage. The depth, wholeness, and state of your focus will determine the entirety of your life. The enjoyment, the suffering, the progress, and the success.
虽然我们的无意识大部分来自心智编程和数百年的演化，但意识心智在“形成无意识能处理什么信息”上仍扮演重要角色。你专注的深度、完整度与状态，将决定你整个人生：那些享受、那些痛苦、那些进步、以及那些成功。
p.20
After a decade of trying to form good habits, instill energizing routines, become a social savant, make money outside of a conventional job, calm the thoughts in my head, and anything else that would result in a higher quality of life - I realized there was something missing.
在花了十年试图养成好习惯、建立提神的日常、成为社交达人、在传统工作之外赚钱、平息脑中的念头，以及一切能带来更高生活质量的事之后——我意识到，少了点什么。
p.20
There was a flaw in the modern methods that people were using to improve their lives. Forming good habits is powerful, but what is the resistance behind forming good habits? Putting yourself in social situations to bust out of your nervous shell is solid advice, but what would make that process seamless? Making money in a creative, leverageable fashion sounds like a dream even when many have done it, but what is the catalyst?
人们用来改善生活的现代方法里，有一个缺陷。养成好习惯很有力，但阻挠好习惯形成的阻力是什么？把自己放进社交场合以打破怯懦的外壳是靠谱的建议，但什么能让这个过程变得顺畅？以创造性、可放大的方式赚钱听起来像做梦——即便很多人已经做到了——但那个催化剂是什么？
p.20
You see, I love to question things. I hope you grow to love it as well. I wanted to build from the ground up. I wanted to find the source of it all. I wanted to go to the beginning of the beginning. To my own surprise, I found what I was looking for. I am here to share this fusion of ideas with you.
你看，我热爱质疑。我希望你也会逐渐爱上它。我想从地基开始重建。我想找到这一切的源头。我想走到“开始之前的开始”。出乎我自己意料的是，我找到了我要找的东西。我在这里，与你分享这套思想的融合。
p.20
My goal is to equip you with the tools necessary to change your life. Not in a cliché motivational way, but in a way where you have a sense of certainty and control over your future while being satisfied and whole in the present. There is more to focus than you think.
我的目标，是给你配备改变人生所需的工具。不是那种陈词滥调的励志，而是让你对未来的确定感和掌控感与当下的满足和完整感并存。专注，远比你以为的更多。
p.20
It is not something that is only utilized when it's time to work. Your focus is the only thing you have control over. It influences your thoughts, emotions, actions, and the positive or negative direction of them all. If you do not focus on one thing that brings awareness to the next, you may not create the
它不是只在“该工作的时候”才动用的东西。你的专注是你唯一能掌控的东西。它影响你的念头、情绪、行动，以及它们全部的正负方向。如果你不先专注于某一件事，从而带出对下一件事的觉察，你可能就不会引发那个
p.21
chain reaction that allows for certain thoughts, emotions, and actions. Your long-term and short-term options are created by when, where, on what, how, and why you focus your attention.
能带来特定念头、情绪和行动的连锁反应。你长期与短期的选项，都由你在何时、何地、对什么、如何、以及为何聚焦注意力所创造。
p.21
Focus influences the quality, impact, and virality of your work.
专注影响你作品的质量、影响力和传播力。
p.21
Habits, routines, goals, health, relationships, finances, mood, and sense of purpose. All the things that you know hold power but can't seem to reap the benefits from.
习惯、日常、目标、健康、关系、财务、情绪、以及意义感——所有这些你知道有力量、却似乎总是拿不到好处的东西。
p.21
You are not a unique case. I was in a similar position. My clients, customers, and peers were in a similar place This is not an overnight process, bu We are attacking the root cause of your problems through focus. The rest will fall into place, because you would only be able to change them if you first brought your attention to them. And without prior attention, like the investment you are giving this book, you may not have realized a crevice of reality where your attention could go.
你不是特例。我也曾处在类似的位置；我的客户、顾客和同行也一样。这不是一夜之间的过程，但……我们是在通过专注，直接攻击你问题的根源。其余的会各就各位，因为只有当你的注意力先落到它们身上，你才有可能改变它们。而在那之前，如果没有注意力——就像你此刻对这本书的投入——你可能根本意识不到现实里还有一道裂缝，可以让你的注意力落进去。
p.21
I am not going to give you advice like "make your bed every morning," because one, I have never made my bed a day in my life beyond when I was forced to as a child or had guests over at my place. Two, it has merit, but misses the point. Making your bed every morning is powerful because of the fact that conscious attention orders the mind. An ordered mind is a happy one and starting your day on that note can build momentum into the rest.
我不会给你“每天早起叠被子”之类的建议。第一，除了小时候被逼着叠、或者家里来客人时，我人生中从没叠过被子。第二，它有价值，但没抓住重点。每天叠被子之所以有力，是因为有意识的注意力会给心智带来秩序。有序的心智是快乐的，以那种状态开始一天，能把动量带到其余时间。
p.21
rom stressing about not being invited to your second-cousin's birthday party You cannot build good habits in all areas of your life without understanding what caused the bad habits in the first place. Focus has a compounding effect. At any given minute, second, millisecond, or moment - your focus is
（此处 OCR 有一行残留）而不是为没被邀请参加二表亲的生日派对而焦虑。如果不先理解坏习惯最初是怎么形成的，你无法在生活的所有领域都建立好习惯。专注有复利效应。在任何一刻——每一分钟、每一秒、每一毫秒——你的专注都在
p.22
channeled. To what degree is dependent on your mental energy and experience.
被引导。到什么程度，取决于你的心智能量和经验。
WHAT TO EXPECT
该期待什么
p.22
p.22
I have written this book to be as cyclical as life is. You can read it 1, 2, 3, or 4 times and make a discovery you hadn't before. Some teachings in later chapters aren't comprehensible without the early chapters, and vice versa. This is my holistic philosophy for better living. I do not intend for it to be presented as dogma. For that reason, I cannot stress critical thought enough. This book does not read in any specific order. You can open a page, pick a line, and extract a lesson from it, even if it takes a decade to experience that lesson in your daily life. A lot of the information will be the same but presented from various perspectives to aid in understanding.
我把这本书写得像人生一样循环往复。你可以读一遍、两遍、三遍、四遍，每次都会有新的发现。后面章节的某些教导，如果不读前面的章节就无法理解，反之亦然。这是我关于更好生活的整体哲学。我不打算把它包装成教条。正因如此，我怎么强调批判性思考都不为过。这本书不按任何特定顺序阅读。你可以随便翻开一页，挑一行，从中提取一课——哪怕需要十年，你才会在日常生活中真正体会到那一课。很多内容其实是同一个东西，只是从不同视角呈现，以帮助你理解。
p.22
Each section will provide a different lesson, yet that lesson will connect to other sections. I would encourage you to be conscious of this and note them down when the avalanche of insight strikes.
每一节都会给出不同的课程，但这一课会与别的章节相连。我鼓励你对此保持觉察，在洞见如雪崩袭来时把它们记下来。
p.22
ou have full permission to take my ideas, make them better, and use them to fuel your creation I encourage you to put my ideas to the test. Research all sides of the topic available. Try to prove me wrong, but You must i There will be ideas and topics that I do not go over in depth. This is intentional. I am leaving out details like my personal methods that are subject to change in the next decade. These methods, systems, and strategies can be found in the free content on my website, in my courses, and in other internet content.
你完全有权把我的想法拿走、改进、并用它们去点燃你的创造。我鼓励你把我的想法拿去检验。把话题所有可得的面向都研究一遍。试着证明我错了。（此处原文 OCR 有残缺）有些想法和话题我不会深入展开。这是有意的。我省略了诸如我个人方法之类的细节——那些方法在下一个十年里就会改变。这些方法、系统和策略，可以在我官网的免费内容、我的课程，以及其他互联网内容里找到。
p.23
Aside from my methods being with the times, the other reason I refuse to include them is that my joy in life came from creating these methods. As you will find, testing new techniques, forging your own path, and "figuring it out" are deeply spiritual experiences. And there's psychological data that displays its effect on the brain. Without getting too technical, it feels incredible to build your own thing.
除了“我的方法会随时代变化”这个原因之外，我拒绝把它们写进来的另一个理由是：我人生中的快乐，正来自创造这些方法。你会发现的：试验新技术、走出自己的路、以及把东西“搞明白”，都是极为深刻的灵性体验。而且有心理学数据表明它对大脑的影响。不用讲得太技术：亲手做出属于自己的东西，那种感觉不可思议。
p.23
This book contains big ideas, not technical details, as those are of much less importance. I want you to approach these ideas with the intent of action. Everyone has a mind that bounces between different states, and the ideas will lead to various results dependent on individual practice and interpretation.
这本书装的是大想法，不是技术细节——因为后者远没那么重要。我希望你带着“行动”的意图来接近这些想法。每个人的心智都在不同状态之间弹跳，这些想法最终带来什么结果，取决于个人的实践与解读。
p.23
For the rest of this book, I ask that you set aside your desire to react, judge, and close your mind in an instant if something does not align with your worldview. Seek to observe and understand regardless of their applicability to your ever-changing niche of a situation. They may not apply to you now, but you may realize their importance later in life.
在本书余下的部分，我请求你：当某个东西与你的世界观不符时，别急着在瞬间反应、评判、关上心门。去观察、去理解——不管它们是否适用于你此刻这个不断变化的处境。它们也许现在不适用于你，但你日后可能会意识到它们的重要性。
p.23
There are enough incredible books out there on spirituality, emotional management, creating a better life, productivity, creativity, and lifestyle design. So, do not suppress your curiosity to explore more teachings. I'm here to lay out the pieces of the Universal puzzle. It's up to you to piece them together in your own endeavors. I am not going to prove anything to you, as that is impossible, and proof is in second order to experience. Only you can allow the ideas into vour mind and chance to react to them in a that that inflicts self-harm.
世上已有足够多精彩的书，讲灵性、情绪管理、创造更好生活、效率、创造力、以及生活方式设计。所以，别压抑自己去探索更多教导的好奇心。我在这里做的，是把“宇宙拼图”的碎片摆出来。把它们拼起来的活，得由你在自己的事业里完成。我不会向你证明任何事——那不可能，而且“证明”在优先级上低于“体验”。只有你自己能决定是否让这些想法进入你的心智，以及是否选择以自伤的方式回应它们。
p.23
This book contains a lot of "whats" and "whys," but only a few "hows." While I understand your desire for a quick-fix step-by-step action plan, you must realize that nobody can give you the perfect one. If they can, you can be replaced, or you will find that the methods fall apart with time, and you will still have to create your own. Simple as that.
这本书里有很多“是什么”和“为什么”，但只有几个“怎么做”。我理解你想要一份快速见效的、一步一步的行动计划，但你必须意识到：没有人能给你完美的那一份。如果有人能，那你就是可被替代的；或者你会发现那些方法随时间崩解，最终还是得你自己去创造。就这么简单。
p.24
Instead, you must become aware of the "what," internalize the "why," and start with what you know. Through trial and error - the essence of science, life, and progress - you create your own "how." If you would like, you can then pass that "how" down to others, potentially in exchange for money in a world that is desperate for holistic solutions.
所以，你必须先觉察“是什么”，内化“为什么”，然后从你所知道的开始。通过试错——科学、生命与进步的本质——你创造出属于你自己的“怎么做”。如果你愿意，之后还能把这个“怎么做”传给他人，在一个极度渴求整体性解法的世界里，这或许能换来金钱。
p.24
You may have purchased this book to learn, but learning is a personal matter. It implies a back and forth of success and failure. I beg of you, please do not seek to outsource your ability to learn to the words in this text. That is but another embodiment of the quick-fix mindset.
你买这本书也许是为了学习，但学习是一件私人的事。它意味着成功与失败来回往复。我恳求你：不要试图把你“学习”的能力外包给这些文字。那不过是“速成思维”的另一种化身。
p.24
To begin, we will paint a philosophical description of life itself. And since the external reflects the internal, we will use that knowledge to navigate and reprogram the self to flow in alignment with life.
我们先从对生命本身的一种哲学描述开始。而由于“外在映照内在”，我们会用这份认知去导航并重编自我，让它顺着生命之流而动。
p.24
Next, we will understand and structure the mind in a manner that is conducive to maximum enjoyment. From this place of understanding, you will be able to navigate tasks, problems, and situations from a higher perspective. One that allows vou to make better choices.
接下来，我们会以一种能带来最大享受的方式去理解并构建心智。从这个理解的位置出发，你将能够从更高的视角去处理任务、问题和处境——一个让你能做出更好选择的视角。
p.24
Lastly, I will give you the tools to become irreplaceable in the third millennium. That is, to leverage the character you have created by pursuing your purpose, discovering your life's work, and passing down your lessons as the trifecta of The Good Life.
最后，我会给你在第三个千年里变得不可替代的工具。也就是说，用你通过追求使命、发现人生事业、并把自己的教训传下去所塑造出的人格去加杠杆——这三者，构成了“美好生活”的三重奏。
FIND
寻找
p.25
MEANING
意义
p.25
THE PRINCIPLES
原则
p.26
p.26
Beginners find value in methods because they offer certainty. Step-by-step action plans to achieve a specific end result sound promising, but if it were as easy as following a blog article of actionable steps, everyone would be happy, wealthy, and wise.
初学者在方法里找到价值，因为方法提供确定性。通向某个具体结果的一步步行动计划听起来很有前途，但如果真像照着博客文章做几步那么容易，那所有人都会快乐、富有、智慧了。
p.26
Masters, on the other hand, rarely need methods given to them. They prioritize high-level understanding, experiment with various techniques, and craft a strategy that allows them to navigate large and small situations with grace.
而大师很少需要别人给的方法。他们优先追求高层次的理解，试验各种技法，并打造出一套策略，让他们能从容应对大大小小的处境。
p.26
Before we dive into the meat of this book, I want to give a rapid-fire explanation of the principles that will act as a foundation for the lessons you are about to receive. As you progress through the teachings, read with intention. Make an effort to connect the principles to the theory and accompanying practices.
在我们深入本书的核心之前，我想连珠炮式地解释一下那些将作为你接下来所学之基础的原则。在推进这些教导时，请带着意图阅读。努力把原则与理论、以及随附的实践连接起来。
p.26
These are the tenets of the system that this book presents to create a good life. Note that this is a system, and it may not plug into your life like the design of an electrical outlet. Question what I say, question your own answer, and dance in the middle without labeling one interpretation as absolute.
这些就是本书呈现的、用来创造美好生活的系统的信条。注意，这是一个系统，它未必能像插座那样无缝插进你的生活。质疑我说的话，质疑你自己的答案，在中间起舞，而不要把任何一种解读当作绝对。
THE SUPREME LAW
最高法则
p.27
p.27
entropy is the supreme law of the universe, which illustrates that systems end toward disorder, chaos, and destruction on all planes of existence unless energy is put into the system Like how the roads get beaten down, need replacement, and may need to expand to fit a growing population If the system does not evolve with the orla, chaos ensues unt a new system emerges.
熵，是宇宙的最高法则：它表明，除非有能量被注入系统，否则系统在存在的所有层面上都趋向无序、混乱与毁灭。就像道路会被压坏、需要翻修、还可能需要扩建以适应增长的人口。如果系统不随世界一起演化，混乱就会滋生，直到一个新系统出现。
SYSTEMS THINKING
系统思维
p.27
p.27
Systems thinking has many definitions. In this book, we will define it as efficient thought processes.
系统思维有很多定义。在本书里，我们把它定义为：高效的思维过程。
p.27
While roads get beaten down and need replacement over time, so does the mental system that you use to make sense of that road. If you walk to the local grocery store every other day, your mind forms grooves to preserve energy because you don't need to think about where you are walking. But if you were to move across the country, the system would be destroyed, and you may get anxious until you find a new path to solidify your routine. PSYCHIC ENTROPY In our daily practical lives, the main problem is that of mental disorder. Not the kind that can be diagnosed and offered a prescription, but Stress, overwhelm, and anxiety culminate to the point of feeling lost with no light at the end of the tunnel. To this point we can thank a lack of engagement with the present moment tnat allows Jom thoughts to penetrate our awarenes
道路会被压坏、随时间需要翻修，你用来理解那条路的心智系统也一样。如果你每隔一天走去本地杂货店，你的心智会为了省能量而形成沟槽，因为你不需要思考自己在往哪走。但如果你搬到国家的另一端，那个系统就被摧毁了，在找到新的路径把日常固化下来之前，你可能会焦虑。心智熵：在我们日常的实践生活里，主要问题就是心智的失序——不是那种能被诊断并开处方的类型，而是压力、不堪重负和焦虑累积到“感到迷失、看不见隧道尽头的光”的程度。对此我们要感谢的是：缺乏对当下的投入，让随机念头得以穿透我们的觉察。
p.28
Clarity is your savior, and we must prioritize programming, maintaining, and evolving the systems our mind runs on.
清晰是你的救主，我们必须优先去编程、维护和演化我们的心智所运行的系统。
CONTENT IN CONSCIOUSNESS
意识中的内容
p.28
p.28
Everything is information, or form, that arises in consciousness. Everything is in and out of formation, as the Buddhist principle of impermanence would hint at. From our genetic code to the language we speak to the light frequencies we perceive to any "thing" we can label, the structure of the information that fills our consciousness impacts how we move in the world. Consciousness is like water that takes the form of content in the structure of a cup. Routines, rituals, business systems, relationship tactics, sports, other self-help advice, and spiritual teachings allow individuals to prevent their mind's decline into chaos for the temporary amount of time that they hold that form within consciousness.
一切都是信息，或者说“形式”，它们在意识中升起。一切都在成形成毁，正如佛教“无常”原则所暗示的。从我们的基因编码，到我们说的语言，到我们感知的光频，到任何我们能命名的“东西”——充满我们意识的信息结构，影响着我们如何在这个世界里行动。意识就像水，在杯子的结构中呈现出内容物的形状。日常惯例、仪式、商业系统、关系策略、运动、其他自助建议以及灵性教导，让个体能在那份形式被保持在意识中的那段有限时间里，阻止心智滑向混乱。
p.28
It is impossible to bind water in a paper envelope. And in a situation like this, you will either lose the enjoyable clarity you had as time progresses, or you will waste precious energy refilling the paper envelope. Instead, it makes sense to maintain clarity by remaining conscious, intentional, and mindful of the information we expose to our mind.
你不可能用纸信封把水兜住。而在这种情况下，你要么随时间失去原本享受的那份清晰，要么就得浪费宝贵的能量去一遍遍续满纸信封。相反，更合理的是：通过保持觉察、有意图、并对我们放进心智的信息保持正念，来维持清晰。
ZOOMING OUT
拉远镜头
p.28
p.28
To zoom out, like a camera, is to broaden your perspective to interpret a situation for what it is. Your perspective determines how you perceive, like focusing a camera's lens, both the cup and the water. That is, to not get trapped in the potentially negative details of a situation that prevents progress.
像相机一样拉远镜头，就是拓宽你的视角，去看清一个处境本来的样子。你的视角决定了你如何感知——就像调焦相机镜头——既包括杯子，也包括水。也就是说，不要被困在处境中那些可能为负的细节里，从而阻碍前进。
p.28
There may not be 1 cup, but 10. And there may only be 1 cup with an infinite number of cups inside of it. The further you zoom out, the more you
杯子也许不止一个，而是十个。也可能只有一个杯子，而其中装着无数个杯子。你拉得越远，就越
p.29
can expand consciousness, or the water, to flow with life, rather than being bound by the limitations of a small cup.
能扩展意识（也就是水），让它与生命一同流动，而不是被一个小杯子的边界所束缚。
SELF-EXPERIMENTATION
自我实验
p.29
p.29
Self-experimentation is not only the way to solve your problems for good, but to make novel discoveries. Experimentation leads to true experience, and true experience is how you differentiate yourself in the marketplace. A doctor can diagnose and prescribe a solution to your problem that he thinks will work. But that solution is often artificial, doesn't attack the root cause, and creates new problems. If it can be prescribed, its results are temporary.
自我实验不只是永久解决你问题的方式，也是做出新奇发现的方式。实验带来真实的经验，而真实的经验正是你在市场里与众不同的原因。医生可以诊断并给你开一个他认为有效的解决方案。但那个方案往往是人为的、不针对根源、还会制造新问题。如果它能被开处方，它的结果就是暂时的。
INTELLIGENT IMITATION
智性模仿
p.29
p.29
As children, we learned through imitation. We imitate everything around us for the sake of survival. Some end up with more problems, some end up with less, but we all end up in a place that can be improved.
作为孩子，我们通过模仿来学习。为了生存，我们模仿周围的一切。有人最终问题更多，有人更少，但我们最终都落在一个可以被改善的位置上。
p.29
The wav you begin to move in a life direction is to make a conscious change in the people, environments, and information that you are exposed to. By immersing yourself in the stimuli that is conducive to your ideal future, you pick up subtle hints that compound into useful knowledge. But, of course, this knowledge must evolve into understanding through conscious action.
你开始朝某个人生方向移动的方式，是有意识地改变你所接触的人、环境和信息。把自己浸泡在有利于你理想未来的刺激里，你会吸收一些微妙的提示，它们复利成有用的知识。但当然，这些知识必须通过有意识的行动，进化成理解。
RADICAL OPEN-MINDEDNESS
彻底的开放心态
p.29
p.29
When you entered this world, you knew nothing. You explored reality with an open-mind and our child-like wonder reflected that. For most people,
当你来到这个世界时，你一无所知。你以开放的心态探索现实，那种孩童般的好奇就是明证。而对大多数人来说，
p.30
others projected their dogmatic worldview on them while further exploration was discouraged.
别人把他们的教条世界观投射到他们身上，同时进一步的探索被劝阻了。
p.30
Nobody wants to cut themselves off from great discoveries, insights, and truths, but that's what social conditioning does. We accept and attach to the limits projected on us.
没有人想把自己与伟大的发现、洞见和真理隔绝开来，但社会规训正是这么做的。我们接受并依附于那些被别人投射到我们身上的限制。
p.30
Life is counterintuitive in nature. Some of the deepest truths are hidden under what seems to be silly on the surface. Open-mindedness is how you explore the depths, while most people exist on the surface.
生命的本性是反直觉的。有些最深的真理藏在表面上看来很傻的东西底下。开放心态是你探索深处的方式——而大多数人只活在表面。
OBSERVE & QUESTION
观察与质疑
p.30
p.30
Observation is perception without an immediate or reactionary interpretation. When you observe and question, you begin to understand a situation from a big-picture perspective. Only from that vantage point can you make a decision that benefits your future in a way that is the least harmful to others.
观察，是不带即时或条件反射式解读的感知。当你观察并质疑时，你开始从大局视角理解一个处境。唯有从这个制高点，你才能做出一个既有利于自己的未来、又对他人伤害最小的决定。
p.30
No idea is too sacred to question, and the more sacred it seems, the more it should be questioned Qu are crazy for questioning. inat is ine beginning of many inspiring ongin stories.
没有任何想法神圣到不可质疑；越显得神圣的，越应当被质疑。（原文此处 OCR 有残缺）那些敢于质疑的人常被认为是疯子——而这是一切鼓舞人心的起源故事的开端。
JUDGMENT VS DISCERNMENT
评判与辨别
p.30
p.30
Don't judge things that you have not experienced. This should be obvious, but we live in a world of armchair philosophers, scientists, and businesspeople.
不要评判你未曾体验过的事物。这本该是显而易见的，但我们活在一个满是纸上谈兵的哲学家、科学家和企业家的世界里。
p.30
You will never have access to another person's state of mind. You don't understand their situation and you will never have the full picture. Don't judge but observe and discern so you can correct your own behavior accordingly.
你永远无法进入另一个人的心境。你不了解他们的处境，也永远不会拥有完整的画面。不要评判，而是观察和辨别——这样你才能相应地修正自己的行为。
EXPECTATION VS REALITY
期待与现实
p.31
p.31
The space between expectation and reality is tension, pain, and suffering. We often interpret a situation as difficult when it isn't supposed to be any other way. It is what it is, and once you experience this profound truth, life becomes sustainably more enjoyable.
期待与现实之间的空间，就是张力、痛苦与煎熬。我们常常把一个本不该是别样的处境解读为“困难”。它就是这样；一旦你体会到这个深刻的真相，生活会以可持续的方式变得更好享受。
p.31
Your expectations of what things should be is not the reality that is in formation. A similar distinction would be that of concept compared to experience, or the map compared to the territory.
你对“事物应该是什么样”的期待，并不等于正在成形中的现实。一个类似的区分是：概念与体验，或地图与疆域。
p.31
The concepts of God, Brahman, Infinity, or The Universe are not those things. A concept is used to label an experience, yet people latch onto concepts and act like they understand to survive the identity they've formed. Being comes before knowing, and permanent knowing is an inaccurate representation of the impermanence of being.
“神”“梵”“无限”“宇宙”这些概念，并不是那些东西本身。概念是用来标记体验的，但人们却抓住概念，装作自己懂了，以维持他们已经形成的身份认同。“存在”先于“知道”，而永恒的“知道”并不能准确代表“存在”的无常。
RADICAL ACCEPTANCE
彻底的接纳
p.31
p.31
Things aren't supposed to be anything other than what they are, and once you accept this, expectation aligns with reality. Focus is no longer split but engaged with the present moment.
事物本就不该是别的样子，只有它们本来的样子；一旦你接纳这一点，期待就与现实对齐了。专注不再被分裂，而是投入到当下。
p.31
Whether you are climbing Mount Everest, arguing with your partner, or losing money in your business, there is nothing you can think that will change the situation. Instead, you must align and act.
无论你是在攀登珠峰、和伴侣吵架、还是在生意上亏钱，你能想到的任何念头都改变不了处境。相反，你必须对齐，然后行动。
KNOWLEDGE VS UNDERSTANDING
知识与理解
p.31
p.31
One can know a lot but understand very little. Knowledge is constructed upward, while understanding is discovered inward. Both are useful, but to think that knowledge will make you happy, healthy, and wise is a fool's endeavor.
一个人可以知道很多，却理解得很少。知识是向上构建的，理解是向内发现的。两者都有用，但以为知识能让你快乐、健康、智慧，那是愚人的事业。
p.32
Knowledge must be acquired, but in order to understand, it must be brushed up against reality to see if it holds its weight. One can philosophize, fabricate, and hold hard-set beliefs by sitting behind a screen. But can they run a business? Nurture a relationship? Or apply their knowledge to the times they live in?
知识必须被获取，但为了理解，它必须被拿去和现实摩擦一下，看看是否经得起掂量。一个人可以坐在屏幕后头哲思、编造、抱着僵硬的信念。但——他能经营一门生意吗？能养育一段关系吗？能把知识应用到他身处的时代吗？
REALITY EXPLORATION
探索现实
p.32
p.32
It is obvious that the only way to make novel discoveries, creations, and innovations is to embrace the unknown, preferably with curiosity as your driver toward a meaningful goal.
显而易见，做出新奇发现、创造与创新的唯一方式，就是拥抱未知——最好是以好奇心为驱动，朝一个有意义的目标前进。
p.32
you want to live a life that has not been lived, you cannot follow the default path that is laid in front of you at birth. The sooner you realize this, the sooner you can wrestle with the fear of doing what you want and win HOLISTIC SYNTHESIS At this point in time, niche compartments of reality have been explored, studied, and documented. The school system is structured to train people into these compartments like chemistry, neuroscience, and literature. Reality is not compartmentalized. Everything is connected, and there ar infinite connections to be made. The world needs more polymaths autodidacts, and modern Renaissance men to further the unity of humat CREATIVITY VS PRODUCTIVITY Humans are not robots. The creative ability of our minds is what separates us from other beings, so we must prioritize that edge. Too many people get
如果你想活出一种未曾被人活过的人生，你就不能跟随那条从出生就铺在你面前的默认路径。你越早意识到这一点，就越早能与“做自己想做之事”的恐惧搏斗并取胜。整体性综合：时至今日，现实的各个细分领域都已被探索、研究、记录。学校系统的结构就是把人训练进这些隔间：化学、神经科学、文学。但现实并没有被分格。一切相连，有待建立的连接是无限的。世界需要更多的博学者、自学者和现代文艺复兴人，来推进人类的统一。创造力 vs 生产力：人不是机器人。我们心智的创造能力，是区分我们与其他存在的关键，所以我们必须优先保住这个优势。太多人
p.33
bogged down with the pursuit of status to be more productive than their peers.
被“比同行更有生产力”的地位追逐拖住了。
p.33
Instead, we want to leverage the efficiency of our minds, systemize mechanical tasks to take up the least amount of time in our day, and make time for creative pursuits.
相反，我们要利用心智的效率，把机械性任务系统化、让它们占掉一天里最少的时间，从而为创造性追求腾出时间。
p.33
The greatest artists, thinkers, and scientists did not impact the world by performing the same repetitive, manual, and replaceable tasks day after day. They prioritized rest, sought to expand their minds, and prioritized creativity to solve big problems.
最伟大的艺术家、思想家和科学家，并不是靠日复一日做同样的、重复的、可替代的任务来影响世界的。他们优先休息，寻求扩展心智，并把创造力放在首位去解决大问题。
STORYTELLING
讲故事
p.33
p.33
Stories house the components that form the foundation of human behavior. Like a good book, life unfolds in chapters and phases. There is a problem, call to adventure, curiosity, exploration of the unknown, struggle, insight, transformation, solution, climax, and more that happen more than once over the course of a lifetime.
故事里装着构成人类行为地基的组件。像一本好书，人生以章节和阶段展开。问题、冒险的召唤、好奇、对未知的探索、挣扎、洞见、转变、解法、高潮……等等，会在一个人的一生中不止一次地发生。
p.33
The problem is that most people are either distracted or stuck in a phase because they lack the ability to see the big picture. Nobody wants to get lost in the unknown and everybody wants to sustain the climax. This is a recipe for disaster.
问题在于，大多数人要么被分心，要么卡在某个阶段，因为他们缺乏看见大局的能力。没有人想在未知中迷失，而每个人都想停在高潮里。这是一份灾难的配方。
FAILURE & STRUGGLE
失败与挣扎
p.33
p.33
Success cannot exist without failure; it just wouldn't make sense. Without failure, you would have nothing of your own worth working toward. You can observe the achievements of others and desire for the same, but the pursuit of another's goals signals a lack of regard for the importance of one's own.
没有失败，成功就无法存在；否则它就没道理了。没有失败，你就没有什么属于自己的、值得为之努力的东西。你可以观察他人的成就并渴望同样的东西，但追求别人的目标，本身就说明你对自己目标的重要性缺乏尊重。
p.34
Failure and struggle are necessary experiences from which you can toss an anchor and pull yourself toward a better future. This way you don't end up living someone else's life, one that you are near guaranteed to dislike. ITERATION & PERSISTENCE Value requires development over time. A profitable product is not built in a week, nor is a strong body. Even though you may only see someone's happy ending of their story, that does not mean they weren't committed for years prior.
失败与挣扎是必要的体验，你可以从中抛下锚，把自己拉向更好的未来。这样你就不会最终活在别人的生活里——那种你几乎注定会不喜欢的生活。迭代与坚持：价值需要时间发展。一个赚钱的产品不是一周建成的，强壮的身体也不是。即便你只看到别人故事里的幸福结局，那也不意味着他们此前没有坚持多年。
p.34
It is wise to try new things, and I would recommend adopting that habit, but you need a project to develop. Without a tangible vessel for your knowledge, skill acquisition, and discoveries, you may end up with years of energy spent with nothing to show for it.
尝试新东西是明智的，我也建议你养成这个习惯，但你需要一个项目去发展。如果没有一个有形的容器来承载你的知识、技能习得和发现，你可能会花掉数年精力却拿不出任何东西。
POLARITY
两极性
p.34
p.34
Reality is not black and white. A coin is not heads or tails. A human is not happy or sad. Those are but temporary dualities that the mind attempts to make permanent with labels, concepts, and ideologies.
现实不是非黑即白的。一枚硬币不是正面或反面。一个人不是快乐或悲伤的。那些只是暂时的二元对立，是心智试图用标签、概念和意识形态把它们变成永久的东西。
p.34
Instead, view 2 sides of the same coin as just that. They have their opposites but are bound by relationship. Success is a higher state on the spectrum of failure and vice versa.
相反，把同一枚硬币的两面就看作那样：它们各有所对立，却被关系绑在一起。成功是失败光谱上的一个更高状态，反之亦然。
p.34
Form would not make sense without space. When you flip the design of a tapestry, you see the ugly mess that lies underneath HUNTING FOR HOLISM
没有空间，“形式”就没道理。当你把一幅挂毯翻过来，你会看到底下那团丑陋的乱线。追寻整体性：
p.35
Reality is perspective, and your perspective is but one of infinite. Often our point of view determines the positive or negative interpretation of a situation, as when someone else can come in with an equally valid perspective but the opposite interpretation.
现实即视角，而你的视角只是无限之一。我们的观点常常决定了对一个处境的正面或负面解读——比如另一个人能带着同样有效的视角进来，却得出相反的解读。
p.35
If you are a truth seeker, your job is to hunt for kernels of truth in every perspective, even those that aren't human. This forces you to reject all ideology, dogma, or belief system that even the masters may hold as absolute truth.
如果你是真理的追寻者，你的任务就是在每一种视角里搜寻真理的内核，甚至包括那些不属于人类的视角。这会迫使你拒绝一切意识形态、教条或信念体系，哪怕是大师们可能奉为绝对真理的那些。
p.35
This is the only path to sustainable peace, enjoyment, and wisdom.
这是通向可持续的平静、享受与智慧的唯一路径。
EGO DEVELOPMENT
自我（EGO）的发展
p.35
p.35
You don't get rid of the ego; you develop it to the point of being at one with reality. It is often for us to assume that we want to "kill the ego," or "kill desire," when that is simply part of what it desires.
你不是要摆脱自我，而是要把它发展到与现实合一的程度。我们常常以为我们要“杀掉自我”或“杀掉欲望”，可那恰恰是它欲望的一部分。
p.35
Instead, we want to transcend and include. That is to use the ego to navigate the relative world we live in while grounded in the absolute.
相反，我们要超越并包含（transcend and include）。也就是说：用自我在我们身处的相对世界里导航，同时扎根于绝对。
LEVEL OF MIND
心智的层级
p.35
p.35
Every problem you encounter in life demands an increase in your level of mind. Your level of mind is synonymous with the openness of your perspective. You must shed your attachment to expectations, concepts, and beliefs that prevent you from perceiving any situation for what it is. When you can perceive a situation for what it is, you can acquire the skill necessary to match the challenge that a problem presents. This is done with self-education, self-experimentation, and persistence to see that the problem is solved not by the prescription of another, but by your own understanding.
你在人生中遇到的每一个问题，都要求你的心智层级提升一级。你的心智层级等同于你视角的开放度。你必须放下对期待、概念和信念的执着——正是它们阻碍你把任何处境看清为本来的样子。当你能把一个处境看清为本来的样子，你就能获得与问题所呈现的挑战相匹配的技能。这要靠自我教育、自我实验和坚持，去见证一个问题不是靠别人的处方、而是靠你自己的理解被解决。
CONCEPTUAL SURVIVAL
概念层面的生存
p.36
p.36
In this modern world, specifically for those reading this book, I can assume that your life is exponentially more comfortable than that of your ancestors, and it will only continue to move in that direction.
在这个现代世界，尤其是对读这本书的人来说，我可以假设你的生活比你的祖先指数级地舒适，而且只会继续朝那个方向移动。
p.36
The human psyche is interesting in that we survive and reproduce on a conceptual level. We impregnate minds with ideas, those ideas create concepts, we may identify with those concepts, and our behavior shifts in alignment with those.
人类心智有趣的地方在于：我们在概念层面上生存与繁衍。我们把想法植入他人的心智，这些想法创造出概念，我们可能与这些概念认同，而我们的行为随之一致地改变。
p.36
The self is the concept of concepts, and the majority of our actions are taken to survive the self.
自我，是“概念之概念”，而我们大部分行动，都是为了“让自我存活下去”。
MASTERY OVER MISERY
以精通战胜痛苦
p.36
p.36
A sushi chef spends years perfecting the preparation of rice. A tennis player obsesses over the angle of their serve. Mastery sets you apart in a world that can't see beyond the surface.
一位寿司师傅花数年时间去完善煮饭。一位网球选手痴迷于自己发球的角度。精通，在一个只能看见表面的世界里让你与众不同。
p.36
To the masters, repetition of the boring fundamentals is not boring. They have developed intrinsic philosophies and reasoning behind their actions. They look forward to it every day, because they understand that nothing good comes from the quick fix.
对大师而言，重复无聊的基本功并不无聊。他们已经为这些动作发展出内在的哲学和理由。他们每天期待去做，因为他们明白：速成的东西给不了什么好东西。
TACTICAL STRESS
战术性压力
p.36
p.36
Tactical stress is the conscious decision to break out of your familiar routine, put yourself in a do-or-die situation, and realize that the only thing stopping you from reaching the next level is fear.
战术性压力，是有意识地决定打破你熟悉的日常、把自己放进一个“要么做要么死”的处境，并意识到：唯一阻止你到达下一层的，就是恐惧。
p.36
If you have the skill to match the challenge, and are honest with yourself, all you need is to rip the bandage off. Not only will you make a leap in
如果你拥有与挑战相匹配的技能，并且对自己诚实，那你需要的只是把创可贴一把撕掉。你不仅会在
p.37
progress, but peace, thanks to the level of mind the stress requires to mitigate.
进步上实现一次跃迁，还会获得平静——因为要缓解这份压力所需的心智层级，会把平静一并带来。
p.37
In business, close the client even if you don't know with certainty that you can deliver results. In life, book the flight across the country even if you don't think you can afford it. Make the decision that requires you to finally execute reaching your next stage of evolution.
在生意上，即便你并不确定能交付结果，也把客户签下来。在生活中，即便你觉得负担不起，也把那张跨越全国的机票订了。去做那个要求你终于着手执行、进入下一进化阶段的决定。
SELFISHNESS AS A PRIORITY
把自私当作优先事项
p.37
p.37
Strip all judgments from your mind surrounding selfishness, as I'm assuming those were programmed into your head by the selfish desires of others. Self-education, self-reliance, self-experimentation, self-control, selfreflection, self-awareness, self-employment, and self-management. Those traits are to be prioritized If you need something from another, it is near impossible to act with authenticity. You will unconsciously manipulate your language to get what you want from them with little regard to their life situation. And if you have not developed the value you have to offer, a "noble" pursuit of selflessness is only stunting both your growth and others.
把一切关于“自私”的评判从脑子里剥掉吧——我猜那些评判是被别人的自私欲望编程进你脑袋的。自我教育、自立、自我实验、自控、自省、觉察、自雇、自我管理——这些特质都该被优先对待。如果你必须从别人那里得到什么，你几乎不可能以真实之力行动。你会无意识地操控自己的语言来从对方身上拿到你要的东西，而几乎不顾对方的人生处境。而如果你没有发展出可提供的价值，那种“高尚的”无私追求，只会同时阻碍你自己和别人的成长。
THE 3 PILLARS
三大支柱
p.38
p.38
Let's imagine you are surrounded by the people you admire most. People that are successful by your standards. The ones that have impacted your life to the core. This is different for everyone, but I'm assuming this room would be filled with entrepreneurs, teachers, public figures, philosophers, intellectuals, and others that create, share, and shape culture with their ideas.
设想你被自己最仰慕的人围绕。按你的标准，他们是成功的。他们曾深深地影响过你的人生。这对每个人都不一样，但我猜这个房间里会坐满创业者、教师、公众人物、哲学家、知识分子，以及其他用想法去创造、分享和塑造文化的人。
p.38
There is enough time to ask them one question, "If you could attribute your success to one thing, what would it be?"
你有足够时间问他们一个问题：“如果只能把成功归结于一件事，那会是什么？”
p.38
A hobby of mine is to study the patterns of successful people. And thanks to social media, I've confirmed one pattern. Every successful person - by any standard, even if that version of success means rejecting the world and living a life of peace in the woods - knows that focus is the catalyst to the good life.
我的一个爱好是研究成功者的模式。多亏社交媒体，我确认了一个模式：每一位成功者——无论按什么标准，哪怕那种成功意味着拒绝世界、在林子里过平静生活——都知道：专注是通向美好生活的催化剂。
p.38
Through self-reflection, I've come to the same conclusion. Focus determined my success in all dimensions of life. Because focus is dimension-agnostic. It fueled my spiritual practice, business, relationships, health, writing, learning, and philosophical endeavors.
通过自省，我也得出同样结论。专注决定了我人生各个维度的成功。因为专注是不分维度的。它驱动了我的灵性修习、生意、关系、健康、写作、学习以及哲学探索。
p.38
The ability to focus your attention on a meaningful goal, holding that in the back of your mind as a distraction repellent, knowing exactly how to
把注意力聚焦在一个有意义的目标上，把它放在脑后当作“防干扰剂”，确切知道如何
p.39
achieve it through prior experience, and refocusing on the choice in front of you is a superpower.
通过过往经验去达成它，并在面前的选择上重新聚焦——这是一种超能力。
p.39
But we all know it's not that simple. Because if it were, you would be able to walk out of your front door and see a utopia. I'm not sure if we will ever create a collective utopia, but a personal one is a different story. Focus is a muscle, and success is reserved for those that train it. Training, in this sense, is done at every passing moment. You are focusing your attention right now, and will continue to throughout your day, week, month, year, decade, and so on.
但我们都知道事情没这么简单。因为如果真这么简单，你一走出家门就该看见一个乌托邦。我不确定我们是否能造出一个集体乌托邦，但个人的乌托邦是另一回事。专注是一块肌肉，成功是留给那些训练它的人的。在这个意义上，训练发生在每一个流逝的瞬间。你此刻就在聚焦你的注意力，并且会在一天、一周、一月、一年、十年里持续如此，等等。
p.39
"Training" is synonymous with conditioning or programming. Conditioning is the engine that shapes our behaviors, thoughts, and emotions through focus. The key with all of these is conscious repetition. What we are repeatedly exposed to shapes who we are. For better or worse.
“训练”等同于“条件化”或“编程”。条件化是通过专注来塑造我们行为、想法和情绪的引擎。所有这些的关键，都是有意识的重复。我们反复暴露于什么，就会塑造我们是谁。无论好坏。
p.39
With the hope of sounding the least self-aggrandizing as I can, focus was the driving force of my success. By the age of twenty-five, I had built a one-person business that made more money than I could handle. So much so that I felt the urge to decrease my income, sell my fancy condo, return the expensive watches, but keep the fast car because why not, I'll let go of it when that time comes. I had as much free time as I desired (but would usually fill it with study because I enjoyed it so much. I was arguably more stable - in mind, body, spirit, and finances - than the world around me. If I started over from zero, my creative ability would allow me to build it back up in record time, in almost any situation.
希望能尽量不显得自吹自擂地说：专注是我成功的驱动力。到二十五岁时，我已经建立起一门一人公司，赚到的钱超出我能应付的范围。甚至多到我想降低收入、卖掉那套高级公寓、退回那些昂贵手表——但留下了那辆快车，因为何乐而不为，等时候到了我再放手。我拥有想要多少就有多少的自由时间（不过我通常会用它来学习，因为我太享受了）。可以说，我的心智、身体、精神和财务状况都比周围的世界更稳定。如果我一切从零开始，我的创造力也能让我以破纪录的速度重建起来，几乎在任何处境下。
p.39
In short, I had created multidimensional freedom through the compounding nature of focus.
简而言之，我通过专注的复利效应，创造了多维度的自由。
p.39
If you are sold on this whole focus thing, good. That is the first step. But this isn't a promise that you can simply focus on becoming healthy, happy, and wise with hopes that your imagined reality will manifest.
如果你已经认同“专注这回事”，很好。那是第一步。但这不是一个承诺：只要你专注于变得健康、快乐、智慧，你想象出的现实就会显化。
p.39
Focus is the first pillar in a mental feedback loop that is woven into reality itself.
专注，是一个被编织进现实本身的心智反馈回路里的第一根支柱。
I: FOCUS
一：专注
p.40
p.40
Imagine having a spreadsheet that displayed how much attention you've invested in any given area of your life. Mind, body, spirit, and business that impact your relationship with the world and those around you. The spreadsheet would be a direct indicator of your quality of life.
设想你有一张电子表格，显示你在人生各个领域投入了多少注意力：心智、身体、精神、事业——它们影响你与世界以及身边人的关系。这张表会是你生活质量的直接指标。
p.40
Focus is a lost art in a distracted world. Not to mention, it is vastly misunderstood. It is not something limited to when you need to focus, like for a productive work session. It is active at any given moment. You are either focused on something or you aren't, and if you aren't, that is but a lower magnitude of focus until you reach the absolute.
在这个充满干扰的世界里，专注是一门失落的艺术。更别提它被极大地误解了。它不是只在“你该专注的时候”才被使用的东西，比如一次高效的工作时段。它在任何一个瞬间都处于活动状态。你要么正专注于某件事，要么没有；而如果你没有，那不过是一个更低量级的专注，直到你抵达绝对。
p.40
Focus has a frame; we call this perspective or worldview. Perspective is malleable. You can transfer your consciousness to other beings, like your pet cat or dog, in search for understanding of their behavior. Through that perspective, we can interpret and form conclusions in the world through our sensory perceptions and past experiences.
专注有一个边框，我们称之为视角或世界观。视角是可塑的。你可以把自己的意识转移到其他存在身上，比如你的猫或狗，去寻求对它们行为的理解。透过那个视角，我们能通过自己的感官知觉和过往经验去解读世界、形成结论。
p.40
I can narrow the focus of my finger and point at something microscopic. I can open the focus of my body and embrace the harmony of nature. I can filter certain smells through my nose and sounds through my ears. And when it comes to a nice dinner, I can pick apart a grainy texture from a salty liquid from a hint of rosemary. This is reality. An ever-flowing quality of experience.
我可以窄化我手指的焦点，指向某个微观的东西。我可以打开我身体的焦点，去拥抱自然的和谐。我可以让某些气味通过我的鼻子、声音通过我的耳朵被过滤。而在一顿美好晚餐面前，我能把颗粒感的口感、咸味的汁液、和一缕迷迭香分别挑出来。这就是现实。一种永远流动的体验质地。
p.40
Each of these external sensations triggers a series of thoughts, emotions, and memories. When I shift my focus inward, I can explore these entities. I can let thoughts trigger thoughts within a belief system. I can follow an emotion to a past experience. Then, I can picture that experience in vivid detail and, if I enjoyed that experience, I can add a brush stroke to the painting of the future I wish to create. From there, I can shift my focus outward once again, learn how to create that future through study, and narrow my attention on the work that will actualize said reality.
每一个这类外部感觉，都会触发一连串念头、情绪和记忆。当我把焦点转向内在，我能探索这些实体。我可以让念头在信念体系内触发念头。我可以顺着一种情绪追溯到过去的体验。然后，我能把那体验在想象中描绘得纤毫毕现；如果我喜欢那个体验，我就能在我想要创造的未来画卷上添一笔。从那里，我可以再次把焦点转向外在，通过学习弄懂如何创造那个未来，并把注意力收窄到那些将把该现实变成真的工作上。
p.41
The entire journey we just took in the inner and outer world is fueled by attention. At any moment, a rogue thought from a painful past, future task that induces stress, or environmental stimuli could snap your attention into an unconscious state.
我们刚刚在内外部世界所走的这整段旅程，都由注意力供给燃料。任何时刻，一个来自痛苦过往的杂念、一项引发压力的未来任务、或一个环境刺激，都可能把你的注意力猛地拽入无意识状态。
p.41
Attention is the currency that runs the world. It is the foundation of existence. If it doesn't occupy your attention, it doesn't exist. And when you notice novelty, or something that may aid in your survival, your attention is drawn to it.
注意力是驱动这个世界的货币。它是存在的基础。如果某物不占据你的注意力，它就不存在。而当你注意到新颖性、或可能有助你生存的东西时，你的注意力就会被它吸引。
p.41
If our ancestors passed by a familiar bare bush every day, there is no reason to see it as important. But if that bush grew berries, someone would notice it on their next passing, by dopamine signaling its importance, and they would register that bush as a potential tool for later survival.
如果我们的祖先每天路过一丛熟悉的、光秃秃的灌木，那没理由觉得它重要。但如果那丛灌木长了浆果，就会有人在下次路过时注意到它——多巴胺在信号它的重要性——并把这丛灌木登记为一个潜在的、日后可用的生存工具。
p.41
In a modern sense, businesses can only exchange money if attention comes first. Religions are only as powerful as the amount of people that give said beliefs attention. Corporate pyramids have more people with less power at the bottom, and less people with more power at the top. The top holds more power because attention-demanding tasks are delegated to those beneath them.
以现代的方式说：生意只有在注意力先到位时才能换到钱。宗教的力量，只等于给它那套信念投注注意力的人数。企业金字塔在底部有更多权力更小的人，在顶部有更少权力更大的人。顶部之所以权力更大，是因为“需要注意力”的任务被委派给了下面的人。
p.41
The captivating message of these societal entities reach our attention early in life, because they can be a tool for survival. But if we allow them to dominate our minds and control our focus, we may miss out on the depth that life has to offer.
这些社会实体的迷人讯息，在我们的生命早期就进入了我们的注意力，因为它们可以成为生存工具。但如果我们任由它们支配我们的心智、控制我们的焦点，我们可能会错过生命所能提供的深度。
p.41
The attention needed to make a decision can only be done after you give attention to a thought about that action. The thought of going to the bathroom pops in your head and you shift your attention toward walking to the bathroom. The thought can only occur when you have given attention to a prior experience, labeled that snapshot in time, and stored it for later use to aid in your survival. We take mental note of dangerous, important, and useful information from our environment.
做一个决定所需的注意力，只有在你先把注意力给予“关于那个行动的念头”之后才能发生。去上厕所的念头在你脑中蹦出来，你把注意力转向走向厕所。那个念头之所以能出现，只因为你曾把注意力给予一个先前的体验、给那个时间切片贴上标签、并储存起来以备日后生存之需。我们对来自环境中的危险、重要和有用的信息做心理记录。
p.41
As we execute certain attention patterns, like going to the bathroom, it becomes more efficient with time. These attention systems allow us to use
当我们执行某些注意力模式（比如去上厕所）时，它会随时间变得更高效。这些注意力系统让我们能用
p.42
our limited conscious attention to learn more information, store more information, and create systems that conserve mental energy to repeat the process.
有限的意识注意力去学习更多信息、储存更多信息，并创造出节省心智能量的系统来重复这个过程。
p.42
Focus compounds. And it is a great metric to know if you are on a meaningful path in life. True progress requires an ever-evolving shift in focus. If you are repeating the same monotonous tasks in life, it is safe to assume that life seems to lack fulfillment.
专注会复利。它也是一个很好的指标，用来判断你是否走在一条有意义的人生路上。真正的进步要求焦点不断演化与转移。如果你在生活中重复同样的单调任务，那基本可以认定：这样的生活似乎缺了成就感。
p.42
When you start, your survival needs will consume your attention until you solve the right problems in that domain. As you solve your money problems, you gain a bit more freedom. Your focus may shift to selfdevelopment, spirituality, or creating a more meaningful career. In business, your focus will shift priority during every stage. Beginner, intermediate, and advanced.
起步时，你的生存需求会占满你的注意力，直到你在这个领域解决了对的问题。当你解决了钱的问题，你就获得多一点自由。你的焦点可能转向自我成长、灵性、或创造一份更有意义的职业。在生意里，你的焦点每个阶段都要转换优先级：初学、中级、高级。
p.42
At the lowest levels of business, you're focused on learning, making mistakes, and cultivating the value you have to offer. At the highest levels, you get to choose the levers you want to focus on. Like writing for ninety minutes each morning. And if you don't like writing, you can outsource it and choose a more enjoyable way to focus your attention.
在生意的最低层级，你专注的是学习、犯错、以及培育你能提供的价值。在最高层级，你可以选择自己想聚焦的杠杆——比如每天早上写九十分钟。而如果你不喜欢写作，你可以把它外包，选一种更享受的方式去投注注意力。
p.42
In modern slavery, where you can get trapped in one stage of the pyramid, challenges cease to exist. Your life's work will require an ever-increasing level of challenge. The challenge will require a certain set of skills. As the complexity of your skill set increases, the perceived level of challenge stays within a narrow margin of difficulty.
在现代奴役中——也就是你被困在金字塔某个层级里——挑战就不再存在了。你的人生事业会要求不断升级的挑战层级。而挑战会要求某一套技能。随着你技能组合的复杂度上升，你所感知到的挑战难度会维持在一个狭窄的区间里。
p.42
Your hierarchy of goals, from the top down, ideal future to present action, will frame your focus in an indistractable manner. When you create and maintain this fickle mental clarity, you begin to flow with the cyclical nature of the Universe. This is what keeps life meaningful, interesting, and fulfilling.
你的目标层级——自上而下，从理想未来到当下行动——会以一种“不可被分心”的方式框定你的专注。当你创造并维持这种善变的心智清晰时，你就开始随宇宙的循环本性一同流动。这正是让生活保持有意义、有趣、且充实的东西。
II: ENERGY
二：能量
p.42
p.43
There is a phrase, "energy flows where attention goes," that has a mountain of depth behind it (as do most simple platitudes). Focus is not only a muscle that can be trained, but a currency that can be spent, and everyone is out to steal this most valuable resource rather than earn it.
有一句话，“能量流向注意力所到之处”——它背后有着山一般的深度（大多数简单的陈词滥调都是如此）。专注不仅是一块可被训练的肌肉，也是一种可被花掉的货币；而所有人都在等着偷走这份最宝贵的资源，而不是去挣得它。
p.43
In this third millennium, mental energy is the most valuable resource. For this book, we will define mental energy as a term that encapsulates the effects of attention, intention, and will that are amplified with consciousness.
