When you focus your mental energy, attention plays a huge role, but the intention may be misaligned, and the will nonexistent. Focus is the vessel for mental energy.
在这第三个千年里，心智能量是最宝贵的资源。在本书中，我们把“心智能量”定义为一个术语，它囊括了被意识放大的注意力、意图与意志三者的效应。当你调动心智能量时，注意力扮演了巨大角色，但意图可能错位，意志可能根本不存在。专注是心智能量的容器。
p.43
You can focus on a positive potential future through visualization and feel an increase in positive energy in your body. Think of the last enjoyable vacation you went on - does that spark any positive emotions for you? What if you imagine yourself going back to that location in the future? The food you would eat. The people you would be around. The warm nights under the stars with a crackling fire casting a warm glow on the side of your face. Get specific. Can you feel the emotions associated with that experience?
你可以通过可视化，把焦点放在一个积极的潜在未来上，并感到身体里正向能量的提升。想想你最近一次愉快的度假——它是否在你心里激起正面的情绪？那如果你想象自己未来重回那个地方呢？你会吃到的食物。你会共处的人。星空下的温暖夜晚，篝火噼啪作响，在你脸颊一侧映出暖光。要具体。你能感受到那份体验带来的情绪吗？
p.43
This doesn't only apply to positive aspects of life, but negative. And due to the raw power of negative energy, this is where most people mentally reside. An inescapable cycle of past emotions being experienced in the present. Unable to focus that energy toward a positive outcome.
这不仅适用于生活中积极的方面，也适用于消极的方面。而由于负能量的原始力量，大多数人心理上就居住在那里。一个无法逃脱的循环：过去的情绪在当下被重新体验，却无法把那股能量聚焦到一个正向的结果上。
p.43
Specific goals demand a specific amount of mental energy to actualize. You can become aware of how this works with distractions in your life. They hold your attention, eliminate intention, and drain your will. But when you focus on something meaningful, it holds your attention through the clarity that comes from intention and generates will.
具体的目标，需要具体量的心智能量才能实现。你可以通过生活中的干扰来体会这套机制是怎么运作的：它们占据你的注意力、消灭你的意图、并榨干你的意志。而当你专注于某件有意义的事时，它通过由意图带来的清晰，牢牢抓住你的注意力，并生成意志。
p.43
My point here is this: thoughts, emotions, goals, environments, art, tasks, conversations, experiences, and the rest trigger an energy that you can feel. That is notable. Not in a pseudoscientific sense, but in a sense that can be directly experienced.
我在这里要说的是：念头、情绪、目标、环境、艺术、任务、对话、体验等等，都会触发一种你能感觉到的能量。这一点值得注意。不是伪科学意义上的，而是能被直接体验到的意义上。
p.44
Let me introduce you to the supreme law of the Universe: entropy. Some call it "nature's tax," but in short, it is the measure of disorder in a system. It is the driving force in evolution. The law of entropy finds that everything falls into chaos, or that nothing lasts forever. But there's always a chance to start all over again or a way for that system to evolve into something completely different.
让我向你介绍宇宙的最高法则：熵。有人叫它“自然的税”，但简言之，它是系统无序程度的度量。它是演化的驱动力。熵的法则发现：一切都会落入混沌，或者没有任何东西能永存。但总有机会重新开始，或者有办法让那个系统演化成完全不同的东西。
p.44
No matter how much mental energy I use to keep my books in order on the shelf, entropy will take its grasp. Dust will accumulate, humidity will warp the spines, the changing seasons dry out pages. I can clean it, dust it, keep the temperature controlled, but after a while, entropy will take over. Even further, and layering systems on top of systems, compare your home bookshelf to a public library. Entropy impacts individual books, but what about the system to organize those books?
无论我花多少心智能量把书架上的书摆整齐，熵都会抓住它。灰尘会堆积，湿气会让书脊变形，季节变换会晒干书页。我可以清理它、除尘、控制温度，但过一阵子，熵就会接管。更进一步：在系统之上再叠系统——把你的家用书架和一座公共图书馆比较。熵影响单本书，但“用来整理那些书的系统”呢？
p.44
At home, if you don't have a system in place to focus your mental energy, books will end up on the counter, at a friend's house, and on the coffee table. The books will become disorganized unless you attempt to maintain order.
在家里，如果你没有一个系统来聚焦你的心智能量，书最终会散落在柜台、朋友家、茶几上。除非你试图维持秩序，书就会变得紊乱。
p.44
In a library, there is more mental energy put toward managing the organization system. Employees filter, organize, and place books on the shelf so people can find them according to the group of expectations, or system, they hold in their mind. The organization keeps chaos at bay for both the organization and the individual. It allows for the efficient use of mental energy.
在图书馆里，有更多心智能量被投入到管理系统上。员工筛选、整理并把书放上书架，好让人们能按照自己脑中持有的那组期待（也就是系统）找到它们。这种组织让混沌对机构和个人都退避三舍。它让心智能量得以被高效使用。
p.44
This is on the microscale. On the macroscale, these layers of systems will still come to an end. The employees will evolve to new positions or find new jobs altogether. People will grow old, books will fall apart, and efficient digital systems will take their place to extend the lifespan of order. This does not reflect in just a library, but almost everything. Society itself is a system with uncountable physical, mental, and financial systems in place. Culture, business, and personal lives all run on a layered set of systems that are fueled from the bottom up by focused mental energy. This is the fabric
这是微观尺度。在宏观尺度上，这些系统层级仍然会走向终结。员工会晋升到新职位，或干脆换工作。人会变老，书会散架，高效的数字化系统会取代它们，延长秩序的生命。这不仅反映在一座图书馆里，几乎反映在一切之中。社会本身就是一个系统，其中安置着数不清的物理、心智和金融系统。文化、商业和个人生活，全都运行在一套分层系统之上，而这些系统的燃料从底层向上供给——那就是被聚焦的心智能量。这就是文明的
p.45
of civilization. If everyone stopped what they were doing for a day, week, or even month, who knows what the world would look like.
织物。如果所有人停下手上的事一天、一周、甚至一个月，谁知道世界会变成什么样。
p.45
No matter how efficient a system is, it will always fall to the law of entropy because the Universe is balanced with this push-pull tension of chaos and order, method and madness, entropy and negentropy. This does not mean that all is lost. It means that focus must shift with time to maintain a proper flow of mental energy in your life. Standing still is not an option, and if you don't choose where to place your focus, it will be chosen for you.
无论一个系统多么高效，它终将服从熵的法则，因为宇宙正是靠混沌与秩序、方法与疯狂、熵与负熵之间这种推拉张力来保持平衡的。这并不意味着一切都完了。它意味着：专注必须随时间转移，以维持你生活中适当的心智能量流动。原地不动不是一个选项；而如果你不选择把焦点放在哪里，它就会被别人替你选好。
p.45
To understand this evolutionary process of survival, we must understand systems. A system is a group of components that work together to achieve a common goal.
为了理解这个演化的生存过程，我们必须理解系统。一个系统，就是一组为了达成共同目标而协同工作的组件。
p.45
Language is a system that helps humanity communicate, but it also plays a role in almost every other goal that can be achieved. Roads are a system for efficient transportation. These roads have evolved and become more efficient as problems revealed themselves.
语言是一个帮助人类交流的系统，但它也在几乎所有其他可被达成的目标里扮演角色。道路是一个高效运输的系统。随着问题暴露，这些道路不断演化、变得更高效。
p.45
Belief systems, like religious ideology, give people certainty going into an uncertain future. These teachings have been translated with the evolution of language to retain their impact. As systems degrade, problems pop up and our natural behavior is to solve these problems for the sake of survival. Not physical survival, but conceptual, to survive the systems that run civilization.
信念系统，比如宗教意识形态，给走向不确定未来的人提供确定性。这些教导随着语言的演化不断被转译，以保住它们的影响力。当系统退化时，问题就会冒出来，而我们天生的行为就是为了生存去解决这些问题。不是生理生存，而是概念生存——为了让那些运行文明的系统存活下去。
p.45
The mind is a complex set of systems that allows us to interact with reality. Meaning, most of what we do, even if it's not for survival, is goal oriented. Some of these goals are conscious, some aren't, and they all direct our focus and consume mental energy.
心智是一组复杂的系统，让我们能与现实互动。也就是说，我们所做的大部分事情，即便不是为了生存，也是目标导向的。其中有些目标是有意识的，有些不是，而它们全都引导我们的焦点、消耗心智能量。
p.45
Now, there is a Universal pattern to notice here. Human behavior is influenced by a desirable goal, system to achieve that goal, and a problem that once made conscious pushes people to act. The degree of clarity that this process provides will influence how people perceive the goal. That is, whether it is worth pursuing or not.
现在，这里有一个值得注意的普世模式。人类行为受三个因素影响：一个渴望达成的目标、实现该目标的系统、以及一个一旦被意识到就会推动人行动的问题。这个过程所提供的清晰度，会影响人如何看待那个目标——也就是它是否值得追求。
p.46
We can consider this entire process a "hierarchy of goals." The desirable end goal is a given, but a system and accompanying problems house goals within themselves. When one spots a problem, a goal to solve that problem Is Implied. To reach that goal, clarty must bridge the gap with a series of goals, descending in order of execution, to order the mind and encourage action.
我们可以把这一整个过程称为“目标层级”。那个渴望的终极目标是既定的，但一个系统和随之而来的问题本身也容纳着目标。当一个人发现一个问题，“解决这个问题的目标”就被隐式地给出了。为了抵达那个目标，清晰必须用一系列目标把缺口填上，这些目标按执行顺序自上而下排列，以给心智带来秩序并促使行动。
p.46
In a world where so few people set, and even fewer achieve, their own goals, one can piece together an argument that a new version of slavery has emerged after the Industrial Revolution. Not physical, but mental.
在一个如此少的人设定、而更少的人达成自己目标的世界里，人们可以拼凑出一个论点：工业革命之后，一种新的奴役出现了。不是肉体上的，而是心智上的。
p.46
If you don't know what you want, you will be told what you want, and you will believe it. If you don't create a purpose, you will be assigned one. If you don't create a career, you will be assigned one. If you don't create a hierarchy of goals to invest your mental energy in, you will be assigned one, like climbing a corporate, religious, or status ladder just to realize you've wasted 80% of your life.
如果你不知道自己想要什么，就会有人告诉你你想要什么，而你会相信它。如果你不创造一份使命，就会有人给你指派一份。如果你不创造一份事业，就会有人给你指派一份。如果你不创造一个目标层级去投入你的心智能量，就会有人替你指派一个——比如爬一架企业的、宗教的、或地位的梯子，最后才发现自己浪费了人生的 80%。
p.46
This is not a conspiracy theory, but the product of evolution that mental enslavement starts at birth. The interplay of culture, society, and survival place multiple hierarchies of goals in front of us. Go to school, get good grades, praise the god you subscribe to, watch the news to stay informed, and retire when you have enough to scrape by with the little time you have left. Question nothing and invest your mental energy in the "certain" system laid in front of you.
这不是阴谋论，而是演化的产物：心智的奴役从出生就开始了。文化、社会与生存的交织，把多个目标层级摆在我们面前。上学、拿好成绩、赞美你皈依的那位神、看新闻以保持知情、然后在仅剩的一点时间里、在有足够钱勉强糊口时退休。什么都不质疑，把你全部的心智能量投入到摆在你面前那个“确定”的系统里。
p.46
These are not bad, and are necessary stepping stones in many cases, but the point stands. It's no wonder so many people seem miserable. You don't need special glasses to see that. You can tap a few buttons on your phone and deduce what goals people are pursuing, the systems their minds are running on, and the superficial problems they take too seriously that result in misery.
这些并不坏，很多时候还是必要的垫脚石，但论点依然成立。难怪那么多人显得很痛苦。你不需要特制的眼镜就能看见这一点。你只要在手机上点几下，就能推断出人们在追求什么目标、他们的心智在运行什么系统、以及他们过分认真对待的那些导致痛苦的表层问题。
p.46
Collective mental energy is what creates modern power. From the bottom up, key pillars of the external world's structure are fueled by unconscious attention, intention, and will.
集体的心智能量，创造了现代的权力。自下而上，外部世界结构的关键支柱，都由无意识的注意力、意图与意志供给燃料。
p.47
When we pull from our experiences to know what we don't want, gain clarity on what we want, and construct a personal hierarchy of goals to frame our focus, the potential for life enjoyment increases dramatically. But if we don't want to be victims of mental entropy, we must create, improve, and allow for the evolution of systems to aid in our personal development. With experience, we can make these systems more efficient with time. The end goal: full control over where we focus our mental energy thanks to our ability to achieve personal goals, create efficient systems, and solve better problems.
当我们从经验中提取出“我们不想要什么”、获得关于“我们想要什么”的清晰、并构建一个个人目标层级来框定我们的焦点时，人生享受的潜能就会急剧上升。但如果我们不想成为心智熵的受害者，就必须创造、改进、并允许系统的演化来助力我们的个人发展。凭经验，我们能让这些系统随时间变得更高效。终极目标是：完全掌控我们把自己的心智能量聚焦在哪里——感谢我们达成个人目标、创造高效系统、以及解决更好的问题的能力。
III: EXPERIENCE
三：体验
p.47
p.47
Most people would agree that they want to maximize the enjoyment in their lives, but their actions do not reflect that. Happiness as a metric has been distorted, and pleasure isn't sustainable, so "enjoyment" is the word of choice here.
大多数人都会同意他们想要最大化人生的享受，但他们的行动并不反映这一点。“幸福”作为一个指标已经被扭曲了，而“快感”不可持续，所以这里选择用“享受”这个词。
p.47
To sustain maximum enjoyment, you need ample experience. What is experience? It is what's right in front of you. Not a projection into the future. Not a reminisce on the past.
要维持最大化的享受，你需要充分的体验。什么是体验？就是你眼前的东西。不是对未来的投射。不是对过去的追忆。
p.47
Everything outside of the present moment is not direct experience, but an experience of the experience, which can spiral into overthinking, overwhelm, and overanalysis. This can be useful in moderation with a tool like self-reflection, and should be a practice in your life, but you may miss out on the only thing that's real. Especially if you get sucked into the superficial pursuits of the materialist paradigm.
当下时刻之外的一切都不是直接体验，而是“对体验的体验”，它可能螺旋式地变成过度思考、不堪重负和过度分析。作为一种工具（比如自省），适度使用它是有用的，也应当成为你生活里的练习；但你可能因此错过那唯一真实的东西。尤其是当你被吸进唯物主义范式那些肤浅追求里的时候。
p.47
It's impossible to know with absolute certainty what the future holds. Yet, that's what the societal machine promises. The results are almost always unnecessary pain, suffering, and lack of passion for life itself. Why? Because we project further away from the present, get lost in the details, and fabricate problems that have nothing to do with our next step. This is
不可能绝对确定地知道未来会带来什么。可是，这正是社会机器所承诺的。结果几乎总是：不必要的痛苦、煎熬，以及对生命本身缺乏热情。为什么？因为我们把自己投射得离当下越来越远，迷失在细节里，编造出和我们下一步毫无关系的问题。这就是
p.48
the negative scenario of overimagination. Don't label any of this as "bad" just yet.
过度想象的负面剧本。先别急着给这贴上“坏”的标签。
p.48
It's possible to know what the past held and, through our self-reflective consciousness directed by an internal shift in focus, we can make quick and decisive choices toward a better future. This process becomes more accurate with time because we all have a starting point.
知道过去是什么，是可能的；而通过被“内在焦点转移”所引导的自省意识，我们能做出快速而果断的选择，走向更好的未来。这个过程会随时间变得越来越精确，因为我们每个人都有一个起点。
p.48
The start will be slow because you may be solving the wrong problem. But if you continue solving your own problems, or correcting your past mistakes, a positive future is inevitable. You will have to face problems that, when fixed, will threaten your conceptual understanding of who you are. Hold the intention in your mind to be open to change throughout this book.
起步会很慢，因为你可能正在解决错误的问题。但如果你持续解决自己的问题，或修正过去的错误，一个正向的未来是必然的。你将不得不面对一些问题——而它们一旦被修好，就会威胁到你对“我是谁”的概念性理解。在读完本书的过程中，请在心中持有“愿意改变”的意图。
p.48
The path of the problem solver, or value creator, is how you escape the world of replaceability. Fall in love with the challenge that problems present, from superficial to metaphysical, and your ideal future will create itself. This is the infinite game.
问题解决者——或者说价值创造者——的道路，正是你逃离“可被替代的世界”的方式。爱上问题所呈现的挑战吧，从最表层到最形而上的，你的理想未来就会自我创造。这是无限游戏。
p.48
Direct experience is the only thing you can make sound conclusions on when it comes to your life. Intentional, conscious decision-making is how you notice the effect of your actions. If you made a mistake, did you notice that mistake? If you did, have you corrected your behavior? If correcting your behavior is difficult, what's the problem standing in the way of reaching the initial problem that sparked this introspection? That is how you slowly bring more enjoyment into your life. Through relentless and nonreactionary questioning, you are forced to face the reality of a situation. I am not here to debate a topic as nuanced as which fad diet is better for the average individual. But if you identify with a diet ideology, follow that diet regardless of its destructive effect on your individual body, and continue to preach it as "the best," you are a slave to an ideal, rather than using direct experience as a self-corrective compass.
就你的人生而言，直接体验是唯一能让你得出可靠结论的东西。有意图的、有意识的决策，是你注意到自己行动效果的方式。如果你犯了一个错，你注意到了吗？如果注意到了，你修正自己的行为了吗？如果修正行为很难，那么挡在“最初那个引发这场自省的问题”之前的那个问题，是什么？这就是你慢慢把更多享受带进人生的方法。通过不懈的、非条件反射式的提问，你被迫去面对一个处境的现实。我不是来争论“哪种流行饮食更适合普通人”这种细腻话题的。但如果你与某种饮食意识形态认同，无视它对你自己身体的破坏性影响仍然照做，还继续把它宣扬为“最好的”——那你就是某个理想的奴隶，而不是把直接体验当作自我校正的罗盘。
p.48
This applies to all domains of life, and I would encourage you to question the routines, regimens, and prescriptive advice you follow that may not be
这适用于生活的所有领域，我也鼓励你质疑那些你遵循的日常、养生法和处方式建议——它们可能并不
p.49
conducive to the future you truly want. This could be a career path, business model, or even something as simple as your morning routine that you copied from a billionaire.
有利于你真正想要的未来。这可能是一条职业路径、一个商业模式，甚至只是你从一个亿万富翁那儿抄来的晨间惯例。
p.49
What is interesting with the first example is that a vegan who reads this will argue that the meat eater is the one destroying their body, while the meat eater will argue the opposite. My point here is to challenge your beliefs no matter what they are. Understand that we are all unique. Structured advice is useful for initial clarity and action but becomes unsustainable if you reject experience for the status that comes with a label like "vegan." We don't differ too much in genetic code but our minds, worldview, biases, interests, goals, upbringing, geographical location, and all of the momentto-moment inputs we've experienced is my point. There is no one-size-fitsall ideology. Direct experience as a priority is how you create optimal experiences for yourself, not others. Evolution is restricted by the unconscious individuals that don't take responsibility for their lives. Every truth is a half-truth in the relative world, and every relative perspective points a finger toward the absolute. When you collect consciousness to broaden your perspective, or increase your level of mind, the profound reveals itself like a puzzle. One finite pixel in the image will show, and you will label that as fact, until you realize that one pixel was only a figment of an infinite masterpiece.
第一个例子有意思的地方在于：读到这里的一位素食者会争辩说是吃肉的人在毁掉自己的身体，而吃肉的人会争辩相反。我在这里的重点是：无论你的信念是什么，都去挑战它。要明白我们每个人都是独特的。结构化的建议对初始的清晰和行动有用，但如果你为了“素食者”这个标签带来的身份地位而拒绝体验，它就变得不可持续。我们在基因编码上差异不大，但我们的心智、世界观、偏见、兴趣、目标、成长环境、地理位置，以及我们经历过的所有逐刻输入——差异巨大，这就是我的重点。没有一刀切的意识形态。把直接体验放在优先位置，是你为自己（而不是为别人）创造最优体验的方式。演化被那些不为自己的生命负责的无意识个体所限制。在相对世界里，每个真理都是半个真理，而每个相对的视角都有一根手指指向绝对。当你收集意识以拓宽视角、或提升心智层级时，深刻之物会像拼图一样向你显现。图像中的一个有限像素会显出来，你会把它称为事实——直到你意识到，那一个像素只是无限杰作中一处虚影。
p.49
The essence of experience, life, and science is trial and error. You cannot take ideas, opinions, or advice as law without the filter of direct experience. Even if that advice is my own. When reading this book, hold all of what I say in the realm of possibility until filtered through direct experience. You need to make mistakes through action: identify problems, solve them, and make your process more efficient by creating a system that you can follow, spot novel problems, fix them as they arise, and evolve when the system inevitably loses its power to get results. Systems allow us to invest our mental energy in a more efficient manner through problem-solving on the path toward our goals.
体验、生命与科学的本质，是试错。你不能把想法、观点或建议当作法律来接受，除非经过直接体验的过滤。即便那建议是我自己的。读这本书时，把我说的所有内容都保持在“可能性”的领域里，直到它们经过直接体验的过滤。你需要通过行动去犯错：识别问题、解决它们，并通过创造一个你能够遵循的系统，让你的流程更高效；发现新的问题，在它们出现时修好它们，并在系统不可避免地失去取得结果的能力时演化它。系统让我们能以更高效的方式投入心智能量——通过“在通往目标的路上解决问题”。
p.50
If these goals, systems, and problems along the way are not conscious, you can imagine the consequences. Humans are creatures of habit. Without a conscious goal, we will pursue one that makes survival seem easy and comfortable, leading to expectations that don't align with reality. Without a conscious system, we will adopt the habits, beliefs, and opinions of those around us and utilize them to reinforce our unconscious path in life. Without making the problems that arise conscious, we will adopt a victim mentality, reject our ability to change who we are, and have our attention manhandled by others' goals.
如果通往目标的这些目标、系统和问题都不是有意识的，你能想象后果。人是习惯的造物。没有有意识的目标，我们就会去追求一个让生存显得轻松舒适的目标，从而产生与现实不符的期待。没有有意识的系统，我们就会采纳身边人的习惯、信念和观点，并用它们去强化我们那条无意识的人生路径。不把出现的问题变得有意识，我们就会采纳受害者心态、拒绝自己改变的能力，并让自己的注意力被别人目标任意摆弄。
p.50
Without questioning our path in life, the "safe and secure" route that is marketed to us at birth and beyond will become the default option. Beliefs are conditioned into our habit-loving brains. Beliefs influence our thoughts. How we interpret those thoughts influences our state of mind. Our state of mind influences our actions. Our actions compound into our future self. Our future self may not be one of our own creation, and that is the source of the concept of evil.
如果不质疑自己的人生路径，那条从出生起（以及之后）就被营销给我们的“安全又稳妥”的路线，就会成为默认选项。信念被条件化进我们热爱习惯的大脑。信念影响我们的念头。我们如何解读这些念头，影响我们的心境。心境影响我们的行动。行动复利成未来的自己。而那个未来的自己，可能并不是我们亲手创造的——这就是“恶”这个概念的本源。
p.50
We will circle back to experience later. We have a lot of work to do in the meantime. Until then, know that direct experience is king. Start identifying your problems that make life less enjoyable. Seek to understand how you can fix those problems. When you do, learn how to fix them, and fall in love with this process. Success in life, business, relationships, and health is about solving a never-ending string of problems that gets better - and more rewarding - with time.
我们稍后会回到“体验”。在此之前我们还有很多活要干。到那时为止，请记住：直接体验为王。开始识别那些让你的人生不那么享受的问题。寻求理解你该如何修好它们。当你明白了，就学会怎么修，并爱上这个过程。人生、生意、关系和健康上的成功，就是解决一串永无止境、但会随时间变得更好——也更有回报——的问题。
THE HUMAN CONDITION
人的处境
p.50
p.50
Human life is smack in the middle, evolutionarily speaking, of animal and spirit. The mind is both the difference and the bridge. Your day-to-day actions are either pushing you forward or backward. We have the choice to transcend our survival needs from a place of unrealized potential.
从演化的角度说，人的生命正好夹在动物与精神之间。心智既是二者的差异，也是二者的桥。你日常的行动，要么在推你前进，要么在推你后退。我们有选择：从一个尚未实现的潜能之处，去超越自己的生存需求。
p.50
You have 2 options in this life: create something bigger than yourself and let it impact the world, I, or regress into your animalistic nature of reaction,
在这辈子你有两个选项：创造出比自己更大的东西，让它影响世界，或者退化回你那动物性的本能——反应、
p.51
viciousness, and lack of reason. Every situation presents 2 difficult options. Both will result in criticism and pain, but the outcomes are vastly different. Struggle is a guarantee, but the direction in which it leads is yours and yours alone.
恶毒、缺乏理性。每一个处境都会给出两个艰难的选项。两者都会招来批评与痛苦，但结果天差地别。挣扎是必然的，但它引向什么方向，完全是你一个人的事。
p.51
Animals are driven to survive with the information in their genetic code. We are as well, but we have the added drive to survive the information in our consciousness. That is, we attempt to replicate our concept of self. Animals do not have such a complex sense of self that goes on to build cities, manipulate the masses, and create art the influences generations. With this awareness, the future of civilization depends on the selves we create and replicate over the centuries. By pursuing something greater than yourself, the future is bright.
动物靠基因编码里的信息求生存。我们也是，但我们额外有一种驱动力：让我们意识中的“信息”存活下去。也就是说，我们试图复制我们关于自我的概念。动物没有那种复杂到会去建造城市、操纵大众、创造影响数代人的艺术的自我感。有了这份觉察，文明的未来就取决于我们在数百年间创造并复制的那些“自我”。通过追求比自己更伟大的东西，未来就是明亮的。
p.51
There seems to be 2 polar ends of focus that result in an above-average experience. (1) Radical narrow focus on the task in front of you. Doing. (2) Radical open focus that grasps at nothing. Being. While both can be goal oriented, neither are focused outside of the present moment. The Greeks made the distinction between "telic" and "atelic" activities. That is, activities that have a goal and activities that don't.
似乎有两个极端的焦点状态，能带来超常水准的体验：（1）对眼前任务的极端窄焦点。做。（2）什么都不抓取的极端开放焦点。在。两者都可以是目标导向的，但两者都没有把焦点放在当下时刻之外。希腊人区分了“目的性”（telic）和“非目的性”（atelic）活动，也就是有目标的活动和没有目标的活动。
p.51
Peak experience occurs when these 2 ends of the spectrum collapse into one. You may have experienced this before when you become obsessed with a certain skill, task, or goal to the point where you detach from the outcome and focus on the process.
峰值体验发生在光谱的这两端塌缩为一的时候。你以前可能体验过：你对某项技能、任务或目标痴迷到某种程度，以至于从结果上抽离，转而专注于过程。
p.51
Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, a best-selling author and evolutionary psychologist, often talks about "autotelic" activities. This term derives from the Greek words "auto," meaning self, and "telos," meaning goal. Autotelic activities are self-contained. They are done without expectation of a desired outcome. The reward is in the contradictory nature of the activity that combines both absolute being and absolute doing. This is what we are here to dissect, discuss, and replicate in your life. The key to maximum enjoyment is to be where you want to be while doing what you want to do.
米哈里·契克森米哈赖，畅销书作者与进化心理学家，常谈“自成目的”（autotelic）活动。这个词源自希腊语 “auto”（自我）与 “telos”（目标）。自成目的活动是自足的。它们不带着对某个渴望结果的期待而被做。奖赏就在活动那矛盾的本性中——它同时结合了绝对的在与绝对的做。这就是我们要在这里解剖、讨论、并在你生活中复制的东西。最大享受的关键，是在你想在的地方，做你想做的事。
p.52
This spectrum can be found in your direct experience when you seek to see beyond the surface that you've grown accustomed to. But the experience throughout the range of narrow and open focus is not always one that feels good.
当你试图看见自己已习以为常的表面之外时，这个光谱就会在你的直接体验中显形。但贯穿窄焦点与开放焦点整个区间的体验，并不总是感觉良好的。
p.52
You can experience this range from an unconscious or conscious state of mind. Unconscious, meaning not by your free will. An automatic reaction as your attention is occupied by tasks, thoughts, and emotions that don't pass through an awareness filter. Conscious, meaning you are aware of where your attention is in the given moment. In the conscious state of mind, thoughts and emotions are perceived as feedback, not your master.
你可以在无意识或有意识的心境下体验这个区间。无意识，意味着不是出于你的自由意志：当你的注意力被未经觉察过滤器筛过的任务、念头和情绪占据时，那是一种自动反应。有意识，意味着你清楚此刻你的注意力在哪里。在有意识的心境中，念头和情绪被感知为反馈，而不是你的主人。
p.52
Unconscious narrow focus leads to feelings like stress, anxiety, and annoyance. Like when a rogue thought about a stressful future pops into your head. Your focus narrows and you experience the stress that you would feel in that future experience. You are projecting into the future and pulling that experience into the now.
无意识的窄焦点，导致压力、焦虑、烦躁之类的感受。比如，一个关于压力山大的未来的杂念蹦进你脑子。你的焦点收窄，你体验到“你在那个未来体验里会感到的压力”。你是在向未来投射，并把那份体验拽进当下。
p.52
Unconscious open focus leads to feeling lost, overwhelmed, and uncertain. If you project into a future that you don't have clarity to reach, the task of consistent execution seems daunting. Your mind begins to open toward a state of chaos, and your attention bounces between past, present, and future without an intention to piece together a solution.
无意识的开放焦点，导致迷失、不堪重负、不确定。如果你投射到一个你没有清晰路径抵达的未来，那么“持续执行”这件事就显得令人生畏。你的心智开始朝混沌状态敞开，你的注意力在过去、现在和未来之间弹跳，却没有一个拼出解法的意图。
p.52
Conscious narrow focus leads to degrees of a flow state, deep work, and efficiency. We've all experienced this when we have clarity on facing the challenge that a task presents, one that you have the skill to complete. Conscious open focus leads to creativity, relaxation, and a sense of peace. A state where you do not attach to any of the potential thoughts, ideas, emotions, or limits that can pass through your awareness. Think about the last time you were in nature, worry free, and felt at one with the environment. That is what we are getting at here.
有意识的窄焦点，导向不同程度的心流状态、深度工作和高效。我们全都体验过：当我们对“任务所呈现的挑战”有清晰认知，并且拥有完成它的技能时。有意识的开放焦点，导向创造力、放松与平静感。一种你不再依附于任何可能从觉察中经过的念头、想法、情绪或限制的状态。想想你最近一次身处自然、无忧无虑、感觉与环境合一的时候。那就是我们在这里要说的事。
p.52
This focus matrix allows us to become aware of our present experience, indicate the state of our focus, and shift toward a better position to bring more enjoyment to our life. There is a balance that we must strike between
这个焦点矩阵，让我们能觉察当下的体验、指示自己的焦点状态、并转向一个更好的位置，为生活带来更多享受。我们必须在
p.53
doing and being, work and rest, progress and peace, and any other variation of inward-focused and outward focused cognition.
做与在、工作与休息、进步与平静、以及任何其他“内向聚焦认知与向外聚焦认知”的变体之间，找到一种平衡。
p.53
The middle way is that of the spiritual warrior. An individual who does not push away any polar end of the human experience but embraces it all. When the individual receives the call to greatness at the inception of a clear goal, they take it, knowing well that it will be the source of their suffering. Suffering that brings fulfillment. And when they have achieved what they have set out to do, they may push further, but it will inevitably lead to a lesson that teaches balance. The period of intense progress will demand contrast with a period of restful peace. If they do not listen, the suffering will only increase.
中道，是精神战士之道。一个不推开人类经验任何一极、而是拥抱全部的人。当个体在一个清晰目标诞生之初接到“伟大的召唤”，他们会接下它，深知这将成为自己痛苦的来源——一种带来成就感的痛苦。而当他们达成了既定之事，他们可以继续推进，但那不可避免地会带来一课，教会他们平衡。高强度的进步期，必然要求与一段安息的平静期形成对照。如果他们不听，痛苦只会增加。
p.53
The middle way is often mistaken for a boring moderation that eliminates the highs and lows that make life worth living. Instead, it is the opposite. The spiritual warrior is one that pushes the limits of both the material and immaterial. They develop their character as much as they stack their achievements. Not the absolute peace of a monk in a secluded monastery, and not the absolute progress of a businessman on a yacht.
中道常被误认为是一种无聊的节制，抹掉了让生命值得活的那些高点与低谷。恰恰相反。精神战士会同时推进物质与非物质的边界。他们塑造人格的程度，与堆积成就的程度一样深。不是隐居修道院里僧人那种绝对平静，也不是游艇上商人那种绝对进步。
p.53
The purpose of this middle path is to expose your mind, body, and spirit to the full range of the human experience. As you move through life, you acquire the resources to create your own sense of freedom, because you are able to filter that which you don't want, so you can create what you want. Humans have a multitude of characteristics that distinguish them from other beings. It is important that we understand these so we can leverage them in our own lives. That is what "successful" people, by any standard, have done. They lean into their human edge.
这条中道的目的，是让你的心智、身体和精神暴露于人类经验的完整区间。当你穿越人生，你会获得创造属于自己的自由感的资源——因为你能够过滤掉你不想要的，从而创造出你想要的。人类有一大堆区别于其他存在的特征。理解这些特征很重要，这样我们才能在自己生活中利用它们。这就是那些“成功的”人（无论按什么标准）做过的事。他们顺着自己“人类的那把刃”倾斜。
p.53
Depth of focus is the trait that umbrellas our other distinctive traits. With this depth of focus, we identify problems and create solutions. From a high level, that is the key to your success.
专注的深度，是那把为其他特征遮风挡雨的伞。有了这种专注深度，我们识别问题并创造解法。从高层看，这就是你成功的关键。
p.53
We, as humans, focus our mind to alter the direction of evolution. This is an incredible realization. With the creative ability of our mind, we can zoom out beyond the cosmos, gain perspective, and dive back in to make tiny
作为人类，我们聚焦心智，去改变演化的方向。这是一个不可思议的领悟。凭借我们心智的创造能力，我们可以拉远到宇宙之外，获得视角，再潜回来，做出微小的、
p.54
compounding choices that send a ripple of impact throughout humanity, circling back beyond the cosmic scale.
有复利效应的选择，让影响之波回荡整个人类，又绕回来，超越宇宙尺度。
p.54
The problem here is that most people are in a shallow, selfish, and pleasureseeking state. They fail to see the big picture, and instead focus on the next thing that will hide them from the struggle that is baked into life itself. Struggle, as with every other thing we've labeled as negative, is a part of the full range of the human experience. When we shift our focus inward, and without rapid judgment, we can explore this range and see it for what it is.
这里的问题在于，大多数人处在一种肤浅、自私、追求快感的状态。他们看不见大局，反而把焦点放在下一个能让他们躲开“生命本身自带的挣扎”的东西上。挣扎，就像其他所有我们贴上“负面”标签的东西一样，是人类经验完整区间的一部分。当我们把焦点转向内在，并且不急于评判，我们就能探索这个区间，看见它本来的样子。
p.54
This "range" of the human experience reflects throughout all of life. By understanding the Universe from the top down, you will be able to navigate your personal life from a heightened level of mind. That is where we will start.
人类经验的这个“区间”，映照在生命的全部之中。通过自上而下地理解宇宙，你将能够从一个更高的心智层级去导航你的个人生活。我们就从那里开始。
THE UNIVERSE
宇宙
p.55
p.55
When we harness the creative ability of our minds to view life from above, we can discover, collect, and harness profound insights that bring us peace and progress below. The Universe is the most conscious and ultimate perspective you can adopt. Humans come somewhere lower on the consciousness scale, and your ideal or "highest" self can be seen as a stepping-stone perspective toward the Universe. Further down the ladder come animals, plants, and intangible intelligence that you can integrate into your perspective to make it less reactive to low-consciousness problems. True philosophy has one question that contains all others: "How do you live the best life?" I assure you that this question cannot be answered by climbing the power ladder placed in front of you as a child. This question is answered by holding the perspective of the Universe in our mind, observing the essence of its movements (which often can't be put into words), and applying those discoveries to our lives in a practical manner.
当我们调动心智的创造能力，从高处审视人生，我们就能发现、收集并运用那些深刻的洞见，为低处的我们带来平静与进步。宇宙（The Universe）是你能采取的最有意识、最终极的视角。人类处在意识尺度的某个更低位置，而你的理想自我——或“最高”自我——可以被视为一个通往宇宙的踏脚石视角。梯子再往下是动物、植物，以及你可以整合进自己视角的无形智慧，好让你的视角对低意识问题不那么条件反射。真正的哲学只有一个问题，而它包含了其他所有问题：“你如何活出最好的人生？”我向你保证，这个问题无法通过攀爬那个从童年就摆在你面前的权力梯子来回答。这个问题要通过在心中持有宇宙的视角、观察其运动的本质（那往往无法被言说）、并以实用的方式把这些发现应用到我们生活中来回答。
p.55
Before we go any further, I want to make a distinction between the Universe and the universe. One with a capital "U" and the other without. The Universe lies far beyond the senses. It is the universe of universes. Beyond our universe and beyond the cosmos, but still a part of our daily lives.
在继续之前，我想区分一下 Universe 和 universe——一个首字母大写，一个不大写。大写的宇宙远在感官之外。它是“宇宙们的宇宙”。在我们这个宇宙之外，在宇宙之外，但它仍是我们日常生活的一部分。
p.56
Some have called this invisible power "God." Others prefer to label it as The Infinite, Source, The Absolute, The All, or Intelligence. In Aztec philosophy, it is called "Teot!" or in Hinduism "Brahman," which is noted as the highest universal principle. The ultimate reality.
有人把这股无形的力量称为“神”。有人更喜欢叫它“无限”“源头”“绝对”“万有”或“智能”。在阿兹特克哲学中它叫 “Teotl”；在印度教中叫 “Brahman”（梵），被视为最高的宇宙原则。终极实在。
p.56
I have my own beliefs and I am sure you have yours. I use the term "God" at times, but I understand how many reactions that can spark in people to ask for scientific proof of a literal man floating in the sky, locking them further into a dangerous intellectual prison that widens the gap between concept and experience. "God," as far as we're concerned, is the identity of reality. My goal is to leave cultural labels out of this description, as the highest truth cannot be put into words. It must be experienced on a personal level When I tell you to think of a "bird," a specific image will pop into your mind. That image will slightly differ from the image that every other person on this planet will have in their own mind. One person may think of a blue jay, while the other a cardinal, but even then those images have faint lines without further context. While the interpretation is different between us all, the underlying truth of what a bird is remains the same, and it is often indescribable when you pierce through the layers of concepts we use to make sense of that part of reality.
我有自己的信念，我相信你也有你的。我有时会用“神”这个词，但我理解它会在多少人心里激起反感——他们会要求拿出科学证据，证明真有个男人飘在天上，而这会把他们进一步关进一座危险的智性牢笼，拉大概念与体验之间的裂缝。就我们讨论的范围而言，“神”就是现实的同一性。我的目标是在这段描述里把文化标签留在外面，因为最高的真理无法被言说。它必须在个人层面上被体验。当我让你想一只“鸟”，你脑中会蹦出一个具体画面。那个画面会和这个星球上其他所有人心中的画面略有不同。有人会想到冠蓝鸦，有人会想到北美红雀——但即便如此，这些画面也都是线条模糊的，除非给出更多语境。虽然我们之间的解读各不相同，“鸟之为鸟”的底层真相仍是同一个，而当你穿透我们用来理解现实中那部分的一层层概念时，它往往是无法描述的。
p.56
For the sake of coherence and understanding, I will use the term Universe, as it will help us describe its nature with examples that can be noticed in our everyday lives. I am not using this word as a noun, but a verb. This is not a religious doctrine, but I do not want this to turn into a shallow self-help book that leaves out the underlying essence that the industry was built on, often stripping away the "fluff" to help readers acquire an immediate yet impermanent result.
为了连贯与理解，我会使用“宇宙（Universe）”这个词，因为它能帮我们用日常生活中能注意到的例子来描述其本性。我不是把这个词当作名词用，而是当作动词。这不是一套宗教教义；但我也不想让这本书沦为那种肤浅的自助书——把这一行业赖以建立的底层本质删掉，常常剥去“废话”，只帮读者拿到一个即时却不持久的结果。
p.56
You see, from a state of open focus, we can understand that the path to the good life cannot be deciphered from one mere human perspective or belief system. You must observe and note patterns from one perspective to another, even if it isn't a human perspective. A constant state of narrow
你看，从一种开放焦点的状态，我们能理解：通向美好生活的路径，无法从某一个人类视角或信念体系里被破译。你必须从一个视角到另一个视角去观察并记下模式，即便那个视角不是人类的视角。持续的窄焦点
p.57
focus is the result of common self-help doctrine. All too focused on the pragmatic aspects of life to the point of inescapable stress.
状态，是常见自助教条的产物。它过分专注于生活中的实用面，以至于陷入无法逃脱的压力里。
p.57
It is not hard to see the intelligence, consciousness, and nature of the Universe at large. Just because it cannot speak your language or solve your mentally fabricated problems - like the "love of your life" breaking up with you - does not mean it is not intelligent. The narrow, collectively accepted notion of intelligence as "smarts" is not what I am talking about here. This Universal, or infinite, intelligence reveals itself through division and unity, creation and destruction, birth and death, growth and decay, order and chaos. An impeccable and self-corrective balance. This is beyond physical, as we are not animals, and animals cannot conceptualize this power as humans have for centuries. With the emergence of self-reflective consciousness, we have access to spirit. Spirit is the intangible connection between minds.
要看见整个宇宙的智能、意识与本性并不难。它不会说你的语言、也解决不了你心理上编造出来的问题（比如“此生挚爱”跟你分手）——但这并不意味着它不智能。这里我说的不是那种狭隘的、“全体共识”的“聪明”意义上的智能。这种宇宙的、无限的智能，通过分裂与统一、创造与毁灭、生与死、生长与腐朽、秩序与混沌来显现自身。一种无可挑剔且能自我校正的平衡。这超越物理，因为我们不是动物，而动物无法像人类数百年来那样把这个力量概念化。随着自省意识的出现，我们得以触及“精神”。精神是心智之间那条无形的连接。
p.57
Our mind can have an internal battle with itself. Two friends can argue with each other. States can have a political battle during elections. Countries can go to war with one another or with themselves. Notice that these are battles between ideas. Like red versus blue politics. Even a physical battle between humans, at its root, is a part of a larger spiritual war.
我们的心智可以与自己内战。两个朋友可以互相争吵。州与州可以在选举中政治交火。国家可以彼此开战，或与自己开战。注意：这些都是观念之间的战斗。就像红与蓝的政治。即便是人与人的肉体战斗，其根源也是一场更大规模的精神战争的一部分。
p.57
There are cycles, patterns, and rhythms that we can notice to ease the uncertainty of our lives. By understanding these patterns, we can align our behavior with them to reap the benefits that nature provides.
有一些循环、模式和节律可以被我们注意到，以缓解生命的不确定性。理解这些模式，我们就能让自己的行为与之对齐，从而收割自然所提供的收益。
EVERYTHING IS CONNECTED
一切皆相连
p.57
p.57
Let's run through a mediocre dissection of the Universe from what we can comprehend The galaxy contains the solar system, the solar system contains 9 debatable planets, those planets contain Earth. Earth contains the oceans, continents, countries, states, counties, cities, neighborhoods, streets, buildings, and
让我们跑一遍对宇宙的一次平庸解剖，从我们能理解的范围开始：星系包含太阳系，太阳系包含 9 颗（有争议的）行星，那些行星包含地球。地球包含海洋、大陆、国家、州、郡、城市、街区、街道、建筑，以及
p.58
rooms, each having a purpose, beds, humans, organs, all the way down to what we call an atom, and the atom going deeper than I care to illustrate here.
房间；每一个都有其用途——床、人、器官；一路往下到我们称之为原子的东西；而原子还可以再往深处去，深到我不想在这里画出来了。
p.58
All of these individual things being a unit of mind. A figment of consciousness, many of which we aren't in direct physical contact with. Each figment of consciousness is layered and given new meaning.
所有这些个别事物，都是一个心智单元。一处意识的虚影，其中很多我们并不以物理方式直接接触。每一处意识虚影都是分层的，并被赋予新的意义。
p.58
When you focus on a car, it is a car. When you focus on the tire, it is a tire. When you focus on a bolt holding the rim in place, it is a bolt holding the rim in place. Both a whole and a part. A whole in itself and a part of something larger. Humans, by this realization, are a whole, but also a part of something bigger than themselves like a life purpose, a community, or the Universe itself. When we become disconnected from any of the above, we notice a drastic dip in the quality of lite.
当你把焦点放在一辆车上，它就是一辆车。当你把焦点放在轮胎上，它就是轮胎。当你把焦点放在固定轮毂的那颗螺栓上，它就是“固定轮毂的那颗螺栓”。它既是一个整体，也是一个部分。它自身是一个整体，同时又是更大事物的一部分。人类由此领悟到：人是一个整体，但也是某种比自己更大的东西的一部分——比如一份人生使命、一个社群、或宇宙本身。当我们与上述任何一环脱节时，我们会发现自己生活质量的急剧下滑。
p.58
We will define these whole parts as "units of mind." A unit of mind is anything that can be given attention on any plane of existence. As the Universe evolves, these units evolve with it. This is a principle that reflects across all units of mind. One notable characteristic of these units is that after a period of conflict, a creative solution emerges, which is a unit in and of itself that transcends and includes that which came before it. Like an ape to human through the conflict of natural selection, gaining clarity in your personal life after a period of feeling lost, or how an author creates a beautiful work of fiction after ending a toxic relationship. Novel units of mind have emerged throughout evolutionary history to create the relative world we live in.
我们会把这些“整体性的部分”定义为“心智单元”。一个心智单元，是任何在存在的任何层面上都能被给予注意力的东西。随着宇宙演化，这些单元也随之演化。这是一个映射在所有心智单元上的原则。这些单元一个显著特征是：经过一段冲突期之后，会涌现出一个创造性的解法——它本身就是一个单元，既超越又包含了先前的一切。就像猿通过自然选择的冲突变成人；就像你在一段迷失期之后于个人生活中获得清晰；或者，一位作者在一段有毒关系结束后创作出一部美丽的小说。在演化的历史中，新的心智单元不断涌现，创造出了我们所生活的这个相对世界。
p.58
Everything is connected because that is the only way these units would make sense to the human mind. We are pattern-recognition machines that acquire knowledge through analogy, comparison, and metaphor. A hand would not have meaning if it was not connected to an arm. A solar system would not make sense to the human mind if it was not contained nor did contain. And if one did not understand what the solar system was, we would need to educate that person on a series of things. They must first understand Earth, its continents, and layout. Then they would have to imagine or see
一切皆相连，因为这是这些单元对人类心智来说唯一能被理解的方式。我们是模式识别机器，通过类比、比较和隐喻来获取知识。一只手如果不连着手臂，就没有意义。一个太阳系如果不被包含、也不包含什么，对人类心智就没有意义。而如果一个人不知道太阳系是什么，我们就需要对他进行一系列教育。他必须先理解地球、它的大陆和布局。然后他必须想象或看见
p.59
pictures of other planets suspended in what we call "space." In a practical sense, you do not understand your potential because you have not sought to learn by your own desire. Only then can you be exposed to the puzzle pieces that form your potential.
我们所称的“太空”中悬浮的其他行星的图片。从实用的意义上说，你不了解自己的潜能，因为你还没有凭自己的渴望去学习。只有那样，你才有可能接触到那些构成你潜能的拼图碎片。
p.59
The connection of these units is not only vertical, but horizontal (or any other direction or measurement we can label). A hand that holds a cup, without the cup being designed as it is, wouldn't make sense without a hand to hold it. I would encourage you to think about the infinite connections that can be made in any directional fashion. Like how a hand connects to a keyboard that connects to the president of the United States. Attempt to fill in the gap with your creative ability.
这些单元之间的连接不仅是纵向的，也是横向的（或者我们能命名的任何其他方向或度量）。一只手托着一只杯子；如果没有一只手的托举，那只杯子若被设计成它现在的样子，也说不通。我鼓励你去想想“在任何方向上都能建立的无限连接”。比如一只手连接到一个键盘，键盘连接到美国总统。试着用你的创造能力把中间的缺口填上。
p.59
A hand connects to a cup, a cup to a cupboard, and a cupboard to a kitchen, with most households having a kitchen, continuing to connect up and down until an immaterial fabric of thought and consciousness that blanket everything we can possibly know, because that is why we can know.
一只手连接到杯子，杯子连接到橱柜，橱柜连接到厨房；大多数家庭都有厨房，就这样一路向上向下连接下去，直到形成一张由思想和意识构成的无形织物，覆盖一切我们可能知道的东西——因为正因如此，我们才能“知道”。
p.59
There is one notable pattern with this infinite web of connected dots: division and reunion. From the top down, the Universe is a whole that is divided into infinite creative parts. This is the engine that runs the relative world Imagine the ocean or a large body of water. The heat from the sun evaporates that water, dividing into many microscopic droplets. Those droplets rise and reunify as clouds. These clouds grow in size and unify as larger clouds. Soon, droplets unify in the clouds until they are heavy enough to rain back down to Earth. Rain creates puddles, streams, and even plays a role in plant life, which is but another infinite story. Eventually, the rain makes its way back to the ocean with time, and the process is repeated. This is not a localized phenomenon of division and unity. It is infinite. The ideas in your mind divide and reunite; we call this creativity. Throughout human history, races have divided and are now reunifying. On the Universal scale, your opinions do not matter about this, nor do mine. In a few centuries, all of our skin may be the same slight shade of what humans
在这个由无数相连的点构成的无限之网里，有一个显著的模式：分裂与重聚。自上而下，宇宙是一个整体，被划分为无限的创造性部分。这就是运行相对世界的引擎。想象海洋，或一大片水体。太阳的热量蒸发那些水，分裂成无数微小的水滴。那些水滴上升，重聚成云。云不断变大，聚合成更大的云。很快，云里的水滴聚得足够重，便化作雨落回大地。雨造出水洼、溪流，甚至参与植物生命——而那又是另一个无限的故事。最终，雨水随时间回到海洋，整个过程再次重复。这不是一个局部现象式的分裂与统一，它是无限的。你脑中的想法分裂又重聚，我们称之为创造力。在整个人类历史中，族群曾分裂，如今正在重聚。在宇宙尺度上，关于这件事你的意见不重要，我的也不重要。几个世纪之后，我们所有人的肤色也许都会是人类所感知到的那种“棕色”的同一色调，
p.60
perceive as brown, and race as a concept will collapse into one. Note that these processes can vary in time. Entropy, division, unity, creation, destruction, or the rest can happen in an instant or over the course of generations.
而“种族”作为一个概念会塌缩为一。注意，这些过程在时间上可以各不相同。熵、分裂、统一、创造、毁灭等等，可以在一个瞬间发生，也可以跨越数代人。
p.60
I would encourage you to notice this pattern wherever you can, even when making your breakfast, writing a book, or using the bathroom. Notice the parts, wholes, and how they dance together across the physical globe and ripple through the collective consciousness. Even if this thought experiment does not make you $1 million tomorrow, it allows you to appreciate the depth of life when most perceive it as mundane (as they chase the next surface-level, shiny object).
我鼓励你在任何能注意到它的地方去注意这个模式——哪怕是在做早餐、写书、或者上厕所。注意那些部分、那些整体，以及它们如何在地球这个物理球体上共舞，并在集体意识中激起涟漪。即便这个思想实验不会让你明天赚到一百万美元，它也能让你在大多数人都觉得生活平庸时（因为他们正追逐下一个表层闪亮之物）去欣赏生活的深度。
p.60
You are a part of something bigger, and that can only be seen through spirit. By doing this, it reveals that the concepts, beliefs, and ideals we hold so dear are not static. When we identify with these mentally constructed entities and regard them as unchanging, you are in for a world of emotional trouble that prevents personal progress.
你是某种比自己更大的东西的一部分，而这一点只能通过精神被看见。这么做之后，它会揭示出：我们如此珍视的那些概念、信念和理想并不是静态的。当我们与这些心智构造出来的实体认同，并把它们当成不变的东西时，你就等着陷入一场情绪上的大麻烦吧，它会阻碍你的个人进步。
p.60
One of the most beneficial habits you can adopt is playing with mental Legos. Sit with an idea, thought, or problem and follow the connections that present themselves. Stay vigilant of distractions. This is how you practice creativity, mindfulness, and deep thinking without any external tools or guides.
你能养成的最有益的習慣之一，就是玩“心智乐高”。坐下来，和一个想法、一个念头、或一个问题待在一起，跟着那些自行呈现出来的连接走。同时保持警惕，不被分心。这就是你不借助任何外部工具或指导来练习创造力、正念和深度思考的方式。
p.60
The big problem on the cultural, social, and personal level is identification with ideology. Humans group ideas into what is supposed to be indivisible unity of ideas. We leave no room for division and reunion. Your sense of self is but a group of ideas that many see as unchanging. If you are unwilling to let ideas flow as the Universe does, you will be unconsciously bound to a suboptimal state of being.
在文化、社会与个人层面上最大的问题，是对意识形态的认同。人类把一些想法聚合成本该是“不可分割的思想统一体”。我们不给分裂与重聚留出余地。你的自我感不过是一组想法，而许多人把它看作不变的。如果你不愿让想法像宇宙那样流动，你就会被无意识地绑在一种次优的存在状态上。
p.60
Ideologies like certain religions, business models, or diets can be considered collective egos or a collective self. And as we will learn, a collective self will work to survive through mental energy. On the personal level, our concept of self will do the same.
像某些宗教、商业模式或饮食法这样的意识形态，可以被视为“集体自我”（collective ego / collective self）。而正如我们将学到的，一个集体自我会为了存活而消耗心智能量。在个人层面上，我们关于自我的概念也会做同样的事。
ONE SONG
一首歌
p.61
p.61
Uni-verse. One song. That is what you are smack in the middle of. Like you are on a rowboat in the middle of the ocean with a storm brewing overhead, and the boat can sink below the surface at any time unless you bucket the water out.
Uni-verse（宇宙）＝一首歌（one verse）。你正处在它的正中央。就像你坐在大洋中央的一艘小船上，头顶正在酝酿风暴，除非你不断把水舀出去，否则小船随时会沉入水面之下。
p.61
At the top of a wave, hope rises as the sight of land becomes clearer. At the bottom, despair sets in as the 10-foot-tall waves obstruct your vision. As the storm disperses and the sun shines through, we feel at ease, but little do we remember that a storm is not a singular occurrence.
在浪尖上，希望升起，因为陆地的轮廓越来越清晰。在浪谷里，绝望降临，因为三米高的浪挡住了你的视线。当风暴散开、阳光穿透，我们感到安宁；但我们很少记得：风暴不是一次性的孤立事件。
p.61
This fantastical song cycles through summer, winter, spring, and fall. High highs and low lows that illustrate the full range of the human experience. We tend to yearn for summer during winter and reminisce on cozy winter nights during summer. To escape the cold, we cover our ears so we don't have to hear the lesson that would propel us into a season of growth, prosperity, and enjoyment.
这首奇幻的歌在夏、冬、春、秋之间循环。极高的高点和极低的低点，呈现出人类经验的完整区间。我们倾向在冬天渴望夏天，在夏天怀念舒适的冬夜。为了逃离寒冷，我们捂住耳朵，好不必听见那本该把我们推进一个成长、繁荣与享受季节的课程。
p.61
Music is beautiful. To reach harmony, multiple vibrations are designed with care. The pluck of a guitar string creates a high note, the repetitive bang of a drum creates a beat, and the bass adds a little punch. Maybe throw in a few piano keys here or there.
音乐是美的。为了达到和谐，多个振动被精心设计。吉他弦一拨，产生一个高音；鼓被反复敲击，产生节拍；贝斯加一点冲击力。也许这里那里再丢几个钢琴键。
p.61
While this song is infinite in nature, it is multifaceted. It is not one sound played at a time, although it very well could be, but not for long. This reflects in your daily life. If you can't focus, tasks, breaks, and that pesky thought about that argument last night could drive you to the brink of insanity.
这首歌在本质上是无限的，同时又是多面的。它不是一次只奏一个声音——尽管它完全可以那样，但持续不了多久。这反映在你的日常生活里。如果你无法专注，任务、休息、以及那个关于昨晚争吵的烦人念头，就能把你逼到精神失常的边缘。
p.61
Harmony. The Universe is in perfect harmony. You can fight with it or flow with it, and the ego loves to fight with it. The question is: what song is actually playing? And what song are you trying to listen to?
和谐。宇宙处在完美的和谐中。你可以与它对抗，也可以与它同流；而自我（ego）最爱和它对抗。问题是：此刻真正在演奏的是哪首歌？而你又在试图听哪首歌？
p.61
On a practical level, this introduces the topic of understanding, clarity, and perception. You wouldn't take one lyric from a song, play it on its own (or
从实用层面说，这引出了理解、清晰与感知的话题。你不会从一首歌里单拿一句歌词，单独播放它（或者
p.62
on repeat in your head), and expect it to make sense. Similarly, you wouldn't take a sentence from someone else's mouth, plug it into your story, and expect it to have the same meaning.
在脑内循环播放），还指望它能讲得通。同样，你不会把别人嘴里的一句话拿过来，插进你自己的故事里，还指望它有同样的意思。
p.62
Yet this is what humans do. We see what we want to see, ignore what allows it to exist, and let negative thoughts flood our mind about how the crazy person is not the one in the mirror.
然而人类就是这么干的。我们只看见我们想看见的，忽略那些让所见得以存在的东西，并让负面念头淹没我们的脑子：那个疯子才不是镜子里的人。
p.62
The mind craves order, and if the information you are feeding your mind lacks a cohesive structure, you will become a victim of entropy. What's funny is that all information is interpreted through our worldview and perception. Meaning, all information that you process (through any sense, not just sight) is usually a part of a story that you tell yourself. That piece of information, most of the time, will not make sense in alignment with your conscious, subconscious, or unconscious goals in life. You must extract, test, and think about how the information can be utilized without judgment. If you are in a low point in life, seek to see the big picture. Understand that the lows are not permanent, they are not unique to you, and they are followed by a season of progress, if you listen to the lesson that life is trying to teach you.
心智渴望秩序，而如果你喂给心智的信息缺乏连贯的结构，你就会成为熵的受害者。有趣的是：所有信息都是通过我们的世界观和感知被解读的。也就是说，你处理的所有信息（通过任何感官，不只是视觉）通常都是你讲给自己听的那个故事的一部分。那条信息大多数时候并不会与你有意识、潜意识或无意识的人生目标对齐地讲得通。你必须提取、检验，并在不评判的前提下去思考这条信息可以如何被利用。如果你正处在人生的低谷，努力去看大局。要明白低谷不是永久的，不是你独有的，而且只要你听见生活试图教给你的那一课，它后面就跟着一个进步的季节。
CYCLICAL STORIES
循环的故事
p.62
p.62
Life unfolds in chapters, phases, and cycles. The Universe is one song, but it's also one story, and one game. They all have the same structure. There is an introduction, rising action, internal conflict, a main battle, falling action, and resolution.
人生以章节、阶段和循环展开。宇宙是一首歌，但它也是一个故事、一场游戏。它们都有同样的结构：引子、上升行动、内在冲突、主战役、下落行动、以及解决。
p.62
While one lyric of a song may not make sense on its own, it is still a unit that can fit into another song. Everything is connected. The same holds true for stories. Letters are wholes and parts of words. Then sentences, paragraphs, sections, and chapters in a potential series of books.
一首歌里的一句歌词单独看也许讲不通，但它仍是一个能嵌进另一首歌的单元。一切皆相连。故事也是如此。字母是整体，也是单词的部分。然后是句子、段落、章节，以及一部可能的系列书。
p.63
Every sentence has a purpose. Every chapter has a purpose. Every book has a purpose. All of these contain accompanying problems standing in the way of clarity. This is how the mind makes sense of the world. If you are lost, it may be that you turned the page into a chapter where the purpose has not been made clear yet.
每个句子都有目的。每一章都有目的。每一本书都有目的。所有这些都含有挡在清晰之路上的、与之相伴的问题。这就是心智理解世界的方式。如果你迷失了，那可能只是因为你翻到了某一章，而那一章的目的尚未被讲清。
p.63
Layers of stories allow us to construct meaning in our lives. A story has a purpose that the teachings of each chapter lead to. Some chapters are exciting, others boring. The main character is at the top of the world in one chapter, but at the bottom of the ocean in another. And if we fail to open our focus to realize that the highs can't exist without the lows, our mind struggles to maintain order and entropy grasps at our sanity.
一层层的故事，让我们能在人生中构建意义。一个故事有一个目的，而每一章的教导都通向那里。有些章节刺激，有些无聊。主角在这一章处在世界之巅，在另一章却沉在大洋之底。而如果我们不能打开焦点去意识到“没有低谷就不可能有高峰”，我们的心智就很难维持秩序，熵就会抓住我们的理智。
p.63
One of the biggest problems in our time is trying to plug the paragraphs of others' stories into our book. It can make sense, but only if you try to see beyond the literal interpretation of words. Advice, education, and conversation must be interpreted from a shared purpose for it to retain its maximum value. If this shared purpose is not found, the words won't register and arguments, problems, and emotions begin to take over. Order does not only apply to an individual mind but collective as well.
我们这个时代最大的问题之一，就是试图把别人故事的段落插进自己的书里。它可以讲得通，但只有当你在字面解读之外去看时才行。建议、教育、对话，必须从一个共享的目的去解读，才能保住它最大的价值。如果找不到这个共享目的，那些话就不会被接收，争吵、问题和情绪就会开始接管。秩序不只适用于个体心智，也适用于集体。
p.63
We invented language by turning images into symbols, symbols into words, words into paragraphs, and so on. All understanding is metaphorical, and you can find deep lessons by seeking to understand the situation at hand, no matter how much your ego doesn't want you to.
我们把图像变成符号、符号变成词语、词语变成段落……就这样发明了语言。一切理解都是隐喻性的；只要你努力去理解眼前的处境，无论你的自我多么不愿意，你都能找到深刻的教训。
p.63
The structure of stories reflects on all planes of existence that impact human behavior from the top down. There is a solar and lunar eclipse. We've noted patterns in the stars to represent astrological symbols that shift with the calendar (I'm a Libra, by the way).
故事的结构自上而下地反映在所有影响人类行为的存在层面上。有日食和月食。我们记下星辰的模式，用来代表随日历推移的占星符号（顺便说，我是天秤座）。
p.63
In our world, there are 4 seasons. Winter, spring, summer, and fall. While these seasons cannot speak words, they are symbolic of so much more. It does not take much mental effort to understand the feelings, purpose, and behavior that each season contains.
我们的世界有四季：冬、春、夏、秋。虽然季节不会说话，它们却象征了多得多的东西。要理解每个季节所包含的感受、目的和行为，并不需要多少脑力。
p.64
In culture, there are holidays like Halloween. We join in spirit to celebrate an idea and our actions follow the purpose or goal that the holiday presents. I've seen some questionable costumes. Children interpret this holiday as having the purpose of acquiring the most candy possible. Others interpret it with the purpose of letting loose and attracting a mate. Every collective cycle, story, or phase can be interpreted by one in a different way than another, depending where they are at personally.
在文化中，有像万圣节这样的节日。我们以精神相聚，庆祝某个想法，而我们的行动跟随这个节日所呈现的目的或目标。我见过一些可疑的服装。孩子们把这个节日理解为“尽可能拿到最多糖果”的目的。另一些人把它理解为“放松一下、吸引异性”的目的。每一个集体循环、故事或阶段，都会因为你个人所处的位置不同而被解读得不同。
p.64
In society, there are political seasons that get people a bit too emotional. There is a tax season that raises the stress of every individual, no matter their income. These strong, unconscious emotions influence your behavior. And if that behavior is bad, it goes on to reproduce in minds across the globe. If behavior changes on a large enough scale, it can influence the health of society, culture, and even the cosmos at large. Your actions have impact.
在社会中，有把人们搞得过于情绪化的政治季节。有报税季，无论收入多少，都会抬高每个人的压力。这些强烈的、无意识的情绪影响你的行为。而如果那个行为是坏的，它还会在全球各地的心智中复制。如果行为在足够大的规模上改变，它能影响社会、文化、乃至整个宇宙的健康。你的行动是有影响的。
p.64
These global cycles have the potential to control your emotions like a puppet when unconscious. But this is not the worst outcome. Having a little team spirit for your political party has its consequences, but not as many as relinquishing your role as the main character in your personal life. I could go on and on about how robotic we are as species. We have much less "self-control" than we think. The unconscious mind is powerful. It's like a sponge. With every repetition, like flowing water forming the Grand Canyon, our behavior becomes more automatic.
这些全球性循环，在无意识状态下有潜力像操纵木偶一样控制你的情绪。但这还不是最糟的结果。为自己的政党抱有一点团队精神有它的后果，但都不如“交出了自己人生主角身份”来得严重。我可以滔滔不绝地讲我们作为一个物种有多机器人化。我们的“自控力”比我们以为的弱得多。无意识的心智是强大的、像海绵一样。每一次重复——就像流水凿出大峡谷——我们的行为都会变得更自动化。
p.64
You have a sleep cycle, an ingestion cycle, a work cycle, an excretion cycle, and sex cycle, even if you don't have a partner. It's important to note that these are only a portion of the habits we have in our personal life. These personal cycles can vary per the individual, like how bodybuilders go through bulking and cutting "seasons." This ripples through the other cycles in their lives.
你有睡眠循环、进食循环、工作循环、排泄循环、还有性循环，即便你没有伴侣。值得注意的是，这些都只是我们个人生活中习惯的一部分。这些个人循环因人而异，就像健美运动员会经历“增肌季”和“减脂季”，而这会涟漪般地影响到他们生活中的其他循环。
p.64
Even more, there are business cycles. You'll have high months and low months. Seasons of progress and regress. Your business can gain a bit too much "fat" in its exponential growth. And if you don't cut down, it will
更不用说，还有商业循环。你会有高产的月份和低产的月份。有进步的季节和退步的季节。你的生意在指数增长中可能长胖了太多。而如果你不减脂，它就会
p.65
cause more unconscious problems. Those problems will demand your focus, drain your energy, and give you the experience that may be ignored. The cycles of the Universe can be brutal; they don't care about your feelings. As you will learn, I am of the mind that everyone is an entrepreneur, as it is in our nature. A steady paycheck is a useful stepping stone but harsh slave master.
引发更多无意识的问题。那些问题会要求你的专注、榨干你的能量、并给你可能被忽略的经验。宇宙的循环可以很残酷；它们不在乎你的感受。如你将会学到的，我持这样的观点：每个人都是创业者，因为那就在我们的本性里。一份稳定的薪水是有用的垫脚石，却也是严酷的奴隶主。
p.65
The Universal patterns of storytelling are how we construct meaning, language, and communication. Now, this is not limited to stories alone, nor is language limited to the written or spoken word. Language is the signifier of cognitive activity. Nature, sculptures, dance, paintings, games, personal style, and every other aspect of existence that we can perceive with infinite combinations of the human senses can be interpreted by the mind.
讲故事的普世模式，是我们构建意义、语言与交流的方式。而这并不只限于故事，语言也不限于书面或口头文字。语言是认知活动的符号。自然、雕塑、舞蹈、绘画、游戏、个人风格，以及一切我们能用人类感官的无限组合去感知的存在面向，都能被心智解读。
p.65
A sculpture mimics the highs and lows of a story in its grooves, texture, and form. This is a beautiful insight but goes beyond the physical world. We have the ability to sculpt our mind, reinvent ourselves, and craft both a physical and intellectual structure that forms a mode of intangible communication with the external world.
一尊雕塑用它自己的沟壑、质地与形体，模仿一个故事的高潮与低谷。这是一个美丽的洞见，但它还超越了物理世界。我们有能力去雕塑自己的心智、重塑自己，并打造一个物理与智性的结构，构成与外界的某种无形交流方式。
p.65
You have the ability to interpret meaning from a combination of your senses. Sculptures are stories frozen in time. Stories are sculptures melted down and molded into an entirely new song. We can walk into a cathedral and hear music in our ears even when music isn't playing. We can taste a 5star meal and imagine ourselves in an elegant location. This is the gift of consciousness and creation.
你有能力从自己感官的组合中解读意义。雕塑是被时间冻结的故事。故事是被熔化后重铸成一首全新歌曲的雕塑。我们可以走进一座大教堂，在明明没有音乐时在耳中听见音乐。我们可以尝到一顿五星级餐食，并想象自己身处一个优雅的地方。这就是意识与创造的礼物。
p.65
Language and meaning, at their core, are a combination of units of mind, which are the smallest building blocks of ideas. Ideas are a novel emergence that offer a direction in which to pave the road of expanded thought, because thought is a program that is limited by the operating system, or language, it operates on. We can only think as far as we know, and narrow focus prevents us from knowing more. From this insight, we can write a personal, societal, global, or cosmic story that is worth telling.
语言与意义，其核心是“心智单元”的组合——那是想法的最小积木。想法是一种新奇的涌现，它提供了一个方向，让你能铺开扩展思维的道路；因为思维是一个受其运行的操作系统（也就是语言）限制的程序。我们能思考的范围不超过我们知道的范围，而窄焦点会阻止我们知道更多。从这个洞见出发，我们可以写出一个值得讲述的个人故事、社会故事、全球故事或宇宙故事。
p.66
The point is to observe the patterns that are all around you and see how they reflect in your personal life. If you are stuck in a rut, that is but an impermanent state that will resolve with time and effort. Above all, your ability to zoom out to a conscious, open-focused state will allow you to see these seasons for what they are: a necessary low that will lead into an inevitable and impermanent high.
要点是去观察你周围的模式，并看看它们如何映照在你的个人生活里。如果你卡在某个困局里，那只是一个无常的状态，会随时间和努力被解决。最重要的是：你拉远镜头、进入有意识的开放焦点状态的能力，将让你看清这些季节本来的样子——一个必要的低谷，它会引向一个不可避免且无常的高点。
AT ONE NOT WAR
合一而非交战
p.66
p.66
Struggle is a universal principle. It is silly to think that it isn't supposed to be a part of your life. But that is what we do. We expect life to be a certain way, when it isn't supposed to be anything other than what it's being. In this cyclical story of life, there will be conflict. It's the most interesting part of the story, in fact. That's why we love stories. A problem is introduced that piques our curiosity, becomes more problematic until the climax, and when resolved we feel relieved after the roller coaster of emotions.
挣扎是一个普世原则。以为它不该是你生活的一部分，那是愚蠢的。但我们就是这么做的。我们期待生活是某种样子，而它本就不该是别的样子，只有它正在是的那个样子。在这循环往复的生命故事里，会有冲突。事实上，那正是故事里最有趣的部分。这就是我们为什么爱故事：一个问题被引入，激起我们的好奇，变得越来越棘手直到高潮，而当它被解决，在情绪的过山车之后我们感到如释重负。
p.66
From the highest perspective, resolved conflict leads to creative emergence. Stars explode every 10 seconds and create new atomic nuclei. A war between nations creates revolutionary advancements in technology. A fight with your significant other, when resolved, creates a new appreciation for their perspective. Turmoil in your own mind, when accepted, creates profound lessons that make the next round more tolerable.
从最高的视角看，被解决的冲突引向创造性的涌现。恒星每 10 秒就有一颗爆炸，制造出新的原子核。国家之间的战争创造了革命性的技术进展。与伴侣的一场争吵，被解决后，会带来对他们视角的新欣赏。你自己内心的动荡，被接纳后，会创造出深刻的教训，让下一轮更容易忍受。
p.66
But we tend to focus on the technical, and often ideological, details of conflict rather than the big picture. We resist conflict by narrowing our minds on the conflict itself, rather than letting it flow as an interesting, and often necessary, part of existence.
但我们往往专注于冲突中那些技术性、且常常是意识形态性的细节，而不是大局。我们通过把心智收窄到冲突本身来抵抗冲突，而不是让它像存在中一个有趣、且常常必要的部分那样流动。
p.66
We can begin to see conflict, struggle, or battles as problems within a system. If they are not solved, entropy ensues. When we zoom out, seek to understand the system, and let go of the outcome, we create room for
我们可以开始把冲突、挣扎或战斗视为一个系统内的问题。如果它们没被解决，熵就会跟上。当我们拉远镜头、寻求理解这个系统、并放下结果时，我们就为
p.67
progress. Progress feels good. Incredible, in fact, but in the opposite sense of instant gratification.
进步腾出了空间。进步的感觉很好。事实上，好得不可思议——但那是与即时快感相反意义上的好。
p.67
This brings up one of the most important topics of our time. Instead of seeing problems as they are, we see them as we think they should be, and that "should be" is easy. So, we seek external sources of motivation to kick us into action. Or we fight with the problem, not physically, but mentally. We perform mental gymnastics to do anything but face reality.
这引出了我们这个时代最重要的议题之一。我们不是看问题本来的样子，而是看我们认为它“应该”的样子，而那个“应该”是容易的。于是我们向外寻求动力来源来把自己踢进行动。或者我们与问题对抗——不是肉体上，而是心智上。我们做心理体操，只为不去面对现实。
p.67
The Universe acts regardless of how it feels. It doesn't need the concept of motivation. It makes mistakes, self-reflects, and iterates on a solution. Feelings, push comes to shove, mean nothing when it comes to action. Still, we let them run our lives.
宇宙的行动与感受无关。它不需要“动力”这个概念。它会犯错、自我反思、并在解法上迭代。“感觉”，当推诿到尽头时，在行动面前毫无意义。可我们仍然让它们掌管我们的生命。
p.67
You can write, and you can write well, regardless of how you feel. You can do the dishes, walk the dog, apply for the job, start the business, leave the toxic relationship, and make holistic progress even if you don't feel like doing it. Feelings are feedback, and we should treat them as such.
你可以写作，而且可以写得好，无论你感觉如何。你可以洗碗、遛狗、投简历、开始创业、离开有毒的关系，并取得整体性的进步——即便你并不想去做。感觉是反馈，我们就该这样对待它们。
p.67
We live in a delusion that we want to make progress without it being hard. People will go insane over the thought of hot weather but can go into a sauna without complaint. The difference is expectation and intention. That is, a conscious goal with clarity on how to overcome the problems standing in the way.
我们活在一个幻觉里：我们想要取得进步，但又不想它难。人们会因为想到炎热天气而发疯，却能毫无怨言地走进桑拿房。差别就在期待与意图：一个有意识的目标，以及对“如何克服挡路问题”的清晰。
p.67
When you're out in the cold, your automatic reaction is to shiver. To fight. It makes sense. The cold is uncomfortable. So, we focus on the negative thoughts that flood our mind. These stem from the grooves formed by our experience with previous cold exposure. The body is warning us that extreme cold is dangerous, but this is not the case in most modern situations. We have luxuries available to us after centuries of evolutionary problem-solving.
当你在寒冷中，你的自动反应是发抖、是抵抗。这有道理——冷让人不舒服。于是我们把焦点放在淹没脑子的负面念头上。它们源自我们以前暴露于寒冷所形成的沟槽。身体在警告我们极端寒冷是危险的，但在大多数现代处境里并非如此。在数百年的进化式问题解决之后，我们身边有奢侈品可用。
p.67
While our body may fight, our mind doesn't have to. If you were to be with it, flow with it, and realize that discomfort is a part of the human experience, you would find that your thoughts are the culprit of your suffering.
身体可以抵抗，但心智不必。如果你与它同处、与它同流、并意识到“不适”是人类经验的一部分，你会发现：你的念头才是你受苦的罪魁祸首。
p.68
Compulsive thought is the battle of battles. Your resistance to conflict stems from thoughts of comfort that distract you from what is. The way to true comfort is to let go and rejoice in the harmony that is all around you. Of course, there will be seasons where problems seem nonexistent. We get comfortable when life is going well, and we remember these times as reference points that our mind seeks to move back to. Out of nowhere, you may feel lost. You may fall back into bad habits. Entropy will take hold when you let your guard down, and a host of new problems threaten the mental comfort that we love to call home.
强迫性思维，是战斗中的战斗。你对冲突的抵抗，源于那些让你从“当下如是”上分心的、关于舒适的念头。通向真正舒适的路，是放下，并为环绕四周的和谐而欢喜。当然，会有一些问题似乎不存在的季节。当生活顺利时我们会变得安逸，并把这些时段记作心智想要回去的参照点。而后，你会突然感到迷失。你可能跌回坏习惯。当你放松警惕时，熵就会占据上风，一大群新问题会威胁到我们深爱的那个叫做“家”的心理舒适。
p.68
Be wary when things are going too well. If you succumb to these comfortable states of mind, you aren't making progress. You are getting rest for the next round of heat. Rest is good, but the modern notion of rest is distorted. Even a season of mediocrity is a necessary learning experience that allows your vision for personal success to take form.
事情太顺利时要当心。如果你沉溺于这些舒适的心境，你就没有在进步。你只是在为下一轮高温休息。休息是好的，但现代对休息的理解被扭曲了。即便一个平庸的季节，也是必要的学习体验，它让你的个人成功愿景得以成形。
p.68
The nature of experience is refinement through struggle. If you are inexperienced, problems will be as problematic as the attention you give them. Awareness is the first step, universal perspective is the second, and if it is real, accepting the battle for what it is comes last. Radical acceptance of present-moment reality is the start of the solution to most, if not all, of your perceived problems.
体验的本性，是通过挣扎被精炼。如果你缺乏经验，问题就会和你投给它的注意力一样“成问题”。觉察是第一步，宇宙视角是第二步，而如果它够真，最后是接受这场战斗本来的样子。彻底接纳当下的现实，是你所感知到的多数（如果不是全部）问题的解法的开端。
p.68
We aren't trying to be at war with it, we are trying to be at one with it. Sit with the problem. Contemplate it. Fight with it until you realize the futility in fighting with fabrication. Then, let go. When you least expect it, the creative breakthrough will come, and the season of intensity will be at your doorstep. It's not a battle, but a dance.
我们不是要与之交战，而是要与之合一。与问题同坐。沉思它。与它搏斗，直到你意识到“与虚构之物搏斗”的徒劳。然后，放手。在你最意想不到时，创造性的突破会到来，而那个高强度的季节会来到你家门口。那不是一场战斗，而是一支舞。
REINVENT
重塑
p.69
YOURSELF
自我
p.69
THE SELF
自我（THE SELF）
p.70
p.70
The human superpower is choice. We no longer need to outsource our choices to biological, sociological, or psychological drives. Instead, we can aim for the future, acquire specific knowledge, and create a sense of self that leaves a dent on the world.
人类的超能力是选择。我们不再需要把选择外包给生物性、社会学或心理学的驱力。相反，我们可以瞄准未来、获取特定知识、并创造出一种能在世界上留下凹痕的自我感。
p.70
By the time a child is 9 months old, they start developing a kinesthetic image of who they are. Parents cover their eyes, so the child follows, and when they shout "peekaboo!" we let our hands drop away and reveal ourselves to the world.
孩子到九个月大时，就开始发展出关于“我是谁”的动觉形象。父母捂住眼睛，孩子也跟着做，当他们喊“躲猫猫！”时，我们让手落下，把自己揭示给世界。
p.70
As we age, we learn nursery rhymes that teach us certain aspects of our body, especially the face, because we cannot see it directly. To label and remember the idea of our face, we point and remember the labels "eyes, ears, mouth, and nose."
随着长大，我们学会一些童谣，它们教我们身体的某些部分，尤其是脸——因为我们无法直接看到它。为了标记并记住“我们的脸”这个概念，我们指着并记住这些标签：“眼睛、耳朵、嘴、鼻子。”
p.70
From this foundational understanding of the human body, the self can begin interacting with others. And when they do, our sensory perceptions store information in a way that aids in our survival.
从这个关于人体的基础理解出发，自我开始与他人互动。而当他们互动时，我们的感官知觉会以有助于生存的方式储存信息。
p.70
With time, our cognitive capacity increases, and our knowledge compounds. We no longer need to think about who we are and how it impacts our lives.
随着时间推移，我们的认知能力增强，知识开始复利。我们不再需要去想“我们是谁”以及它如何影响我们的生活。
p.71
Once we feel like we have a solid grasp on this thing called "life," physical survival becomes less of a threat, and this is where humans begin to differentiate themselves in a drastic manner.
一旦我们觉得对“人生”这个东西有了牢固的把握，生理生存的威胁就变小了——而正是在这里，人类开始以剧烈的方式分化自己。
p.71
The next phase of survival transcends the physical plane. Modern survival is about mindset. We adopt goals, identify with them, and our behavior changes to achieve, or survive, those goals. This is where things can skew toward good or evil. If you don't define your own goals, standards, and expectations for success, you may end up a slave to someone else's. When we step back and observe the masses, we can see this unfold in a negative manner. From religion to business to sports to jobs, we become a part of a whole of someone else's creation, unconsciously identify with it, and act to survive that identity.
生存的下一阶段超越了物理层面。现代的生存关乎心态。我们采纳目标、与之认同，而我们的行为随之改变去达成——或者说去让目标存活。这时，事情就可能偏向善或恶。如果你不定义自己的目标、标准和成功期待，你可能最终成为别人目标的奴隶。当我们退后一步观察大众，就能看到它以负面方式展开。从宗教到商业、到体育、到工作，我们成了别人所创造之整体的一部分，无意识地与之认同，并为了“让这个身份存活”而行动。
p.71
This alone points toward an answer to sustainable enjoyment in our lives, because this alone is responsible for the majority of our suffering. When we unconsciously act to survive an identity that is often greater than ourselves, the pain can be unbearable.
仅这一点，就指向了“可持续享受人生”的一个答案——因为仅这一点，就为我们大部分的痛苦负责。当我们无意识地行动，去让一个常常大于我们自身的身份存活时，那种痛可以无法承受。
p.71
If we are conscious of the impact of our identity, replace the faulty pieces, and use survival to our advantage in the pursuit of our goals, we can flip our perception of struggle from suffering to fulfillment.
如果我们觉察到身份的影响，替换掉有缺陷的部分，并把“生存机制”用于追求我们自己的目标，我们就能把对挣扎的感知从“煎熬”翻转成“成就”。
SELF AND OTHER
自我与他者
p.71
p.71
Most of the answers to your burning questions about your existence can be encapsulated under 2 meta questions. Who am I? (intrinsic). What is my purpose? (extrinsic).
你关于自身存在那些炽热问题的答案，大多可以归结为两个元问题：我是谁？（内在）我的目的是什么？（外在）
p.71
When we use the words "I" or "me," we are referring to a mental construct. Other people can tell you who you are, but they will never have access to your state of mind. Your friends hold an idea of who you are in their heads, but this is missing billions of bits of information you've processed with your conscious mind throughout your life that form your experience. This
当我们用“我”这个字时，我们指的是一种心智构造。别人可以告诉你你是谁，但他们永远无法进入你的心境。你的朋友脑中持有一个关于“你是谁”的想法，但它缺少你一生中用意识心智处理过的、构成你经验的那数十亿比特信息。这个
p.72
idea is formed by their interactions with you, which I'm assuming is a fraction of the time you spend with yourself.
想法是由他们与你的互动形成的——我猜，那只是你与自己相处时间的一小部分。
p.72
Let's do a thought experiment to understand the concept of self. I want you to picture yourself as a newborn. As you age, you begin to focus your attention on certain things in the world. When you focus on any aspect of reality, a "string" is formed This string is metaphorical. It represents that experience as a snapshot in time. And when these experiences are repeated, the strings become stronger. We often call this "conditioning" or "programming." Now, depending on the perceived importance of that which held your attention, a certain type of string is attached between the self and other. This is a personal distinction that aids in your survival.
我们做一个思想实验来理解“自我”这个概念。我想让你把自己想象成一个新生儿。随着长大，你开始把注意力放在世界上的某些东西上。当你聚焦现实的任何一面时，一根“线”就被形成了。这根线是隐喻性的，它把那段体验表征为一个时间切片。而当这些体验被重复，这些线就变强。我们常称之为“条件化”或“编程”。现在，根据那个抓住你注意力之物的被感知重要性，一种特定类型的线被系在“自我”与“他者”之间。这是一个有助于你生存的个人区分。
p.72
When you first learn about a cloud, you relate it to who you are and what it means to your life. The same goes for your parents, food, bed, grass, and every unit of mind you become aware of. This is including the moment-tomoment perceptions of the situation. How did you feel? Was it positive or negative? Do you want to experience it again? Do you want to fill your experience with more of that thing? Through gradual exposure to the world, we layer experiences on top of each other, forming an invisible web of expectations that allow us to understand the world.
当你第一次听说“云”，你把它与你是什么、以及它对你的生活意味着什么联系起来。对你父母、食物、床、草地，以及每一个你意识到的“心智单元”也是如此。这甚至包括对处境逐刻的感知：你感觉如何？是正面还是负面？你想再体验一次吗？你想让自己的经验里塞满更多那种东西吗？通过逐渐暴露于世界，我们把一层层体验叠在彼此之上，形成一张无形的期待之网，让我们能理解世界。
p.72
Some strings are made of a fickle yarn, others are layered, braided, and strengthened to the point of what would seem like steel wire that is an inch in diameter. The yarn strings are easy to cut, but the steel strings... not so much.
有些线是用脆弱的毛线做成的，另一些则被层层编织、加固，直到看起来像一根直径两厘米多的钢丝。毛线做的线很容易剪断，钢丝做的线……就没那么容易了。
p.72
The yarn strings don't conduct or transfer much energy, but the steel strings can result in a high voltage electric shock, and you won't even see it coming. The stronger the attachment, the stronger the emotional reaction when that illusory identification is threatened. These strings are not only formed from material perception, but immaterial. Beliefs, biases, ideology, ideas, and language that allow you to make sense of the world around you.
毛线线传导不了多少能量，但钢丝线能带来高压电击——而你甚至看不见它来。依附越强，当那个虚幻的认同受到威胁时，情绪反应就越强。这些线不仅由物质感知形成，也由非物质形成：信念、偏见、意识形态、想法，以及让你能理解周围世界的语言。
p.73
This is how the notion of "self" is created. When I say self, I am talking about who you think you are, not who you really are. A mental construct built on a groundless foundation.
“自我”这个概念就是这样被造出来的。当我说自我，我指的是你以为你是谁，而不是你真正是谁。一个建在无根地基上的心智构造。
p.73
Neurotransmitters like dopamine signal that something outside of you is important. Dopamine levels increase in the brain when something new registers in your awareness. When you are young, everything is important. Everything is new. Like a puppy in fresh grass, children explore a world of wonder until it becomes normal to them. As adults, our web of expectations is so developed that life seems to lose its zest. And when something doesn't fit into that narrow worldview, we lash out with negative emotion until we can make sense of it, rather than opening our mind to the wonder of the unknown.
多巴胺之类的神经递质，会发出“你之外有东西很重要”的信号。当新东西进入你的觉察时，脑内多巴胺水平上升。当你年幼，一切都重要，一切都是新的。像一只踩在鲜草上的小狗，孩子探索着一个惊奇的世界，直到它对他们变得平常。作为成年人，我们的期待之网已经如此发达，以至于生活似乎失去了滋味。而当某个东西不符合那个狭隘世界观时，我们带着负面情绪发作，直到能把它弄明白为止——而不是向未知的惊奇敞开心。
p.73
Throughout your personal evolution, your attention roams free and soaks in everything it can to get on the same page as everyone else. A string is formed for a cloud. Another is formed when you perceive the distinction between a light and dark cloud, and yet another when the dark cloud lets out drops of water called "rain." This is rather harmless, but it is only the beginning.
在你的个人演化过程中，你的注意力自由漫游，尽可能吸收一切，好与其他人站在同一页上。为一朵云形成一根线。当你感知到明云与暗云的区别时，又形成一根。当暗云落下叫做“雨”的水滴时，再形成一根。这相当无害，但它只是开始。
p.73
If we remember the division and reunion of a body of water, like the ocean to clouds to rain to puddles to ocean, we can start to understand that a cloud is not static. Since this principle of impermanence is universal, nothing is static, not even you, your state of mind, or who you think you are. The harm is done when we resist life through the power of thought.
如果我们记得一片水体的分裂与重聚——海洋→云→雨→水洼→海洋——我们就开始理解：一朵云不是静态的。由于这个“无常”原则是普世的，没有任何东西是静态的，连你、你的心境、或你以为的自己都不是。当我们用思维的力量去抵抗生命时，伤害就发生了。
p.73
No longer do we live in a time where this signal of importance would indicate a common bush that has newly grown edible berries. Our world is different. Our cultural and social survival needs have evolved, but our psyches are stuck with the wiring of our ancestors. Humans do not primarily survive on a physical level, but on a conceptual level.
我们已不再生活在一个“重要性信号指向一丛刚长出可食浆果的普通灌木”的时代。我们的世界不同了。我们的文化与社交生存需求已经演化，但我们的心智仍卡在祖先的线路上。人类主要不是在物理层面生存，而是在概念层面。
p.73
As we age, and if we retain a low capacity for critical thought, certain beliefs can form strings so strong that when cut, the emotional response is on par with physical death. When the illusory self identifies with something
随着变老，如果我们批判性思维的能力保持在低位，某些信念就能形成强到剪断时情绪反应等同于肉体死亡的线。当那个虚幻的自我与某种东西认同——
p.74
like a religious ideology, and all of its inner workings, it becomes a part of who you are. Who you think you are, that is.
比如一套宗教意识形态及其全部内部构造——它就变成了你的一部分。你“以为”的你的一部分。
p.74
What's the problem with this? The hundreds of thousands - if not billions of strings that form the self over time do just that. They form the self. They are your identity. They influence your thoughts, emotions, and actions. The concept of self is a puppet master to those that do not realize this. The same principle applies to any value system, affiliation, or any other teaching that is often taken as law or touted as the best option. When the identity is threatened, we act to survive the mental construct, because the feeling of threat is real, but often misinterpreted.
这有什么问题？那些随时间构成自我的数十万——如果不是数十亿——根线，正是在做这件事。它们构成了自我。它们就是你的身份。它们影响你的念头、情绪和行动。对于那些没意识到这一点的人来说，“自我”这个概念就是操控木偶的人。同样的原则适用于任何价值体系、任何归属、或任何其他常被当作法律或吹嘘为最佳选项的教导。当身份受到威胁时，我们行动去让那个心智构造存活——因为“受威胁”的感觉是真实的，只是常常被误读。
p.74
Have you not seen this across the news, in your personal life, or on social media? Whether it be political, religious, academic, or scientific, we tend to burst out with extreme, uncontrollable emotion to defend the strings that we have formed to birth, refine, and survive the self.
你在新闻里、个人生活中、或社交媒体上难道没见过吗？无论是政治的、宗教的、学术的、还是科学的，我们往往会爆发出极端、无法控制情绪，来捍卫那些我们为了“让自我出生、被精炼、并存活”而形成的线。
p.74
Know that these strings can attach the self to any unit of mind that you assign importance to. Anything. Like when I was young and would get angry when my brother crossed more than a centimeter through my door. It was the boundary of my room, wasn't it? Why should he be allowed in if I don't want him to be?
要知道，这些线能把自我系到你赋予重要性的任何心智单元上。任何东西。比如我小时候，我弟弟只要越过我房门一厘米，我就会发火。那是我房间的边界，不是吗？如果我不想让他进来，凭什么他可以进来？
p.74
Are you a coffee drinker? If I brought to your awareness that you have a mild addiction and could use a break, how would you react? For many people, they would come back with an immediate answer. No critical thought. No self-awareness. No honesty. A compulsive, fabricated lie to end the conversation as fast as possible. How else are you going to survive the coffee drinker in you?
你喝咖啡吗？如果我把“你有轻度成瘾、该歇一歇”这件事带进你的觉察，你会怎么反应？很多人会立刻给出一个答案。没有批判性思考。没有自我觉察。没有诚实。一个强迫性的、编造的谎言，只为了尽快结束这场对话。不然你怎么让“你体内的那个咖啡饮用者”活下来？
p.74
Some may ask, why would I get defensive about being a coffee drinker? It may not be the coffee itself, but the benefits of feeling as if you belong to the coffee-drinking tribe. Again, something larger than yourself. A part within a whole. The clothes you wear, the places you hang out, and the potential partners you can find that share a love for coffee are on the line. Or it can be that you use coffee to enhance your productivity at work. If
有人可能会问：我为什么要为“我是个咖啡饮用者”而防御？也许不是咖啡本身，而是“感觉属于咖啡饮用部落”带来的好处。又是某种大于你自己的东西。一个整体里的一个部分。你穿的衣服、你出没的地方、以及你能找到的那些同样热爱咖啡的潜在伴侣，都命悬一线。也可能是因为你用咖啡来提高工作效率。如果
p.75
your coffee usage is questioned, your productivity is threatened, and your livelihood comes into the survival equation.
你的咖啡使用量被质疑，你的效率就受到威胁，而你的生计就进入了生存方程式。
p.75
These examples showcase our emotional on-and-off nature. Something as simple as my brother stepping into my room would have me trying to survive the idea of My Room, as I assigned that importance to it and everything in it.
这些例子展示了我们情绪“开—关”的本性。简单到“我弟弟踏进我房间”这种事，都会让我努力去让“我的房间”这个想法存活下去——因为我把重要性赋予了它和其中的一切。
p.75
Treat negative feelings as a test of awareness. When you feel a disturbance in your inner peace, follow that feeling along the string until you reach the source, which may be much, much deeper than you could ever imagine.
把负面感受当作对觉察的一次测试。当你感到内在平静被扰动时，顺着那种感觉沿着那根线回溯，直到你找到源头——而它可能深得远超你的想象。
SURVIVAL SYSTEMS
生存系统
p.75
p.75
Humans survive on a conceptual level. We are not animals, but we have transcended and included aspects of their existence. While we both work to survive the information in our genes, humans work to survive nongenetic information in our consciousness like language, social and cultural constructs, and most notably those which compose our sense of self.
人类在概念层面生存。我们不是动物，但我们超越并包含了动物存在的某些面向。我们都会为让基因里的信息存活而运作，但人类还会为让我们意识中的非基因信息存活而运作——比如语言、社会与文化构造，尤其是那些构成我们自我感的信息。
p.75
