Animals survive their physical form; humans survive their conceptual form. Forms in consciousness change like rain to the ocean, but the mind attempts to make the impermanent permanent due to the evolutionary nature of our psyche. Your "self" is your psychic body, and conceptual forms look out for psychic threats like a narrative, contradiction, or idea within its worldview. When our identity is threatened, we have a physical stress response on par with that of a mouse, moments before death, with 2 poison-dipped fangs penetrating its side. On top of that, you wouldn't see a giraffe getting offended because you challenged its beliefs. This is a human phenomena. Physical survival is still a threat, of course, but we don't live in a world where we must worry about a wild animal latching onto our throat, even in prison much of the time. Through evolution, we have drastically reduced the mental energy required to sustain our physical survival.
动物让它们的物理形态存活；人类让他们的概念形态存活。意识中的形态像“雨水入海”那样变化，但由于我们心智的演化本性，它会试图把无常变成恒常。你的“自我”是你的心理身体，而概念形态会像看待叙事、矛盾、或世界观内部的某个想法那样，警惕心理层面的威胁。当我们的身份受威胁时，我们会有一个与“一只老鼠在死亡前一刻被两颗毒牙刺入侧腹”同级别的生理压力反应。更别说，你不会看到一只长颈鹿因为你质疑它的信念而觉得被冒犯。这是人类特有的现象。当然，生理生存仍是一种威胁，但我们并不生活在一个必须担心野兽咬住我们喉咙的世界里——很多时候，即便在监狱里也不是。通过演化，我们已经把维持生理生存所需的心智能量大幅降低了。
p.76
The notable pattern here is that humans pursue goals of survival and status. And once status is acquired, we work to survive the identity we've attached to that status. If this is unconscious, it works against us. We become a slave to our own mind.
这里显著的模式是：人类追求生存与地位的目标。而一旦地位被获得，我们就努力去让“我们依附于那个地位的身份”存活。如果这是无意识的，它就会对我们不利。我们会成为自己心智的奴隶。
p.76
When your significant other breaks up with you, or even worse, passes away, it feels as if a part of you has died. You feel the accompanying physical sensations that make you feel as if you are dying. When we form relationships, we share the ideas that are important to us. Those ideas shape the perspective of the other person in the relationship and go on to mold their identity. This is how humans replicate their psychic body.
当你的伴侣和你分手，或者更糟——去世了，感觉就像你的一部分死掉了。你能感到随之而来的生理感受，让你觉得自己正在死去。当我们建立关系时，我们分享对自己重要的想法。那些想法塑造了关系中另一方的视角，并进而塑造他们的身份。这就是人类复制自己“心理身体”的方式。
p.76
Another example would be that of Ben Gunn, a boy who was thrown in prison after beating his friend to death. Ben accidently let his deepest secret spill, had his conceptual life flash before his eyes, and couldn't seem to control himself as the emotions rose with the piece of furniture in his hands used as a murder weapon.
另一个例子是本·冈恩（Ben Gunn），一个把朋友打死之后被丢进监狱的男孩。本不小心把自己最深的秘密漏了出来，他的概念生命在眼前闪过，他控制不住自己——情绪随着他手中用作凶器的家具一起升了起来。
p.76
Beyond that and thirty years into Ben's sentence, he had made a name for himself in prison. He became the "jailhouse lawyer" and helped his fellow inmates fight the system. Even after he fell in love with a visiting teacher that attempted to coax him out to a cottage oasis in the England hills, he didn't want to leave. On his release on August 23, 2012, he found himself curled into a ball rocking back and forth for 2 weeks. According to his online blog, he still doesn't feel the same. Ben had experienced a swift conceptual death.
除此之外，在本服刑三十年后，他在监狱里打出了名声。他成了“监狱律师”，帮狱友对抗体制。甚至在他爱上一位前来探监、试图把他引到英格兰丘陵间一处小屋绿洲的老师之后，他也不愿离开。2012 年 8 月 23 日出狱那天，他蜷成一团、来回摇晃了两个星期。据他的在线博客说，他至今仍感觉不对劲。本经历了一次迅速的概念性死亡。
p.76
Once we identify with a purpose, which is limited by our experience, we collect information to survive the identity associated with that purpose. The information we notice in day-to-day life is limited by our identity. Our identity houses our perspective, our perspective influences how we perceive situations, and our perception influences if we act in a conducive manner toward the right goals. Your field of awareness will register what it perceives as important for its survival.
一旦我们与某个目的认同——而那个目的受我们经验的限制——我们就会去收集信息，以让与那个目的相关的身份存活下去。我们在日常生活中注意到的信息，受我们身份的限制。我们的身份容纳着我们的视角，视角影响我们如何感知处境，感知影响我们是否以有利于正确目标的方式行动。你的觉察场域，会登记它认为对其生存重要的东西。
p.77
Everyone has direct experience of this phenomenon. Like when you see a specific car for the first time, and then you see it everywhere. Or when you notice a brand of clothing you like - because it aligns with your unconscious goal of fitting in with others as a survival mechanism - and then you see it everywhere.
每个人都直接体验过这个现象。比如你第一次看到某个特定车型，然后你就到处都能看到它。或者当你注意到一个你喜欢的服装品牌——因为它与你“融入他人”这个无意识的生存目标相契合——然后你就到处看到它。
p.77
Naturally, we will shift our behavior in alignment with this identity. We will act in a specific way, within a specific perspective, and reinforce a specific identity until it becomes effortless. Our identity shapes our habits, and our habits reinforce our self-image. Habits are the grooves in your mind that preserve mental energy when it comes time to act.
自然而然地，我们会随这个身份调整自己的行为。我们会以特定方式行动、在特定视角之内行动，并强化一个特定的身份，直到它变得毫不费力。我们的身份塑造我们的习惯，而我们的习惯强化我们的自我形象。习惯是你脑中的沟槽，在需要行动时节省心智能量。
p.77
In other words, we develop unconscious survival systems that dictate our actions, large and small. Our actions determine who we are, and if we spend the majority of our lives unaware of the identities, perspectives, and accompanying goals we are working to survive, we may end up as a person we hate when we finally decide to wake up.
换句话说，我们发展出无意识的生存系统，它们支配着我们大大小小的行动。我们的行动决定我们是谁；而如果我们人生的大部分时间都没觉察到自己正在为了存活而运营的那些身份、视角及相应目标，那么当我们最终决定醒来时，可能会发现自己成了一个自己讨厌的人。
p.77
The mental energy we invest in the system that survives our identity will influence our experience. This alone explains the gap between the miserable and the fulfilled. The miserable allow their focus to be manhandled by their environment. The fulfilled understand the external world through observation and control their focus within it.
我们投入到“让身份存活”这一系统里的心智能量，会影响我们的体验。仅这一点就能解释痛苦者与满足者之间的差距。痛苦者让自己的焦点被环境任意摆弄。满足者通过观察理解外部世界，并在其中掌控自己的焦点。
p.77
To make this more practical, the reason we attempt to survive an identity is because of the goals that form that identity. The more mental energy you invest in a meaningful goal, the more important it becomes to you. When you are consciously investing in that goal, the feeling of pure progress is incredible. You know that you are moving forward toward your goal. You have feedback.
让它更实用一点：我们之所以努力让某个身份存活，是因为形成那个身份的那些目标。你在一个有意义的目标上投入越多心智能量，它对你就越重要。当你是有意识地投入那个目标时，那种纯粹的进步感不可思议。你知道自己正在朝目标前进。你有反馈。
p.77
Most people think they "find" their passion when in reality, they create it by investing mental energy into a goal. Only then can they cultivate an intrinsic reasoning that pulls them to achieve that goal. If you wait until you feel passionate enough to act, you will never discover what is truly meaningful to you.
大多数人以为他们是“找到”了自己的热情，而现实中，他们是通过把心智能量投入一个目标而创造了它。只有到那时，他们才能培育出一种内在的理由，把自己拉向那个目标。如果你一直等到自己“感到足够有热情”才行动，你将永远发现不了对你真正有意义的东西。
p.78
If you stop making progress, you begin to feel less satisfied with life, and if it drags on too long, the pain can be unbearable. Why? Because you subconsciously know that you are wasting the mental currency you've invested in a goal by not achieving it. If you don't have the feedback of progress to remind you that you are on the right path, you begin to feel lost. This is only half of the story. Survival is not only about preserving who we are through defensive strategies, but offensive. We don't only try to survive our sense of self but reproduce it. Conceptual reproduction is the drive to spread the ideas, beliefs, and biases that make you, you.
如果你停止进步，你就开始对生活感到更不满足；如果拖得太久，那种痛可以无法承受。为什么？因为你潜意识里知道自己正在浪费投入到某个目标上的心智货币，因为你没有达成它。如果你没有“进步”这条反馈来提醒你走在正确的路上，你就开始感到迷失。这只是故事的一半。生存不只是用防御策略保存我们是谁，也是进攻性的。我们不仅试图让自我感存活，还试图复制它。概念性复制，是那个想要传播“让你成为你”的想法、信念和偏见的驱动力。
p.78
There is a reason we feel the pull to create. An author's drive to write a book is not only for the joy of creation, but to impregnate the minds of others with their ideas so they can live on long beyond their physical death. When we engage in conversation with a friend, we can often find a shared perspective in which to exchange ideas to strengthen each other's worldview. As humans we give, notice, and accept the ideas that will aid in the achievement of our goals, for better or worse.
我们感到那股“创造”的拉力，是有原因的。一位作者写书的驱动力，不只是创作的喜悦，也是把自己的想法植入他人的心智，好让它们在自己肉体死亡之后长久存活。当我们与朋友交谈，我们常常能找到一种共享的视角来交换想法，从而强化彼此的世界观。作为人类，我们会给予、注意并接受那些有助于达成我们目标的想法——无论好坏。
p.78
Of course, this can flip on its head very fast. If our beliefs are threatened, emotions flood our mind, and we feel the urge to lash out in a verbal storm of parroted ideas to survive whatever beliefs we subscribe to. This becomes apparent during political seasons, mass media hysteria, and even religious parents that seek to reproduce their selves in a rebellious child that questions their beliefs.
当然，这可以极快地翻个底朝天。如果我们的信念受威胁，情绪就会淹没心智，我们感到一股冲动要在一场由鹦鹉学舌式观点构成的语言风暴中发作，以让我们所信奉的任何信念存活下去。这在政治季节、大众媒体歇斯底里、甚至那些想在叛逆孩子身上复制自己的宗教父母身上都表现得很明显——那个孩子在质疑他们的信念。
p.78
If we seek to understand our nature, we can start playing the real game that boils down to one question: how do we make survival the most meaningful? HARMONIC OSCILLATION You feel bad because your future self is watching your every move, and they don't like what they see. By the time we are near adulthood, our mind
如果我们寻求理解自己的本性，我们就能开始玩那场真正的游戏，它归结为一个问题：我们如何让“生存”变得最有意义？简谐振荡：你之所以感觉糟糕，是因为你未来的自己正在看着你的一举一动，而他们不喜欢看到的东西。到我们接近成年时，我们的心智
p.79
is like an overweight sculpture waiting to be chiseled down, revealing the god-like physique that has developed underneath.
就像一尊超重的雕塑，等待被凿掉多余的料，露出底下已经长成的神一般的形体。
p.79
Chiseling requires small, skilled, and accurate taps to maintain the foundation of the material. If you strike too hard, you may send a crack through the core. If you strike too soft, you will get discouraged at your inability to change.
凿刻需要小而精准、有技巧的敲击，以保住材料的根基。你敲得太重，可能在核心处打出一道裂纹。敲得太轻，你会因为无法改变而灰心。
p.79
Now that we have a big picture understanding of our concept of self, we can work to change it. Meaning that we must deconstruct the mind, see all its parts, and remove what isn't supposed to be there. This way we can act from a place of authenticity while developing a character that is conducive to our ideal future and present enjoyment.
既然我们对“自我”这个概念有了大局的理解，我们就可以着手改变它。也就是说，我们必须解构心智，看清它的所有部件，并移除那些本不该在那里的东西。这样我们就能从一个本真的地方行动，同时发展出一种有利于理想未来与当下享受的人格。
p.79
In classical and quantum mechanics, a harmonic oscillator is one of the most important concepts to understand regarding the behavior of certain systems. While the science can be difficult to understand, the point is simple.
在经典力学和量子力学中，“简谐振子”是理解某些系统行为最重要概念之一。科学本身可能难懂，但要点很简单。
p.79
When you apply external force to a particle, it is displaced from equilibrium. Like if you were to flick a doorstopper as a kid to hear the funny noise it made. When we would flick the metal stopper, it would shake back and forth, depending on the force we applied, until coming to a stop back in the position it was.
当你对一个粒子施加外力，它就会偏离平衡。就像小时候你拨一下门挡，听它发出的那种滑稽声响。当我们拨动那个金属门挡，它会根据我们施力的不同而前后晃动，直到回到原来那个位置才停下。
p.79
A better example would be a string attached to 2 objects, forming a relationship between them. If that string was plucked, or one of the objects moved in a quick manner, the string would bounce up and down like a wave until coming back to a calm state.
一个更好的例子是：一根绳子系在两个物体之间，在它们之间形成一种关系。如果这根绳被拨动，或者其中一个物体快速移动，这根绳就会像波一样上下弹动，直到回到平静状态。
p.79
Under another lens, we can think of the mental construct of self as a house, but not a home. When you build a house, you start with a sturdy foundation, add the structure, and paint over it in a way that appeals to the eye. Thanks to entropy, the house tends toward disorder. You need layers of systems to maintain the structure with invested mental energy to match. The paint will chip unless you hire a painter. Rooms will get dirty unless
换一面透镜看，我们可以把自我这个心智构造想成一栋房子——但不是家。当你建一栋房子，你从牢固的地基开始，加上结构，再用悦眼的方式刷漆。由于熵，房子趋向无序。你需要层层系统，并投入与之匹配的心智能量来维持结构。漆会剥落，除非你请个漆匠。房间会变脏，除非
p.80
everyone cleans them. The dishes won't be washed unless someone does it physically or uses technology to save mental energy.
每个人都去打扫。碗碟不会自己洗，除非有人亲自去洗，或用技术来节省心智能量。
p.80
Not only that, but if you want to change the structure of the house, you must be precise and knowledgeable. It is common sense to not demolish the house as a whole, because that is on par with death of the house itself and everything inside it. You also wouldn't remove a foundational piece of the house as your starting point.
不仅如此，如果你想改变房子的结构，你必须精准且有知识。不把整栋房子拆掉是常识，因为那等同于房子本身以及它里面一切的死亡。你也不会把一块地基性的部件当作起点拆掉。
p.80
Instead, you start your reconstruction with what you know. You learn, experiment, and improve your understanding of the house as you iterate on a long-term plan.
相反，你从你知道的东西开始重建。你在一个长期计划上迭代的过程中去学习、实验、并提升你对这栋房子的理解。
p.80
When we translate this to our mind, and change the identity that no longer serves us, when you try to remove a part of your house, you are applying an external force. If that part of your house is foundational, the emotional response will match.
当我们把这翻译到心智上，去改变那个不再服务我们的身份时：当你试图移除房子的一部分，你就是在施加外力。如果那部分是地基性的，情绪反应就会与之匹配。
p.80
When most people seek to change and take the painful actions necessary, they often fail to see those low points as necessary. We fight with the emotions that wash over us and allow them to influence our actions.
当大多数人寻求改变并采取必要的痛苦行动时，他们往往看不到那些低点其实是必要的。我们与冲刷而过的情绪搏斗，并任由它们影响我们的行动。
p.80
On the Universal scale, our thoughts, emotions, and actions oscillate between the creation of heaven or hell, but few people recognize that responsibility. Your actions will only serve a collective heaven after you experience the personal hell that comes with identity change. From that chaotic rock bottom, it is your responsibility to bring order to your life. The dualistic nature of reality is tricky because we often isolate 2 extremes of a pair with the distinctive thoughts in our head. Black would not make sense without white, nor up without down, love without hate, happy without sad, matter without space, something without nothing, or finity without infinity.
在宇宙尺度上，我们的念头、情绪和行动在“创造天堂”与“创造地狱”之间振荡，但很少人认出这份责任。只有在经历了身份改变所带来的个人地狱之后，你的行动才会服务于一个集体性的天堂。从那个混乱的谷底开始，把秩序带回你的生活是你的责任。现实的双重本性很棘手，因为我们常常用脑中的那些区分性思维去把一对两极孤立开。没有白，黑就说不通；没有下，上就说不通；没有恨，爱就说不通；没有悲伤，快乐就说不通；没有空间，物质就说不通；没有“无”，有就说不通；没有无限，有限就说不通。
p.80
When we neglect the complementary existence of these entities and see them as standalone, our mind gets stuck as the Universe pushes toward evolutionary progress. Our imaginary sense of self stays the same while
当我们忽视这些实体的互补性、把它们看成独立存在时，当宇宙朝演化进步推进时，我们的心智就会卡住。我们那想象出来的自我感保持不变，而
p.81
reality continues to change with each passing moment. And when our expectations fail to align with the actuality of a situation, emotional lash out is often the result.
现实却随时间流逝不断变化。而当我们的期待与现实状况无法对齐时，情绪发作往往就是结果。
THE PULL INWARD
向内的拉力
p.81
p.81
Everyone has felt the pull. The call to greatness. The silent yearning for more, but not in a materialistic sense. Can you feel it? Or is your focus limited by the intellectual structure you call home?
每个人都感受过那股拉力。伟大的召唤。对“更多”的无声渴望——但不是物质意义上的。你能感觉到它吗？还是你的焦点被那个你称之为“家”的智性结构限制住了？
p.81
The pull inward demands outward problem-solving, from superficial to metaphysical, while maintaining as holistic of a perspective as you are able. The path of mastery is obvious, but our conditioning prevents us from seeing it.
向内的拉力要求你向外解决问题，从表层的到形而上的，同时尽可能保持一个整体性的视角。精通之路显而易见，但我们的条件化让我们看不见它。
p.81
You are being attracted to your highest version, and the depth of your core can sense it.
你正在被吸引向你最高的版本，而你内核的深度能感觉到它。
p.81
The external call to evolve requires you to chisel inward beneath the mental constructs that have been layered through your conditioning. Your internal state must become one with the ever-changing external state.
那份要求你演化的外部召唤，要求你向内凿进、凿到那些经年累月被条件化层叠起来的心智构造之下。你的内在状态必须与不断变化的外在状态合一。
p.81
You identify problems in your life and solve them. That's it. That's how you live with purpose, unless you get distracted. But most people want to solve the problems of the world before they solve their own. This is a recipe for disaster. How can you help the world if you haven't helped yourself? If you have not developed the identity that you reproduce in every interaction, you are contributing to a collective hell on Earth unless you make the conscious decision to evolve.
你在生活中识别问题并解决它们。就这样。这就是你如何带着目的生活——除非你被分心了。但大多数人想在解决自己的问题之前先去解决世界的问题。这是灾难的配方。如果你还没帮过自己，你怎么帮世界？如果你没有发展出那个你在每一次互动中都在复制的身份，你就是在为地球上的一个集体地狱做贡献——除非你有意识地决定演化。
p.81
Start with what's right in front of you. You know, the superficial things that you sweep under the rug because you have the desire for bigger, better, and selfless pursuits to veil what is staring at you in the mirror. Don't ignore your personal problems that are begging to be solved. You wouldn't build a temple on a foundation of chipped wood and bent screws.
从眼前的东西开始。你知道的，就是那些被你扫到地毯下的表层问题——因为你有追求更大、更好、更无私的事业的欲望，好去遮掩镜子里正盯着你的东西。别忽略那些乞求被解决的私人问题。你不会用开裂的木头和弯掉的螺丝做地基去建一座神殿。
p.82
Are you overweight? Do you hate your job? Are you tired all the time? Did you just go through a breakup? Are you trapped in a cloud of negative emotions? You must sit with these problems, observe them from a state of open focus, and become aware of how they impact your life. Then, you must gather the knowledge, skills, and resources that allow you to dive in with clarity in your day-to-day life.
你超重吗？你讨厌你的工作吗？你是不是总是疲惫？你刚经历一场分手吗？你被困在一团负面情绪的云里吗？你必须与这些问题同坐，从一个开放焦点的状态观察它们，觉察它们如何影响你的生活。然后，你必须收集那些能让你在日常中带着清晰一头扎进去的知识、技能和资源。
p.82
It takes time to realize how one problem spreads into all areas of your life. Like how a lack of money can prevent optimal health, moving to a beneficial environment, and silently destroy your relationships. Or how a lack of health leads to low physical energy, which impacts your quality of work, how you look, your self-esteem, and your ability for clear thinking. You must hunt for a reason, a "why," for solving that problem. One that makes sense to you. One that makes action seamless. One that you find in conversations, books, and not distracting yourself with mindless entertainment. With the intrinsic energy from that "why," you create a goal to overcome that problem. This is your purpose until the next reveals itself. Once you begin to invest mental energy into that goal, momentum begins to take over, because nobody likes the feeling of a wasted investment.
要意识到“一个问题如何蔓延到你生活的所有领域”，是需要时间的。比如缺钱如何妨碍最佳健康、妨碍搬到一个有益的环境，并悄悄毁掉你的关系。或者缺乏健康如何导致身体能量低下，进而影响你的工作质量、你的外表、你的自尊、以及你清晰思考的能力。你必须为“解决那个问题”寻找一个理由、一个“为什么”。一个对你有意义的。一个让行动变得无缝的。一个你从对话、书籍中找到的，而不是靠无脑娱乐分心获得的。带着那个“为什么”提供的内在能量，你创造出一个克服该问题的目标。这就是你的目的，直到下一个目的显现。一旦你开始把心智能量投入那个目标，动量就开始接管——因为没人喜欢“投入被浪费”的感觉。
p.82
Intention is a magnet toward a desired future that is enhanced with reason. As you trek toward your goals, continue hunting for "whys" to reinforce your positive behavior. The initial reason you started will lose weight with time and entropy. Collect the pieces of a philosophy that uphold your pursuit to a better life.
意图是一块朝向理想未来的磁铁，而“理由”会把它增强。当你跋涉向目标时，继续寻找“为什么”来强化你的正向行为。你起步时的那个理由，会随时间和熵而减重。去收集那些支撑你追求更好生活的哲学碎片。
p.82
If you need clarity, adopt the mindset of the silent observer. Pay close attention to the actions of those around you. Comparing yourself to others, which is often demonized, can be a useful tool for understanding what you don't want. From there, you can flip that on its head to gain clarity on what you want. When you are at the grocery store, observe what others are putting in their baskets. Observe how they look. Transfer consciousness into them and craft a story for how they live, feel, and act without reason. This is not judgmental or unethical if you are doing it for the sole reason of correcting your own behavior.
如果你需要清晰，就采取沉默观察者的心态。密切关注周围人的行动。与他人比较——常被妖魔化——其实可以是一个有用的工具，帮你理解你不想要什么。从那里，你可以把它翻个头，获得关于你想要什么的清晰。当你在超市里，观察别人往篮子里放什么。观察他们看起来什么样。把意识转移到他们身上，为他们如何生活、感受、以及无理由地行动编一个故事。只要你纯粹是为了修正自己的行为，这就不是评判性的，也不是不道德的。
p.83
If someone has a mind, body, or lifestyle you desire, use that as fuel to educate, execute, and iterate as you learn more about yourself. If somebody has a mind, body, or lifestyle you despise, use that as fuel to push in the opposite direction.
如果某人拥有你渴望的心智、身体或生活方式，把它当作燃料，去教育、执行和迭代，同时更了解你自己。如果某人拥有你厌恶的心智、身体或生活方式，把它当作燃料，往反方向推。
p.83
You need a plan. A strategy. A clear set of goals that form a system that, when backed by focused effort, will create a meaningful future. There isn't any other way. Because if you don't have a plan, society does, and it's been planning your life for decades. When you discover your lesser or greater purpose in life, you must bridge the gap between you and it by creating order in the mind. A plan is structured information that you can bring your attention to when mental chaos ensues.
你需要一个计划。一个策略。一组清晰的目标，它们构成一个系统，在被聚焦的努力支撑时，会创造一个有意义的未来。没有别的办法。因为如果你没有计划，社会有——而它已经替你规划了几十年的人生。当你发现了自己人生中较小或更大的目的，你必须通过在心中创造秩序，把“你”与“它”之间的缺口搭起来。计划是被结构化的信息，当心智混乱袭来时，你可以把注意力带到它上面。
p.83
Realize that you do not have one purpose. To chisel down to your core and discover who you really are, you must solve the problems that are staring you straight in the face. Once you bust through that karma, greater purposes will begin to reveal themself to you if you stay on the path.
要意识到你并不是只有一个目的。要凿到你的内核、发现你真正是谁，你必须解决那些直直盯着你脸的问题。一旦你穿透了那份业力，只要你留在路上，更大的目的就会开始向你显现。
p.83
The paradox here is that to dive inward you must solve superficial problems outward. Once those problems are solved, you are both closer to the authenticity of your core while increasing the value you can provide to the external world.
这里的悖论是：要向内深潜，你必须向外解决表层问题。一旦那些问题被解决，你就同时更接近你内核的本真，又提升了你能够提供给外部世界的价值。
p.83
As an example, let's look at a teenager that just went through a breakup. At first, they are overwhelmed with emotion. They feel lost. Little progress is made. A chapter of their life is coming to an end. As the emotions fade to a manageable level, they seek to invest their newly found mental energy in a new goal, because they don't need to maintain the relationship anymore. For the pursuit of status, they become aware of how training and exercise can help increase their perceived value to meet a more desirable partner. They came across this reasoning because the intention to improve beyond their low point in life allowed them to register information that will aid in resolving their conscious pain. They did not distract themselves from their problem.
举个例子，看一个刚经历分手的少年。起初，情绪把他淹没。他感到迷失。几乎没有进展。他人生的一个章节正在结束。当情绪褪去到可控水平，他会寻求把新获得的这份心智能量投入一个新目标——因为他不再需要维持那段关系了。为了追求地位，他意识到训练和健身可以如何帮他提升被感知的价值，从而配得上一个更理想的伴侣。他能想到这个理由，是因为“要超越人生低点”的意图，让他得以登记那些有助于解决他意识痛苦的信息。他没有用分心去逃避自己的问题。
p.84
With the thought of a new purpose, they invest mental energy in education. As they are exposed to more information, they gain clarity on how to actualize that goal. As they make progress, they learn a valuable lesson that reinforces their pursuit. That they are in control of their fate. They may go through their own mental battles, but the thought of wasting their energy investment outweighs the thought of returning to baseline. If their journey pans out as many others do, their superficial "why" would transform into a sense of mastery behind their pursuits. They would continue with their health journey simply because they fell in love with the process. That alone will attract a more developed partner, and by that point, they won't feel as if they need that partner to be happy.
带着新目的的念头，他把心智能量投入学习。随着暴露于更多信息，他获得了关于如何实现那个目标的清晰。随着取得进展，他学到一课宝贵的东西，强化了他的追求：他掌握着自己的命运。他可能会经历自己的心理战役，但“浪费投入”的念头压过了“回到基线”的念头。如果他这段旅程像很多人的那样展开，他那个表层的“为什么”会转化成一种对追求本身的精通感。他会继续他的健康之旅，只因为他爱上了这个过程。仅这一点就会吸引到一个更成熟的伴侣；而到那时，他不会觉得自己需要那个伴侣才能快乐。
p.84
This situation does not apply to everyone but illustrates a strong pattern in the start of an individual's self-development journey. I would encourage you to note similar patterns in your life. You now have the awareness; the rest is on you.
这种情况并不适用于所有人，但它展示了一个人在自我成长之旅起步时的一个强模式。我鼓励你在自己的生活中注意类似的模式。现在你有了觉察，其余的靠你自己。
THE GAME
游戏
p.85
p.85
On November 23, 2004, a software development company, Blizzard Entertainment, released one of the most popular games of the 21st century. Little did they know they created a microcosm of life that would impact the world far beyond the limits of its predecessors.
2004 年 11 月 23 日，一家软件开发公司——暴雪娱乐——发布了 21 世纪最受欢迎的游戏之一。他们当时几乎不知道，自己创造了一个生活的微缩宇宙，其影响将远超前辈们的边界。
p.85
The game was a massive multiplayer online role-playing game - or MMORPG - called World of Warcraft. Think of it like real life. But if that life took place in a time when dragons, castles, and spell-casting elves or shapeshifting bear-like creatures were a thing.
那款游戏是一款大型多人在线角色扮演游戏（MMORPG），叫《魔兽世界》。把它想成现实生活——但那个生活发生在一个有龙、有城堡、有会施法的精灵、还有能变形的熊形生物的时代。
p.85
Let's imagine you were a player in this game. When you first boot up, you are prompted with a series of choices. First, you choose your race, which isn't a possibility in the physical world, but let's use our imagination here. Do you want to be a human? What about an orc, troll, or gnome? You would be correct in assuming these aren't the conventional interpretations of "race," often assumed from skin tone. Instead, the races of this game were tied to a culture that was constructed by the software company itself. That way, players could become even more immersed in the virtual world. This is no different from cultural programming in reality.
设想你是这个游戏里的一名玩家。你第一次启动时，会被给出一系列选择。首先，你选择种族——这在物理世界里是不可能的，但我们在这里动用一下想象力。你想当人类吗？还是兽人、巨魔、侏儒？你猜得没错，这些不是“种族”的常规解释（通常从肤色推断）。相反，这个游戏里的种族绑定在由软件公司自己构建的文化上。这样玩家就能更沉浸于这个虚拟世界。这与现实中的文化编程并无不同。
p.85
Next, you choose your class, preferably one that you would enjoy playing as. You have free reign to become a warrior, mage, or something more utilitarian, like a paladin. Keep in mind that your choice here will determine
接下来，你选择职业，最好是你会享受扮演的那个。你可以自由成为战士、法师，或者更实用主义的，比如圣骑士。记住，你在这里的选择将决定
p.86
the opportunities available to you in the future. One quick decision could lead to a game you don't care to play anymore.
你未来可用的机会。一个草率的决定，可能带出一个你不再想玩的游戏。
p.86
After changing your hair, stature, and other cosmetic details (all impacting your enjoyment of the game, you are launched into a specific starting zone. In this zone, you run through a tutorial that teaches you the fundamentals, rules, and mechanics of the game. You practice slaying monsters, level up a few times, and begin your journey as the main character of the world. Once you understand the game, you begin completing a series of quests that form a storyline - to gain experience. As you gain experience, new opportunities become available to you. You unlock dungeons. You can join a guild. You can travel to new locations to complete different quests. In the real world, we often aren't aware of what these opportunities can be, so we choose to remain stagnant, comfortable, and ignorant.
在改完发型、体型和其他外观细节之后（所有这些都影响你对游戏的享受），你被投放到一个特定的新手区。在这个区里，你跑完一段教学，它教你游戏的基础、规则和机制。你练习杀怪，升了几级，然后作为这个世界的“主角”开始了你的旅程。一旦你理解了这场游戏，你就开始完成一系列串成故事线的任务——从而获得经验。随着经验累积，新的机会向你敞开。你解锁副本。你可以加入公会。你可以前往新的地图去完成不同的任务。而在现实世界里，我们往往不知道这些机会能是什么，于是选择原地不动、安逸、无知。
p.86
Dungeons contain bosses and bosses contain valuable loot. Higher-level dungeons require more skill, experience, and time playing the game. If you want valuable items, you need to develop your character to take on the challenge necessary to receive those items. It's not instant, but the most difficult challenges present the most profound lessons.
副本里有 boss，boss 身上有值钱的掉落。更高级的副本需要更多技能、经验和游玩时间。如果你想要值钱的物品，你必须发展你的角色，去接下获得那些物品所必需的挑战。它不是即时的，但最难的挑战会带来最深刻的教训。
p.86
Guilds are like a community. They support each other, craft strategies to win, and help you level up faster than playing alone. But you can't just join any guild. Every guild has specific needs dependent on their collective goal. If you aren't a good fit, you can't join. Guilds often join together or fight against each other like political parties or people that subscribe to a specific diet. When people join together to form a collective self, their shared purpose can be actualized much faster. But the potential destruction they are capable of is not to be taken lightly.
公会就像一个社群。他们互相支持、制定取胜策略、并帮你比单打独斗升得更快。但你不能随便加入任何公会。每个公会根据其集体目标都有特定的需求。如果你不合适，你就进不去。公会常常结盟或互相开战，就像政党，或像信奉某种特定饮食法的人。当人们联合起来形成一个“集体自我”时，他们共享的目的可以被实现得快得多。但他们所能造成的潜在破坏，也不可小看。
p.86
For each of these, you will serve a specific purpose depending on your prior choices. The path you take influences how you will play the game in the future. How you are able to play the game determines your enjoyment of playing the game.
对上述每一项而言，你都会依据自己先前的选择而服务于某个特定目的。你走的路径影响你未来会如何玩这个游戏。你能够如何玩这个游戏，决定了你玩这个游戏的享受度。
p.87
Be mindful, because if you want to have fun in the future, your present actions must reflect that.
要留意，因为如果你想在未来玩得开心，你当下的行为必须反映这一点。
p.87
In this game, the big important decisions compound into a personal heaven or hell. In a game like this, you are almost forced to be conscious of your choices. In reality, social conditioning leads to mindless action that when gone unchecked can take years of stagnation to undo the damage. Wake up now.
在这个游戏里，那些重大的决定会复利成一个个人的天堂或地狱。在这样一款游戏里，你几乎是被迫对自己的选择保持觉察。而在现实中，社会条件化导致无脑行动；一旦不加检查，可能要好几年停滞才能弥补损失。现在就醒来。
p.87
The last notable pattern in this virtual world is the currency system. There is a public auction where you can buy and sell resources, power-ups, and upgrades. Each of these hold a different value that is determined by the players' goals within the game.
这个虚拟世界里最后一个显著模式，是货币系统。有一个公开拍卖行，你可以买卖资源、增益道具和升级品。每一样都持有不同的价值，由玩家在游戏中的目标决定。
p.87
The profession you specialize in, the abilities you upgrade, and the skills you stack will determine how much gold you can acquire. If you specialize in blacksmithing, the items you craft may be more valuable than what someone else can create. But will you enjoy that path? Or are you doing it for the money? And if you are doing it for the money, will you remain a slave to it? Or do you have a plan to use it as leverage toward your ideal future?
你专精的职业、你升级的能力、以及你叠起来的技能，将决定你能获取多少金币。如果你专精锻造，你打造的物品可能比别人造的更值钱。但你会享受那条路吗？还是你在为钱做它？而如果你是为钱做它，你会不会仍然是它的奴隶？还是你有计划把它当作杠杆，去撬动你的理想未来？
p.87
The skills you acquire will determine the challenges you take on. Those challenges expand your awareness of profitable opportunities. Profitable, in this sense, goes far beyond a dollar amount.
你获得的技能将决定你接下什么挑战。那些挑战扩张你对“有利可图的机会”的觉察。这里的“有利可图”，远远超出一个美元数字。
p.87
My generation is notorious for transferring their obsession for video games into the real world. A majority of my colleagues learned how to level up their character, stack gold, and have the discipline to log on every day and repeat the same boring actions that lead to exponential results. It's no wonder they have multimillion-dollar businesses doing what they enjoy. Whether you've played these games or not, there is a lot we can learn from them. That is what I am here to help you understand.
我这代人出了名地把对电子游戏的痴迷搬进了现实世界。我的大多数同行都学会了如何给角色升级、堆金币、并拥有每天登录、重复同样无聊却带出指数级结果的动作的自律。难怪他们拥有做着喜欢之事的百万美元级生意。无论你是否玩过这些游戏，我们都能从中学到很多。这就是我在这里要帮你理解的东西。
THE COLLECTIVE HARD DRIVE
集体硬盘
p.87
p.88
Life is a game and the select few that are aware of its existence are the ones that can play to win, maximize their enjoyment, and sleep well, knowing that they are in control of their future.
人生是一场游戏，而少数意识到它存在的人，才能玩着赢、最大化享受、并安心入睡——因为他们知道自己掌控着未来。
p.88
The game of life makes sense from a macro perspective. But it is all too common for people to narrow their minds on the micro games of life. The new car that you want so badly. The person that cut you off in traffic. Maybe even the argument you had with your significant other. The situation has passed, and you haven't won the meaningless game. Your mind keeps dragging your focus back to it, as if it can still be won.
人生的游戏从宏观视角看是讲得通的。但人们太容易把心智收窄到人生的微观游戏上：你那么想要的新车。在车流中别你一下的人。甚至你和伴侣吵的那一架。那个处境已经过去了，而你并没有赢下那场毫无意义的游戏。你的心智却不断把你的焦点往回拖，仿佛它还能被赢下来。
p.88
If you can mold your mind to see a situation for what it is, a game, by creating a beneficial end goal, constructing a path to get there, and deciphering the most advantageous actions you can take, even mundane situations can become enjoyable.
如果你能塑造自己的心智，把处境看清为本来的样子——一场游戏——办法是创造一个有益的终极目标、构建一条通往那里的路径、并破译你能采取的最有利行动，那么即便平凡的情境也能变得令人享受。
p.88
As humans, we have a perpetual thirst to learn more, primarily for survival. All our actions are influenced by the need, not want, to go on. It's in our blood. Everyone has the opportunity to master, transcend, and include their survival. This takes development over time but is a worthwhile pursuit for those that want less stress, more creativity, and the ability to choose the games they want to play.
作为人类，我们有一种永不停歇的渴望去学更多——主要是为了生存。我们所有的行动都受“必须”活下去、而非“想要”活下去所影响。它就在我们血液里。每个人都有机会去精通、超越并包含自己的生存。这需要时间发展，但对那些想要更少压力、更多创造力、以及能自己选择玩哪些游戏的人来说，是一条值得走的路。
p.88
We learn and learn and learn from our parents, teachers, and friends, who learned from their parents, teachers, and friends, who were influenced by their life path, culture, and society. Schools, governments, and religious institutions rank the highest in authority and are often the first sources of information you are exposed to when seeking an answer to solve your problems. To be good in school, society, and religion, you must wash your mind with the teachings of school, society, and religion. A social fabric that relies solely on itself to make sense. Groundless, but necessary. A tool, not a master.
我们学、学、学——向父母、老师、朋友学，而他们又向自己的父母、老师、朋友学，而那些人受他们的人生路径、文化和社会影响。学校、政府和宗教机构在权威上排得最高，往往是你为了解决问题而寻求答案时最先接触到的信息源。要在学校、社会和宗教里表现好，你必须用学校、社会和宗教的教导洗自己的脑子。一张只靠自身来讲得通的社会织物。无根，但必要。是一件工具，不是主人。
p.88
This vicious learning process began at the inception of human consciousness and continued for eons until this very moment. Layer after layer, we overloaded our minds, and our minds efficiently stored that
这个恶性的学习过程始于人类意识的诞生，延续了亿万年，直到此刻。一层又一层，我们把心智堆得过载，而我们的心智高效地储存了那些
p.89
information - so we have the mental energy to learn more - to aid in our survival.
信息——好让我们有心智能量去学更多——以助我们生存。
p.89
The problem is a lack of questioning. When we are young, we don't know any better. Who is going to question what they are told when they don't even know what a question is?
问题在于缺乏质疑。我们年幼时不懂事。当一个人连“问题”是什么都不知道时，谁会去质疑别人告诉他的东西？
p.89
Throughout this evolutionary process, human nature began to reflect in larger entities, like society. Similar to how we stored information in our minds to free up more mental energy to learn, we built solutions for worldly problems. Layer after layer.
在这整个演化过程中，人性开始映照在更大的实体上，比如社会。就像我们把信息储存在脑中，以腾出更多心智能量去学习一样，我们为世界性的问题造出了解法。一层又一层。
p.89
Plowing fields took a lot of work, so we used our creative ability to solve that problem with a tractor. Trade was unfair, so we created currency. Communication was limited, so we created social media. The pattern here is that problems are never solved forever. Your problems don't go away, you just get better at solving them. Some view this as daunting, while others view it as their way out of suffering.
耕地要花很多功夫，所以我们用创造能力，用拖拉机解决了那个问题。交易不公平，所以我们创造了货币。交流受限，所以我们创造了社交媒体。这里的模式是：问题永远不会被永久解决。你的问题不会消失，你只是变得更会解决它们。有人把这看作令人畏难的事，另一些人把它看作脱离痛苦的方式。
p.89
To create, the idea must come first. To innovate, the creation must come first. The tractor would be an impossibility without the plow, and you can't fix a problem that doesn't exist (because the creation that creates the problem doesn't exist).
要创造，想法必须先到位。要创新，创造物必须先到位。没有犁，拖拉机就是不可能的；而你也无法修好一个不存在的问题（因为那个“制造出该问题的创造物”还不存在）。
p.89
To keep a long story short, modern society emerged and the collective psyche was conditioned to reflect that. Those that teach us when we are young already have a game that they want us to play. Retirement is how you win, schooling and high-status jobs are how you play, and our decisions occur without conscious choice. Our fate is decided unless you are made aware of a better path and choose to create, play, and win your own game. This is less about an evil overlord planning to enslave humanity and more about humans wanting to survive in the most efficient way possible. The collective unconscious got you into this mess. The conscious individual can get you out.
长话短说：现代社会出现了，而集体心智被条件化去映照它。那些在我们年幼时教我们的人，已经有一个他们想让我们玩的游戏。退休是你赢的方式，上学和高地位的工作是你玩的方式，而我们的决策在没有有意识选择的情况下发生。除非你被带进觉察，看见一条更好的路，并选择去创造、去玩、并赢下你自己的游戏，否则你的命运是被决定好的。这与其说是一个邪恶霸主在策划奴役人类，不如说是人类想以最高效的方式生存下去。集体无意识把你推进了这团乱麻。而有意识的个体能把你带出来。
p.90
The game is programmed onto the collective psyche. You can't change it, but you can understand it. Once you do, you can deconstruct it, recreate it, and maneuver yourself to the top in a fulfilling manner.
这场游戏被编程在集体心智上。你无法改变它，但你能理解它。一旦你理解了，你就能解构它、重建它，并以一种有成就感的方式把自己挪到顶端。
THE NON-PLAYER CHARACTER
非玩家角色（NPC）
p.90
p.90
Every thing is a mental construct, a unit of mind, and only some are aware that their accepted web of expectations controls their lives. Those that aren't aware of its existence have a hidden agreement that these floating buildings are reality.
每样东西都是一个心智构造、一个心智单元，而只有一部分人意识到：他们接受的那张期待之网在控制他们的生活。那些没意识到它存在的人，默认达成了一项隐秘共识：这些漂浮的建筑就是现实。
p.90
You can opt out of playing the game, whether it be social, personal, or anything in between. That is to say, you don't have to take control of your life. But you can't escape survival. Even when you stand still, you are forced to move. By doing nothing, you become a modern slave. Not in the physical sense, but mental.
你可以选择不玩这场游戏，无论是社交的、个人的，还是介于其间的任何东西。也就是说，你不必去掌控自己的人生。但你无法逃脱生存。即便你原地不动，你也被迫在移动。什么都不做，你就成了一个现代的奴隶。不是物理意义上的，而是心智上的。
p.90
.. Attention, not labor.
……被奴役的是注意力，而不是劳动。
p.90
The mind craves order. Our attention will always gravitate toward a hierarchy of goals, that form a game, to ease the sense of uncertainty that is baked into life itself. If you don't focus your mind on what you want, it will be focused on what others want for you.
心智渴望秩序。我们的注意力总会倾向于某个构成游戏的“目标层级”，以缓解生命本身自带的那个不确定感。如果你不把心智聚焦在你想要的东西上，它就会被聚焦在别人希望你拥有的东西上。
p.90
The masses flock to secure career paths and belief systems. An illusion of certainty to avoid struggle. They are convinced that this path is the one of the least risk, when it is the opposite.
大众涌向稳妥的职业路径和信念体系。一种“避免挣扎”的确定性幻觉。他们确信这条路风险最小——而事实恰恰相反。
p.90
In a video game, a non-player character, or NPC, is any character that is not controlled by a player. They are programmed to do what they are told. NPCs can be vendors, teachers, dungeon bosses, and even public figures. They help guide players through their own story by providing a structure for the game to operate. A video game wouldn't be that fun if it was you alone without anybody to interact with.
在电子游戏里，非玩家角色（NPC）是任何不由玩家控制的角色。他们被编程去做被交代的事。NPC 可以是商人、老师、副本 boss，甚至公众人物。他们通过为游戏提供一套运转结构，来帮玩家走完自己的故事。如果只有你一个人、没有任何可互动的对象，电子游戏就不会那么好玩。
p.90
In the real world, NPCs can be considered modern slaves. They are human like the rest of us, but they never questioned their conditioning. Their mind
在现实世界里，NPC 可以被视为现代奴隶。他们和我们一样是人，但他们从未质疑过自己的条件化。他们的心智
p.91
soaked up cultural and social constructs like a sponge. When you interact with these individuals, they will spew information to survive the identity they have adopted. This is how they guide your attention toward the "safe" path.
像海绵一样吸满了文化与社会构造。当你与这些人互动时，他们会为了让自己所采纳的身份存活而狂喷信息。这就是他们如何把你的注意力引向那条“安全”之路。
p.91
Understand that polarity still applies here. Across all domains of life exists a spectrum of personal consciousness and unconsciousness. We are all NPCs at times and main characters at others. The goal is to reduce our time spent in the former with time and reflection.
要明白两面性在这里仍然适用。在生活的所有领域里，都存在一个个人意识与无意识的光谱。我们有时都是 NPC，有时都是主角。目标是通过时间和反思，减少我们待在前者里的时长。
p.91
In Western culture, by the time the average individual turns eighteen, their life is already mapped out for them. Their beliefs are static. Their career path is static. Their sense of self is static. Immovable.
在西方文化里，普通人到十八岁时，人生已经被替他们规划好了。他们的信念是静态的。他们的职业路径是静态的。他们的自我感是静态的。不可撼动。
p.91
Unless an individual can question everything - and I mean everything they will embark on the path of the NPC. Little chance at personal evolution, which has vast ramifications.
除非一个人能质疑一切——我指的是质疑一切——否则他将走上 NPC 之路。个人演化的机会微乎其微，而这会带来巨大的后果。
p.91
In the 3rd millennium, where the status quo is cracking at the seams, every individual has a chance to become the highest version of themself. When most people have a sense of self that is the product of the external world, you have the chance to peel back the layers. You can build a self that is a conscious, personal creation that works less, earns more, and enjoys life. RULES OF THE GAME Games present the big goal of winning, accompanied by a descending series of goals - each presenting their own level of challenge - to bring clarity to your decision-making as you play. That way, we don't get overwhelmed by the demands of winning the game.
在第三个千年，当现状正在接缝处开裂，每个人都有机会成为自己的最高版本。当大多数人拥有的自我感是外部世界的产物时，你有机会把那些层一层层剥开。你可以建立一个作为有意识的个人创造物的自我——它工作更少、赚得更多、并享受生活。游戏规则：游戏给出“获胜”这个大目标，并伴随一系列自上而下的目标——每个都呈现自己的挑战层级——以便在你游玩时给你的决策带来清晰。这样我们就不会被“赢下游戏”的要求压垮。
p.91
If your ideal future - or life's work, vision, or purpose - seem out of reach, this can cause you to hesitate when acting toward a better future. Because it is uncertain, which invokes anxiety. A plan creates clarity, and clarity creates action.
如果你那个理想未来——或者人生事业、愿景、目的——显得遥不可及，这会导致你在朝更好未来行动时犹豫。因为它不确定，而不确定会引发焦虑。计划创造清晰，清晰创造行动。
p.92
In a game, the default grand plan has been strategized with data and made static. All players can learn to play. But your life is unique. Nobody can create a plan for you. If they can, you relinquish the most important trait you can choose to develop, which is the creative ability of your mind. Instead, it is wise to learn the game, deconstruct its parts, break a few things, and create a better one that doesn't get you in too much trouble. In society, the end goal is retirement. To win, you are supposed to be a good student, memorize every fact without nonacademic question, and work your way up the status ladder until you can get some of your time back.
在一款游戏里，那个默认的宏大计划已经被用数据策略化并固化为静态。所有玩家都能学会怎么玩。但你的人生是独特的。没有人能替你制定计划。如果有人能，你就交出了你最可以选择去发展的那个特质——你心智的创造能力。相反，明智的做法是去学习这场游戏，解构它的部件，弄坏几样东西，并创造出一个更好的、不会给你带来太多麻烦的版本。在社会里，终极目标是退休。为了赢，你应该做一个好学生、记住每一个事实而不提出非学术性问题、并沿着地位阶梯往上爬，直到你能拿回一点自己的时间。
p.92
In a video game, the end goal is reaching the highest level (and, in many games, there is no highest level, the progression is endless). You will have to slay monsters, improve your skill set, and log on in a consistent fashion to complete time-bound quests.
在电子游戏里，终极目标是抵达最高等级（而且在很多游戏里根本没有最高等级，进程是无限的）。你必须杀怪、提升技能组合、并持续登录去完成有时限的任务。
p.92
In a board game like chess, the end goal is defeating your opponent. To do that, you must outwit them with every move. Big-picture strategy is king; don't get trapped in the technical details.
在象棋这样的棋盘游戏里，终极目标是击败对手。要做到那点，你必须在每一步上都比对方更聪明。大局战略为王；不要被困在技术细节里。
p.92
In everyday situations, like your spouse shopping for home decorations, she wins by finding the perfectly affordable match for the goal she holds in her mind. You may find this incredibly boring. You may even start an argument with her. But if you were to order your mind by creating your own game like finding the stupidest-looking decoration - then you also have a chance at winning regardless of someone else's decisions. The enjoyable time with your spouse is, of course, an added bonus.
在日常情境里，比如你配偶在挑选家居装饰，她靠找到那个“与她脑中持有的目标完美契合、又买得起”的东西来获胜。你可能觉得这无聊透顶。你甚至可能因此跟她吵起来。但如果你能通过创造自己的游戏来给心智建立秩序——比如“找出最丑的装饰”——那么无论别人做什么决定，你也有机会赢。当然，与配偶共度的愉快时光是额外红利。
p.92
Aside from a hierarchy of goals to guide your attention, games have 3 important qualities to help reduce the potential for distraction even further: frame, rules, and mechanics.
除了用一套目标层级来引导你的注意力，游戏还有三个重要特质，可以进一步降低被分心的可能：框架、规则和机制。
p.92
The frame is the playing field. It is a constructed reality that allows your mind to focus on what is occurring within that reality. The frame is mental and begs understanding. If you don't understand what game you are playing, you will get bored, anxious, or overwhelmed.
框架，是游戏的场域。它是一个被构造出来的现实，让你的心智能聚焦在那个现实内部正在发生的事上。框架是心智性的，且需要被理解。如果你不理解自己在玩什么游戏，你就会变得无聊、焦虑或不堪重负。
p.93
In the real world, the frame is your perspective. We will dig into this later, but your perspective allows for accurate perception of the problems within a situation. If you are shopping with your spouse, your perspective - which holds and influences your beliefs, thoughts, and emotions around the situation - will dictate how enjoyable the situation is for you.
在现实世界里，框架就是你的视角。我们晚些会深入，但你的视角让你能准确感知处境中的问题。如果你在陪配偶购物，你的视角——它持有并影响你关于该处境的情念、想法和情绪——将决定这个处境的享受度。
p.93
Within that frame there are rules. Rules are conditions, limits, or distinctions that the game makers enforce to narrow your attention on the task at hand. When your attention becomes one with the task, you increase the potential of tapping into an addictively enjoyable state of mind, where distractions do not phase you. In this state, you are making pure progress toward a conscious goal.
在那个框架之内，存在规则。规则是游戏制作者所施加的条件、限制或区分，用来把你的注意力收窄到手上的任务上。当你的注意力与任务合一，你就更有可能触及一种令人上瘾般享受的心境——在那里，干扰不再动摇你。在这个状态里，你正在朝一个有意识的目标做出纯粹的进步。
p.93
From a Universal perspective, rules are synonymous with limits on infinity. Or content in consciousness. This is how we operate as a collective and bring ordered information to the mind of the individual. If you were the only being in this world, you would have no use for things like language, money, or games. You would sit back in pure experience as the infinite song unfolds before you.
从宇宙视角看，规则等同于“对无限的限制”。或者说，意识中的内容。我们就是这样作为一个集体运转，并把有序的信息带到个体的心智中。如果你是这个世界上唯一的存在，你就不需要语言、金钱或游戏这样的东西。你会退坐到纯粹的经验里，任由那首无限的歌在你面前展开。
p.93
Anything that can be put into words is a self-imposed limit that prevents us from understanding what can't be put into words. This isn't bad, because we need to be on the same page as everyone else, but it is a useful distinction to avoid getting trapped on the surface. Limits provide structure for our mind and ground our attention in reality, but there is a depth to this life that most people never realize. Conditioning creates conditions for your happiness. Use them but see through them.
任何能被言说的东西，都是一种自我施加的限制，它阻止我们去理解那些无法被言说的东西。这并不坏，因为我们需要与其他人站在同一页上；但这是一个有用的区分，可以避免被困在表面。限制为我们的心智提供结构，让我们的注意力扎根于现实，但这一生有一种大多数人从未意识到的深度。条件化为你的幸福创造了“条件”。用它们，但看穿它们。
p.93
In a game, these limits and conditions are called rules. But these rules aren't introduced all at once. It is a progression. From novice to intermediate to advanced. As you increase your skill, and the rules become second nature, more are introduced that increase the complexity of the game. That way you don't get overwhelmed.
在游戏里，这些限制和条件被称为规则。但这些规则不是一次全部给出的。它是一个进程：从新手到中级到高级。随着你技能提升、规则变成第二天性，会有更多规则被引入，从而提升游戏的复杂度。这样你就不会被压垮。
p.93
Lastly, there are the mechanics of the game. These are a sequence of actions that you practice to increase your skill level. This requires you to learn, fail,
最后，还有游戏的机制。它们是一连串你为了提升技能水平而练习的动作。这要求你去学习、失败、
p.94
and improve to gain experience. Learning the rules through theory will only get you so far. You must implement what you learn by practicing the mechanics of any game in front of you. You get better at something by doing it. Social skills, writing, design, making money, getting a job, creating your life's work, cooking, and any other skill or trait that your character can adopt. You suck at it because you will do everything but that. This is a harsh truth that nobody wants to hear (and everybody will search for endless theory to avoid).
并改进，从而获得经验。通过理论去了解规则只能带你到这里为止。你必须通过练习眼前任何游戏的机制，来落实你所学的东西。你在做某件事中变得更好。社交技能、写作、设计、赚钱、找一份工作、创造你的人生事业、做饭，以及你的角色所能采纳的任何其他技能或特质。你在这件事上很烂，是因为你会去做一切，唯独不做那件事。这是一个没人想听（而所有人都会去找无止境的理论来逃避）的严酷真相。
p.94
If you can break the compulsive pattern of mechanical thoughts, emotions, and actions, you create space to expand your mind, set conscious goals, create clarity, and refocus your attention toward conducive action.
如果你能打破那种强迫性的机械式念头、情绪和行动的循环，你就创造出空间去扩展心智、设定有意识的目标、创造清晰，并把注意力重新聚焦到有益的行动上。
HOW TO PLAY
怎么玩
p.94
p.94
When you have absolute clarity on how to win and a sprinkle of challenge that matches your skill level, the world goes quiet, and you become at one with the river that is reality. Formless, boundless, limitless. Top athletes describe their performances as spiritual. They've developed themselves to a point where their skill becomes art. Intuitive. Natural. Creative. They've transcended the need to think about what they are doing. They just do. Pure progress is a blissful experience. Some call it the flow state. When you are at one with what's right in front of you, leaning into the flow of nature, problems lose their weight and nothing else matters. All is well.
当你对“如何获胜”拥有绝对清晰，再加上一点与你技能水平相匹配的挑战时，世界安静下来，你与那条名为现实的河流合一。无形、无界、无限。顶尖运动员把他们的表现形容为精神性的。他们已经把自己发展到这样一个程度：技能成了艺术。直觉的。自然的。创造性的。他们已经超越了“必须思考自己在做什么”的需求。他们只是做。纯粹的进步是一种至福的体验。有人称之为心流状态。当你与眼前的东西合一时，靠着向自然的流动倾斜，问题失去了重量，别的都不再重要。一切都好。
p.94
If you start playing a game, especially without reading the rule book, will the experience be enjoyable? Probably not. And even if you knew the rules, it wouldn't become enjoyable until you grasp the mechanics of the game. If you were a level one character, an absolute beginner, and somehow managed to battle a level one hundred, a seasoned expert, would it be fun? First, you'd lose immediately. Two, it would only have the possibility of being fun if you mold your mind to create a new game. Like if you were to
如果你开始玩一个游戏，尤其是不读规则书，体验会愉快吗？大概不会。而即便你知道规则，也要等你掌握游戏的机制之后它才会变得愉快。如果你是一级角色、绝对的新手，却不知怎么去和一个一百级的资深高手战斗，那会好玩吗？第一，你会立刻输。第二，它只有在你把心智塑造成创造一个新游戏时，才有好玩的可能。比如你
p.95
attempt to lose as fast as possible, which may be fun, but won't get you anywhere in the world.
试着尽可能快地输掉——这也许好玩，但在这个世界里不会让你到任何地方。
p.95
If you had played chess a few times with your friends, would you even consider entering a competition? Or playing against a Grand Master? What about the mind game of emotional turmoil? Have you practiced the skill of mindfulness to mend your mental fractures and trek onward toward your goals? What about an argument with your spouse? Nobody wants to label this situation as a "game,' " but that's what it is. Do you have the education, techniques, and experience to find a common perspective, work through your problems, and heal the relationship?
如果你跟朋友下过几次象棋，你会考虑去参加比赛吗？或者跟特级大师对局？那么，情绪动荡这盘心智游戏呢？你是否练习过正念的技能，去修补心理裂痕、继续向你的目标跋涉？跟配偶吵架呢？没人愿意把这个处境标成“游戏”，但它就是。你有没有那种教育、技法和经验，去找出一个共同视角、解决你们的问题、并治愈这段关系？
p.95
If your skill doesn't match the challenge that the game presents, you're in for a bad time. If your skill is high and the challenge low, you will get bored. If your skill is low and the challenge is high, you will get anxious. When the challenge is just above your skill level, but you have absolute confidence in your ability to execute, you tap into what is arguably the most enjoyable point in the human experience (that is accessible without drugs, herbs, or other external compounds, of course).
如果你的技能与游戏所呈现的挑战不匹配，你就等着难受吧。技能高而挑战低，你会无聊。技能低而挑战高，你会焦虑。当挑战刚好高于你的技能水平、但你对“我能执行”有绝对信心时，你就触及了人类经验中可以说是最令人享受的那一点（当然，是在不使用药物、草药或其他外部化合物的前提下可达到的）。
p.95
The boredom stems from self-centeredness. Your focus breaks, a new desire pops into your head, and related thoughts start to fill your attention. If you are bored at work, you will start thinking of more productive things you could be doing.
无聊源自自我中心。你的焦点断裂，一个新欲望蹦进脑子，相关念头开始填满你的注意力。如果你在工作中感到无聊，你就会开始想“我本可以去做哪些更有产出的事”。
p.95
The anxiety stems from self-consciousness. Your focus turns toward your concept of self, and again, related thoughts start penetrating your field of awareness.
焦虑源自自我意识。你的焦点转向你关于自我的概念，于是相关念头同样开始穿透你的觉察场域。
p.95
"Wow, I'm not as good as I thought."
“哇，我没自己想得那么好。”
p.95
"I really need to work on my backswing."
“我真得练练我的后摆。”
p.95
"That girl is way out of my league."
“那姑娘完全不是我这个级别的。”
p.95
Notice the use of "I" and "my" that implies a comparison. This comparison leads to entropy: the mind tending toward disorder unless you focus your
注意“我”和“我的”的用法，它暗示着一种比较。这种比较引向熵：除非你把
p.96
mind on the frame, system, or game that forms the structure of the situation. Ordered information must be processed by the conscious mind for energy to flow.
心智聚焦到构成该处境结构的框架、系统或游戏上，否则心智就趋向混乱。有序的信息必须被意识心智处理，能量才能流动。
p.96
This pattern gives us incredible insight. By understanding the delicate balance of challenge and skill, we can turn a mundane and stressful situation into one of meaning and mastery.
这个模式给我们不可思议的洞见。通过理解挑战与技能之间那条微妙的平衡线，我们能把一个平凡而压力重重的处境，变成充满意义与精通的处境。
p.96
As a teenager, I despised sports. Anytime my friends or family would invite me to watch, I would have a little chuckle in my head. Sports? Why would I waste my time watching other people compete? Why wouldn't you just go and compete yourself?
少年时，我鄙视体育。任何时候朋友或家人邀我去看比赛，我都会在心里偷偷笑一下。体育？我为什么要浪费时间看别人比赛？你为什么不自己去比？
p.96
When I did watch a sports match, my mind would turn to immediate boredom. I didn't understand the depth and skill that went into playing the sport at such a high level, so my focus was not engaged with the players on the screen. I did not have a predictive game in my head that I was playing like everyone else. My attention gravitated toward the thought of doing something worth my time.
当我看一场体育比赛时，我的心智会立刻转向无聊。我不理解在如此高水平玩这项运动所需的深度和技巧，所以我的焦点没有投入屏幕上的球员。我脑中没有一个像其他人那样正在玩的预测性游戏。我的注意力倾向于“去做点值得花时间的事”这个念头。
p.96
As another example, if your spouse likes shopping for vintage items and antiques, assuming that you don't, you won't have an enjoyable time shopping with them. Your spouse is in flow checking prices, details of the item, and asking questions about its origin.
再举个例子：如果你配偶喜欢淘古着和古董，假设你不喜欢，那你陪她购物就不会愉快。她正处在心流中，查价格、看物品细节、追问它的来历。
p.96
Your potential for boredom is high unless you create a frame to engage your attention with specific information that the situation presents. If you don't have the time to study the art of antique hunting, you can create a game that you are skilled enough to play. Like finding the smallest, oldest, or most interesting item.
你无聊的可能性很高——除非你创造出一个框架，让注意力投入该处境所提供的特定信息。如果你没时间去研究古着猎寻这门艺术，你可以创造一个你技能足够玩的游戏。比如找出最小、最旧、或最有趣的那件东西。
p.96
As a practice, we need to understand the distinction between content and structure. Most people flood their consciousness with the content of a game without a big-picture understanding of the structure. This allows other ideas from your perspective to fill in the blanks in a chaotic manner. In a metaphorical sense, pure content is like water flowing from a faucet. Structure is a solid cup to hold the water. In between is like trying to bind
作为一种练习，我们需要理解“内容”与“结构”的区分。大多数人用游戏的内容淹没了自己的意识，却没有对结构的大局理解。这会让来自你视角的其他想法以混乱的方式填补空白。打个比方：纯粹的内容像从水龙头里流出的水。结构是盛水的坚固杯子。介于两者之间，就像试图把
p.97
water in a paper envelope which, as you can imagine, will only lead to frustration.
水兜在纸信封里——你可以想象，那只会带来挫败。
p.97
The game is the structure that is reinforced with rules, mechanics, and other nuances that create a mental house that we can navigate with ease. If you don't zoom out to observe, learn, and understand the structure, you will drown in the technical details of each situation.
游戏，就是那个被规则、机制和其他细微之处强化出的结构，它造出一栋我们能在其中自如穿行的心智之屋。如果你不拉远镜头去观察、学习、理解这个结构，你就会淹死在每个处境的技术细节里。
p.97
The traffic system is the structure of the transportation game. I wouldn't recommend treating it as a competitive match, of course. But there is a starting point, an end goal of arriving at your destination, and laws that you must abide by to arrive there safely that order the content of your consciousness.
交通系统就是出行这场游戏的结构。当然，我不建议把它当成一场竞技比赛。但它有一个起点、一个“抵达目的地”的终极目标、以及你必须遵守才能安全抵达的法律——它们给你意识的内容带来秩序。
p.97
If you were to hop into your parents' car as a fifteen year old to "take it for a spin," the challenge would outweigh your skill in a manner that doesn't engage your attention. Your mind would be flooded with thoughts of a stressful future, where you are punished for your immature actions.
如果你十五岁时跳进父母的车里“溜一圈”，挑战会以某种无法调用你注意力的方式压过你的技能。你的心智会被关于压力的未来的念头淹没——在那个未来里，你会为自己的不成熟行为受罚。
p.97
As you are driving, you wouldn't know where to stop, how to stop, how to maintain speed, how to maneuver the car in a roundabout, what to do if you arrive at the same time as another at a 4-way stop, and so on. Most of those reading this book can drive like they walk. It is a skill they have developed over time with a set societal system so that everyone can operate in a mutually beneficial manner. We often don't stop to think how many micro decisions we make while driving. The system is so efficient that it requires little mental energy to get to your destination.
开车时，你不会知道该在哪停、怎么停、如何保持车速、如何在环岛里操作车辆、如果在四向停车同时到达该怎么办，等等。读这本书的大多数人都能像走路一样开车。那是一项他们随时间发展出来的技能，有一套被社会设定的系统，好让每个人都能互惠地运作。我们常常不会停下来想：开车时我们做了多少微观决策。这个系统如此高效，以至于抵达目的地几乎不需要心智能量。
p.97
This concept is best understood through practice. Take a moment and think about the game-like structure of culture, society, corporate jobs, and other aspects of reality that were conditioned into your mind as a child.
这个概念最好通过实践来理解。花一点时间，想想文化、社会、公司工作，以及现实中其他在你童年被条件化进脑袋的面向，它们的“游戏式结构”。
p.97
In future chapters, I'll walk you through the process of creating your own games. Like building a creative income source, actualizing your ideal future, and handling negative or mundane situations through the art of focus. Note that I may not explicitly label these as "games." I would encourage you to make that connection for yourself.
在后面几章，我会带你走过“创造你自己的游戏”的过程。比如建立一个创造性的收入来源、实现你的理想未来、以及通过专注这门艺术去处理负面或平凡的情境。注意，我可能不会明确把它们标为“游戏”。我鼓励你自己去建立这个连接。
p.98
If you remember anything, remember this. You need a challenging end goal that you want to achieve, clarity on how to get there, and a simplified first step to reduce the friction of getting started.
如果你只记住一件事，就记住这个：你需要一个有挑战性、你又想达成的终极目标，关于“如何抵达”的清晰，以及一个被简化过的第一步，以降低启动时的摩擦。
p.98
The push-pull nature of increasing your skill to match the challenge of a situation makes sense. But there are developmental stages in any game you choose to play. Beginner, intermediate, advanced, and more, depending on the game.
“提升技能以匹配处境挑战”这种推拉本性是讲得通的。但无论你选择玩什么游戏，都有发展阶段：初学、中级、高级，甚至更多，取决于游戏。
p.98
This is the path of mastery. As you push toward your ideal future, you will be forced to upskill to match the challenge that any hierarchy of goals presents. Be wary of those that put a clear path in front of you. In a world where the masses flock toward the promise of a certain future, a wise decision is to embrace the uncertain nature of life itself and create your own certainty through focus.
这就是精通之路。当你朝理想未来推进时，你被迫提升技能，以匹配任何目标层级所呈现的挑战。要警惕那些把一条清晰路径摆在你面前的人。在一个大众涌向“确定未来”承诺的世界里，明智的决定是拥抱生命本身的不确定本性，并通过专注创造出你自己的确定性。
THE LENS
透镜
p.99
p.99
Everyone is playing their own game, both macro and micro. Everyone is at different levels of the games. Everyone has their own unique skills, traits, and specialties. Everyone is a part of their own faction, guild, and group of confidants.
每个人都在玩自己的游戏，宏观的和微观的。每个人都在游戏的不同层级上。每个人都有自己独特的技能、特质和专长。每个人都是自己那个阵营、公会和密友圈的一部分。
p.99
Everyone has taken a unique path to where they are now and will have a unique path to where they are going. Your ability to mold your mind to understand the goals that others are pursuing from their individual skill level will make you less reactionary (it will also make you more money). This practice alone is responsible for much of the peace in my life. Everyone may seem wrong, but when you take their conscious or unconscious goals into account, they are right.
每个人都走了独特的路径来到现在，也将走独特的路径去往未来。你有能力塑造自己的心智，从他人各自的技能水平出发去理解他们追求的目标——这会让你不那么条件反射（也会让你赚更多钱）。仅这个练习，就为我的人生带来了大量平静。每个人看起来也许都是错的，但当你把他们有意识或无意识的目标纳入考量，他们就是对的。
p.99
You can't control the details of every situation, but you can control the vantage point from where you interpret those details. Then, you can filter the insignificant noise that does not serve you. All that's left is a signal of importance that pushes you toward action.
你无法控制每个处境的细节，但你能控制“你从哪个制高点去解读那些细节”。然后，你可以过滤掉那些对你无用的、无关紧要的噪声。剩下的就只有一条推动你行动的重要性信号。
p.99
Like a film set. A scene is composed of the camera angle, focal length, lighting, props, quality of equipment, actors, and script that determines how the scene manifests. If you are an actor, it is easy to get absorbed in the details of the scene. You may forget that you were even filming a movie. If
就像电影片场。一个场景由机位、焦距、灯光、道具、器材质量、演员，以及决定这个场景如何呈现的剧本共同构成。如果你是演员，很容易被场景的细节吸收。你甚至会忘记自己正在拍一部电影。如果
p.100
you are the director, you understand that everything that goes into the scene serves a purpose for creating that reality.
你是导演，你就明白：进入这个场景的一切，都为“创造那个现实”服务着某个目的。
p.100
Every aspect of that situation is crafted in a way that makes the scene interesting to the person watching the film. One that both the director and viewer can get immersed in. So much so that they forget about their worries. In the real world, we do not see ourselves as the director of our own film, and we especially don't see others as the director of their own. So, we compartmentalize reality and see what we want to see. We love what serves our fabricated identity and hate what we don't understand. When someone makes an upsetting remark, you snapshot that individual, thought, or emotion as "bad" in your mind based on your conditioned and relative perception of what "bad" is. In fact, that upsetting remark could have been the catalyst to you taking control of your life. It may have held truth that you didn't want to face. You must realize that your inability to see this never-ending movie for what it is makes you reactionary. And that is usually not in your best interest.
那个处境的每一个面向，都以让场景对观影者有趣的方式被精心打造。一个导演和观众都能沉浸其中的场景。沉浸到他们忘记自己的烦恼。在现实世界里，我们不把自己看作自己那部电影的导演，尤其也不把别人看作他们自己电影的导演。于是我们把现实分格，只看见我们想看见的。我们爱那些服务于我们虚构身份的东西，恨那些我们不理解的东西。当有人说出一句让人不快的话，你基于自己被条件化的、相对的“坏”的感知，把那句话、那个想法、或那个情绪在心智里快照为“坏”。事实上，那句让人不快的话，可能正是你夺回人生掌控权的催化剂。它可能持有你不想面对的真相。你必须意识到：你无法看清这部永不结束的电影本来的样子，正是你之所以条件反射的原因。而那通常不符合你的最大利益。
p.100
The tragedy of human nature is that we consider a situational snapshot as an explanation for the entirety of a person's being, ourselves included. In reality, one situation that you perceived as negative, meaning it is only negative to you, comprises such a small percentage of someone's life that it wouldn't be worth writing out here, because the moment has passed. We see less than a 0.001% of someone's life and yet we think we understand the complexity of their mind, being, and self.
人性的悲剧在于：我们把一个处境的快照，当作一个人（包括我们自己）整个存在的解释。现实中，一个被你感知为负面的处境，只构成别人人生中那么小的一个百分比——小到不值得在这里写出来，因为那一刻已经过去了。我们看见某人人生不到 0.001%，却以为我们理解了对方心智、存在与自我的复杂度。
p.100
Humans make sense of the world by telling themselves a story. Even if we see it as someone else's story, we interpret it as a part of our own, as that is the only way we can make sense of it. Since we will never have access to another person's state of mind, we take what we see and make sense of it based on our past experiences, future goals of varying consciousness, and our interpretation of the situational game we are playing. This is a recipe for suffering.
人类通过给自己讲故事来理解世界。即便我们把它看作别人的故事，我们也会把它解读成自己故事的一部分——因为这是我们能理解它的唯一方式。由于我们永远无法进入另一个人的心境，我们就把所见之物、基于过往经验、不同意识程度下的未来目标、以及我们对“自己正在玩的情境游戏”的解读，来理解它。这是一份痛苦的配方。
ARSENAL OF LENSES
透镜库
p.101
p.101
You are a perspective vessel in a subjective reality. You have the ability to shift that perspective beyond a narrow identity to view situations from a higher, more holistic perspective that encapsulates the background, foreground, and detail of the situation.
你是一个处于主观现实中的“视角容器”。你有能力把这个视角从狭隘的身份中移开，去从更高、更整体的视角看待处境——那个视角囊括了处境的背景、前景与细节。
p.101
Your concept of self, at this moment in time, is forged by the ideologies, dogma, and forms of the outer world that you identify with as static. This limits the potential experience available to you. Nobody can escape this, and the moment you think you can is the moment you become trapped in the pursuit of spiritual materialism. Thinking of yourself as higher, more noble, or less egoic is still a status game that the ego loves to play. For understanding, let's think of perspective as a DSLR camera, one of those big fancy ones that photographers use. The body of the camera has its limits due to how it's programmed. You can attach different lenses to the camera to capture a situation in a way that influences how the image is perceived based on your intention with the shot.
你此刻关于自我的概念，是由你静态地与之认同的外在世界的意识形态、教条和形式锻打而成的。这限制了你可获得的经验潜能。没人能逃脱这一点；而你以为自己能逃脱的那一刻，就是你被困在“灵性唯物主义”追求里的时刻。把自己想得更高、更高贵、或自我更少，仍然是一种自我最爱玩的地位游戏。为了便于理解，让我们把视角想成一台单反相机，摄影师用的那种又大又花哨的。相机机身由于它的编程而有其局限。你可以给相机装不同的镜头，以某种方式捕捉一个处境，从而根据你拍摄的意图影响图像的观感。
p.101
As you trek through life, you capture photographs and develop them through your level of mind, accompanying emotional state, and degree of focus. This is how you interpret any situation you are in, and that interpretation is confined by the structure you operate within.
当你跋涉过人生，你拍下照片，并根据你的心智层级、伴随的情绪状态和专注程度把它们冲洗出来。这就是你如何解读身处的任何处境，而这种解读受限于你所运行的那个结构。
p.101
Let's think of the field of view, frame, or perspective of the lens as your field of awareness. When you hone in and fixate your focus on one thing, the background blurs. This also impacts how you interpret a situation. So, if your camera is positioned on top of the world, but your lens allows you to focus on a skyscraper, the entirety of the world will look like a big blob of blues and greens while the skyscraper is crisp and clear. This is an illustrative description of how you "zoom out" to gather truths, patterns, and creative resources and "zoom in" to apply them in your practical life.
让我们把镜头的视野、框或视角想成你的觉察场域。当你收束并把焦点钉在一样东西上时，背景就模糊了。这也影响你如何解读一个处境。所以，如果你的相机架在世界之巅，但镜头让你能聚焦在一栋摩天楼上，那么整个世界的其他部分看起来就是一大团蓝绿相间的模糊，而摩天楼则清晰锐利。这是对你如何“拉远镜头”去收集真相、模式和创造性资源，以及如何“拉近镜头”把它们应用到实际生活中的说明性描述。
p.102
We can consider what is "clear" to be conscious and what is "blurred" to be subconscious or unconscious. This can work for or against you. If you hold the perspective of your future self in your mind and focus tightly on a task that will create your vision, distractions won't register in your field of awareness. This is what we want. Clear and unbroken focus on what is important to us. At least until a new importance is discovered as the last one inevitably fades.
我们可以把“清晰”的部分视为有意识的，把“模糊”的部分视为潜意识或无意识的。这可能对你有利，也可能对你不利。如果你在心中持有你未来自我的视角，并紧紧聚焦在一个能创造你愿景的任务上，干扰就不会登记进你的觉察场域。这就是我们想要的：对重要之物清晰且不被切断的专注。至少，直到新的重要性被发现，而上一个不可避免地褪色。
p.102
But if you limit your perspective to your concept of self and focus on a problem, like a negative emotion within that perspective, your field of awareness does not have the possibility of seeing the situation for what it is. This is the default state for most people. They spot and interpret problems from a narrow perspective and often the least conducive one to a better future.
但如果你把视角限制在“自我”这个概念上，并聚焦在一个问题上——比如那个视角内的某种负面情绪——你的觉察场域就不可能看清这个处境本来的样子。这是大多数人的默认状态。他们从一个狭隘的视角去发现并解读问题，而那往往是对更好未来最不利的那个视角。
p.102
To prepare ourselves to make better decisions in alignment with our goals, we must collect consciousness so we can mold our mind in a way that reduces the friction to act.
为了准备好做出与目标一致的最好决定，我们必须收集意识，从而以降低行动摩擦的方式塑造心智。
p.102
You collect consciousness by studying multiple perspectives with the goal of holistic understanding. If you are an atheist, and have not experienced a Christians perspective, how are you going to align yourself with the highest truth? Both perspectives that are heavily influenced by culture and experience hold half-truths, and when you experience both, you inch your way toward deeper understanding.
你通过研究多种视角、以整体性理解为目标，来收集意识。如果你是位无神论者，又从未体验过基督徒的视角，你如何让自己与最高真理对齐？两种被文化和经验深刻影响的视角都持有半个真理，而当你同时体验两者，你就向更深的理解寸寸推进。
p.102
Rather than becoming attached to a specific way of doing things, see it for what it is, a perspective in a subjective reality. When you study different perspectives, you are collecting lenses for your camera. You expand your mind beyond one limiting worldview. Spirituality, atheism, Christianity, veganism, fruitarianism, freelancing, and small business ownership are all lenses for modeling meaning, nutrition, and business from an angle that highlights specific tactics that help individuals with specific goals. The perspectival background of principles can be useful to anybody, but the foreground of tactics requires a self that fits into the puzzle. Your brain is a pattern-recognition machine, and when you study with a mind open beyond
与其依附于某种特定的做事方式，不如把它看清为本来的样子：一个主观现实中的一个视角。当你研究不同视角时，你正在为你的相机收集镜头。你把心智扩展到某个限制性世界观之外。灵性、无神论、基督教、纯素主义、果食主义、自由职业、小型企业主——全都是透镜，用来从某个角度为意义、营养和商业建模，而这个角度凸显了能帮到具有特定目标之人的特定战术。原则层面的视角背景对任何人都可能有用，但战术层面的前景需要一个能嵌进那块拼图的“自我”。你的大脑是一台模式识别机器；当你以一种开放的、超越
p.103
the surface, you allow truth to blur in the middle and develop a self that is less reactive to the external world.
表面的心智去学习时，你让真相在中间模糊，并发展出一个对外部世界不那么条件反射的自我。
p.103
If you start a business to solve your money problems, start training to improve your health, or study social dynamics to help with your dating success, study the big picture. Understand the overarching principles, without getting attached to individualized tactics, and let experience reveal your own way.
如果你为了解决问题而开始创业、为了改善健康而开始训练、或为约会成功而研究社交动力学，那就研究大局。理解那些总括性的原则，而不要依附于个体化的战术，让经验揭示你自己的方式。
p.103
With time, and as you collect an arsenal of lenses, you become conscious of patterns that are packaged up in an enticing way with a specific label slapped on them. These patterns often represent the fundamentals, principles, and levers that contribute to progress on the Universal scale. MAKING BETTER DECISIONS You, at this very moment in time, are a manifestation of your past mental, physical, financial, and spiritual choices. Who you want to become is a manifestation of the choices you make at this moment, and the next, until it all comes to an end. Not in the sense of physical death, but until your ideas stop rippling through the Universe that houses the selves created by said ideas.
随着时间推移，当你收集起一座镜头库时，你会觉察到那些被以诱人方式包装、并贴上特定标签的模式。这些模式往往代表那些在宇宙尺度上促成进步的基本要素、原则和杠杆。做出更好的决定：此刻这个时刻的你，是你过去心智、身体、财务和精神选择的一个呈现。你想成为的人，是你在此刻以及下一刻所做选择的一个呈现，直到一切结束。不是肉体死亡意义上的结束，而是直到你的想法不再在“容纳由这些想法所创造之诸自我”的宇宙中激起涟漪。
p.103
The importance of decisive accuracy cannot be stressed enough. But most people can't get themselves to act on anything without immediate benefit. Their mind is narrow, but not open to the future.
果断而准确的重要性，怎么强调都不为过。但大多数人无法在没有即时收益的情况下让自己付诸任何行动。他们的心智是狭隘的，并不向未来敞开。
p.103
The average individual will not register potential opportunities because their field of awareness does not register it as important. They do not have a meaningful hierarchy of goals to position their perspective as a lens to view daily situations from. They may spot one, like a business opportunity with shallow promises, because it would tickle their fancy for status, but their mind quickly distracts itself back to a state of cyclical, immediate, and destructive pleasure.
普通人不会登记潜在机会，因为他们的觉察场域不把它登记为重要。他们没有一套有意义的目标层级，来把他们的视角定位成透镜，去观察日常处境。他们也许会看到一个，比如一个承诺浅薄、却会挠到他们地位痒处的商业机会，但他们的心智很快又把自己分心回一种循环的、即时的、破坏性的快感状态。
p.104
Life is a mind game, and if you don't have the skill, you won't be able to continue playing. Your quality of life is dependent on the quality of games you choose to play, because those demand a specific quality of mind to play them. Beware that this path is a beautifully painful one. A certain level of mind breeds a certain level of loneliness. With every level of mind there are less people occupying that state. But when you find them, the connection you have is one that lasts a lifetime.
人生是一场心智游戏，如果你没有技能，就无法继续玩下去。你的生活质量取决于你选择玩哪些游戏的质量，因为那些游戏要求特定质量的心智才能玩。要当心，这条路是美丽而痛苦的。一定层级的心智会孕育一定层级的孤独。每上升一个心智层级，处于那个状态的人就越少。但当你找到他们时，你们之间的连接会持续一生。
p.104
The mind game houses infinite mind games. Each game has a string of goals. Each goal presents an increasingly difficult challenge that demands an increase in mental skill. All skills are of the mind, and mental mastery is how you fight back in a world that wants to steal your attention, manipulate your thoughts, and make you feel helpless.
这场心智游戏里容纳着无限的心智游戏。每一场游戏都有一串目标。每个目标都呈现一个越来越难的挑战，要求你提升心智技能。所有技能都是心智的，而心智的精通，就是你在一个想偷走你注意力、操纵你想法、让你感到无助的世界里反击的方式。
p.104
The problem is this: people get trapped in a specific mind game, fail to understand the situation, and don't practice the skill that will take them to the next level. A gradual increase in awareness through silent observation, contemplation, and questioning leads to deep understanding. If we want to see your problems for what they are, you must learn the art of zooming out. Unless you are a mechanic or have a passion for it, you don't need to know the technical details of a car to understand its implications on your life and the world. Instead, you understand a car's role in the world, learn through study and experience, and practice the skill of driving with an accepted system that orders individual and collective minds.
问题在这里：人们被困在某一场特定的心智游戏里，不理解那个处境，也不去练习能把自己带到下一层的技能。通过沉默观察、沉思和质疑而逐渐提升的觉察，会引向深刻的理解。如果我们想看清你的问题本来的样子，你必须学会“拉远镜头”这门艺术。除非你是机械师或对此有热情，否则你不需要知道一辆汽车的技术细节，才能理解它对你生活和世界的意义。相反，你理解汽车在世界中的角色，通过学习和经验去了解，并在一个被共同接受的系统里练习驾驶技能——那个系统给个体和集体的心智带来秩序。
p.104
The same does not hold true for driving through life. Your mind is the engine, and the more you deconstruct, study, and experiment with certain aspects of it, you can drive with speed through the mental roads that compose reality itself. You must develop a passion for the mind itself if you want to get to the root of existence.
而“驾驶人生”就不一样了。你的心智是引擎，你越是去解构、研究、并实验它某些方面，你就越能以速度驶过那些构成现实本身的心智之路。如果你想触及存在的根本，就必须对心智本身发展出热情。
p.104
Understanding is infinite. It is how you raise your consciousness in an upward fashion. Most teachers, gurus, or masters help you in a downward fashion through tools like meditation. Which is necessary to increase the
理解是无限的。它是你向上提升意识的方式。大多数老师、上师或大师，是通过冥想之类的工具，以“向下”的方式帮助你——那是通过让心智安静下来、来扩大
p.105
space between your thoughts by quieting your mind. Both are necessary but the former is often neglected.
你念头之间空间所必需的。两者都必要，但前者常常被忽视。
p.105
Similar to a human's depth of focus, understanding is another unique and inherent aspect of our being. Knowing is not understanding. Knowing implies a label, limit, or distinction that the mind creates. Understanding is different. It is how you explore the interconnectedness of life through observation.
与人类专注的深度类似，理解是我们存在中另一个独特且固有的面向。知道不等于理解。知道暗示着心智创造的一个标签、限制或区分。理解不同。它是你通过观察去探索生命相互连接的方式。
p.105
I can understand a game from the top down by questioning not only its source but its impact on the world. If you don't zoom out to see the entirety of its implications, you won't be able to see if you are climbing the right mountain.
我可以自上而下地理解一场游戏——不仅质疑它的来源，也质疑它对世界的影响。如果你不拉远镜头去看它全部的意义，你就无法判断自己是不是在爬对的那座山。
p.105
To help illustrate this difference in human consciousness, we can observe apes. Our furry predecessors do not plan or ask questions to the degree that we do. A human, with time and practice, can throw a football and hit a bullseye from fifty yards out. As can we create a vision for the future and actualize that reality through conscious practice. An ape, on the other hand, can fling feces, but it usually ends up straight on the ground in front of them. I'm assuming that you don't want to be feces flung at the ground, which stresses the importance of going beyond yourself through your creative ability, not regressing into your animalistic nature.
为了帮助说明人类意识中的这一差别，我们可以观察猿。我们那些毛茸茸的前辈不会像我们这样去规划或提问。人类通过时间和练习，可以从五十码外扔出一个橄榄球命中靶心。我们同样能创造关于未来的愿景，并通过有意识的练习把这个现实变成真。而一只猿能扔粪便，但通常那粪便就落在它正前方的地上。我猜你不想成为被扔到地上的粪便——这强调了通过创造能力去超越自我、而不是退化回动物本性是何等重要。
p.105
Human understanding, which has a direct correlation with quality of life, comes down to asking quality questions. Apes don't do this. They can learn sign language and communicate in a half-baked manner, but to my knowledge they don't attempt to create new knowledge through questioning. They don't realize that other beings can know things they don't.
人类的理解——它与生活质量直接相关——归根结底在于提出高质量的问题。猿不这么做。它们能学手语并以半生不熟的方式交流，但据我所知，它们不会试图通过提问来创造新知识。它们意识不到其他存在能知道它们不知道的事。
p.105
As a thought experiment, let's look at a common ingredient like honey. Simply asking, "Where was this honey made?" can lead me down a rabbit hole of discovery. I can follow that line of questioning to the bees that made it, the pollinated flowers, the beekeepers involved and their ethical treatment of their bees, where the honey was distributed across the globe,
作为一个思想实验，我们来看一个常见食材，比如蜂蜜。仅仅问一句“这蜂蜜是在哪里做的？”，就能把我带进一个发现的无底洞。我可以顺着这条提问线索追到造蜜的蜜蜂、被授粉的花朵、参与的养蜂人以及他们对待蜜蜂的伦理方式、蜂蜜在全球的分配路线、
p.106
what meals the honey is used for, the health benefits of raw and unfiltered honey, the health detriments of processed honey, when bees emerged on the evolutionary timeline, what their purpose is in more than just ecological function, and how any of that information can help in the achievement of my goals. Everything you see has an iceberg of understanding beneath the surface. Observe and question.
这些蜂蜜被用于哪些餐食、生蜜与未过滤蜂蜜的健康益处、加工蜂蜜的健康损害、蜜蜂在演化时间线上何时出现、它们除了生态功能之外还有什么目的，以及这些信息如何有助于达成我的目标。你看见的每样东西，表面之下都有一座理解的冰山。去观察，去质疑。
p.106
You can try to apply this same practice to any negative thought, emotion, or situation that you do not enjoy. Question it. Follow it to its source. Observe how all the moving components in the system impact your life both right now and onward into your ideal future.
你可以把这同一个练习应用到任何你不喜欢的负面念头、情绪或处境上。质疑它。顺着它追到源头。观察系统里所有运动中的组件如何影响你的生活——既在当下，也在通往你理想未来的路上。
p.106
Understanding your problems means to perceive them from the highest level of mind available to you. From that expanded perspective, you can begin to experiment, iterate, and create a long-term personal solution. For now, attempt to adopt the perspective of your ideal self. Perceive situations through their lens and embody their values through action. Who do you want to become, what actions does that identity perform daily, and how can you integrate that into your current lifestyle regardless of how long you spend on those activities?
理解你的问题，意味着用你所能获得的最高心智层级去感知它们。从那个被扩展的视角出发，你可以开始实验、迭代，并创造出一个长期的个人解法。现在，试着采取你理想自我的视角。透过他们的透镜去感知处境，并通过行动具现他们的价值观。你想成为谁？那个身份每天执行哪些行动？无论如何要在那些活动上花多少时间，你如何把它整合进你现在的生活方式？
p.106
Problems are only problems if you interpret them that way. If you don't feel like getting out of bed, zoom out and realize how measly your problem is from a higher perspective.
问题只有在你把它解读为问题时才是问题。如果你不想起床，拉远镜头，意识到从更高视角看你的问题有多微不足道。
p.106
With time, you can seek to zoom out further and embody the perspective of the Universe. What behavior is your problem influencing and how does it impact the world as would a jar of honey? Can you make sense of and find relief in the fact that your situation matches the ebb and flow of the Universe? Are you a slave to the fabricated expectations of reality? Or can you zoom out and see life for what it is? The actions you take, or lack thereof, have a widespread impact on your future that can't be seen through the lens of your problem. Problems that prevent positive choices can only be solved by the emergence of a new perception that stems from a higher level of mind.
随时间推移，你可以寻求拉得更远，并具现宇宙的视角。你的问题正在影响什么行为？它又如何像一罐蜂蜜那样影响世界？你能否理解并从中得到宽慰——你的处境与宇宙的潮起潮落是相匹配的？你是“被编造的对现实的期待”的奴隶吗？还是你能拉远镜头，看见生活本来的样子？你所采取的行动，或缺乏的行动，对你的未来有广泛影响，而那些影响无法透过你问题的透镜被看见。阻止你做出正面选择的问题，只能靠一个源自更高心智层级的新感知的涌现来解决。
p.107
When mental battles are at your doorstep, don't fight with it, flow with it. Pause, zoom out, observe, and when you gain clarity through the intangible resources you've acquired, dive back in and execute with focused effort. 125 BILLION BITS The conscious mind can process fifty bits of information per second. If you live until the ripe age of eighty years old, you can process around 125 billion bits of information in your lifetime. This information is processed through focus, which expends mental energy and results in a varying quality of experience.
当心智战役来到你家门口，不要与它交战，与它同流。暂停、拉远、观察，而当你凭已获得的那些无形资源获得清晰之后，再一头潜回去，用聚焦的努力执行。1250 亿比特：意识心智每秒能处理五十比特信息。如果你活到八十岁的高龄，你一生中可以处理大约 1250 亿比特信息。这些信息通过专注被处理，而专注消耗心智能量，并带来质量各异的体验。
p.107
A large chunk of that information will be processed by necessities like grooming, cooking, and running errands. The rest will be processed by work, rest, play, and the distractions that pull you away from giving your full attention to meaningful living.
其中很大一块会被仪容、做饭、跑腿之类的必要事项处理掉。剩下的会被工作、休息、玩乐，以及那些把你从“把全部注意力给予有意义的生活”上拉走的干扰处理掉。
p.107
Imagine your life potential as the 125 billion bits of information you can process. If your focus isn't strategic and you become a victim of modern mental enslavement, your potential is already decided. Your attention will be manhandled, your sense of self will be an unconscious monstrosity, and you will end up an average clone without your knowing. Nobody wants to wake up wondering where the time - or information - went.
把你的人生潜能想象成你能处理的那 1250 亿比特信息。如果你的专注没有策略、你成为现代心智奴役的受害者，那你的潜能就已经被决定了。你的注意力会被任意摆弄，你的自我感会是一个无意识的怪物，而你会不知不觉地成为一个平庸的复制品。没人想在醒来时纳闷：时间——或者说信息——都去哪了。
p.107
The unconscious mind can process eleven million bits of information per second. This is incredible and shines a light on the fact that most of what we think, say, and do is not an absolutely conscious decision.
无意识心智每秒能处理一千一百万比特信息。这不可思议，也照亮了一个事实：我们所想、所说、所做的大部分，都不是绝对有意识的决定。
p.107
