As we improve our mental skill that is built by our physical, spiritual, and financial development, life becomes more enjoyable with time and practice. Learning how to walk is a skill. It's as difficult, if not more difficult, than learning how to build a cash-cow software business. But once that skill is acquired, you can expend a fraction of the mental energy and stack complimentary skills through focus until you create a powerful character.
随着我们提升由身体、精神和财务发展所构建的心智技能，生活会随时间和练习变得更享受。学走路是一项技能。它和学“如何打造一门现金牛软件生意”一样难，甚至更难。但一旦这项技能被获得，你就能花其中一小部分心智能量，并通过专注叠加互补技能，直到你创造出一个强大的角色。
p.108
As we learn and become more comfortable with any aspect of reality, that information is stored and used by the unconscious mind. Do you have to think about walking, or do you just walk? Do you know how you are doing it, or do you just do it? I'm not asking for a scientific breakdown of knowledge, proof, and labels that came into existence after our ability to walk. I'm assuming you don't hold every muscle fiber and biomechanical formula in your mind while strolling down the street. In fact, walking is close to nothing compared to the unconscious Universal processes unfolding all around you.
随着我们学习并变得更熟悉现实的任何一面，那份信息会被无意识心智储存并使用。你需要想着走路吗，还是你就走了？你知道自己在怎么走吗，还是你就走了？我不是在要求你用科学方式拆解那些在我们走路能力之后才出现的知识、证据和标签。我猜你在街上漫步时，脑中并不装着每一根肌肉纤维和每一条生物力学公式。事实上，与正在你周围展开的那些无意识的宇宙过程相比，走路几乎不算什么。
p.108
The default state of consciousness is chaos. You have experienced this before. Unless your mind is engaged with a thought, task, or stimulus, it will wander off in a negative direction, anxiety, or boredom. When we allow randomness into our lives, negativity increases in potential.
意识的默认状态是混乱。你以前体验过。除非你的心智投入到某个念头、任务或刺激上，否则它会朝一个负面方向漫游——焦虑，或无聊。当我们允许随机性进入生活，负面的可能性就上升了。
p.108
When you set the goal of achieving "good financial health," as a mediocre example, the thought ends there. And if we don't maintain our focus on that outcome with a plan, perspective, and distraction mitigation, negative thoughts flood our mind that influence our ability to act.
举个平庸的例子：当你设定“实现良好的财务健康”这个目标时，念头到那里就结束了。而如果我们不用计划、视角和干扰抑制来维持对那个结果的专注，负面念头就会淹没心智，影响我们行动的能力。
p.108
The thought of making a lot of money is great, but since you have not achieved it, that is the only positive outcome unless reinforced with evolving reasoning as to why you want to achieve it. On the flip side, your mind can wander to the bills you need to pay, the school loans you forgot about, a potential tax audit, paying your friend back, the rising gas prices, the cost of energizing food, and each of those can splinter your focus infinitely with the negative thoughts associated with each.
“赚很多钱”这个念头很棒，但既然你还没实现，那它就是唯一一个正面结果——除非你用不断演化的“我为什么想实现它”的理由来强化它。反过来说，你的心智可以漫游到你需要付的账单、你忘了的助学贷款、一场可能的税务审计、还朋友的钱、上涨的油价、能供能的食物的成本，而每一项都能用与之相关的负面念头把你的焦点无限地碎裂开。
p.108
Nobody can make up their minds on the best mental, physical, or financial plan because it has become increasingly difficult to order our minds on a meaningful hierarchy of goals. The modern information landscape will throw you into a chaotic loop of overwhelm if you lack the ability to focus. The only option is to forge your own path. You must set a conscious goal, create clarity through self-education and experimentation, and abide by the principle of progressive overload: to increase the challenge, practice until
没有人能就“最好的心智、身体或财务计划”拿定主意，因为我们越来越难把心智整理到一个有意义的目标层级上。现代信息景观会在你缺乏专注能力时，把你扔进一个不堪重负的混乱循环。唯一的选项是走出你自己的路。你必须设定一个有意识的目标，通过自我教育和实验创造清晰，并遵守“渐进超负荷”原则：提高挑战，练到
p.109
your skill is up to par, and repeat the process as life lessons compound into a personal philosophy that can be shared to advance the collective mind. The average individual yearns to break free of what used to bring order to their mind, like working a job, because the challenge has stopped increasing. They've been doing the same old thing for too long. Their mind races toward anxiety at the thought of future work, and while we are there, we think of something better we could be doing.
你的技能达标，然后重复这个过程，同时让那些人生课程复利成一套可以分享出去、以推进集体心智的个人哲学。普通人渴望挣脱那些曾经给他们的心智带来秩序的东西（比如上班），因为挑战已经不再升级了。他们同样的事情做太久了。一想到未来的工作，他们的心智就朝焦虑狂奔；而当我们处在焦虑里，我们就会想“我本可以去做点更好的事”。
p.109
We look forward to the weekend and, come midday on a Sunday, we find ourselves with "nothing to do," gravitate toward boredom and seek to fill our time with whatever entity, often negative, that pops into our heads. As the day goes on and worldly responsibilities close in, the anxiety starts to creep in.
我们盼着周末，而到了周日的正午，我们发现自己“无事可做”，于是倾向无聊，寻求用任何蹦进脑子的东西（往往是负面的）来填满时间。随着白天推进、世俗责任逼来，焦虑开始悄悄爬进来。
p.109
The solution to this endless negative oscillation is education, clarity, and action. This book, up until now, has been for education and awareness. For clarity, we need a firm understanding that we can only have full control over one thing: our focus. The order we create in consciousness.
这个无尽的负面振荡，解法是教育、清晰和行动。这本书到目前为止，是为了教育和觉察。为了清晰，我们需要牢固地理解：我们只能完全掌控一件事——我们的专注。我们在意识中创造的秩序。
p.109
Through focus, we can control what goes into our mind, how we interpret that information, and what we produce with it. If we want to create and maintain an enjoyable order in our lives, we need a progression of engaging external stimulation to dedicate our focus to.
通过专注，我们能控制什么进入心智、我们如何解读那些信息、以及我们用它产出什么。如果我们想在人生中创造并维持一种令人享受的秩序，我们就需要一连串有吸引力的外部刺激，来让专注有所投注。
p.109
We clearly want to fill the 125 billion bits of our finite focus, or potential, with the information that will make life most enjoyable. But it takes time to dig yourself out of the programmed hole you find yourself in around fifteen years old; most realize this even later.
我们显然想用那些能让生活最享受的信息，去填满我们有限的专注（也就是潜能）那 1250 亿比特。但要从你在十五岁左右落入的那个“被编程的坑”里把自己挖出来，是需要时间的；大多数人意识到这一点还要更晚。
p.109
When you combine necessities like grooming, cooking, and errands with fifteen years of unconscious buildup, our potential decreases even further. You no longer have a full 125 billion bits to fulfill, but don't let this split your focus into a state of anxiety. While this is an urgent matter for those that know they are meant for more, you cannot change where you are; you can only change the perspective you hold that will lead to beneficial action.
当你把仪容、做饭、跑腿之类的必要事项，与十五年的无意识累积加在一起，我们的潜能会进一步下降。你不再拥有完整的 1250 亿比特去充填——但别让这一点把你的焦点撕裂成焦虑状态。虽然对那些知道自己是“为更多而生”的人来说这是个紧急事项，你无法改变你在哪里；你只能改变你所持有的、将带来有益行动的视角。
p.110
Reflect on your past. Has there ever been a point where you learn something new, become obsessed with it, and feel like you are on top of the world? A new diet can bring you physical energy, but we tend to neglect that most of that sudden boost is the result of clarity.
反思你的过去。是否曾有那样一个时刻：你学到新东西，对它着迷，感觉自己站在世界之巅？一套新饮食可以给你身体能量，但我们容易忽略：那种突然的提振，大部分其实是“清晰”的结果。
p.110
When we follow a routine without waver, stick to a new meal plan, or discover a new passion, we feel good. This presents a potential trap. Many people attribute the good feeling to the ideology, method, or tactic that brought it into their life. Those that realize the source of enjoyment is clarity will be able to experiment with methods in an open state of mind. From there, they can create their own method so that when the other inevitably fails them, they aren't boxed into a state of mental turmoil. The quality of your human experience is most influenced by the structure of the information you process. When you create a meaningful hierarchy of goals, acquire the skill necessary to achieve those goals, and act from the perspective of your highest self, life becomes enjoyable. This is in your control but is not immediate.
当我们毫不动摇地遵循一套日常、坚持一份新餐单、或发现一种新热爱时，我们感觉良好。这里潜藏着一个陷阱。很多人把这种良好感受归功于那个把它带进生活的意识形态、方法或战术。而那些意识到“享受的来源是清晰”的人，将能以开放的心态去试验各种方法。从那里，他们能创造出自己的方法，这样当别的法子不可避免地让他们失望时，他们不会被困在心智混乱的状态里。你人类体验的质量，最受你处理的信息结构影响。当你创造出一个有意义的目标层级、获得达成那些目标所需的技能、并从你最高自我的视角行动时，生活就变得令人享受。这在你掌控之内，但不是即时的。
p.110
When the external is aligned with the internal, and focus is tight, the unconscious powerhouse of a mind sends resources to fuel your presentmoment actions. Being and doing collapse into one. I'm convinced that most people have experienced this wonderful state of consciousness but have no clue how to replicate or sustain it. A beautiful harmony of progress being made without a worry in the world.
当外在与内在对齐、专注紧实时，那个无意识的强大心智会输送资源去为你此刻的行动供能。“在”与“做”塌缩为一。我确信大多数人都体验过这个奇妙的心境，但完全不知道如何复制或维持它。一种美丽的和谐：进步正在发生，而世间无忧。
p.110
As we push back against entropy, our focus must evolve as we do. We must structure the game we wish to play, learn how to play, win, and create the next one. Because if you continue playing the same game, it will either become boring, or you will be caught up in one that you may not care to play. And if you choose to play a game that you are not skilled enough for, you will either get anxious, or you will find an excuse to quit altogether. Infinite games are that of the mind. The path of mastery in your endeavors. One can begin physical training, but if they don't evolve beyond the superficial pursuit of looks, the game will collapse and life will lose meaning. Enjoyment is found in the small improvements made in all
当我们顶住熵，我们的专注必须随我们一同演化。我们必须构筑我们想玩的游戏、学会怎么玩、赢下它、并创造下一个。因为如果你继续玩同一个游戏，它要么变得无聊，要么你会陷进去，而那个游戏你可能并不想玩。而如果你选择玩一个你技能不够的游戏，你要么会焦虑，要么会找个借口彻底退出。无限游戏是心智的游戏。是你各项事业中的精通之路。一个人可以开始体能训练，但如果他不进化到超越那份对“外形”的表层追求，游戏就会崩塌，生活就会失去意义。享受是在生活所有领域中做出的微小改进里被找到的。
p.111
domains of life. And improvements are infinite if you continue to expand who you are.
而只要你继续扩展“你是谁”，改进就是无限的。
THE PATH OF MASTERY
精通之路
p.111
p.111
The closed-minded quick-fix attitude toward life is the greatest trap of our times, and it runs much deeper than the average person believes. Which is ironic, because the reason they think they aren't a victim of closedmindedness is closed-mindedness in itself.
那种封闭心态的速成生活态度，是我们时代最大的陷阱，而它比普通人以为的深得多。这很讽刺，因为他们认为自己不是封闭心态受害者的理由，本身就是封闭心态。
p.111
Closed-mindedness encapsulates a host of other problems like distraction, reactivity, surface-level living, falling for get-rich-quick schemes, lack of commitment in business and relationships, and the inability to discover and pursue one's purpose.
封闭心态囊括了一大堆其他问题：分心、条件反射、表层生活、上当于快速致富的骗局、在生意和关系中缺乏承诺、以及无法发现并追求自己的目的。
p.111
The biggest culprit of this problem is your inability to increase your level of mind beyond your programmed perspective. You become a victim to the web of expectations, concepts, and beliefs that circulate from situation to situation.
这个问题最大的元凶，是你无法把心智层级提升到你被编程的视角之上。你成了那张期待、概念和信念之网的受害者——它从一个处境循环到另一个处境。
p.111
Your perspective houses your beliefs, thoughts, and experiences that you hold unconsciously as absolute truth in a subjective reality. When these become static, they are limits on what you perceive as possible in life itself or individual situations. Unless you can expand your mind beyond them, you are doomed to a life of the limits you imposed on yourself through unconscious acceptance.
你的视角容纳着你无意识地持有、在一个主观现实中当作绝对真理的信念、想法和经验。当这些变成静态的，它们就成了限制，限制你在生活本身或个别处境中所感知到的可能性。除非你能把心智扩展到它们之外，你注定要过一种由你通过无意识接受而自我施加的限制所构成的生活。
p.111
You can observe this in your everyday life to become aware of your own mindless actions. When political elections roll around, each party will defend their stance as the best, because that's what they were told, and they failed to question. The same happens with entrepreneurs and ideologues defending their business model or belief system as the best.
你可以在日常生活中观察到这一点，从而觉察到自己的无脑行动。当政治选举来临，每个党派都会把自己的立场捍卫为最好的——因为那是他们被告知的，而他们从未质疑。创业者和意识形态者把它们的商业模式或信念体系捍卫为最好的，也是一样。
p.111
Missing the point, essence, or message of any situation is the next culprit. People read the bible from a literal - as opposed to metaphorical - point of
错过任何处境的要点、本质或讯息，是下一个元凶。人们用字面的（而非隐喻的）观点读《圣经》，
p.112
view and end up identifying as atheists. People also interpret God as a literal man in the sky instead of a symbol for an experience or phenomenon. This misinterpretation applies to everything, not just spiritual belief systems. People close their minds at the literal interpretation of words so they can win the unconscious status game they are playing. They don't care to follow the words to the essence of reality that words are meant to guide awareness to. I don't blame them, of course, but there is an entire world of meaning that lies beyond literal interpretations that change from culture to culture and generation to generation.
最后把自己认同为无神论者。人们也把“神”解读为天上一个字面意义上的男人，而不是一种体验或现象的符号。这种误读适用于一切，不只是灵性信念体系。人们把心门关在文字的字面解读上，好让他们赢下自己正在玩的那场无意识地位游戏。他们不在乎顺着文字走到现实的本质——而文字本是为了把觉察引向那里。我当然不怪他们，但确实存在一整个意义世界，它位于字面解读之外，而字面解读会随文化和世代而变化。
p.112
People will hear the words from someone's mouth, which illustrates a microscopic fraction of who they truly are, then go on to plug those words into the story playing in their head. When this piece doesn't fit in their puzzle, they get offended, reactive, and negative because they lack understanding. This isn't a fulfilling way to live.
人们会听到某人嘴里说出的话——那话只展示了他真实所是的一个微小百分比——然后把这些话插进自己脑子里正在播放的故事。当这块碎片嵌不进他们的拼图时，他们就觉得被冒犯、条件反射、负面，因为他们缺乏理解。这不是一种能带来成就感的活法。
p.112
The difference between the quick-fix path and the path of mastery is that of climaxes. The pleasure seeker falls into a pit of endless climaxes that creates the largest-scale addiction known to modern man. The master leans into the Universal story, embraces struggle, and basks in the climax to come (but does not attempt to maintain that high).
速成之路与精通之路的差别在于“高潮”。追求快感的人掉进一个无尽高潮的坑里，制造出现代人已知的最大规模成瘾。而大师向宇宙的故事倾斜，拥抱挣扎，并沐浴在即将到来的高潮中（但不试图维持那个高点）。
p.112
You can observe the pleasure seeker's nature in media and advertising. In a beer advertisement, you see somebody at work for what seems to be 5 minutes before the scene cuts to them slouched on the couch, beer in hand, drinking the night away to escape the stress of tomorrow's workday. The path of mastery is a cyclical process of increasing our skill as we take on more difficult challenges, so we don't default to a state of anxiety or boredom. This process is most difficult at the start but becomes easier and more pleasurable with time.
你可以在媒体和广告里观察到追求快感者的本性。在一则啤酒广告里，你看到某人在工作，似乎只过了五分钟，镜头就切到他瘫在沙发上、手里拿着啤酒、整夜喝酒来逃避明天工作日的压力。精通之路是一个循环过程：随着我们接下更难的挑战而提升技能，从而不默认落入焦虑或无聊。这个过程在起点最难，但随着时间变得更容易、更愉悦。
p.112
When you start your journey of education, skill acquisition, and goal achievement, you will encounter a series of plateaus. At the start, these will be short and rewarding. You will see quick progress. As you endure, the plateaus get longer and longer. You are met with 2 options: quit and pursue a new climax or learn to fall in love with the process.
当你开始教育、技能习得和目标达成的旅程，你会遇到一连串平台期。起初它们短且回报丰厚。你会看到快速进步。随着你忍耐下去，平台期越来越长。你会面对两个选项：放弃、去追求一个新的高潮；或者学会爱上这个过程。
p.113
To fall in love with the process, you must refocus your mind on the depth and detail of the present moment. Like how a writer senses the smell of fresh coffee on a gloomy morning before typing the first letter of an unknown written journey. Or how a chef finds appreciation in the flow of water across their hands as they prepare a fine cut of regenerative grass-fed steak. The path of mastery is a goalless journey that is directed by selfgenerated goals. A paradox that teaches you that goals help with order and direction, but that ritual, presence, and clarity bring ultimate satisfaction. It takes certain complexity of mind forged through struggle to expend mental energy beyond the surface-level challenges of a chosen endeavor.
要爱上这个过程，你必须把心智重新聚焦到当下的深度和细节上。就像一位作家在一个阴郁的清晨，在敲下一个未知文字旅程的第一个字母之前，闻到新鲜咖啡的香气。或者一位厨师在洗手准备一块上好的再生草饲牛排时，在水流流过手背的过程中找到欣赏。精通之路是一段没有目标、却由自我生成的目标所指引的旅程。一个悖论，它教会你：目标有助于秩序与方向，但仪式、临在、清晰带来终极满足。那需要一种经挣扎锻打出的特定心智复杂度，才能把心智能量投到超出某一选定事业表层挑战之外的地方。
p.113
A notable aspect of this process is the perception threshold. Any challenge, lifelong or local, is not perceived as difficult at the start. Maybe the act of starting is, and that is a challenge in itself, but actually starting any activity is usually the easiest part. As we continue on, the perceived difficulty increases, and thoughts begin to flood our head. Where most people quit is where greatness is born.
这个过程一个值得注意的面向，是“感知阈值”。任何挑战，无论终身的还是局部的，在开始时都不被感知为困难。也许“启动”这个动作本身就是挑战，但真正开始任何活动通常是最容易的部分。随着我们继续，所感知到的难度上升，念头开始淹没脑袋。而大多数人退出的地方，正是伟大诞生的地方。
p.113
When we reach the point of immense difficulty, our mind gravitates toward expectations of how things should be, not what they are. If you persist through the mental discomfort, you will be forced to expand your mind to see reality for what it is. You cannot solve a problem from the same level of mind that created it. At this point, life offers a lesson to your problems, and you break through the perception threshold.
当我们抵达极其困难的那一点，我们的心智倾向于“事物应该是什么样”的期待，而不是它本来的样子。如果你穿越这份心智上的不适坚持下去，你将被迫扩展心智，去看清现实本来的样子。你无法用“制造出这个问题的同一个心智层级”去解决这个问题。在这一点上，生活为你的问题提供一课，而你突破了感知阈值。
p.113
A perception, or how you interpret a situation, is a unit of mind. There are infinite ways to perceive a difficult situation. After each struggle, a new perspective emerges that allows you to perceive that situation in a more conducive manner. With time, and as you expose yourself to more experience, your perspective integrates aspects of the human experience and menial problems lose their impact on your well-being. When you stick out the difficulty of a situation and break through the resistance, you see a leap in mental skill that can take on higher challenges.
一种感知——或你如何解读一个处境——是一个心智单元。感知一个困难处境的方式有无限种。每一次挣扎之后，一个新的视角涌现，让你能以更有利的方式感知那个处境。随时间推移，随着你把自己暴露于更多经验，你的视角整合了人类经验的各个面向，琐碎问题失去了对你身心状态的影响。当你熬过一个处境的困难、突破那层阻抗，你会看到一次心智技能的跃迁，足以接下更高的挑战。
p.113
Some know this as the "runners high," where one overcomes a mental battle, their mind quiets, and even when it is an extremely difficult
有人称之为“跑者高潮”：一个人克服了一场心智战役，心智安静下来，即便处境极其困难，
p.114
situation, one can stick it out without complaint. This is normal to someone who enjoys running. The activity in itself is enjoyable because of the selfdiscovered philosophy that has shaped their worldview with time. This is a pattern found in the pursuit of any long-term or short-term goal. This lesson is best learned through experience, and now that you have the awareness of this phenomenon, I would encourage you to persist through the next challenge that makes you want to quit any meaningful pursuit.
他也能毫无怨言地坚持下去。对一个享受跑步的人来说这是常态。这项活动本身之所以令人享受，是因为那套随时间塑造了他们世界观的、自我发现的哲学。这是一个在任何长期或短期目标追求中都能找到的模式。这一课最好通过经验来学，而既然你现在有了这个现象的觉察，我鼓励你在下一次让你想放弃任何有意义追求的挑战中坚持下去。
p.114
Thanks to our default state of chaos and our inability to assume a difficult path between where we are and where we want to be, we procrastinate on our dreams and resort to a state of mental discomfort, which we often perceive as comfortable, because that's all we know.
多亏我们默认的混乱状态、以及我们没能力在“我们在哪”和“我们想在哪”之间设想出一条艰难路径，我们拖延自己的梦想，退回到一种心智不适的状态——而我们常常把那感知为舒适，因为那是我们唯一知道的。
p.114
Let's use starting a business as an example. After all, it's the next evolution for those that inevitably hit a challenge ceiling while working for someone else (and that ceiling comes quick). If I told you to work for free for fifty people and expect nothing in return, you would think I'm crazy. Or maybe you would try it for a bit, realize its difficulty, and come to the same conclusion of my delusional mental state. Then, due to a reinforced closed mind, you will go on searching for new tactics that promise faster results just to repeat the process while standing still for years on years.
拿“开始创业”当例子。毕竟，对那个在给别人打工时不可避免地撞上能力天花板的人（而且那个天花板来得很快）来说，这是下一步的进化。如果我告诉你免费为五十个人工作、不期待任何回报，你会觉得我疯了。或者你会试一会儿，意识到它的难度，然后得出和我一样“精神错乱”的结论。接着，由于被强化过的封闭心态，你会继续去搜寻承诺更快结果的新战术，只是为了在不挪动一分的情况下原地重复这个过程，年复一年。
p.114
If you can't see yourself doing something every day, why are you doing it? If you say you want to do this work for 5 to 10 years, why does it matter if you don't get paid for the first 6 months? When you expand your time horizon and question what you want, you'll realize what the quick-fix behavior is really worth: close to zero.
如果你看不见自己每天都做某件事，那你为什么在做它？如果你说你想做这份工作做 5 到 10 年，那么前六个月没有报酬又有什么关系？当你扩展你的时间视野、并质疑你想要什么时，你会意识到速成行为真正值多少：接近于零。
p.114
This applies to every aspect of life, not just business. You didn't need a quick fix for learning to walk, speak, and brew your favorite coffee. You adopted them as a part of your everyday behavior after a grueling difficulty in acquiring the skill. The only difference between your goals then and now are the illusory mental barriers that prevent you from facing reality.
这适用于生活的每个面向，不只是生意。你学走路、学说话、学冲你最爱的那杯咖啡，都不需要什么速成。在经历一段艰难的技能习得期之后，你把它们当成了日常行为的一部分。你当时和现在的目标之间唯一的区别，只是那些阻止你面对现实的、虚幻的心智屏障。
THE FORMULA
公式
p.115
p.115
You can do nothing with your life, nobody is going to stop you, but you won't escape survival.
你可以一辈子什么都不做，没人会阻止你，但你逃脱不了生存。
p.115
By doing nothing, the default outcome of your life will be mindlessness, chaos, and destruction. This is no exaggeration. You have the choice to go beyond yourself through spirit or regress into the animalistic senses you transcended and were meant to include, not become a slave to. Human behavior boils down to problem-solving in alignment with a goal, whether it be conscious or unconscious, meaningful or meaningless, or the decision between creation and destruction.
什么都不做的话，你人生的默认结果就会是无脑、混乱与毁灭。这不是夸张。你有选择：通过精神去超越自己，或者退化回你曾超越、且本该去“包含”（而不是沦为奴隶）的动物性感官。人类行为的本质，是与某个目标对齐的问题解决——无论那目标是有意识还是无意识的、有意义还是无意义的，也无论那选择是创造还是毁灭。
p.115
When you aren't able to pay your bills, that's a problem. Most people will adopt a survival goal of getting a job that can fix their money problems. When they get that job, they may remain unconscious as to how they fit into the machine that the company is. They lack a big-picture understanding of the company's impact. Some people may go on to work as a simple secretary for the military industrial complex, yet they are associated with the bombing of civilians halfway around the world.
当你付不起账单时，那是个问题。大多数人会采纳一个生存目标：找份能解决钱问题的工作。当他们得到那份工作，他们可能仍然无意识地不清楚自己如何嵌进了这家公司这台机器。他们缺乏对该公司影响力的全局理解。有些人可能会继续去给军工复合体当个普通的秘书，而他们与半个地球之外的平民轰炸产生了关联。
p.115
If one were to become truly conscious of the impact of that company, they would be forced to create a new goal to solve a more meaningful problem that starts with their personal life. They wouldn't be able to do this in an
如果一个人真正意识到那家公司的影响，他将被迫创造一个新目标，去解决一个更有意义的问题——从个人生活开始。他当然无法在
p.116
instant, of course, but they would see the potential of positive universal impact if they began to set goals and contemplate their vision.
一瞬间做到，但如果他开始设定目标并沉思自己的愿景，他就会看见积极影响整个宇宙的潜能。
p.116
Since their money problems have been temporarily solved thanks to the job, the stress that accompanies survival lowers to a manageable level. From that higher state of mind, they can set a goal to build a creative income source that serves a higher purpose.
既然钱的问题已经被那份工作暂时解决了，伴随生存而来的压力降到可控水平。从那个更高的心境出发，他可以设定一个目标：去建立一个服务更高目的的创造性收入来源。
p.116
The unfortunate reality is that most people will not become aware of how their actions ripple across the globe. Not only in their line of work, but in every single goal they pursue that influences every single one of their actions. But the few that do, hopefully with the help of this book, are the future leaders that have first dibs at the good life.
不幸的现实是，大多数人不会意识到他们的行动如何在地球上激起涟漪——不只是工作，而是他们追求的每一个目标，那会影响他们每一个行动。而那少数意识到的人——希望这本书能帮到他们——是未来的领袖，他们拥有对美好生活的优先权。
p.116
Don't fall into the trap of conscious nobility. Like someone who just learned about the concept of spirituality and uses it as a moral high ground. If you are deep in an unconscious way of life, it is impossible to switch exclusively to nondestructive actions. Everyone has a shadow, and the most successful individuals use what could be unethical skills as an ethical way to integrate their dark tendencies. And those that don't often manipulate others without knowing it.
不要掉进“有意识的高尚”这个陷阱。就像那种刚学到灵性概念、就把它当作道德制高点的人。如果你深深处在一种无意识的生活方式里，是不可能完全切换到非破坏性行动的。每个人都有阴影，而最成功的个体，会把那些可能不道德的技能，当作一种合乎伦理的方式来整合自己的黑暗倾向。而那些不这么做的人，往往在不知不觉中操纵他人。
p.116
You will have to manipulate, cheat, and contribute to evil. Nobody wants to admit that, and that's what chains them to it. Evil exists and is a necessary balance that allows good to exist. We all make mistakes, and it is foolish to think that those mistakes shouldn't be a part of your life. A majority of the population hides behind an unconscious moral high ground that contributes to more evil than the conscious individual that attempts to integrate, transmute, and harness their dark energy.
你将不得不操纵、欺骗、并为恶做出贡献。没人愿意承认这一点，而正是这一点把他们锁在上面。恶存在，并且是一个让善得以存在的必要平衡。我们都会犯错，认为那些错误不该成为你生活的一部分是愚蠢的。大多数人都躲在一个无意识的道德制高点后面，而那个制高点所贡献的恶，比一个试图整合、转化并驾驭自己黑暗能量的有意识个体更多。
p.116
When you encounter a problem, you have a choice. For most, this choice is automatic and made in a way that best serves the unconscious manipulation of others that was conditioned into their psyche. Personal responsibility is understanding that you have the power to choose regardless of how you feel, and you must take it. Your future does not have to be the outcome of your past.
当你遇到一个问题，你有一个选择。对大多数人来说，这个选择是自动的，并且以最能服务那种被条件化进他们心智的、无意识操纵他人的方式来做出。个人责任，就是理解“无论你感受如何，你都有选择的权力”，并且你必须接过它。你的未来不必是你过去的产物。
p.117
We need to create conscious goals for the problems in our lives. These goals act as a decision filter for making the best decision in that situation. When you inevitably make a mistake, and a new problem reveals itself, that too must be filtered and corrected with time.
我们需要为生活中的问题创造有意识的目标。这些目标充当决策过滤器，帮助你在那个处境中做出最好的决定。当你不可避免地犯了一个错、一个新问题显现出来时，那也必须被过滤，并随时间被纠正。
p.117
A game is a system that requires individual choice. If we create, maintain, and invest mental energy into the games that will actualize our ideal future, we meet meaning and fulfillment.
一个游戏，是一个要求个体做出选择的系统。如果我们创造、维护、并把心智能量投入到那些将实现我们理想未来的游戏里，我们就会遇上意义与成就。
ANTI-VISION
反愿景（ANTI-VISION）
p.117
p.117
If I start to visualize my father's eventual death, I get teary-eyed. A ball of energy radiates in my chest. Emotional energy. A powerful build-up of tension ready to be directed and released toward a goal. There isn't a specific story, aside from the thousands of experiences I hold with my parents, that accompanies this. Anyone can dig into the experiences of their past, generate a potent energy source within them, and focus that energy though action toward an intrinsic hierarchy of goals. This is the secret of the disciplined and successful. Self-discipline is when the desire to become the highest version of yourself outweighs the desire for cheap pleasures. When I am stuck, I'll go on a walk. On that walk, I allow thoughts to trigger thoughts, which I will attempt to deconstruct into their smaller parts. When a thought catches my attention more than the next, I will sit with it, question it, and imagine the extreme situations that could arise from that thought, both negative and positive.
如果我开始想象我父亲终将死去，我的眼睛会湿润。一团能量在胸口辐射开来。情绪能量。一股强大的张力累积，准备好被引向并释放到某个目标上。除了我与父母共有的那数千段经历，这里并没有一个特定的故事。任何人都能挖进自己过往的经验，在内在生成一个强效的能量源，并通过行动把那能量聚焦到一个内在的目标层级上。这就是自律且成功者的秘密。自律，是“成为自己最高版本的渴望”压过“对廉价快感的渴望”。当我卡住时，我会去散步。在那次散步中，我允许念头触发念头，然后我会试着把它们解构成更小的部分。当某个念头比下一个更抓住我的注意力时，我会与它同坐、质疑它，并想象由那个念头可能引发的极端情境——负面的和正面的。
p.117
When a thought of my father pops into my head I ask, "Have I called him enough? He's getting older, Dan, you know that. Have you spent enough time with him? Would he be proud of what you've accomplished? Or does this all even matter? What about Mom? Would she appreciate a spontaneous trip to her favorite spot? Do I have the time for that? Why is this all about time? Is my work taking away or adding to what I can give back to the parents that spent eighteen years of their lives raising me? I should call them."
当一个关于我父亲的念头蹦进脑子，我会问：“我给他打电话够多吗？他在变老，丹，你知道的。你陪他的时间够吗？他会为你所成就的感到骄傲吗？还是这一切根本不重要？那妈妈呢？她会喜欢一趟去她最爱的地方的即兴之旅吗？我有那个时间吗？为什么一切都跟时间有关？我的工作是在剥夺、还是在增加我能够回报给那两个花了十八年养我的父母的东西？我该给他们打电话。”
p.118
From that paragraph, I gain a mixture of anger, sadness, ambition, and love circulating from my belly to chest to head. It feels terribly good, and boy am I ready to take on any challenge that gets in the way of the best future I can create for myself, loved ones, and those that come in contact with me. You've experienced this same phenomenon. Think back to the last enjoyable vacation you went on. How did the sun feel on your skin? Did the trees, beaches, or mountains leave you in awe? And the place you stayed the night, did it give you inspiration for your future home?
从那一段落里，我获得一种混合了愤怒、悲伤、雄心和爱的感受，从我的腹部循环到胸口到头部。它感觉极其好，而我简直等不及要接下任何挡在“我能为自己、所爱之人、以及与我有接触之人所创造的最好未来”路上的挑战。你体验过同样的现象。回想你最近一次愉快的度假。阳光照在皮肤上是什么感觉？树木、海滩或山峦是否让你惊叹？而你过夜的那个地方，是否给了你未来家的灵感？
p.118
When you were a child, what was something that you absolutely hated? That thing you felt forced to do. That thing you never want to do again. Pull the feelings associated with that experience into the now.
你小时候，有什么东西是你绝对讨厌的？那种你觉得被迫去做的事。那种你再也不想做的事。把那种体验带来的感受拉到当下。
p.118
If you want to get ahead of the majority of the population, here's a good exercise. Keep a notebook or journal handy. You'll be encouraged to use it throughout the rest of this book.
如果你想走在多数人前面，这里有个好练习。准备好一个笔记本或日记。在本书余下的部分里，你会被鼓励去用它。
p.118
First, become brutally aware of 2 things: (1) What you don't want. (2) Where you will end up if you keep doing what you've been doing. Observe the masses and see where mindless action leads. It's not pretty.
首先，残酷地觉察两件事：（1）你不想要什么。（2）如果你继续做你一直在做的事，你最终会在哪里。观察大众，看看无脑行动引向何处。它并不好看。
p.118
When I reflect on my past, this alone brought clarity to my future. Like collecting the puzzle pieces that I didn't see when the situation first passed. I love my parents, and they taught me incredible lessons, but nobody is perfect. Throughout my childhood, schooling, and religious indoctrination, I made mental note of the future I did not want to live.
当我反思我的过去，仅这一点就为我的未来带来了清晰。就像收集那些在当初处境过去时我没看见的拼图碎片。我爱我的父母，他们教了我不可思议的东西，但没人完美。在我的童年、学校教育与宗教灌输过程中，我在心里记下了我不想过的那种未来。
p.118
It's easier to know what you don't want - from experience - than it is to know what you want - from imagination. But realize that imagination holds a lot of power. You need experience to fuel imagination. And when the 2 are combined, you create a frame that is impossible to distract your focus. Create an anti-vision for your future. Write out every single thing you don't want, why you don't want it, and how you are going to avoid it. Throughout this process, you won't get immediate answers. Being conscious of your
从经验出发知道“你不想要什么”，比从想象出发知道“你想要什么”更容易。但要意识到，想象力握有巨大的力量。你需要经验来给想象供能。当两者结合，你就创造出一个无法被分心的框架。为你的未来创造一个反愿景。把每一件你不想要的事写出来、为什么你不想要它、以及你将如何避开它。在这个过程中，你不会立刻得到答案。对自身错误的觉察，
p.119
mistakes will serve as your light in the dark. It may take weeks, months, or years to get answers to your burning internal questions. This is natural. How do we understand what we don't want? Through a series of questions. I cannot create or answer these for you. Let these serve as a starting point. A spark to the fire. A thought that triggers further reflection. What does an unfulfilling day look like to you? What kind of person would you avoid as a significant other? How do you not want to look, feel, and act? How much money is too little to sustain your lifestyle? Why is it too little? What won't you be able to do with that money? What environment would you hate living in? Why?
将成为你在黑暗中的光。回答你内心那些炽热的问题，可能需要数周、数月或数年。这很自然。我们如何理解我们不想要什么？通过一连串问题。我无法替你创造或回答这些问题。让它们充当一个起点。一粒点燃火焰的火花。一个触发进一步反思的念头。对你来说，一个没有成就感的日子是什么样的？什么样的人你会避开、不当作伴侣？你不想自己看起来、感觉、表现得如何？多少钱对你维持生活方式来说太少了？为什么太少？用那笔钱你将无法做什么？你会讨厌住在什么样的环境里？为什么？
p.119
Get meticulous here. Spend some time with your thoughts. If questions keep coming up, don't stop. And when you feel thoroughly uncomfortable, transmute that negative energy toward the opposite. Flip to a new page, refer back to the questions above, and write out what you think you want in your future. From your anti-vision, create a vision in which you can dance between the 2 to make better decisions daily.
在这里要细致。花点时间与你的想法共处。如果问题不断冒出来，别停。而当你感到彻底不舒服时，把那股负能量转化到它的反面。翻到新的一页，回到上面那些问题，写下你认为你在未来想要什么。从你的反愿景，创造一个愿景，让你能在两者之间起舞，从而每天做出更好的决定。
p.119
The highest-paid individuals are the visionaries, strategists, and creative problem solvers of the world. Your vision is greater than yourself. It gives you a soft direction to focus the goals and actions that stem from it. Your vision should be big, not limited by belief, and emotionally compelling when you marinate your mind in the growing detail.
收入最高的人，是这个世界上的愿景者、战略家和创造性问题解决者。你的愿景大于你自己。它给你一个柔和的方向，用来聚焦由它衍生出的目标和行动。你的愿景应当宏大，不被信念限制，并且当你让心智在那不断生长的细节中浸润时，它能从情绪上打动你。
p.119
Your vision is your gift. Not a fancy machines on wheels, vacations, or the amount of money made from that vision. When you are walking down a busy street, it will show in your strut. When you are alone with yourself, you will feel at ease. When you are in the market for a potential partner, they will sense your dedication.
你的愿景是你的天赋。不是炫酷的车、假期，或那个愿景带来的金钱数额。当你走在繁忙街头，它会在你的步态中显现。当你独处时，你会感到自在。当你在物色一个潜在伴侣时，对方会感觉到你的投入。
p.119
A clear vision is an eternal source of energy when consistently refined through self-reflection and conscious decision-making. Through the art of focus, you can tap into this intrinsic motivation at any time. Come back to your writing at least once a month to revise and remove limits on your potential that you had not seen before.
一个清晰的愿景，是一个永恒的能量源——只要你持续通过自省和有意识的决策去精炼它。通过专注这门艺术，你可以在任何时候动用这份内在动机。至少每月回到你的文字一次，去修订、并移除那些你之前没看见的、对你潜能的限制。
PURPOSE PATH PRIORITY
目的 · 路径 · 优先级
p.120
p.120
The foundation of human behavior is purpose-oriented problem solving, and if you don't find a purpose with meaningful problems to solve, you will be assigned a purpose with mindless problems to solve. If you do not choose meaning, you will be assigned the opposite, because life demands movement even if you want to stand still and let it pass you by.
人类行为的地基，是目的导向的问题解决。如果你不找到一个有有意义问题可解的目的，你就会被指派一个有无脑问题可解的目的。如果你不选择意义，你就会被指派它的反面——因为生活要求移动，即便你想原地不动、让它从你身边溜过。
p.120
Purpose is elusive. New-age teachers seem to do a great job at telling people to live with purpose but fail to explain it in a coherent fashion. A purpose is a meaningful goal. From that goal stems a problem that you must focus your attention on solving through education, action, and whatever allows you to move toward the goal.
目的是难以捉摸的。新纪元老师们似乎很擅长告诉人们“要带着目的生活”，却没能以连贯的方式解释它。一个目的，就是一个有意义的目标。从那个目标衍生出一个问题，你必须通过教育、行动，以及任何让你朝目标移动的东西，把注意力聚焦到解决它上面。
p.120
Your purpose is the most pressing problem in your life at this very moment. The one that you have been putting off addressing. The one that you have not contemplated to realize the havoc it wreaks on your potential by preventing you from acting on a deeper purpose. Your life's purpose is the big problem you want to solve in the world, but most people don't have the personal, professional, or social development to pursue that. Purpose evolves from superficial to metaphysical and you cannot skip steps. If you attempt to skip steps, you may see progress, but you will be out of touch with reality until you are forced to snap back and solve the low-level problems preventing you from pushing further.
你的目的，就是此刻你生活中最紧迫的问题。那个你一直拖着不去处理的问题。那个你还没沉思过、因此还没意识到它通过阻止你去行动在一个更深的目的上，对你的潜能造成了多大破坏的问题。你的人生目的，是你在世界上想解决的那个大问题，但大多数人没有那份个人、职业或社交发展去追求它。目的从表层演化到形而上，而你不能跳过阶梯。如果你试图跳过，你也许能看到进步，但你会在现实之外，直到你被迫猛地弹回来，去解决那些阻止你走得更远的低层级问题。
p.120
To open up room for curiosity, creativity, and consciousness, you must master your survival. That is, you must create a hierarchy of goals, solve the problems along the path, and prioritize where you focus your finite mental energy. Realize that mastery is a process. We never escape survival, but we create systems that are efficient enough to maintain a baseline level of stress while staying vigilant of becoming overly robotic.
要为好奇心、创造力和意识打开空间，你必须精通你的生存。也就是说，你必须创造一套目标层级、解决沿路的问题、并优先安排你把自己有限的心智能量投到哪里。要意识到精通是一个过程。我们永远无法逃脱生存，但我们会创造出足够高效的系统，来维持一个基线水平的压力，同时保持警觉，不让自己变得过于机器人化。
p.120
Before you go off to solve big problems in the world, you must solve the big problems in your life. How else are you going to act with authenticity? If you haven't met your basic needs, like having enough money to live stress free in that domain, you will always need something from someone
在你出去解决世界上的大问题之前，你必须解决你生活中的大问题。不然你怎么以本真行事？如果你还没满足基本需求，比如在那个领域有足够的钱无忧生活，你将永远需要从别人那里
p.121
else. And yes, unless you plan to live off the grid and fend for yourself, money is a basic need in the current world. It is close to impossible to act with authenticity when your actions are influenced by need of something outside of yourself.
得到什么。而没错，除非你打算离网自给自足，金钱就是当下世界的一项基本需求。当你的行动受“对外部某物的需要”影响时，以本真行事几乎不可能。
p.121
With time, you will realize that selfishness and selflessness are 2 polar ends. They cannot be separated like oil and water. They are constantly mixing according to the situation at hand. People have been conditioned to think that selflessness in and of itself is the highest good. In reality, conscious selfishness will always come full circle into selflessness. From the highest perspective of the Universe, you and other are not separate. You are One. And through self-actualization, you benefit the world more than the person that gives, gives, gives out of the unconscious selfishness disguised as absolute selflessness.
随时间你会意识到，自私与无私是两个极端。它们不能像油和水那样被分开。它们根据眼前处境不断混合。人们被条件化去认为：无私本身就是最高的善。现实中，有意识的自私总是会完整地绕回无私。从宇宙的最高视角看，你与他者并非分离。你们是一。而通过自我实现，你给世界带来的益处，多于那个出于“伪装成绝对无私的无意识自私”而付出、付出、再付出的人。
p.121
If you haven't developed yourself in any capacity, your current purpose, and the ones following, will increase in meaning as you solve your own problems. Start with what's right in front of you. Are you overweight and sluggish? Do you hate your job? Are you dealing with relationship issues? Is your mind a storm of negative thoughts and emotions? You must confront what's causing the most pain in your life, dance with that pain, and create a plan to solve the problem. When you solve that problem, not only will you build momentum into the next, but your other problems will become easier to solve. This is not a linear process. Your problems are a tight-knit web that bind you to your current situation. Problems don't exist on their own. Life is hierarchical, and there are 2 types of hierarchies. The first is a dominator hierarchy. This is what gives the term a bad reputation.
如果你在任何方向上都没有发展自己，那你当前的目的、以及随后的那些，都会随着你解决自己的问题而变得更有意义。从眼前的东西开始。你超重且迟钝吗？你讨厌你的工作吗？你正在处理关系问题吗？你的心智是一场负面念头和情绪的风暴吗？你必须面对你生活中造成最多痛苦的东西、与那份痛苦共舞、并创造一个解决该问题的计划。当你解决了那个问题，你不仅会为下一个积累动量，你其他的问题也会变得更容易解决。这不是一个线性过程。你的问题是一张紧密编织的网，把你绑在你当前的处境上。问题并不独立存在。生活是层级性的，而有两种层级。第一种是支配型层级。正是它让“层级”这个词名声不好。
p.121
Dominator hierarchies reflect in nature. The alpha ape is at the top of the pyramid. He has his pick of women, food, and other resources.
支配型层级映照在自然中。那只 alpha 猿处在金字塔顶端。他可以随意挑选女人、食物和其他资源。
p.121
The wisdom of nature reflects in mental constructs like society, most prevalent in corporate jobs. There are fewer people with more power at the top, and fewer people with more power at the bottom. You can try to climb the ranks with your conditioned beliefs of "hard work" and doing what you're told, but the probability of reaching the top is miniscule. You must
自然的智慧映照在社会之类的智性构造中，在公司工作中最为普遍。顶端是更少的人拥有更大的权力，底端是更少的人拥有更大的权力（译注：原文如此，指底端人多而权力小）。你可以试着用你那套被条件化的“努力工作”信念、以及照吩咐做事去往上爬，但到达顶端的概率微乎其微。你必须
p.122
develop and earn with the creative ability of your mind. That is how you create your own hierarchy, or game, within the system itself.
用你心智的创造能力去发展并赚取。这就是你如何在这个系统内部创造你自己的层级，或游戏。
p.122
The common trait of dominator hierarchies is that they are not natural. They are characterized by a pathological unit of that hierarchy attempting to dominate the rest. Like a cancer cell attempting to replicate within the body. These hierarchies eventually self-destruct unless the pathological unit is healed or reintegrated into the natural hierarchy.
支配型层级的共同特征是：它们不是自然的。它们的特征是该层级中某个病态单元试图支配其余部分。就像一个癌细胞试图在体内复制。这些层级最终会自我毁灭——除非那个病态单元被治愈，或被重新整合进自然层级。
p.122
The second type of hierarchy is a natural or actualization hierarchy. Best illustrated through creative emergence that transcends and includes its parts after a period of struggle, conflict, or pain. Like matter to plants to animals to humans. Or an atom to molecule to cell to organism. Or word to sentence to paragraph to book.
第二类层级，是自然的、或实现型层级。它最好通过“在一段挣扎、冲突或痛苦之后，超越并包含其组成部分的创造性涌现”来说明。就像物质→植物→动物→人类。或者原子→分子→细胞→有机体。或字→句→段→书。
p.122
Natural hierarchies continue to push toward evolution through emergence and inclusion. If the parts within the emergent whole are forgotten or destroyed, the whole ceases to exist. We can think of this under the lens of the fundamental hierarchy: physical to biological to mental to spiritual. If we do not care for the ecology or environment that we evolved from, we are literally committing suicide, as it is impossible for humans to exist without the inclusion of biology beyond the vessel that we call our body. By harming the biological or physical, we are harming ourselves. And by not seeking to connect with the spiritual, something greater than ourselves, we are preventing our personal to collective evolution.
自然层级通过涌现与包含，不断朝演化推进。如果涌现出来的整体之内的那些部分被遗忘或被摧毁，整体就停止存在。我们可以在“基础层级”这面透镜下思考它：物理→生物→心智→精神。如果我们不照料那个我们从其中演化而来的生态或环境，我们实际上就是在自杀——因为如果不去包含我们称之为身体的那个容器之外的生物界，人类就不可能存在。伤害生物界或物理界，就是伤害我们自己。而如果不寻求与精神（某种大于我们自身之物）连接，我们就是在阻止我们从个人到集体的演化。
p.122
Life is a process of self-reflection and problem-solving in a way that makes survival meaningful by increasing your level of mind to solve better problems. So, we must use our purpose to create an actualization hierarchy from the top down. We must pursue a purpose while integrating the aspects of our past - both positive and negative - that create the character we use to navigate the subjective world. And if we don't, or we attempt destroy that part of our past, the ramifications can be deadly.
生活是一个自省与问题解决的过程，而它的方式是：通过提升你的心智层级去解决更好的问题，来让生存变得有意义。所以，我们必须用我们的目的，自上而下地创造一个实现型层级。我们必须在追求一个目的的同时，整合我们过往中那些——正面的和负面的——构成我们用来导航这个主观世界之人格的部分。而如果我们不这么做，或试图摧毁我们过往的那一部分，后果可以是致命的。
p.122
The path of mastery that will help you achieve your purpose is a series of goals that create clarity, frame your attention, and repel distractions. If your
那条会帮你实现目的的精通之路，是一连串能创造清晰、框定注意力、并驱散干扰的目标。如果你的目的是改善身体，就创造一个你能挂到未来愿景上的宏大总目标。
p.123
purpose is to improve your body, create a big overarching goal that you can tack on to your vision for the future. Get detailed, specific, and reasonable as to how it will impact your life in more areas than health. How will that one lifestyle puzzle piece ripple throughout your life, your family's lives, and the lives of your community, customers, and anyone that comes into contact with you?
就它将如何在健康之外的更多领域影响你的生活，写得细致、具体、合理。那一块生活方式拼图，将如何在你的整个人生、你家人的人生、以及你的社群、客户和任何与你接触之人的人生中激起涟漪？
p.123
With the notebook you pulled out earlier, break this big goal, or purpose, into a clear path to gain clarity on your priority actions. The more detailed you are, the better. Spend time writing out yearly, monthly, weekly, and daily goals that will actualize the accompanying purpose. Don't get caught in the technicalities of goal setting. Be specific, be actionable, be vain if you want to. Your purpose will evolve as all things do, and when it does, set aside time to repeat this clarity generation process.
拿出你之前抽出的笔记本，把这个大目标或目的，拆成一条清晰的路径，以获得对优先行动的清晰。你写得越细越好。花时间写出年度、月度、周度和每日目标，它们将把相配套的目的变为现实。别被困在目标设定的技术细节里。要具体、要可行动，如果你想的话，可以“虚荣”一点。你的目的会像万物一样演化，而它演化时，就留出时间来重复这个“创造清晰”的过程。
p.123
Now that you've set a big, deconstructed goal for one domain of your life, we want to set a few more to help bring clarity to your vision for the future. Health, wealth, relationships, and happiness are the 4 domains that allow you to master your survival. Create a big goal for each to bring added brush strokes to the painting of your future. You don't have to act on these immediately, because that may overwhelm you, but they are useful for broadening your perspective. From that perspective, you can challenge yourself on the mental plane to open your mind in each situation to view problems from the lens of your higher self. As you begin to go about your days, hold your purpose and written path in your mind. When a choice must be made, put effort into making the one that aligns with your vision. By investing mental energy in your goals, you will begin to forge the system that will carry you to success.
既然你已经为生活的一个领域设定了一个宏大的、被拆解过的目标，我们想再设定几个，来帮你把未来愿景弄得更清晰。健康、财富、关系与幸福，是让你精通自身生存的四大领域。为每一个都创造一个宏大目标，为你未来的那幅画添上更多笔触。你不必立刻对它们动手，因为那可能会把你压垮，但它们有助于拓宽你的视角。从那个视角出发，你可以在心智层面上挑战自己，在每个处境中打开心智，从更高自我的透镜去看问题。当你开始过日子，把目的和已写下的路径放在心里。当一个选择必须做出时，努力去做那个与你愿景一致的选择。通过把心智能量投入你的目标，你将开始锻造那个载你走向成功的系统。
p.123
If this sounds too time consuming or difficult, I would ask you to question the distraction attempting to penetrate your mind at this moment. Nothing is more important than your potential. Not your phone, not the TV, not anything that is begging to stimulate your brain's reward system right now. The purpose, path, and priority framework is Universally applicable to your life, human behavior, and social dynamics like business, dating, and
如果这听起来太耗时或太难，我会请你质问此刻正试图钻进你心智的那个干扰。没有任何东西比你的潜能更重要。不是你的手机，不是电视，也不是此刻任何正乞求刺激你大脑奖赏系统的东西。目的、路径、优先级这套框架，普遍适用于你的生活、人类行为，以及商业、约会、
p.124
communication. In any situation, you either set or remind yourself of a meaningful goal to broaden your own or find a shared perspective with others. From that perspective, you can solve problems for profit, love, communication, and other forms of conscious personal and mutual benefit. We will discuss the application of this framework in business in later chapters.
沟通这样的社会动力学。在任何处境中，你要么设定一个有意义的目标来拓宽自己的视角，要么提醒自己它本来是什么，或者与别人找到一个共同视角。从那个视角出发，你可以为解决“利润、爱、沟通”等问题以及其他形式的、有意识的个人与相互利益去解决问题。我们会在后面几章讨论这套框架在商业中的应用。
p.124
When a goal is made conscious, an intention is set, and you are able to perceive that situation from the lens of that goal. Like how a healthy individual is able to say "no" to a tempting dessert, because the survival of their identity depends on that situation. The potential death of who they are is more important than a 10-second indulgence in a treat.
当一个目标被变得有意识，一个意图就被设定了，你就能从那个目标的透镜去感知该处境。就像一个健康的人能对一份诱人的甜点说“不”，因为他们身份的存活依赖那个处境。他们“所是”的潜在死亡，比一次 10 秒钟的甜点沉溺更重要。
p.124
When you pour mental energy into a meaningful goal, you feel obligated to achieve it; otherwise, it is a wasted investment. In terms of finding passion for your work, that comes after a specific amount of energy is invested into your work. Progress is a better metric to focus on, as that is how anyone can create enjoyment in the pursuit of a better life.
当把心智能量倾注进一个有意义的目标，你会感到有义务去达成它；否则，它就是一笔被浪费的投资。至于对工作找到热情，那是在特定数量的能量被投入到你的工作之后才来的。进步是一个更好的焦点指标，因为任何人都能通过它在追求更好生活的路上创造出享受。
p.124
If your purpose is to write a book, you will perceive life situations through that lens. You will interpret what you read, see, or hear in a way that allows you to notice information that will aid in the survival or creation of the book.
如果你的目的是写一本书，你就会透过那个透镜去感知生活处境。你会以一种让你注意到达成该书存活或创造所需信息的方式，去解读你读到、看到或听到的东西。
p.124
You can read any book, regardless of topic, through the lens of your current purpose and receive insight that will aid you on the path. You will not be interpreting the information as literal, because paragraphs, sentences, and choice of words will be noticed over the educational material of the book itself. If your goal is to learn the material from the book, then you will survive that goal by reading through that lens.
你可以用你当前目的的透镜去读任何书——不论主题——并获得能在这条路上帮到你的洞见。你不会把那些信息解读为字面的，因为相比于书本身的教育材料，段、句和用词的选择更会被你注意到。如果你的目标是从书中学习那些材料，那你就要透过那个透镜去阅读，以让那个目标存活。
p.124
In 2 years from now, you can return to that book, and it will hold an entirely different meaning because your goals have changed. Perceiving situations through the lens of a meaningful goal makes life meaningful. You can attach different purpose-based perspectives to unveil the details of life that would have normally gone unnoticed.
从现在起两年后，你可以回到那本书，而它将持有一种完全不同的意义，因为你的目标变了。透过一个有意义目标的透镜去感知处境，让生活变得有意义。你可以依附不同的、以目的为基础的视角，去把那些本该被忽略的生活细节揭示出来。
p.125
With time, our goal is to acquire as much perspective as we can, broadening ours to that of the Universe to realize that All is One. When accomplished, the technical details of your life that cause you stress would wash away and lose their impact. Instead, you would see them through an enlightened lens. The rippled design of a summer leaf will bring a smile to your face. For now, adopt the perspective of your ideal self. Set big goals for every domain of your life, allow experience to culminate into potent vision, and perceive daily situations through the lens of the meaningful goals that form the foundation of your perspective.
随时间推移，我们的目标是尽可能多地获取视角，把我们的视角拓宽到宇宙的视角，去意识到“万有归一”。当这实现时，那些让你压力重重的生活技术细节会冲刷而去、失去影响。相反，你会透过一双开悟的眼睛看它们。夏日叶片上那涟漪状的纹理会让你脸上泛起微笑。而现在，先采纳你理想自我的视角。为你生活的每个领域设定大目标，让经验汇聚成强有力的愿景，并透过那些构成你视角基础的有意义目标的透镜，去感知每日处境。
p.125
We will discuss the process of clarity in future chapters, but this simplifies the process fairly well: If you're lost, the answer is education. If you're educated, the answer is execution. If you're executing, the answer is consistency. Even if it doesn't seem like it, there's always a next step forward.
我们会在后面几章讨论获得清晰的过程，但这已相当好地简化了它：如果你迷失了，答案是教育。如果你受过教育了，答案是执行。如果你在执行了，答案是一致性。即便看起来不像，前路总有一个下一步。
p.125
Your priority actions to actualize your goals are ones that get results. The "lead domino," if you will. The levers that pull you toward your desired outcome regardless of the amount of time they take to perform. If you have financial problems but can't start a business due to having too many responsibilities, then don't start a business. Face reality and experiment with a budgeting technique, increasing your professional development through skill acquisition, and potentially searching for a new job. Once the lead domino is knocked over and momentum is built, you can begin working on your dream of starting a business.
你用来实现目标的优先行动，是那些能带来结果的行动。那第一张多米诺骨牌，如果你愿意这么说。那些不管花多少时间、都会把你拉向理想结果的杠杆。如果你有财务问题，却因责任太多而无法创业，那就先别创业。面对现实，去试验一种预算技术、通过技能习得提升你的职业发展，并可能去找一份新工作。一旦第一张骨牌被推倒、动量被建立起来，你就可以开始动手实现你“创办一门生意”的梦想了。
p.125
This is how your life system is created, maintained, and improved. Systems have a desired outcome, a process that results in that outcome, and inputs that meet the demands of the process. As your purpose evolves, the layer of systems that allow you to evolve become more complex. Meaning your character becomes more complex. You acquire the skill necessary to take on higher challenges.
你的生活系统就是这样被创造、维护和改进的。系统有一个理想结果、一个导致那个结果的过程，以及能满足那过程要求的输入。随着你的目的演化，那些让你得以演化的系统层级变得更加复杂。也就是说，你的人格变得更复杂。你获得接下更高挑战所必需的技能。
p.125
If you lack clarity along the path, realize that obstacles don't prevent clarity. Creating a lesser goal that matches your current skill level can absolve all doubt in your ability to act toward your future. When you feel
如果你在路上缺乏清晰，要意识到障碍并不妨碍清晰。创造一个与你当前技能水平相匹配的小目标，能消解你对自己“能否朝未来行动”的一切怀疑。当你感到
p.126
overwhelmed, lost, or anxious, it is usually because you are projecting too far into the future. You don't have the education, skill, or conscious challenge to bridge the gap between you and it.
不堪重负、迷失或焦虑，通常是因为你把自己投射到未来太远了。你没有足够的教育、技能或有意识的挑战，去搭起你与那个未来之间的桥。
p.126
When faced with any decision, use your plan as a filter and adapt it as necessary. Perceive every situation in a way that allows you to act in alignment with your purpose. And if you can't make a choice, the answer is no, which often means doing nothing to let the fabricated problem blow over.
面对任何决定时，用你的计划当过滤器，并按需调整它。以让你能与目的保持一致行动的方式去感知每个处境。而如果你做不出选择，答案就是“不”——这往往意味着什么都别做，让那个被虚构出来的问题自己消散。
THE EDGE OF THE KNOWN
已知的边缘
p.126
p.126
Even if you choose to do nothing with your life, you will be forced to move. You will adopt the goals of others through evolutionary imitation, play status games to achieve them, and get trapped in a level of the social hierarchy that leads to surface-level living.
即便你选择什么都不做，你也会被迫移动。你会通过演化性的模仿去采纳别人的目标、玩地位游戏去达成它们，并被困在社会层级的某一层里，引向表层生活。
p.126
Psychological time poses one of the greatest threats to the human experience, because humans are the only ones that can experience it. Psychological time is illustrated by our desire to live in the past or future in a way that does not help us but harms us. Animals seem to live in the eternal present moment. They may learn from the past for the sake of their survival, but you would not see a dog stressing at night because they have to go on a walk the next day. You will only see them stress when the source of that stress is a part of the present.
心理时间对人类经验构成最大的威胁之一，因为人类是唯一能体验它的物种。心理时间表现为：我们渴望以一种不帮我们、反而伤我们的方式生活在过去或未来里。动物似乎活在永恒的当下。它们或许会为生存而从过去学习，但你不会看到一条狗因为明天必须去散步而在夜里焦虑。你只会看到它在压力源成为当下的一部分时才焦虑。
p.126
We've discussed how we do not want to regress into our animalistic nature and instead pursue something beyond our self, but that does not mean we can't learn from animals and integrate their useful parts. You can observe a dog, child, or other being that doesn't have years of mental programming under their belt and pull some profound insights from their actions. Like how a puppy is fascinated by fresh grass while we glance over it because we already think we know what it is.
我们讨论过我们不想退化回动物本性，而要去追求某种超出自身之物；但这并不意味着我们不能向动物学习、并整合它们有用的部分。你可以观察一条狗、一个孩子，或其他没有背负数年心理编程的存在，从它们的行动中抽出一些深刻的洞见。就像一只小狗被鲜草迷住，而我们只是扫一眼，因为我们已经以为自己知道那是什么。
p.127
As humans, we reminisce on a familiar past, something we have experienced before, and allow thoughts of that point in time to flood our mind. Those thoughts pull your past experience into the present. You feel what it was like to be in that time. As you can visualize a positive potential future that leads to a great feeling, you can do the same from a negative past. As you repeat these thoughts, emotions, and experiences, this pattern is conditioned into your mind and becomes automatic. Mental habits are dangerous when executed without intention, purpose, or conscious thought. By reminiscing on a negative past without transmutation of those feelings toward a potential future, you remain as your past self. We live out the same negative experiences over and over again. We literally don't change. We feel the same, do the same, and are the same day after day as our body ages with the physical world.
作为人类，我们会追忆一段熟悉的过去、一件我们以前经历过的事，并允许关于那个时间点的念头淹没心智。那些念头把你过去的经验拉进当下。你感受到身处那个时代是什么感觉。既然你能把一个引向美妙感受的、正面的潜在未来视觉化，你也能对一个负面的过去做同样的事。随着你重复这些念头、情绪和体验，这个模式被条件化进你的心智并变得自动化。当心智习惯在没有意图、目的或有意识的想法下被执行时，它们是危险的。通过追忆一段负面过去而不用那些感受去炼化成潜在未来，你就仍然停留在过去的自己里。我们把同样的负面体验一遍又一遍地活出来。我们真的一成不变。我们感觉一样、做一样、日复一日地是同一个自己，而身体随物理世界一起变老。
p.127
The same thing happens when projecting into the predictable future based on your past experiences. Again, you feel that experience in the present. You think you know what has happened and what will happen and that locks your mind in a world of its own creation. Your destiny is decided. Most people wake up in the morning, project into a stressful future, and by doing so they wake up as the past version of themselves. There is a habit of thinking about the same old stressful task at work, saying "hello" to the coworker you despise, and coming home to a spouse that is going to start an argument. Rather than setting a new conscious goal to change the day's outcome, we psych ourselves into having yet another bad day.
当你基于过去经验投射到那个可预测的未来时，同样的事也会发生。再次地，你在当下感受到了那份经验。你以为自己知道已经发生了什么、将会发生什么，而这把你的心智锁在了一个它自造的世界里。你的命运已被决定。大多数人在早晨醒来，投射进一个压力重重的未来，而通过这么做，他们以过去版本的那个自己醒来。有一种习惯：想着工作上同样的老压力任务、跟那个你讨厌的同事说“你好”、然后回家面对一个即将挑起争吵的配偶。与其设定一个新的有意识目标去改变这一天的结果，我们给自己做心理建设，去过又一个糟糕的日子。
p.127
The only way to break the surface-level living cycle and change who you are is to become an explorer of the unknown. You must think new thoughts, set new goals, learn new skills, have new ideas, and execute on those ideas to build yourself out of the hole you were born and raised in. Your psyche demands novelty for progress, but most people get theirs from the endless sources of instant cheap pleasures. Exploring the unknown is how you live in accordance with nature.
打破表层生活循环、改变自己“是谁”的唯一方式，是成为一个未知的探索者。你必须想新的念头、设新的目标、学新的技能、有新的想法，并在那些想法上执行，把自己从你出生并长大的那个洞里建出来。你的心灵要求新奇才能进步，但大多数人从那些无限的即时廉价快感源里获取新奇。探索未知，就是你如何与自然保持一致地生活。
p.128
Most people are a walking contradiction, but not in the way that makes one interesting. They pursue the safe, certain, and secure route in life on autopilot. Big aspirations but low risk tolerance. What they don't realize is that the default path presents the greatest risk of them all: staying the same just like everyone else.
大多数人是一个行走的矛盾体，但不是那种让人显得有趣的方式。他们在自动驾驶模式下追求安全、确定、有保障的人生路线。宏大的抱负，却极低的风险容忍度。他们没意识到的是，那条默认路径呈现着所有人中最大的风险：像其他所有人一样，保持不变。
p.128
There is an extreme method for sparking change, but it is only for a select few. I call it "tactical stress." The conscious decision to put yourself in a door-die situation, knowing that you have the skill to make it work, and will accept nothing less than success.
有一种能激发变化的极端方法，但它只适用于少数被选中的人。我把它叫做“战术性压力”。有意识地把自己放进一个“不成功便成仁”的处境，同时知道自己有技能让它成，并且除了成功什么都不接受。
p.128
Pull an all-nighter. Sign up for a marathon. Book a flight across the globe. Move to a location that demands 3 times more than what you can afford, so you are forced to make your business work. Ask the client for double your normal rates. Do the thing that other people will think you are crazy for doing, because that's how you make leaps of meaningful progress. This is how you create a glitch in the matrix and have reality deliver you a slew of novel insight.
熬一个通宵。报名一场马拉松。订一张飞越全球的机票。搬到一个需要你收入三倍才有资格的地方，好迫使你把生意做起来。向客户要平时两倍的价。去做那件别人会觉得你疯了的事，因为那正是你做出有意义飞跃的方式。这就是你如何在矩阵里制造一个故障（glitch），让现实给你送来一连串新奇洞见。
p.128
That is one option, and I do not recommend doing it often. It is a good way to shock you out of the life you've grown too comfortable living. Beyond that, we want to aim for slow, consistent progress that increases our surface area for exponential growth.
那是一个选项，但我不建议经常这么做。它是把你从那种你已过得太舒服的生活里震出来的好办法。除此之外，我们想要瞄准缓慢、一致的进步，从而增加我们的表面积以实现指数级增长。
p.128
I want you to picture a map in a video game. When you start playing, the only thing you can see on the map is the location you are currently in. As you follow the questline, new locations show on the map, but most of them remain dark. The places you've traveled are the known, and the areas you cannot see are the unknown. By following the storyline you are told, and by never pursuing your curiosity, you imprison yourself to a life of everdecreasing meaning. There are areas to explore outside of the default storyline you have been assigned. The good life is for those that take the first, second, and third step beyond what they know.
我想让你想象一张电子游戏里的地图。你开始玩时，地图上你唯一能看见的就是你当前所在的位置。当你沿着任务线走，新的地点在地图上显示出来，但大多数仍是一片漆黑。你去过的地方是已知，你看不到的区域是未知。通过遵循被交代的故事线、且从不追求你的好奇心，你把自己囚禁在一种意义不断衰减的生活里。在你被分配的那条默认故事线之外，还有区域可以探索。好生活属于那些迈出第一步、第二步、第三步、走出他们所知之外的人。
p.128
Now, let's think of the unknown as a big dark room. Your vision, albeit unclear at first, will bring a dim light to the room that gets brighter as you
现在，让我们把未知想成一间巨大的暗房。你的视力起初虽然不清楚，但会给房间带来一点微光，而随着你
p.129
gain experience. You are in one corner of the room and you can see your purpose, a candlelight off in the distance. Your hierarchy of goals, or plan, is a line of candles that increase in brightness from your purpose to you. The closeness of the candle signifies the level of challenge you have the skill to take on because you can see the surrounding area better than the others. If the candle is bright and close, you will not get anxious, but if you stay there for too long, you will get bored. Fulfillment is found at the edge of the known. If we want to sustain fulfilling progress in our lives, we must make tiny compounding improvements toward our vision.
积累经验，它会越来越亮。你在房间的一个角落里，能看到你的目的——远处的一点烛光。你的目标层级，也就是计划，是一串从你的目的延伸到你这里、亮度递增的蜡烛。蜡烛的远近，标示出你有技能去接下那个挑战的层级，因为你能比看别处更清楚地看见周围区域。如果那根蜡烛既亮又近，你不会焦虑，但如果你在那儿待太久，你会无聊。圆满是在已知的边缘被找到的。如果我们想在生活中维持带来圆满的进步，我们就必须朝愿景做出微小而复利的改进。
p.129
Bodybuilding is a microcosm of life that serves as a perfect example. When taking the first step to sign up for a gym, most people want to lift as much weight as possible. But trained individuals understand it doesn't work that way. The smallest plates are the most conducive to progress. While the occasional leap in progress can be made, it is wise to add the smallest amount of difficulty to sustain growth over time. When you master a weight, you increase by the smallest increment to not only keep things interesting but prevent you from declining into a chaotic spiral of boredom and pleasure seeking.
健身是生活的一个微缩宇宙，是个完美的例子。当迈出第一步报名健身房时，大多数人想举起尽可能大的重量。但训练有素的人明白事情不是那样运作的。最小的杠铃片最有利于进步。虽然偶尔可以来个进步上的飞跃，但明智的做法是加上最小的难度增量，以维持长期增长。当你精通了某个重量，你就以最小的增量增加，这不仅让事情保持有趣，也防止你退化成无聊与追求快感的混乱漩涡。
p.129
As you dig deeper into the unknown, people will look at you differently. They will say, "You've changed," and your only response should be, "Yes, the tiny improvements are starting to add up."
随着你向未知挖得更深，人们会用不同的眼光看你。他们会说：“你变了。”而你唯一的回答应该是：“是的，那些微小的改进开始累积起来了。”
THE ICEBERG OF OPPORTUNITY
机会的冰山
p.129
p.129
Awareness begets awareness and ideas beget ideas. If you want to become aware of the potential for your future, you won't find it in a mindless lifestyle. Most people lack passion, drive, and general interest in life because they haven't been exposed to the idea that would change it all for them. They aren't aware that a better life exists.
觉察生觉察，想法生想法。如果你想觉察到你未来的潜能，你不会在一种无脑的生活方式里找到它。大多数人缺乏热情、驱动力和对生活的一般兴趣，因为他们从未接触过那个会为他们改变一切的想法。他们没有觉察到一种更好的生活是存在的。
p.129
We discussed how the map in a video game reveals locations based on the ones you've visited. This metaphor helps illustrate the unknown but lacks the true depth of what's going on here.
我们讨论了电子游戏里的地图如何基于你已访问过的地点来揭示新地点。这个隐喻有助于说明未知，但缺少这里真正发生之事的深层。
p.130
Let's play a mind game. Imagine an iceberg. A small tip above water holding one-hundred times its depth underneath. Imagine infinite icebergs, side-by-side, across the X-axis spanning across the Earth. Now imagine infinite icebergs covering the surface of Earth. Down into the core. Up into the sky. Expanding lightyears across the universe in all directions known to man. And this is only the tip of the iceberg that these icebergs reside in. The process repeats. This is the fabric of reality. Infinite, unknown, and connected units of mind calling to be explored.
我们来玩一个脑内游戏。想象一座冰山。水面上一个小小的尖，底下托着一百倍于它的深度。想象无限的冰山，一座接一座，横跨 X 轴铺过整个地球。现在想象无限的冰山覆盖了地球表面。向下直到地核。向上直到天空。朝人类已知的所有方向扩张到许多光年之外。而这仅仅是“这些冰山所栖居的那座冰山”的尖。这个过程不断重复。这就是现实的织物。无限的、未知的、相互连接的心智单元，呼唤着被探索。
p.130
Most people live a surface-level existence. A tree is a tree and its purpose in serving the interconnected ecosystem remains unconscious. Your job is a job and even if you hate it, the thought of a creative income is too uncertain to entertain, and the job you were so excited to start loses its spark in less than a week. They said what they said and if it doesn't fit into your concrete view of reality, you have a mental battle with yourself to justify why you are right and they are absolutely wrong. This isn't a way to live.
大多数人过的是表层存在。树就是树，它在服务那个相互连接的生态系统中的目的仍然是无意识的。你的工作就是一份工作，即便你恨它，“创造性收入”这个念头也太不确定、不容考虑，而你曾那么兴奋开启的这份工作不到一周就失去了火花。他们说了他们所说的话，而如果它嵌不进你那个具体的现实观，你就要和自己打一场心智仗，去论证“你是对的、他们绝对错了”。这不是一种活法。
p.130
Curiosity is the spark that creates potential. The process of turning "what if?" into "aha!" The shift that turns expectations into questions. Curiosity is the trait that reveals itself when you tap into your authentic self, which is nonexistent when dwelling in a state of unconscious conceptual survival. Without this spark of curiosity, possibility and potential do not exist. A new reality cannot be created. It should be considered a crime to deny your potential. In some cases, it is. When you deny your curiosity through numbing activities, it becomes second nature. You start to believe that you "aren't a curious person." There is no such thing as an "uncurious" person. Everyone has a spark that can be lit. But you must tend it, fuel it, and let the fire grow in your belly.
好奇心，是创造潜能的那颗火花。把“如果……会怎样？”变成“啊哈！”的过程。那个把期待转化为问题的转变。好奇心是那种当你触及本真自我时会显现出来的特质——而当你栖居在无意识的概念性生存状态里时，本真自我是不存在的。没有这颗好奇心的火花，可能与潜能就不存在。一个新的现实无法被创造。否定自己的潜能应当被视为一种罪行。在某些情况下，它确实就是。当你通过麻痹性活动去否定自己的好奇心时，它就成了第二天性。你开始相信“自己不是一个好奇的人”。世上没有“不好奇”的人。每个人都有可以点燃的火花。但你必须照料它、给它加燃料，让那团火在你肚子里长大。
p.130
Dopamine is the miracle chemical behind motivation. Both extrinsic and intrinsic. We are searching for the intrinsic, the good and sustainable kind. Extrinsic motivation isn't bad. It is a useful tool, not a master. The feeling of potentially making progress is what allows dopamine levels to increase. It feels good. It makes you want more. It creates a cascade effect that, if you ride it out, can result in a massive experience boost.
多巴胺是动机背后的奇迹化学物质。外在的和内在的都是。我们寻找的是内在的那种，好的、可持续的那种。外在动机并不坏。它是一件有用的工具，不是主人。有可能取得进步的那种感觉，正是让多巴胺水平上升的东西。它感觉很好。它让你想要更多。它创造一种级联效应，你若能顺着它骑下去，就能带来一次巨大的经验值暴涨。
p.131
Through the pursuit of curiosity, you fuel your mind with a potent source of energy. A fuel that you have test driven before but had no idea as to how it got in there. I am here to make you aware of this and give you the focal areas to manipulate these chemicals at will.
通过追求好奇心，你用一股强效的能量源给你的心智加油。一种你以前试驾过、却完全不知道它是怎么进去的燃料。我在这里，就是让你觉察到这一点，并给你一些焦点区域，好让你能随心所欲地操纵这些化学物质。
p.131
Curiosity is the start. Creating the motivation necessary to bring the energy of the future to you right now. This motivation will turn into drive, the sustainable resource, as we dive deeper into the iceberg of our choosing. Of course, you can't pursue everything. You don't want to live your life in the potential future. That would just be mental masturbation. Instead, we want to act in the present. Planting and cultivating seeds of awareness that will birth our ideal future.
好奇心是起点。创造出能把未来的能量在此时拉到你身边的必要动机。随着我们朝自己选定的那座冰山潜得更深，这份动机会变成驱动力——那种可持续的资源。当然，你无法追求一切。你不想把人生活在潜在未来里。那只会是精神自慰。相反，我们想在当下去行动。播下并培育觉察的种子，让它们孕育出我们的理想未来。
p.131
Everything is an iceberg of opportunity. The honey that we dissected in a previous chapter. Your favorite article of clothing. The phone you hold in your hand. The craft coffee, beer, or wine you love. The identity that your friends, family, or spouse have forged. The can of diet soda, its branding, the intention behind its design, how many people drink it, the manufacturing process, the stores that sell it in more than just a can, how it compares to other soda brands, the marketing campaigns that reproduce in minds across the globe, how many fluid ounces are in the can with a certain amount being water ... don't get me started on water. The point is that the interconnectedness of the relative world creates depth and detail that can be used to expand your consciousness through a curious mind.
一切都是机会的冰山。我们在前一章解剖过的那罐蜂蜜。你最爱的那件衣服。你手里握着的手机。你钟爱的精品咖啡、啤酒或红酒。你的朋友、家人或配偶锻造出的那个身份。那罐无糖汽水、它的品牌、它设计背后的意图、有多少人喝它、制造过程、卖它的那些不只卖罐装形式的商店、它与其他汽水品牌相比如何、在全球无数心智中复制的营销战役、罐子里有多少液体盎司、其中多少是水……别让我开始聊水。重点是：相对世界的相互连接性创造出的深度与细节，可以用来通过一颗好奇的心扩展你的意识。
p.131
There are 4 paths you can take to pursue your curiosity further. First, you can appreciate it for what it is. Walk with a mind of gratitude for the facets of the world we live in, be open-minded and awestruck by the depth of the forms that compose your present-moment experience, and let others pursue things without your negative projections, assumptions, and judgments. Second, you can seek to understand it. When you feel the pull to go deeper, don't suppress it. Learning and understanding will always aid in the infinite, interconnected fabric of reality. You can seek to understand many situations, experiences, and units of mind, but your time is limited
你可以在追求好奇心这条路上走得更远的四条路径。第一，你可以欣赏它本来的样子。带着感恩之心行走于我们所处世界的各个面向，对构成你当下体验的那些形式的深度保持开放与惊叹，并让别人去追求他们的事物，不带着你的负面投射、假设和评判。第二，你可以寻求理解它。当你感到那股想更深潜的拉力，不要压制它。学习与理解，总会在现实那张无限、相互连接的织物里帮到你。你可以寻求去理解许多处境、经验和心智单元，但你的时间有限。
p.132
Third, you can master it. Mastery and understanding go hand in hand. When it comes to your life's work, you must seek to understand multiple areas of life, but only a few will stick with you enough to include them on your path. If you become curious about technology, appreciate it, understand it deeply, and fall in love with its depth, and attempt to master it as a modality for your survival.
第三，你可以精通它。精通与理解携手同行。说到你的人生事业，你必须寻求理解生活的多个领域，但只有少数会与你相契到足以被包容在你的路径上。如果你对技术产生好奇，就欣赏它、深入理解它、爱上它的深度，并尝试把它精通为一种用于你生存的模态。
p.132
Fourth, you can monetize it. Anything is monetizable nowadays. Honey, the cup you are holding, the emotions you encounter and how you overcome them, the clothes you are wearing, anything. On the path of mastery, monetization becomes a necessary aspect to sustain your love for what you do. In fact, monetization and business strategies are a part of the depth your craft has to offer. If you truly love what you do, you will truly love the utility that skills like marketing, sales, and self-promotion provide in your ability to pursue it for life.
第四，你可以把它变现。如今什么都能变现。蜂蜜、你手里那个杯子、你遇到的情绪以及你如何克服它们、你穿的衣服，任何东西。在精通之路上，变现成为维持你对所做之事的爱的一个必要面向。事实上，变现和商业策略就是你技艺所提供的深度的一部分。如果你真正热爱你所做的事，你就会真正热爱营销、销售、自我推广这类技能为“让你能终身追求它”所提供的效用。
p.132
Dive into the unknown by pursuing your vision-aligned hierarchy of goals. Educate yourself to gain clarity, execute on the smallest priority task, and keep an open mind to discover new potentials for your life. Seek to appreciate every facet of reality you encounter. If you feel the pull to go deeper, seek to understand. When passion is born in your pursuit, attempt to master the craft. From there, know that business is the modern vessel for living with purpose. It only makes sense to monetize what you master with the vast resources available to you in this developed point in civilization.
通过追求你与愿景一致的目标层级，潜进未知。教育自己去获得清晰，执行那个最小的优先任务，并保持开放的心去发现你生活中新的潜能。寻求欣赏你遇到的现实的每一个面向。如果你感到想更深潜的拉力，就去寻求理解。当热情在你的追求中诞生，就尝试精通这门技艺。从那以后，要知道商业是现代“带着目的生活”的载体。把你所精通之物，用这个文明发展到今天所提供给你的海量资源去变现，是再合理不过的。
CREATE YOUR
创造你的
p.133
IDEAL FUTURE
理想未来
p.133
THE SHIFT
转变
p.134
p.134
The beautiful thing about the internet is that you don't need money, tools, a degree, or a physical location to provide value anymore. You can learn, teach, build, and sell with the technology everyone has in their hands. Some countries don't have the same technology, but they will soon enough as Earth's technological baseline continues to rise.
互联网的美妙之处在于，你如今不再需要钱、工具、学位或一个实体位置去提供价值。你可以用每个人手里都握着的技术去学习、教授、构建和销售。有些国家还没有同样的技术，但随着地球的技术基线持续上升，它们很快就会有。
p.134
We are living through what seems to be a second Golden Age. The formal education system is being challenged by independent educators, journalists, experts, and artists that sought to remove the cap from their salary and physical reach. The banking system is being challenged by decentralized currency programmers. The government is being challenged by remote work and the desire for multi-nation citizenship to pay less taxes.
我们正身处看似第二个黄金时代之中。正规教育系统正被独立教育者、记者、专家和艺术家挑战——他们寻求摘掉自己薪资与物理触及范围的天花板。银行系统正被去中心化货币的程序员挑战。政府正被远程办公、以及为少交税而追求多国公民身份的愿望挑战。
p.134
The technological advancements that provide us with these new freedoms come at a cost. There is an overwhelming number of options for a better life, so much so that any given person is unaware of 95% of them, and the other 5% still cause anxiety toward the future. Older generations are set in their ways and don't understand the options that the younger generations have. Parents would rather their kids go to school and lock in a secure $50,000 salary when the kids could just as easily make $100,000 or more in less time online. The school system has been the symbol of security for a little over a century, but its time may soon come to an end. Thanks, entropy.
为我们提供这些新自由的技术进步，是有代价的。关于更好生活的选项多到令人不堪重负，多到任何一个人对其中的 95% 都一无所知，而剩下那 5% 仍引发对未来的焦虑。年长世代固守自己的方式，不理解年轻世代拥有的选项。父母宁愿孩子去上学、锁定一份 5 万美元的保障薪资，而孩子们只要在网上花更少时间，就能同样轻松地赚到 10 万美元甚至更多。学校系统在一个多世纪里一直是安全的象征，但它的时代可能很快就要终结。多谢，熵。
p.135
Humans are lazy (I mean "efficient," apologies). We have created solutions to make our lives easier for the entirety of our evolutionary timeline. At the time of this writing, the problem on most people's minds is the phasing out of labor jobs and low-skill work due to artificial intelligence and automation.
人类是懒的（我是指“高效”，抱歉）。在我们整个演化时间线上，我们一直在创造让生活更轻松的解法。在写下这句话时，多数人脑中的问题是：体力劳动和低技能工作正因人工智能和自动化而被逐步淘汰。
p.135
Fast food and grocery store workers are being threatened by automated kiosks and robots that don't cost the company an hourly wage - no matter how small. Semi-truck drivers are being threatened by self-driving trucks that can be controlled from a remote location anywhere in the world. Even writers, artists, and programmers are being threatened by artificial intelligence tools that can spit out words, masterpieces, and code at the click of a button.
快餐店和杂货店的员工正被自动点餐机和机器人威胁——它们不给公司造成任何小时工资成本，无论那成本多小。半挂卡车司机正被自动驾驶卡车威胁——那些卡车可以从世界任何地方远程控制。甚至连作家、艺术家和程序员也正被人工智能工具威胁——它们一点按钮就能吐出文字、杰作和代码。
p.135
In times like these, it makes sense why everyone is losing their minds. Their survival is at stake in more ways than physical, they don't have the time to learn about their potential options, and they are comfortable to the point where even a few minutes out of their mundane routine is perceived as "hard."
在这样的时代里，每个人都快疯了是有道理的。他们的生存受到威胁，而且不只是物理层面的；他们没有时间去了解自己潜在的选项；而他们舒服到连“从日常惯例里抽出几分钟”都被感知为“难”。
p.135
In a world ruled by money, it may not make you happy, but there is a baseline you must reach to sustain a fulfilling lifestyle. Money is the lifeblood of society, and if you want to participate in any aspect of it, money is now one of the most important basic needs in the world. You can play the status game of "not needing to make a lot of money to be happy," but unless you reject the world to live off in the woods, you are fooling yourself. Low-skill labor jobs are being phased out at an exponential rate, and I can't help thinking that this is exactly what the world needs. One man's labor cannot scale, but the creative ability of his mind can. You have the opportunity to solve your own problems, help others solve their own, and impact the world at scale while generating a creative income with the power of the internet. Education, entertainment, and inspiration now form the pillars of an emerging digital society. Purpose, profits, and peace are no longer mutually exclusive.
在一个由金钱统治的世界里，它也许不会让你快乐，但你必须达到一个基线，才能维持一种有圆满感的生活方式。金钱是社会的血液，如果你想参与其中任何一个面向，金钱如今已是世上最重要的基本需求之一。你可以玩“不需要赚很多钱才能快乐”这场地位游戏，但除非你拒绝这个世界、去林子里自给自足，你就是在骗自己。低技能劳动工作正以指数级速度被淘汰，而我忍不住想：这正是世界所需要的。一个人的人力无法规模化，但他心智的创造能力可以。你有机会去解决自己的问题、帮别人解决他们自己的问题、并以规模化影响世界，同时借助互联网的力量生成一份创造性收入。教育、娱乐和灵感如今构成了一个新兴数字社会的支柱。目的、利润与平静，不再是互斥的。
EMERGING EDUCATION
新兴教育
p.136
p.136
When I was a child, I felt alone. I was a rebel. I questioned almost everything that I was told to do, whether it was having to go to church, after-school sports, or college. I am grateful for my programming, because it allowed me to get a leg up on my peers who listened and obeyed without question.
小时候，我感到孤独。我是个叛逆者。我几乎质疑所有我被要求去做的事，无论是去教堂、课后运动，还是上大学。我感激我的这套编程，因为它让我比那些听话、不加质疑就服从的同伴领先一步。
p.136
Formal education has its place, but people are losing trust in its ability to secure their future. And I would argue that they never had trust in its ability to secure a fulfilling future. People inherently know that enjoyment in their life is their choice, but nobody wants to face that reality, so they outsource their future to schools and jobs.
正规教育自有它的位置，但人们正在失去对“它能保障自己未来”的信任。而我要说，他们从来就没信任过它能保障一个有圆满感的未来。人本能地知道，自己生活中的享受是自己的选择，但没人想面对那个现实，于是他们把未来外包给了学校和工作。
p.136
It's all too common for someone to spend 4-12 years and tens of thousands of dollars just to be placed in low-paying jobs that require a fraction of what they were taught in school. That is the ideal case. Most of the time, students need to self-educate on the side to secure an income outside of what they went to school for. The degree, at that point, serves as proof that you can do something that you hate for years, so they happily hire you.
某人花 4 到 12 年、几万美元，最后只被安排进低薪工作——那些工作只需用到学校里所教的一小部分——这种事太常见了。而那还是理想情况。大多数时候，学生需要在课外自学，才能在“他们上学所学”之外挣到一份收入。到那时，那张学位证的作用只是证明“你能忍受做一件你讨厌的事很多年”，于是他们乐意雇你。
p.136
The education system has its benefits, as all things do, but for those that want fulfilling work and an open schedule, a glorified piece of paper called a "degree" isn't going to get you there. In my eyes, the college experience is worthwhile. Depending on the individual's personality, they can form a powerful network, land a great job, and build a future worth helping others achieve. That's the problem in itself: the college experience is dependent on their personality. Their sense of self. The concept that the individual attaches to that is forged by years of social conditioning. Colleges create educational material that holds a high authority on the internet. Students form their worldview from this information because it allowed them to do well in college. Students grow up and create families with the same worldview. Families create selves that go to college without question and continue to fuel the outdated machine. The main reason people go to college is because they haven't questioned who they are, what they want, and developed themselves to the point of self-reliance.
教育系统有它的好处，就像万物一样；但对那些想要有圆满感的工作和开放日程的人来说，一张被称为“学位”的、被美化的纸不会把你带到那里。在我看来，大学体验是值得的。取决于个人性格，他们能建立一个强大的人脉网络、拿下一份好工作、并建立起一个值得帮别人去达成的未来。问题本身就在这里：大学体验取决于他们的性格。取决于他们的自我感。个体附加于其上的那个概念，是由多年社会条件化锻造出来的。大学创造出在互联网上持有高权威的教育材料。学生从这些信息中形成自己的世界观，因为它让他们在大学里表现出色。学生长大、建立家庭，带着同样的世界观。家庭创造出那些不加质疑就去上大学、并继续为这台过时机器添燃料的自我。人们上大学的主要原因是：他们还没有质疑过自己是谁、想要什么，也没有把自己发展到自立的程度。
p.137
We are all here to maximize our human experience. That's it. That's all we are looking for. Some attempt to find happiness in the short term, some in the long term, but we are all on the same path. We don't want to suffer, and education should reflect that. When we bust through our selfish karma, we then open up room for selflessness, and we can impact the world from a more enlightened perspective. This higher perspective cannot be reached by conforming to the formal education system.
我们都在这里为了最大化自己的人类体验。就这样。这就是我们所寻找的全部。有些人在短期里试图找到快乐，有些人在长期里，但我们都在同一条路上。我们不想受苦，而教育应当反映这一点。当我们冲破自己那套自私的业力，我们就为无私腾出了空间，并能从一个更开悟的视角去影响世界。这个更高的视角，无法通过顺从正规教育系统而抵达。
p.137
In my opinion, kids don't need to be taught an idealized version of health and gender studies. Nor do they need to memorize concepts in algebra and physics that don't transfer over to living a life of enjoyment and impact through a nuanced lens. People can find enjoyment in the interests that college can introduce them to, but one does not need to follow the same path as everyone else to find those interests.
在我看来，孩子们不需要被教一个理想化的健康与性别研究版本。他们也不需要去背那些代数与物理里、无法透过细致的透镜迁移到“一种享受与影响的生活”中的概念。人们可以在大学能介绍给他们的兴趣里找到享受，但要找到那些兴趣，并不意味着必须走与所有人相同的路。
p.137
The first lesson of any teaching should be to encourage the questioning of any teaching. The second should be to lean into the curiosity that will allow you to fail the fastest. From there, we can include topics on persuasion, mental models, research skills, critical thinking, and entrepreneurship as vessels for applying any skill the individual may learn.
任何教学的第一课，都应该是鼓励质疑任何教学。第二课，应当是向那种“让你最快失败”的好奇心倾斜。从那里，我们可以把说服、心智模型、研究技能、批判性思维和创业这些主题，作为“应用个体可能学到的任何技能”的载体包容进来。
p.137
This will never happen, since the education system is interwoven into the social fabric of corporate jobs and government agencies. The government influences the general curriculum, and the curriculum influences the job opportunities that students have available to them. From the outside looking in, this is a cyclical yet groundless system that reduces novel emergence, innovation, and personal development.
这永远不会发生，因为教育系统与公司工作和政府机构的社会织物交织在一起。政府影响总体课程，而课程影响学生可获得的工作机会。从外面看进来，这是一个循环的、却无根基的系统，它抑制了新奇的涌现、创新和个人发展。
p.137
At worst, the school system conditions convergent thinking, conformity over authenticity, memorization over process, failure as something to avoid, authorities as unquestionable, long work over efficiency, and intelligence dictated by book smarts. At best, this pricey status symbol will give you the experience you need to make better decisions as you enter your prime years. You will make mistakes, party a bit too much, and meet lifelong friends that you wouldn't find in your hometown.
最坏的情况下，学校系统条件化了收敛性思维、顺从胜于本真、记忆胜于过程、把失败当作要避免的东西、把权威当作不可质疑的、长工时胜于效率、以及由书本聪明所支配的智力。最好的情况下，这个昂贵的地位象征会给你所需的经验，让你在进入黄金年华时做出更好的决定。你会犯错、派对玩得有点过、并遇见你在家乡找不到的一生之友。
p.138
After 5 years and twenty-thousand dollars down the drain with 2 more years to complete my degree, I was fed up. There was a lot on the line, and the thought of getting a job was the bane of my existence. I knew I could acquire the skills to avoid that reality. In my final year, I took a class on basic computer programming. This was the first class I was interested in. So much so that I spent 3-4 hours a day studying outside of class with online courses and tutorials. This is when the reality of formal education slapped me in the face.
