Within 2 weeks, I had learned the entirety of the college course curriculum through self-study on the internet. I stopped going to class but still aced the tests.
在 5 年、两万美元打了水漂、学位还差 2 年才能拿完之后，我受够了。当时风险很大，而一想到要找工作，那简直是我存在之祸。我知道我能获得足以避开那个现实的技能。在最后一年，我选了一门基础计算机编程课。这是我第一门感兴趣的课。感兴趣到我在课外每天花 3 到 4 小时，用在线课程和教程自学。就在那时，正规教育的现实给了我一记耳光。两周之内，我通过在网上自学，学完了整门大学课程的课程大纲。我不再去上课，但仍把考试考得很好。
p.138
Computer programming was an in-demand skill, and my intense bouts of obsessive study opened a world of possibilities. I could freelance and avoid getting a job. I could build my own app and attempt to get paying users. Or if all things went wrong, I could get a high-paying job. The tech industry didn't care about a degree at the time, and more gigs were moving in this direction.
计算机编程是一门需求旺盛的技能，而我那些猛烈的、痴迷式的学习打开了一个充满可能的世界。我可以做自由职业，避开找工作。我可以做自己的 App，试着获得付费用户。或者如果一切出错，我也能拿到一份高薪工作。那时科技行业不在乎学位，而更多的活儿正在朝这个方向移动。
p.138
That was in 2018, and the world has continued to shift toward individuality, decentralization, and accessible information. You can learn any skill, cultivate your value, and distribute that value to the people that care about what you have to say.
那是 2018 年，而世界继续朝个体化、去中心化和可获取信息的方向转变。你可以学任何技能、培育你的价值、并把那份价值分发到在意你所要说之话的人们手中。
SPECIFIC KNOWLEDGE
特定知识
p.138
p.138
For the first eighteen years of our lives, depending on where you live, society is designed to strip our child-like curiosity from us. This is a blessing and a curse. A blessing for those that realize it, a curse for those that don't. Again, I want to make clear that this is not some kind of conspiracy theory. It is human nature manifested over centuries that has created an efficient system for reducing collective entropy. It has its perks, of course, but has ruined more lives than it has exposed to their potential. Curiosity is the path to doing the things you want to do. Curiosity is what makes you, you, and that is a necessity heading into the future of automated
在我们人生的前十八年里——取决于你住在哪里——社会是被设计来把我们的孩童般好奇心剥走的。这既是福也是祸。对觉察到它的人是福，对没觉察到的人是祸。再次地，我想说明：这不是某种阴谋论。它是人性在数个世纪里的显现，创造出一个降低集体熵的高效系统。它当然有它的好处，但它毁掉的人生，比它让人看见自身潜能的人生更多。好奇心是去做你想做之事的路径。好奇心造就了你之所以为你，而那正是朝自动化未来前行时的一项必需——
p.139
work. If you learn the same thing as everyone else to be trained into the select few jobs that are left, you can be replaced by almost anyone. The solution is specific knowledge.
工作。如果你学的是跟所有人一样的东西，只为了被训练进那些“剩下的少数精选岗位”里，那几乎任何人都能替换你。解法是特定知识。
p.139
Specific knowledge is difficult to find where general knowledge is taught. It takes a vision, hierarchy of goals, and dedicated time for curiosity-based self-education in alignment with those goals. If you are learning the same thing as everyone else, you will fight for the same replaceable opportunities as everyone else. The difference between formal education and selfeducation is being able to choose the material you learn according to your self-generated goals.
特定知识很难在“教授通用知识”的地方被找到。它需要一个愿景、一套目标层级，以及为与那些目标一致的好奇心驱动的自学而专门投入的时间。如果你学的是跟所有人一样的东西，你就会为跟所有人一样那些可替换的机会去竞争。正规教育与自我教育的区别，就在于你能根据自己的、自生成的目标去选择所学的材料。
p.139
The online education industry has hit exponential growth since the year 2020, and I don't see it slowing down any time soon. Jobs are being threatened left and right, and it only makes sense that people search for a new path. Formal institutions have joined this battle, of course, by using their capitalistic leverage to flood the online learning space. But they only have a fraction of the manpower that individual creators have to teach based on real-world experience.
在线教育行业自 2020 年以来实现了指数级增长，而我看不出它有任何短期内放缓的迹象。工作正被左右开弓地威胁，人们去寻找一条新路是再合理不过的。当然，正规机构已经加入这场战斗，用它们的资本杠杆淹没了在线学习空间。但它们能基于真实世界经验去教学的人力，只是个体创作者拥有的一小部分。
p.139
The incredible aspect of this education revolution is that the information is accessible to anyone in the world. You no longer need to move across the country to attend a prestigious school for the sake of developing a professional network.
这场教育革命令人不可思议的面向在于，信息对世界上任何人都可获取。你不再需要为了发展职业人脉而搬去另一个州、上一所名校。
p.139
In a watered-down description of an overly optimal situation, you can purchase a course, acquire a skill, and send a direct message to a high-status individual online to work for them. Or you can use that skill to build your own business with close-to-zero startup costs. Of course, this takes time. But the focused individual can acquire an irreplaceable skill stack in a fraction of the time as those that came before them.
用一个被极度理想化的情境来稀释地描述：你可以购买一门课程、获得一项技能，然后给网上某个高地位个体发一条私信去为他工作。或者你可以用那项技能、以接近零的创业成本去建立你自己的生意。当然，这需要时间。但那个专注的个体，能以远少于前人的时间获得一套不可替换的技能组合。
p.139
I like to think of specific knowledge as zip files for the mind. Independent educators teach through a specific perspective that can be shared by the students. That alone creates a more diverse and effective learning experience. With the student's goals, level of mind, and current skills taken
我喜欢把特定知识想成给心智用的压缩文件包。独立教育者通过一个可以被学生共享的特定视角去教学。仅这一点就创造出更多元、更有效的学习体验。把学生的目标、心智层级和当前技能纳入考量后，
p.140
into account, specific information can be injected into their brain in a way that blooms their understanding of the topic.
特定的信息可以被注射进他们的大脑，以绽放他们对那个主题的理解。
p.140
I'm convinced that the future of schooling will be done online, with creators as teachers, and each student can join the "school" that aligns the most with their interests, values, and preferred method of learning. One school system wouldn't dominate twelve-plus years of their life. Students would evolve beyond one after a few months or years, go on to the next, and eventually be able to start their own - if the other schools have the underlying principle of critical thinking and personal experience.
我确信学校教育的未来会在线上进行，创作者当老师，而每个学生都能加入那所与他们的兴趣、价值观和偏好学习方式最契合的“学校”。不会有一个学校系统支配他们人生中十二年以上。学生会在几个月或几年后超越一个、前往下一个，并最终能够开创自己的——前提是其他学校都持有批判性思维和个人经验这两条底层原则。
p.140
If creator- and community-based schools followed patterns of the Universe, their teachings would evolve as they do. This would desaturate the education market below it, allowing new educators to come in and teach beginners from a fresh lens.
如果以创作者和社群为基础的学校遵循宇宙的模式，它们的教导也会像宇宙那样演化。这会为它下方的教育市场腾出空间，让新的教育者进来，以新鲜的透镜去教初学者。
p.140
The teacher learns more than the student, and if students eventually become the teachers, we create a holistic and self-correcting education system through the unlimited nature of the internet. Students would pursue their goals, seek relevant specific knowledge, and forge a unique path in reality that can be passed down to future generations through their own public school. This is already happening in the new economy. Who knows what heights we could reach if the awareness were spread, and individuals were encouraged to create in alignment with their interests? People would stop creating to make money but would start making money to create.
老师学到的比学生更多，而如果学生最终成为老师，我们就通过互联网无限的本性，创造出一个整体性的、自我纠错的教育系统。学生会追求他们的目标、寻求相关的特定知识，并在现实中锻造出一条独特的路径，通过他们自己的“公开学校”传给未来世代。这在新经济里已经在发生。谁知道如果我们把这份觉察传播出去、并鼓励个体与自己的兴趣一致地去创造，我们能抵达怎样的高度？人们会停止“为了赚钱而创造”，而开始“为了创造而赚钱”。
p.140
These "zip files of specific knowledge" are not to be taken lightly. Humans raise their level of consciousness through understanding. Over the eons of our existence, we have been creating new knowledge that allows individuals to understand complex topics faster.
这些“特定知识的压缩文件包”不可小看。人类通过理解提升自己的意识层级。在我们存在的亿万年里，我们一直在创造新知识，让个体能更快地理解复杂主题。
p.140
If language paves the road that thought can operate on, and newly created knowledge through experience is being distributed without regulation, the future of work is being forged right before our eyes. This may have been the intention with interpretations of religious texts, but people read from a literal lens. If there were a simple preface that encouraged people to read
如果语言铺就了思想得以运作的道路，而通过经验新创造出的知识正被无管制地分发，那么工作的未来正在我们眼前被锻造出来。这可能正是解读宗教文本的本意，但人们从字面的透镜去读。如果有一段简单的序言，鼓励人们从
p.141
from a metaphorical lens, much of today's arguments, anger, and closedmindedness would be resolved All it takes is one big idea that registers well with an individual to cause an avalanche in the mind called insight. Insight leads to an exponential leap in consciousness. This begs the need for individuals educating themselves from a perspective that reaps maximum understanding.
隐喻的透镜去读，今天许多的争论、愤怒和封闭心态都会被化解。只需要一个能很好地被个体登记的大想法，就能在脑中引发一场被称为“洞见”的雪崩。洞见引向意识的一次指数级跃迁。这呼唤着个体需要从一个能收获最大理解的视角去自我教育。
p.141
This also begs the need for individuals educating other individuals to help reveal their blind spots. Another major downside of formal institutions is the static curriculum. It changes with the times, yes, but not as fast as a passionate individual can learn something new and post a message for hundreds of thousands of eyes to see.
这也呼唤着个体需要去教育其他个体，帮他们揭示自己的盲点。正规机构的另一个主要缺点是静态的课程。它确实随时而变，但变的速度比不上一个充满热情的个体学到新东西、并发布一条供数十万双眼睛阅读的消息。
p.141
Universities that churn tens of thousands of students through the same curriculum, with government influence sewn into the social fabric, in big classrooms, with underpaid professors that don't have much say over what they teach is not conducive to a future of conscious leaders.
那些让数万名学生通过同一套课程流水线走出的大学，政府的影响被缝进社会织物里，大教室里坐着那些对自己教什么没什么发言权的低薪教授——这不是一个有利于“有意识的领袖之未来”的配置。
p.141
If business professors understood the changing business landscape, they would have a business. Some teach out of passion, which is incredible, but why not reach more people and not have your teachings regulated by an outdated system? If any professor was a true master of their craft, they would be teaching curious individuals online, because that's where modern business takes place. Their income would reflect the results they are able to get for their students.
如果商学院教授们理解了正在变化的商业景观，他们自己就会有一门生意。有些人出于热情而教，这很了不起，但为什么不触及更多人、并且不让自己的教导被一个过时的系统管制？如果任何教授是自己手艺的真正大师，他们就会在网上教那些充满好奇的个体，因为现代商业就发生在那里。他们的收入会反映他们能为学生取得的结果。
p.141
Creating a course, or other form of educational material like internet content or writing a book, is the opposite. The smart creators understand that a course is the next logical step for their business after they get results. It is a way of increasing their income without more time invested while providing massive value to the world Yes, there are scammers and cheats, but that usually isn't a problem for those that have basic critical-thinking skills. And if you do fall prey to one of these bad actors, you now have the experience to make better decisions when choosing who to learn from. Like how many come to the realization
而制作一门课程，或其他形式的教育材料——比如互联网内容或写一本书——是反过来的。聪明的创作者明白：课程是他们生意在取得结果之后的合乎逻辑的下一步。它是一种在不投入更多时间的情况下增加收入的方式，同时向世界提供巨大价值。没错，有骗子和奸商，但对那些具备基本批判性思维技能的人来说，这通常不是问题。而如果你确实栽在其中一个坏角色手里，你现在就有了经验，在选择跟谁学习时做出更好的决定。就像许多人最终意识到，
p.142
that they were to a degree "scammed" by the formal education system. I'm not worried about this. It may have been common 5-10 years ago, but as with any developing industry, it either corrects itself or dies off, and I don't see it dying off any time soon.
自己某种程度上被正规教育系统“骗”了。我不为此担心。这在 5 到 10 年前可能很常见，但如同任何发展中行业一样，它要么自我纠错，要么消亡，而我看不出它会在短期内消亡。
p.142
The difference between a professor and creator is results. The creators solve their own problems, document the solutions, and package it up with a dash of personal experience to provide a life-changing learning experience without breaking the bank for the recipient.
教授与创作者的区别，在于结果。创作者们解决自己的问题、把解法记录下来、并用一撮个人经验把它包装起来，从而在不榨干接受者钱包的情况下，提供一次能改变人生的学习体验。
p.142
In other words, they aren't teaching outdated material. They are on the cutting edge of global opportunity. Yes, the new educators are making a lot of money, but that money reflects the value they provide at scale.
换句话说，他们教的不是过时材料。他们处在全球机会的最前沿。没错，新教育者们赚了很多钱，但那笔钱反映的是他们以规模化方式所提供的价值。
CAREER CREATION
职业创造
p.142
p.142
Knowledge not found in schools is the source of money not found in employment; and the internet has democratized wealth generation for those that take responsibility for their education, skill acquisition, and selfpromotion.
学校里找不到的知识，是雇佣关系里找不到的金钱之源；而互联网已经为那些愿意为自己教育、技能习得和自我推广负责的人，使财富生成民主化了。
p.142
At this point in time, the year 2023, there is a statistic that 85% of jobs that will exist in 2030 have not been invented yet. The keyword here is "invented." Another statistic is that 60% of labor jobs will be automated within the next decade. Technological advancements are allowing for the rapid evolution of the workspace. Jobs that were the beacon of career security are disappearing overnight, and jobs that nobody could fathom emerge with the highest earning potential. The problem is that the skills required to perform these jobs can only be learned from the passionate individuals that explored that new crevice of reality and distributed the information on the internet.
在这个时间点，也就是 2023 年，有一项统计：2030 年将存在的岗位中，有 85% 至今尚未被发明出来。这里的关键词是“发明”。另一项统计是：未来十年内，60% 的体力劳动岗位将被自动化。技术进步正让工作空间快速演化。那些曾是职业安全灯塔的岗位一夜之间消失，而那些谁都无法想象的岗位以最高收入潜力涌现出来。问题在于，执行这些岗位所需的技能，只能从那些探索了现实那个新裂缝、并把信息分发到互联网上的充满热情的人那里学到。
p.142
The future demands that we earn with our mind, not our time. The only way to earn with your mind is to break out of the narrow-focused state of survival. You must expand, organize, and focus your mind in an iterative
未来要求我们用自己的心智去赚取，而不是用自己的时间。用心智赚取的唯一方式，是打破那个狭隘聚焦的生存状态。你必须以迭代的方式去扩展、组织并聚焦你的心智，
p.143
nature as you solve local, social, global, and potentially cosmic problems and beyond, in that order.
去解决本地的、社会的、全球的、乃至潜在宇宙的以及更远的问题，按这个顺序。
p.143
I am fascinated by the emergence of the creator economy. A "creator" is someone who becomes a fountainhead of value through personal development, shares that value in public, and makes a creative income doing so. Mostly on social media, but the philosophy of a creator is not limited to the online space.
我被创作者经济的涌现深深吸引。一个“创作者”是通过个人发展成为价值之源、公开分享那份价值、并以此获得一份创造性收入的人。多半是在社交媒体上，但创作者这个哲学并不局限于线上空间。
p.143
Similar to how our ancestors each had their unique strengths and served their communities, creators lean into their curiosity and share their knowledge. Since we live in a comfortable world and have nearly eliminated our need to perform manual labor, what's left is knowledge and consciousness work. Through knowledge we shape the language, and therefore expansion of conscious thought, for the next generations. When we increase our level of mind through personal problem-solving, we create a ripple effect for decades to come.
类似于我们的祖先各自拥有独特的长处并服务自己的社群，创作者们向自己的好奇心倾斜并分享自己的知识。既然我们生活在一个舒适的世界里、几乎已经消除了体力劳动的需要，剩下的就是知识与意识层面的工作。通过知识，我们为未来世代塑造语言，从而塑造有意识思想的扩展。当我们通过解决个人问题提升自己的心智层级，我们就创造出一个延续数十年的涟漪效应。
p.143
It makes sense that information is the most valuable resource in our times. And it makes even more sense why lack of focus is the biggest problem of our time. The Industrial Age solved big problems in labor. The Information Age solved big problems in knowledge. And the Imagination Age will solve big problems in consciousness. You have the chance to be a part of this phase in human evolution.
信息在我们这个时代是最宝贵的资源，这是合理的。而“缺乏专注是我们这个时代最大的问题”就更合理了。工业时代解决了劳动中的大问题。信息时代解决了知识中的大问题。而想象时代将解决意识中的大问题。你有机会成为人类演化这个阶段的一部分。
p.143
People forget that they have the world's most powerful supercomputer between their ears. You must prioritize your mind. Mental mastery is how you fight back in a world that wants to steal your attention, manipulate your thoughts, and make you feel helpless. When you align your search for knowledge with your vision, goals, and present purpose, the potential for distraction decreases dramatically. You will spot future opportunities and self-correct your learning endeavors.
人们忘了，他们两耳之间装着世界上最强大的超级计算机。你必须优先对待你的心智。在一个想偷走你的注意力、操纵你的想法、让你感到无助的世界里，心智精通是你反击的方式。当你把对知识的搜寻与你愿景、目标和当下的目的对齐时，被分心的可能性会剧烈下降。你会辨认出未来的机会，并自我纠正你的学习努力。
p.143
The result of personal development is a career that you create, not one that society gives you. The creator economy is a newly emerged digital society. The goods exchanged in this economy have depth, passion, and a personal
个人发展的结果是一个“你创造出来的”职业，而不是社会给你的一个。创作者经济是一个新涌现的数字社会。在这个经济里被交换的商品，背后有深度、有热情、有一股个人
p.144
philosophy behind them. I know someone that sells barefoot shoes to fix postural health. I know someone that sells handmade wooden kitchenware to avoid the dangers of plastic. I know someone that sells stylish blue light glasses to help with eye strain and sleep. I know someone that sells fresh herbs, milk, and meat without the cruelty of factory farming. This seemingly self-sufficient online community I've found myself in provides everything 1 could need for a good life. And when I provide a product, my community will support me as well.
哲学。我认识一个人，他卖赤足鞋来修复体态健康。我认识一个人，他卖手工木制厨具来避开塑料的危害。我认识一个人，他卖时髦的蓝光眼镜来缓解眼疲劳、改善睡眠。我认识一个人，他卖新鲜的香草、牛奶和肉，不带工厂化养殖的残忍。我发现自己身处的这个看似自给自足的线上社群，提供了过上美好生活所需的一切。而当我也提供一个产品时，我的社群也会支持我。
p.144
Creative people get paid for doing what they enjoy doing. Armchair creatives often get stuck playing status games of who can create the best "art" that the market rejects. True creatives know that given enough time, they can turn passion into profit while maintaining their authenticity. We are smack in the middle of both the Digital Dark Ages and the Digital Renaissance. With an open mind, access to the internet, and a high-value skill stack, you can escape the former and join the latter.
有创造力的人因做自己享受的事而获得报酬。空谈式的创作者常被困在地位游戏里，比谁“创造”出最好的、被市场拒绝的“艺术”。真正的创作者知道，只要给他们足够的时间，他们能把热情变成利润，同时保持自己的本真。我们正处在数字黑暗时代与数字文艺复兴的正中间。带着开放的心、能上网、以及一套高价值技能组合，你可以逃离前者、加入后者。
UNDERSTANDING THE INTERNET
理解互联网
p.144
p.144
I have realized a common theme in my life (and the lives of many others). Obsession. As a kid, I was obsessed with finding a better way of living. I don't know what sparked this. All I know is that I was a silent observer. Everywhere I went, I paid close attention to people's actions. Not in a judgmental way, but in a discerning way.
我意识到自己生活（以及许多他人生活）里的一个共同主题。痴迷。小时候，我痴迷于寻找一种更好的活法。我不知道是什么引发了它。我只知道我是个沉默的观察者。无论我去哪里，我都密切注意人们的行动。不是以评判的方式，而是以辨察的方式。
p.144
How did that person get to that point in life? Why did they look that way? Was it because they were going through their closest fast-food drive through for breakfast each morning? Extra this, extra that, or was it because they could only view the world from their conditioned lens? Many things didn't sit well with me.
那个人是怎么走到人生那一步的？他们为什么看起来那样？是因为他们每天早上开车去最近的快餐得来速买早餐？多加点这个、多加点那个，还是因为受条件化的透镜限制，他们只能那样看待世界？很多事让我不安。
p.144
One of them was the conventional career path. Go to school. Think you know what you want to do at eighteen years old. Possibly get a good job the first time around. Possibly enjoy life while having zero control over 70% of
其中之一就是那条常规的职业路径。去上学。以为十八岁的自己知道想做什么。也许第一次就找到一份好工作。也许能享受生活，同时对自己一天中 70% 的时间拥有零控制权。
p.145
your day. Finally have the freedom to do whatever you want with your time at sixty-five years old. Sign me up!
最后在六十五岁时终于有自由，用你的时间做任何你想做的事。给我报名！
p.145
Nope. Didn't like that. A "secure" future didn't sound so secure when I pierced through the veil. So, I spent my time in the gym, learning from people I aspired to be like on social media, learning whatever skill could help me with new opportunities, and failing at 7+ business models. To many, this sounds like a hellish existence. To me, it was the only thing I could find true satisfaction in. Two sides of the same coin with a difference in perception.
不了。我不喜欢那个。“有保障的”未来在我透过那层帷幕看进去之后，听起来就没那么有保障了。所以，我把时间花在健身房、向我在社交媒体上仰慕的那些人学习、学任何能帮我获得新机会的技能，并在 7 个以上商业模式上失败。对很多人来说，这听起来像地狱般的存在。对我来说，这是我唯一能找到真正满足感的事。同一枚硬币的两面，差别只在感知。
p.145
I found solace in the creator economy early. Individuals that took advantage of the social media boom had my dedicated attention. They gave me a foundational understanding of the things that mattered. With a consistent self-education habit with matching execution, I took control of my mental, physical, and financial health. Through direct experience, I was able to solve my own problems, systemize the solution, and use my mental energy on creative endeavors that spread passion to others.
我很早就从创作者经济里找到了慰藉。那些利用了社交媒体浪潮的个体，得到了我全神贯注的注意。他们给了我关于那些要紧之事的基础理解。带着一致的自学习惯和与之匹配的执行，我掌控了自己的心智、身体和财务健康。通过直接经验，我得以解决自己的问题、把解法系统化，并把我的心智能量用在与他人分享热情的创造性事业上。
p.145
The future of work will not be work. It will be play. The human psyche is wired for survival. Entrepreneurship is modern-day survival. But most people have a twisted view of entrepreneurship. It's not about starting the next billion-dollar company. It's about leveraging your stack of skills, unique story, and finite focus to create a life of meaning. Everyone is an entrepreneur. Some just get paid for the value they cultivate outside of the conditioned path.
工作的未来不会是工作。它会是游玩。人类心灵是为生存而布线的。创业就是现代版的生存。但大多数人对创业有一个扭曲的看法。它不在于创办下一家千亿美元公司。它在于利用你的技能组合、独特故事和有限专注，去创造一种有意义的生活。每个人都是创业者。有些人只是为自己在条件化路径之外培育的价值得到了报酬。
p.145
We don't have as much control over human evolution as we think, but we do have control over the novelty we seek, gather, create, and trade. The path is already laid out and it is unfolding rapidly before our eyes. Those that hop on the train will thrive and others will experience neurobiological decay.
我们对人类演化的控制没有我们想的那么多，但我们确实能控制自己所寻求、收集、创造和交换的新奇。那条路已经被铺好了，并且正快速在我们眼前展开。跳上这趟列车的人会茁壮成长，其他人则会经历神经生物学的衰退。
p.145
Meaningless dopamine sources have people in chains, while meaningful dopamine is reserved to those that hunt and evolve. That is, pursuing your curiosity in alignment with self-generated goals, making novel discoveries
无意义的多巴胺源让人们身陷锁链，而有意义的多巴胺则保留给那些狩猎并演化的人。也就是说，与你自生成的目标一致地去追求好奇心，在
p.146
in the unknown, and being able to maintain an impactful lifestyle in a world that is shifting from corporation to individual.
未知中做出新奇的发现，并能在一个正从“公司”转向“个体”的世界里维持一种有影响力的生活方式。
p.146
The goal is to tap into your creative genius, create solutions to true problems, condense valuable information, and raise the well-being of the collective through your efforts.
目标是接通你的创造性天赋、为真正的问题创造解法、压缩有价值的信息，并通过你的努力提升集体的福祉。
p.146
The internet is the hunting ground, so let's begin to dissect it for big-picture understanding. There are billions of people that have access to the internet, while only a fraction don't or choose not to. If you want to reach almost anybody, there are 2 things you need to understand.
互联网是狩猎场，所以让我们开始解剖它，以获得大局的理解。有数十亿人能上网，只有一小部分人不能或选择不上。如果你想触及几乎任何人，有两件事你需要理解。
p.146
The back end of the internet is code. Unless you plan on becoming a programmer, we don't need to get technical here. Code is the series of commands, functions, and systems that delivers interactive information to your screen.
互联网的后端是代码。除非你打算成为程序员，我们不需要在这里变得技术化。代码是一连串向你的屏幕交付交互式信息的命令、函数和系统。
p.146
The front end of the internet is media. Every single person should have a foundational understanding of media because it is a microcosm of life itself. Media is composed of writing, speaking, and visuals that distribute a valuable message. In essence, media is an extension of the personal and collective mind. We put out our ideas, beliefs, and opinions that form a digital society, cultures, and world.
互联网的前端是媒体。每个人都应该对媒体有基础理解，因为它是生活本身的微缩宇宙。媒体由文字、口语和视觉组成，用于分发一个有价值的信息。本质上，媒体是个体心智与集体心智的延伸。我们放出自己的想法、信念和观点，它们构成一个数字社会、各种文化和世界。
p.146
The "valuable message" you distribute is subjective. What we perceive as valuable fluctuates on a daily, monthly, and yearly basis. At night, you may find value in watching a good movie. During the day, you may find value in learning a new skill.
你分发的那个“有价值的信息”是主观的。我们感知为有价值的东西，按天、按月、按年波动。夜里，你可能会在看一部好电影中找到价值。白天，你可能会在学一项新技能中找到价值。
p.146
The principles of a valuable message are less subjective. The goal with media is to leverage human psychology to capture attention, hold attention, and deliver value on that attention through problems, stories or games, and solutions. Media is but another song frozen in time, floating around in intangible code. Impactful media mimics the ebb and flow of the Universe itself.
有价值信息的原则则不那么主观。媒体的目标，是利用人类心理学去捕获注意力、保持注意力、并通过问题、故事或游戏、以及解法，在那份注意力上交付价值。媒体不过是另一首被冻结在时间里的歌，在无形的代码中飘荡。有影响力的媒体，模仿着宇宙本身的潮起潮落。
p.147
The internet is a public resumé, school, job board, note-taking system, and podium if you perceive it as such. There are brands, creators, students, consumers, and those that are transitioning from one phase to another, from distracted to focused or vice versa.
如果你这样去感知，互联网就是一份公开简历、一所学校、一块招聘板、一套笔记系统和一个讲台。那里有品牌、创作者、学生、消费者，以及那些正从一个阶段过渡到另一个阶段的人——从分心到专注，或反过来。
p.147
Brands and creators host media that educates, entertains, and inspires their audience. If they don't have a product, their self-promotion doesn't go to waste. Employers are online, and they are very active in hiring those that distribute the most value. In other words, even if you aren't sold on becoming a "creator," you won't escape digital survival. You either create and distribute value or drastically limit the opportunities available to you. Those that have realized the mindful power of the internet would be considered students. They learn from brands and creators until their time inevitably comes to join them. Then, there are consumers. For the sake of distinction, "consumers" will be defined as those without a vision that are consuming surface-level information that is not conducive to their nonexistent ideal future. Everyone is a consumer, yes, but as the dualistic nature of life goes, one must also become a creator so that extreme consumerism doesn't overtake their potential.
品牌和创作者宿主那些教育、娱乐并启发其受众的媒体。如果他们没有产品，他们的自我推广也不会浪费。雇主在网上，他们非常积极地招聘那些分发最多价值的人。换句话说，即便你不认同成为“创作者”，你也逃不掉数字生存。你要么创造并分发价值，要么剧烈限制你所能获得的机会。那些意识到互联网这份正念力量的人，会被算作学生。他们向品牌和创作者学习，直到他们的时机不可避免地到来、加入其中。然后，还有消费者。为了区分的缘故，“消费者”将被定义为那些没有愿景、消费着对其不存在的理想未来无益的表层信息的人。没错，每个人都是消费者；但正如生活的双重本性所示，一个人也必须成为创作者，以免极端的消费主义压倒自己的潜能。
p.147
We will discuss this in depth in the coming sections, but understand this: observation, awareness, and correcting your focus through self-reflection is the greatest teacher for understanding human nature. By understanding how you interact with the world both physical and digital, you understand others, and can apply that knowledge to increase the impact of anything you create.
我们会在接下来的章节里深入讨论这个，但请理解这一点：观察、觉察、以及通过自我反思去纠正你的专注，是理解人性的最伟大的老师。通过理解你如何在物理世界和数字世界中互动，你就理解了他人，并能把那份知识应用出去，来增加你所创造之物的影响力。
THE NEW RICH
新富人
p.148
p.148
Happiness is a skill. It is not given but created. As with all skills, it must be practiced, refined, and adopted as a part of your life. When isolated, happiness loses its meaning, as it cannot exist without an unhappy reference point of prior experience.
幸福是一项技能。它不是被给予的，而是被创造出来的。如同所有技能一样，它必须被练习、被精炼、并被采纳为你生活的一部分。当被孤立时，幸福会失去意义，因为没有一段不快乐的过往经验作为参照点，它就无法存在。
p.148
This is the problem with new-age positivity. You can think positive thoughts all day long. But people fail to realize that every positive thought holds a negative seed. This is why almost every great success comes after great failure. If you want to be happier, you need to expose yourself to more negative experiences that allow you to create the positive ones. You can think your way to a positive future, but the image of that future is forged through an equal and often more painful past. Without a negative experience as an anchor, you have nothing meaningful to move toward. There are 2 states of mind to become aware of: stillness and movement. Being and doing. Peace and progress. When your focus is occupied by the background of your ideal future and the foreground of your priority actions, these 2 states of mind collapse into the present moment. Everyone wants money, muscles, and a desirable partner. The act of achieving those goals feels incredible at the start. If you don't have a philosophical sense of mastery behind your material pursuits, you are in for a rude awakening.
这就是新纪元式积极心态的问题所在。你可以整天想正面的念头。但人们没意识到，每一个正面念头都持有一颗负面的种子。这就是为什么几乎每一次伟大的成功都跟在伟大的失败之后。如果你想更幸福，你需要让自己暴露于更多负面体验，好让你能创造出那些正面体验。你可以靠“想”来抵达一个正面未来，但那个未来的图景，是通过一段同等、且往往更痛苦的过去锻造出来的。没有一段负面体验作为锚，你就没有有意义的东西可朝之移动。有两种心之状态需要被觉察：静止与运动。存在与行动。平静与进步。当你的专注被你理想未来的背景和优先行动的前景所占据，这两种心之状态就塌缩进当下这一刻。每个人都想要钱、肌肉和一个理想的伴侣。达成那些目标的行为在开始时感觉不可思议。如果你在物质追求背后没有一个哲学层面上的精通感，那你就要大难临头了。
p.149
Even if your actions don't change, the "why" behind them can. A bodybuilder that got started after a tough breakup can find meaning in the microcosm of life that weight training is if they allow their mind to see beyond their identification with their seemingly material pursuits. Most people would be considered superficial for owning a nice car, but a mechanic that loves dissecting every bolt, part, and speck of paint? Cars are where they find maximum enjoyment. You can enjoy flashy things. Most people just acquire them for the mindless pursuit of status.
即便你的行动不变，其背后的“为什么”也可以变。一个在痛苦分手之后开始健身的健美者，如果能让自己心智看见超出他与那些看似物质追求之认同之外的东西，他就能在“健身作为生活微缩宇宙”中找到意义。大多数人拥有一辆好车会被视为肤浅，但一个热爱解剖每一颗螺栓、每个零件、每一粒漆点的机械师呢？车是他们找到最大享受的地方。你可以享受浮华之物。大多数人获得它们，只是为了无脑地位追求。
p.149
Many that do acquire their material desires change on the outside, but not the inside. Society is filled with people who turn a physical sixty years old with the mind of a twelve-year-old going through an emotional puberty. The main Buddhist teaching is that of impermanence. That is, nothing can be isolated and held static by the mind. This includes ideas, feelings, emotions, people, locations, and everything else that we label and expect to stay the same forever.
许多确实获得了物质欲望的人，外表变了，内在却没变。社会里充满了那些身体六十岁、心智却像正在经历情绪青春期的十二岁小孩的人。佛教的核心教导是无常。也就是说，没有任何东西能被心智孤立并静态地持有。这包括观念、感受、情绪、人、地点，以及所有其他我们贴上标签并期待永远不变的东西。
p.149
The identification with ideology, dogma, and other static mental constructs are the source of our suffering. When they are threatened, so is our happiness. However, realize that this still holds true for your purpose. The goals you pursue are the axis of your suffering. Choose them wisely, as fulfillment would not hold meaning without painful experiences as a reference point.
对意识形态、教条和其他静态心智构造的认同，是我们痛苦的源头。当它们受威胁时，我们的幸福也受威胁。然而，要意识到这对你的目的同样成立。你所追求的目标，正是你痛苦的轴心。明智地选择它们，因为没有痛苦体验作为参照点，圆满就不会持有意义。
p.149
Thinking is not bad and often necessary when critical. But when gone unchecked, compulsive thoughts can create a personal reality of inescapable turmoil. When one is still, their mind wants to move. When one is moving, their mind wants to be still.
思考并不坏，在关键的时候往往是必要的。但一经不加检查，强迫性念头就能创造出一种无法逃脱的动荡的个人现实。当一个人静止时，他的心智想动。当一个人运动时，他的心智想静。
p.149
Without deliberate practice, the mind will latch onto the past or future in an attempt to make the impermanent permanent. This is the cause of unhappiness but is not to be demonized, as that is against the point. When you feel unhappy, observe that feeling. Lean into it. Let it point "a finger at the moon" and present the lesson that life is trying to teach you. From that low, lean into the coming high.
没有刻意的练习，心智会缠上过去或未来，试图把无常变成恒常。这是不快乐的原因，但不该被妖魔化，因为那违背了要点。当你感到不快乐，观察那份感受。向它倾斜。让它“指向月亮”，并呈现生活正试图教给你的那一课。从那个低点，倾向那即将到来的高点。
p.150
The new rich are those that can refine their lifestyle to sustain a schedule filled with stillness, movement, and a lack of mindless chatter in the skull. The activities that create this blissful state of mind are personal. You must observe, hypothesize, experiment, fail, learn, and repeat this never-ending process even once you have reached conscious success. Because even that isn't permanent.
新富人是那些能精炼自己生活方式、以维持一个充满静止、运动、以及颅腔内没有无脑唠叨的日程的人。创造这种至福心境的活动是私人的。你必须观察、假设、实验、失败、学习，并重复这个永无止境的过程，即便在你已经抵达有意识的成功之后。因为连那个也不是永久的。
YOUR LIFE'S WORK
你的人生事业
p.150
p.150
Work.
工作。
p.150
Does that spark any stressful thoughts about tomorrow? If so, that's a problem. Work consumes a vast amount of the finite mental energy you have in this lifetime. If the majority of your days are filled with something you hate, how do you think your life will turn out?
这两个字是否激起了你关于明天的压力念头？如果有，那是个问题。工作消耗掉你这一生所拥有的有限心智能量中的一大块。如果你大部分的日子都被你讨厌的事填满，你觉得你的人生会变成什么样？
p.150
In a world where most people see overwork as a badge of honor and rest as an inconvenience, it's no wonder so many people are unfulfilled and bitter. Nobody said they wanted to work forty-plus hours a week, numb their mind with mindless entertainment, and put off their dreams just to wake up one day wondering where the time went. Yet that's what everyone does.
在一个多数人把过度工作看作荣誉徽章、把休息看作不便的世界里，这么多人不圆满、苦涩，一点也不奇怪。没人说自己想要每周工作四十多个小时、用无脑娱乐麻痹心智、把梦想推后，只为了某天醒来时纳闷时间都去哪了。然而所有人都这么做。
p.150
Why? Because they didn't ask "why" earlier. They let it happen because that's always how it was supposed to happen, at least to their knowledge. Work is a necessary part of life and would lose meaning without dedicated rest. But people don't see the relationship between the 2 and oscillate between the unconscious extremes of both. It's either stressful work they hate, or a delusional idea of an endless summer sipping margaritas on the beach.
为什么？因为他们早些时候没有问“为什么”。他们让它发生，因为那一直就是“应该”发生的方式，至少按他们的认知是这样。工作是生活中必要的一部分，没有专门的休息就会失去意义。但人们看不见这两者之间的关系，于是在两者的无意识极端之间振荡。要么是他们讨厌的压力工作，要么是一个在沙滩上啜饮玛格丽特的、无尽夏日的妄想。
p.150
I have lived the life of early retirement in a tropical setting, and I can tell you with confidence that it normalizes. Eventually, your mind will seek movement through challenge, and that desire will become so strong that
我在热带环境里过过提前退休的生活，我可以自信地告诉你，它会变得习以为常。最终，你的心智会通过挑战去寻求运动，而那份渴望会强到
p.151
even the most pleasurable vacation will lead to anxiety and boredom thanks to psychic entropy.
连最愉悦的假期都会因为心灵熵而引向焦虑与无聊。
p.151
Everyone has the desire to be free. This is a sign in the direction that you should move. All that freedom is, when pertaining to the mind, is the dissolution of barriers that comes from adopting a higher perspective. When you adopt a higher perspective, you can start to see things for what they are. You don't want absolute freedom, you want autonomy. The difference is that freedom implies a lack of structure, where autonomy is your ability to choose within a structure. Hopefully one that is composed of a strong vision, evolving purpose, and meaningful problems worth solving.
每个人都有成为自由的渴望。这是一个指向“你应该朝哪移动”的信号。当涉及心智时，自由的全部含义，就是通过采纳一个更高视角而来的障碍消融。当你采纳一个更高视角，你就能开始看清事物本来的样子。你想要的不是绝对自由，而是自主。区别在于：自由暗示着缺乏结构，而自主是你在一个结构之内进行选择的能力。但愿那个结构由一个坚强的愿景、不断演化的目的、以及值得解决的有意义问题所构成。
p.151
When the average individual thinks about work, their mind floods with the string of tasks waiting for them when they clock in. When they think of rest, they see it as an inconvenience that prevents them from reaching the same status as their peers. No matter where they turn, the modern individual meets 4 cushy walls that look like a fun house but is actually an insane asylum.
当普通人想到工作，他们的心智就涌满打卡后等着他们的那串任务。当他们想到休息，他们把它看作妨碍自己抵达与同伴同等地位的一件不便。无论他们转向哪里，现代人都撞上四面柔软的墙，看起来像游乐屋，实际上却是疯人院。
p.151
Now, don't let my doomsday perspective make you lose hope. At the same time, don't let the importance of taking control of your life go unnoticed. Getting a job is only bad when made permanent. Everything evolves. Lowto high-paying jobs should be viewed as a series of stepping stones to aid in the discovery of your life's work. It is unwise to think that you already have the skill to make millions of dollars doing what you love when you haven't even become aware of what you love.
现在，别让我这末日式的视角让你失去希望。同时，也别让“掌控自己的人生”的重要性被忽视。找工作只有在它被做成永久时才坏。万物都在演化。低薪到高薪的工作，应该被视为一串垫脚石，帮你去发现你的人生事业。在你甚至还没意识到自己热爱什么的时候，就以为“自己已有技能靠热爱之事赚到数百万美元”，这是不明智的。
p.151
For now, depending on your age and responsibility, choosing a job that presents a matching level of challenge will make you happier than going all in on the uncertain path. When that job stops presenting ample challenge, don't get complacent. Acquire new skills and pursue the purpose that reveals itself through struggle.
而现在，取决于你的年龄和责任，选择一个呈现出与你匹配的挑战层级的工作，会让你比“押上一切走那条不确定的路”更快乐。当那份工作不再呈现出足够的挑战，不要变得自满。去获得新技能，并追求那个通过挣扎显现出来的目的。
p.151
The notion of having a "life's work" may seem like an impossibility. If you're drowning in tasks, responsibilities, and escapism through
拥有“人生事业”这个念头，也许看起来是不可能的。如果你正被任务、责任、以及通过
p.152
momentary pleasure, I don't blame you. And you're not alone. Keep your mind open a bit longer for me.
瞬时快感的逃避所淹没，我不怪你。而且你并不孤单。再为我保持一会儿开放的心。
p.152
Everyone has the ability to do work that brings meaning to their lives. Some find it early, others within a few decades, and the rest don't find it at all. The key is to find the one thing that makes all the sacrifices worth it after extended periods of experimentation.
每个人都有能力去做那种给生活带来意义的工作。有些人很早就找到，有些人在几十年内找到，剩下的人则永远找不到。关键是在长期的实验之后，找到那件能让所有牺牲都值得的事。
p.152
That's the kicker: it will demand sacrifice. Pursuing your life's work won't be all dandelions and roses.
关键就在这里：它会要求牺牲。追求你的人生事业不会全是蒲公英和玫瑰。
p.152
After sufficient learning, failure, and persistence, you will feel compelled to decline any and every external request to build out a meaningful project. This is when you lock yourself in your room, harness your obsession, and build something meaningful with the mental skill you've developed. Then, you will need to create a balance that doesn't turn you into a workaholic that misses out on the finer things in life.
在足够的学习、失败和坚持之后，你会感到有必要谢绝任何和一切“要你去构建一个有意义项目”的外部请求。这时你要把自己锁进房间，驾驭你的痴迷，用你已经培养出的心智技能去构建某种有意义的东西。然后，你需要创造出一种平衡，让你不至于变成一个错过生活中更美好事物的工作狂。
p.152
Your life's work is an inherent part of your vision for the future. It is how you spread the impact of the value you develop over time to others and, with the power of the internet, it has never been so feasible. Feasible, but not to be mistaken for easy.
你的人生事业是你未来愿景中固有的一部分。它是你如何把你随时间培育出的价值影响力扩散给他人；而有了互联网的力量，它从未如此可行。可行，但别把它误认为容易。
p.152
Your life's work is how you spread love, passion, and consciousness in a way that ripples beyond locality. For one individual, this may be their obsession with beer, no matter how many people label it as a destructive substance. They explored that crevice of reality, turned matter into meaning, and served it with a smile on their face to the customers of their brewery. For another, it could be video game development, philosophy, or basket weaving. Nothing is off limits, but there are many limits in the way. Your job is to explore the unknown, dig beyond the surface, and let curiosity pull you up, down, left, and right until you find the center.
你的人生事业，是你以超越本地的方式扩散爱、热情和意识的方式。对某个人来说，这可能是他对啤酒的痴迷——无论多少人给它贴上“有害物质”的标签。他们探索了现实的那个裂缝、把物质转化为意义、并带着脸上的微笑把它端给自己酿酒厂的顾客。对另一个人来说，它可能是电子游戏开发、哲学，或编织篮子。没有什么被排除在外，但路上有许多限制。你的工作是探索未知、挖过表层，并让好奇心把你拉上、拉下、拉左、拉右，直到你找到那个中心。
p.152
When you find the center, plant your seed, and let the roots spread to strengthen that passion. You will need more skills than one to make that passion a sustainable aspect of your life.
当你找到中心，种下你的种子，让根系蔓延来强化那份热情。要让那份热情成为你生活中可持续的一部分，你需要的技能不止一项。
p.153
I regret to inform you that I don't have a rapid solution for this problem you are meant to solve. This process isn't immediate, and that's what makes it worth it. You will feel lost, you will lose hope, but when you stumble across the experience that shows you it's possible, there's no going back.
我很遗憾地告诉你，对于这个注定要由你来解决的问题，我没有一个快速的解法。这个过程不是即时的，而正是这一点让它值得。你会感到迷失，你会失去希望，但当你偶然撞上那个向你证明“它是可能的”的经验时，就再也回不去了。
p.153
As with many things in this book, this is a seed of awareness. If you were not made aware of potential problems in your life and the possibility of solving them, would you even think to work toward that reality? When was the last time you even thought of your life's work?
如同这本书里的许多东西，这是一颗觉察的种子。如果你不曾被提醒你生活中潜在的问题、以及解决它们的可能性，你甚至会不会想到朝那个现实去努力？你上一次想到自己的人生事业，是什么时候？
p.153
Through the pursuit of curiosity and self-experimentation, you will unveil what you were put on this Earth to do. Take small risks until you feel the pull to go all in. You may realize that the pull was a lesser purpose that needed to be fulfilled. This is fine. Let that chapter end.
通过追求好奇心和自我实验，你将揭开自己为何被放到这地球上。承担小风险，直到你感到那股“押上一切”的拉力。你可能会意识到，那拉力只是一个需要被实现的较小目的。这没关系。让那一章结束。
LIFESTYLE DESIGN
生活方式设计
p.153
p.153
I've always had some form of aversion toward Western work culture.
我一直对西方工作文化有某种形式的反感。
p.153
Eighty-hour work weeks are encouraged. High-pressure environments.
八十小时工作周被鼓励。高压环境。
p.153
Little time for rest and recovery. Everyone complains about going to work, when they can go home, and what they are going home to. An endless cycle.
几乎没有时间休息和恢复。每个人都在抱怨去上班、什么时候能回家、以及回家要面对什么。一个无尽的循环。
p.153
It never felt "right" to me, and from past experiences, I know that is a feeling that one should always question. Why would I want to waste my entire day knowing that within 2-3 hours my focus would fade and work quality would suffer?
它对我来说从来就感觉“不对”，而根据过往经验，我知道那是一种人应该永远质疑的感觉。我为什么要浪费一整天，明知在 2 到 3 小时内我的专注就会消散、工作质量就会受损？
p.153
Four-hour workdays, singular focus, and meaningful work are becoming the norm in small pockets of the internet, and for good reason. Ancient Romans and Greeks, Steve Jobs, Charles Darwin, and an ever-growing list of visionaries, strategists, and innovators attribute their success to surprisingly low work times accompanied by an abundance of restful activities like long walks.
四小时工作日、单一焦点、有意义的工作，正成为互联网小圈子的常态，而且理由充分。古罗马人和古希腊人、史蒂夫·乔布斯、查尔斯·达尔文，以及一份不断增长的远见者、战略家和创新者名单，都把他们的成功归功于惊人地低的工作时间，伴随大量像长距离散步这样的休息性活动。
p.154
When we see someone with a respectable body of creative work, we would expect them to work long hours, obsessing into the night about the details of their next piece. Instead, we see the opposite. Like Darwin arriving in his study by 8 after his morning walk and breakfast. He would work for an hour and a half, take a break to read the mail and write letters, then return to more serious work, where he conducted his experiments. By noon Darwin would stop his workday and head out on a long walk. After reading and answering a few more letters, he would take a nap, take another walk, and return to his study for another work block. Four to five hours of work paired with active rest seems to be the sweet spot for most impactful creatives. Writers from multiple domains like Hemingway, Tarantino, and Ogilvy would spend the majority of their days lounging by the pool, talking to beautiful women, and doing everything aside from what they deemed work. They gave room for the creative emergence of ideas that fueled the impact of their work. If they can change culture and business with their methods, why can't corporate workaholics do the same?
当我们看到一个拥有可观创造性作品的人，我们会以为他们工作时间很长，夜里还在痴迷地推敲下一件作品的细节。相反，我们看到的是反面。就像达尔文早上散步和早餐后八点抵达书房。他会工作一个半小时，休息一下读信、写信，然后回到更严肃的工作——在那里他做实验。到正午，达尔文会停止工作日，出门长距离散步。再读并回几封信后，他会小睡一会儿、再散一次步，然后回书房进行另一个工作时段。四到五小时的工作加上主动休息，似乎是多数有影响力的创作者的最佳点。来自多个领域的作家——海明威、塔伦蒂诺、奥格威——会把一天大部分时间用在泳池边闲躺、跟漂亮女人交谈、以及做一切他们不认为是工作的事。他们为那些点燃其作品影响力之想法的创造性涌现留出了空间。如果他们的方法能改变文化和商业，公司里的工作狂为什么不能同样做到？
p.154
Rest is important in the age of automation because it demands creativity from those that don't want to live a mechanical and predetermined life. Rest is the driving force behind your mind's creative ability. Humans aren't robots, yet most of our lives are spent in an unconscious repetition of tasks that are graded by time spent rather than results.
在自动化时代，休息很重要，因为它向那些不想过机械式、被预定好人生的人索取创造力。休息是你心智创造能力背后的驱动力。人类不是机器人，然而我们人生的大部分时间，都花在对任务的无意识重复上，而那些任务是按花费的时间、而非结果来评分的。
p.154
As technology advances, so does efficiency, and those that choose to be workaholics should do so by their own conscious choice. Some people are happier when they work more on the things they enjoy. But for most people, a balance of meaningful work and ample rest can help prevent life from losing its spark. Much of the time, the 2 complement each other to the point of enhancing the effects of both.
随着技术进步，效率也在提升，而那些选择当工作狂的人应当出于自己有意识的选择才那么做。有些人在更多地去从事自己享受之事时更快乐。但对大多数人来说，有意义的工作加上充足的休息这一平衡，能帮生活不失去火花。很多时候，这两者相互补足，甚至到增强彼此效果的程度。
p.154
The pride of overwork is for those climbing a status ladder. A balanced, fulfilling lifestyle is for those that do what they want. When forging your own path, productivity is difficult to measure. Instead, we can measure the amount of engagement with our work and the mental energy required to
过度工作的自豪感是留给那些在地位阶梯上攀爬的人的。一种平衡的、有圆满感的生活方式，是留给那些做自己想做的事的人的。当你锻造自己的路径时，生产力很难测量。相反，我们可以测量我们与工作的投入程度，以及
p.155
produce valuable creations. You measure this through self-reflection and how difficult a challenge was according to your level of skill.
产出有价值作品所需的心智能量。你通过自我反思、以及“一个挑战相对于你的技能层级而言有多难”来衡量它。
p.155
Balance does not mean stuck in the middle. Balance is the dance between extremes. Extreme focus and extreme rest. Full engagement with being or doing. Locked into reality itself.
平衡并不意味着卡在正中间。平衡是在极端之间的舞蹈。极端的专注与极端的休息。全然投入于存在或行动。被锁进现实本身。
p.155
The paradox of productivity is the less you work, the higher quality your work is. Imagine training in the gym for 8 hours trying to be as "productive" as possible. In one day, you would run out of exercises, tax your nervous system into poverty, and may even opt to go on a 5-mile run because your boss expects you to perform and you want to survive the job title you've been given.
生产力的悖论是：你工作得越少，你的工作质量越高。想象一下在健身房里训练 8 小时、试图尽可能“高产”。一天之内，你会用光所有动作、把神经系统压榨到破产，甚至可能选择去跑 5 英里，因为你的老板期望你表现，而你想在给你那个职位头衔下活下来。
p.155
Now, would you be able to come back and give it your all the next day? How about 5 days in a row? Would you be able to tough it out until you can use your paid vacation time to recover and do it all over again?
那么，你第二天还能回来全力投入吗？连续 5 天呢？你能硬撑到用带薪假期恢复过来，然后再把所有这一切重来一遍吗？
p.155
Your body would be decimated. As would your focus. Instead, we train for forty-five to ninety minutes at a time. We push ourselves at the expense of physical - or mental - energy. We create a routine and schedule it into our days so we can prioritize rest, recovery, and general quality of life. This is a phenomenon that must be directly experienced. I have personally gone through many cycles of losing trust in long workdays. When an important task was scheduled outside of work and I forced myself to take rest, the quality of my work the next morning saw a notable increase in quality. When I made it into a habit, my quality of life met the same increase.
你的身体会被摧毁。你的专注也一样。相反，我们一次训练四十五到九十分钟。我们以消耗身体或心智能量为代价去逼自己。我们创建一套惯例并把它安排进日程，以便优先安排休息、恢复和总体生活质量。这是一个必须被直接体验的现象。我个人经历过许多次“对长工作日失去信任”的循环。当一个重要任务被安排在工作之外，而我强迫自己休息时，我第二天早上的工作质量明显提升。当我把它变成习惯时，我的生活质量也取得了同样的提升。
p.155
While corporate culture is handing you a pretty paycheck to incentivize sustained intensity by exploiting your survival, you must push back. Intensity is powerful, but not sustainable. It's not rocket science. Sustainability, consistency, and creativity must be prioritized before we even mention the word "productivity."
当公司文化递给你一张漂亮的薪水支票、通过剥削你的生存本能来激励你持续高强度工作时，你必须顶回去。强度很强大，但不可持续。这不是火箭科学。在我们甚至提到“生产力”这个词之前，就必须优先考虑可持续性、一致性和创造力。
p.156
In this modern world, it is possible to create a daily routine filled with the activities that bring you the most enjoyment. The keyword here is "create." It will take a few iterations of experimentation, identifying problems, testing new solutions, and systemizing them to best utilize your mental energy.
在这个现代世界里，创造一个充满那些给你带来最大享受的活动的日常惯例是可能的。这里的关键词是“创造”。它需要几轮实验迭代、识别问题、测试新解法、并把它们系统化，以最佳利用你的心智能量。
p.156
To understand this lifestyle design process, let's start small and practical. This is a process I run through when life gets a bit too messy. Like when you're constantly thinking back to a time when "life was better." Or when your routines succumb to entropy, fall apart, and all these little tasks pop up that suck up the little time you have in a day.
为理解这个生活方式设计过程，让我们从小而实际的地方开始。这是我每当生活变得有点太乱时会跑一遍的流程。比如当你不断回想“生活曾经更好”的那个时候。或者当你的惯例屈服于熵、土崩瓦解，而所有这些小任务冒出来、吸干你一天中仅有的那点时间。
p.156
Pull out a journal and take note of how you feel. Write down exactly what you are doing on a daily basis. Every little detail. Take 10 minutes and get specific on what you do, why you do it, and how you feel in the morning, afternoon, and night. This is important for identifying unconscious parasites (time and energy suckers).
拿出一本日志，记录你的感受。写下你每天到底在做什么。每一个小细节。花 10 分钟，具体写出你做什么、为什么做、以及你在早上、下午和夜里感觉如何。这对识别无意识的寄生者（时间和能量吸血鬼）很重要。
p.156
From your brain dump, prioritize, remove, and restructure. The reason you aren't making progress is because you feel pressed for time, don't have the energy to get results, or you stopped doing the things that got results. Prioritize the things that will get results. Remove the things that snuck their way into your day. Restructure specific tasks and obligations to free up more time. Get the chaotic structure of your mind on paper and reorganize it.
从你的脑内倾倒里，排出优先级、移除、并重构。你没有取得进步的原因，是你感到时间紧迫、没有精力去取得结果，或者你停止做那些曾带来结果的事。把能带来结果的事排到前面。移除那些偷偷溜进你一天的那些事。重构特定的任务和义务，腾出更多时间。把你心智那混乱的结构落到纸上，并重新组织它。
p.156
Next, create a weeklong system. You are in this chaotic state because of psychic entropy, disorder of the mind. The organization of your life tends toward disorder if you don't perform mental housekeeping. You will pick up unconscious habits that may wreak havoc without you noticing.
接下来，创造一套为期一周的系统。你处在这个混乱状态里是因为心灵熵，也就是心智的失序。如果你不做心智上的家务，你生活的组织就会趋向失序。你会拾起一些无意识的习惯，它们可能在你没注意的情况下造成浩劫。
p.156
Habits are difficult to break, but you can make the process easier with conscious clarity practice. Write out every single thing you are going to do for the next week. Keep this simple and don't overthink. Just jot it down. This is how you reduce the friction of making better decisions.
习惯很难打破，但你可以用有意识的“清晰练习”让这个过程更容易。把你在接下来一周将做的每一件事都写出来。保持简单，不要过度思考。就把它记下来。这就是你如何降低做出更好决定的摩擦。
p.157
Plan out your morning routine, focused work routine, other tasks and meetings, and your nightly routine. You will have to experiment as you go. If the routine doesn't flow, go back to your notebook and refine the system. With this mental housekeeping process, you gain as much control as you can over your day. You will unveil aspects that prevent you from filling your routine with enjoyable activities. Treat these as problems in your system that will be solved through focused education, experimentation, and effort.
规划你的晨间惯例、专注工作惯例、其他任务与会议，以及你的夜间惯例。你得一边走一边实验。如果惯例不流畅，就回到笔记本精炼系统。有了这个心智家务流程，你就能对你的每一天取得尽可能多的控制。你会揭示出那些妨碍你用愉快活动填满惯例的面向。把它们当作你系统里的问题，靠专注的教育、实验和努力去解决。
FILL EMPTY USE
填满 · 清空 · 使用
p.157
p.157
To ensure maximum mental output, creativity, and life enjoyment, there are 3 things to consider: how you fill your mind, how you empty your mind, and how you use your mind.
为确保最大的心智产出、创造力和生活享受，有三件事要考虑：你如何填满心智、你如何清空心智、以及你如何使用心智。
p.157
It is up to you to create a daily system with time and practice. If your energy is highest in the morning, schedule your work around that. The same goes for night owls. Gain awareness of when your natural energy is highest and use that time for narrow-focused output. Remember that we are attempting to create our ideal lifestyle. This isn't a one-and-done type deal. This is a lifelong series of experiments that may never reach perfection but will always reach a higher level of enjoyment.
创造一套日常系统、投入时间和练习，取决于你。如果你的能量在早晨最高，就把工作围绕那个来安排。夜猫子也一样。觉察你的自然能量何时最高，并把那段时间用于狭隘聚焦的产出。记住，我们在试图创造自己的理想生活方式。这不是一次搞定的交易。这是一连串终身的实验，也许永远到不了完美，但总会抵达一个更高的享受层级。
p.157
We set the scene in the afternoon, not the morning, why? First, personal preference. Second, because this approach is holistic. Deep work hacks that only mention the time, usually morning, to be productive will always fail. Productivity and creativity are not one-time things, they are states of mind on the spectrum of focus.
我们把场景设在下午，而不是早上，为什么？第一，个人偏好。第二，因为这种方法更整体。那些只提到时间（通常是早晨）的深度工作窍门，总是会失败。生产力与创造力不是一次性的事，它们是专注光谱上的心境状态。
p.157
It is not a matter of deep work. It is a matter of the balance and degree that you engage in deep play, deep rest, and deep work. Living fully is a lost art in a world that overvalues the surface.
这不是“深度工作”的问题。这是平衡与程度的问题：你以何种程度投入深度游玩、深度休息和深度工作。在一个过度看重表层的世界里，完整地活着是一门失落的艺术。
p.157
For value creators, those that intend to put good out into the world, you must adopt the habit of conscious study and education. Without expanding
对价值创造者——那些打算把好东西放进世界的人——你必须采纳有意识的学习与教育这个习惯。不通过让自己暴露于未知中的新奇视角来扩展
p.158
your worldview, mind, and knowledge through exposing yourself to novel perspectives in the unknown, how do you plan to create?
你的世界观、心智和知识，你打算怎么去创造？
p.158
Creativity, in most practical aspects, is about pulling from multiple sources and mashing them together. To be creative from one source, you must deconstruct a topic, learn about its parts through study, and piece together your own creation from those parts like mental Legos.
创造力，在大多数实际层面，就是多方取材、并把它们糅在一起。要从单一来源做到有创造力，你必须解构一个主题、通过研究了解它的各个部分，并像拼心智乐高一样，从那些部件拼出你自己的创造。
p.158
Idea generation is a pillar for the creative worker. You cannot create if the idea does not come first. Novel ideas emerge from conflict of the multiple ideas you hold in your mind from study. As you begin to fill your mind, it would be wise to have a place, physical or digital, to note down ideas. You will struggle to comprehend, make sense of, and piece together ideas from different sources. This is a good sign. When the time is right, the perfect idea will spring into your field of awareness.
想法生成是创造性工作者的支柱。如果想法不先到，你就无法创造。新奇的想法从你因研究而持有的多个想法之间的冲突中涌现。当你开始填满心智时，明智的做法是有一个地方——物理的或数字的——来记下想法。你会挣扎于理解、厘清、并把来自不同来源的想法拼在一起。这是个好迹象。当时机成熟，那个完美的想法会弹进你的觉察场域。
p.158
When aligned with your vision, you can consume information with the intention to understand and apply. This can begin to act as a vessel for raising your consciousness. Don't study to learn the material. Instead, study through the lens of the vision, goal, or problem that is most prevalent in your life. This is how you read a book 3 times in different phases of your life and gain entirely new insights each time around.
与你的愿景对齐时，你可以带着理解并应用的意图去消费信息。这能开始充当一个提升你意识的容器。不要为学材料而学。相反，透过你生活中最突出的那个愿景、目标或问题的透镜去学。这就是你如何在人生不同阶段把一本书读三遍、每次都获得全新的洞见。
p.158
You start to gain clarity on your life's work through exposure to the novel information that sparks excitement in you. This excitement signals that you've found a new potential for your life in the unknown. If you don't know where to start, reread the book that changed the way you move in the world; it will do it again. From there, pick a topic or idea that you did not entirely understand from the book. Research recommendations for information on that topic. Then, repeat the process until you have 5-10 sources that begin to form your life philosophy.
你开始通过暴露于那些在你心里激起兴奋的新奇信息，获得关于自己人生事业的清晰。这份兴奋，标志着你在未知中发现了一个你生活的新可能。如果你不知道从哪开始，重读那本曾改变你在世界中行动方式的书；它会再来一次。从那里，挑一个你从书中没有完全理解的主题或想法。去查找关于该主题的信息推荐。然后重复这个过程，直到你有 5 到 10 个来源开始形成你的人生哲学。
p.158
You fill your mind through self-education in alignment with the purpose you are trying to fulfill or the burning problem you are trying to solve. You cannot create if you don't consume. My recommended way to retain the information you are consuming is to initiate intellectual conversation with
你通过与“你试图实现的目的”或“你试图解决的燃烧问题”一致的自学来填满心智。如果你不消费，就无法创造。我推荐的、用来记住你所消费信息的方式，是与任何人
p.159
anyone and everyone. Talk about your discoveries, let your passion show, and identify your knowledge gaps so you know what to study next.
和每一个人发起智性对话。谈论你的发现，让你的热情显出来，并识别你的知识缺口，好让你知道下一步该学什么。
p.159
In psychology, there is a concept called the Default Mode Network (DMN). From Alex Soojung-Kim Pang, the author of Rest, the DMN is "a series of interconnected sections that activate as soon as people stop concentrating on external tasks and shift from outward-focused to inward-focused cognition." This is how you empty your mind.
在心理学里有一个概念叫默认模式网络（DMN）。据《休息》一书的作者 Alex Soojung-Kim Pang 说，DMN 是“一连串相互连接的区段，一旦人们停止专注于外部任务、并从外向聚焦的认知转向内向聚焦的认知，它们就立刻启动”。这就是你如何清空心智。
p.159
When the DMN is "activated" through restful, meditative, or open-focused activities, the brain isn't any less active than it would be when engaged in something like focused work, or something that demands narrow focus and concentrated attention. This is incredible. Your brain is as active, if not more, when you are at rest than when you are at work.
当 DMN 通过休息性、冥想性或开放聚焦的活动被“启动”时，大脑并不比它投入深度工作、或某项要求狭隘焦点与集中注意力的活动时更不活跃。这不可思议。你在休息时，大脑的活跃程度与工作时相同，甚至更高。
p.159
This can be associated with presence, surrender, and divine inspiration that many masters harp on in their teachings. When your focus is open, your subconscious mind is still working hard and munching on solving the problems in the way of your goals.
这可以联系到许多大师在其教导中反复强调的临在、臣服与神圣灵感。当你的专注是开放的，你的潜意识仍在努力工作、咀嚼那些挡在你目标路上的问题。
p.159
Many computer programmers understand this well. They will often work on a project, encounter a bug, struggle to fix it, give up, and go about their day. At the most unexpected time, the solution will pop into their head and the excited programmer will rush to open their code base and test it out. "Shower thoughts" are the method by which the balanced worker shakes the world From personal experience, my greatest insights come after a period of struggle. My attention is engaged with the natural battle raging in my head to the point of seeing its pointlessness. At this realization, I drop everything but the pillars of my life. I start from scratch. I drop everything and see what sticks without conscious effort. Like magic, the idea I needed comes to me within a few days, and births a season of intensity to actualize that part of my vision.
许多计算机程序员很懂这一点。他们常常会做一个项目、遇到一个 bug、挣扎着修它、放弃、去过自己的日子。在最意想不到的时候，解法会弹进他们脑袋，而兴奋的程序员会冲去打开代码库测试它。“洗澡时的念头”，正是那个平衡的工作者撼动世界的方法。从个人经验看，我最伟大的洞见都来自一段挣扎之后。我的注意力投入到脑中那场自然之战，直到看见它的徒劳。在这个领悟时刻，我放下一切，只留下我生活的支柱。我从零开始。我放下一切，看看在没有刻意努力的情况下什么会留下来。像魔法一样，我所需要的那个想法在几天内来到我这里，并诞生出一个把愿景那部分变为现实的强度季节。
p.159
When you are hyper-focused on a problem in your life, the best way to solve it is counterintuitive. Letting go and engaging with life itself gives
当你高度专注于生活中的一个问题时，解决它的最好方式是反直觉的。放手、投入生活本身，给
p.160
room for the subconscious to work its magic and deliver the "aha!" moment to the conscious mind. Rather than writing to get the best reaction out of your reader, just write. Rather than golfing to get your first hole-in-one, just golf. Rather than speedrunning your favorite hike, just hike. Competition has its place, but when you are stuck on a problem, the best thing you can do is let reality win.
潜意识留出空间去施展它的魔法，并把那个“啊哈！”时刻交付给意识心智。与其为了从读者那里得到最好的反应而写，就只是写。与其为了打出第一个一杆进洞而打高尔夫，就只是打。与其速通你最爱的那条徒步路线，就只是徒步。竞争有它的位置，但当你卡在一个问题上时，你能做的最好的事就是让现实赢。
p.160
Do not confuse restful activities for the modern notion of self-care. While they have their place, true rest does not include emotional binge eating, bubble baths with wine, and late-night movies to escape the thoughts of work the next morning.
别把休息性活动与现代的“自我关怀”观念搞混。它们有各自的位置，但真正的休息不包括情绪性暴食、配红酒的泡泡浴、以及为逃避“明天早上要工作”的念头而看的深夜电影。
p.160
Instead, restful activities are those shift your attention away from work. Go on a long walk. Bathe in nature. Train in the gym. Brain dump your ideas, plans, and compulsive thoughts onto a blank page to clear your mind before bed. Experiment with different activities at all times of the day until you find the ones that are most conducive to your vision.
相反，休息性活动是那些把你的注意力从工作上移开的活动。去长距离散步。沐浴在自然里。在健身房训练。把你的想法、计划和强迫性念头脑内倾倒到空白页面上，好在睡前清空心智。在一天中的各个时段试验不同活动，直到你找到那些对你愿景最有助益的。
p.160
Fill your mind in the afternoons with books, learning, and conversation. Empty your mind with walks, training, and contemplation. Use your mind in the morning with creation, output, and focus.
下午用书、学习和对话填满你的心智。用散步、训练和沉思清空你的心智。早晨用创造、输出和专注使用你的心智。
p.160
Now that we understand the importance of filling our mind with creative firepower and emptying our mind to allow space for creative emergence, we must use that to fuel our focused work.
既然我们理解了“用创造火力填满心智”和“清空心智以便为创造性涌现留出空间”的重要性，我们就必须用这些去为我们的专注工作供能。
THE 4-HOUR WORKDAY
四小时工作日
p.160
p.160
Four hours of focused work is better than 8 hours of distracted work. I don't have an exact date, but as I was building my first freelance business, the idea of a 4-hour workday registered in my awareness. There were talks of 4-hour workweeks by people like Tim Ferris, but a 4-hour workday sounded realistic enough to make work for my level of mind at the time. The challenge pushed me toward long-term action rather than anxiety. I
四小时的专注工作胜过 8 小时的分心工作。我没有确切日期，但当我正在建立我第一门自由职业生意时，“四小时工作日”这个想法登记进了我的觉察。当时有人在谈论蒂姆·费里斯那样的“四小时工作周”，但“四小时工作日”听起来足够现实，能为我当时的心智层级所用。那个挑战把我推向长期行动，而不是焦虑。
p.161
knew I had the resources, mental capacity, and desire to make that lifestyle real, even if it took a decade.
我知道我有资源、心智容量和渴望，去把那种生活方式变成现实，即便要花十年。
p.161
This seemingly crazy idea stuck in my mind for years to come and throughout my plethora of business failures. Subconsciously, I was making decisions to limit how much I worked to 4 hours each day. I was loosely identified as someone who would work less yet achieve more than others, so my actions naturally followed to survive that identity I was building. This alone changed the direction of my life. Why? First, I perceived anything more than 4 hours of work as a problem. I had conditioned myself to view anything more than 4 hours of work as abnormal. Few people do this. Most people label this lifestyle as "impossible" and then it becomes so. If I had never registered anything more than 4 hours of work as a problem, my mind would not register opportunities to create a solution for those problems. A meaningful goal acts as a filter for the information you are exposed to daily.
这个看似疯狂的想法在我脑中停留了许多年，贯穿我那一连串的商业失败。潜意识里，我在做决定，把每天的工作量限制在 4 小时。我松散地把自己认同为一个“工作更少却成就比他人更多”的人，所以我的行动自然跟着走，以让那个我正在构建的身份存活。仅这一点就改变了我人生的方向。为什么？第一，我把任何超过 4 小时的工作都感知为一个问题。我把自己条件化成“把超过 4 小时的工作视为不正常”。很少有人这么做。大多数人把这种生活方式贴上“不可能”的标签，然后它就真的变成不可能。如果我从没把“超过 4 小时的工作”登记为一个问题，我的心智就不会登记“为那些问题创造解法”的机会。一个有意义的目标，充当着你每天所暴露信息的一个过滤器。
p.161
This forced my mind to work on a creative solution for these specific problems to eliminate, systemize, or automate low-leverage work. At a job, that means organizing your highest-priority work, identifying distractions, and being honest with yourself about how much work you actually have to do. Many people can reduce how much they work at their job, then spend that new free time on actualizing their life's work. In business, that means outsourcing, productizing, or building more leverage. So that's what I did. For most people, this idealistic 4-hour workday cannot be accomplished immediately. It can, however, become a potent aspect of your vision so that you can begin to register opportunity in your awareness. The tips we discuss can help reduce the time you spend on work at your job, help you build out a side project in record time, or help you bring order to the uncertain nature of your entrepreneurial endeavors.
这迫使我的心智去为这些具体问题想出一个创造性的解法，去消除、系统化或自动化低杠杆的工作。在一份工作上，那意味着组织你最高优先级的任务、识别干扰，并对自己诚实：你到底有多少工作必须做。许多人能减少自己在工作岗位上工作的时间，然后把那新腾出的空闲时间用于实现自己的人生事业。在生意上，那意味着外包、产品化，或建立更多杠杆。所以我就那样做了。对大多数人来说，这个理想化的四小时工作日无法立即实现。然而，它可以成为你愿景中一个强有力的面向，让你能开始在你的觉察中登记机会。我们讨论的这些小技巧，能帮你减少在工作上花的时间、帮你以创纪录的速度建出一个副项目，或帮你把创业努力那不确定的本性带入秩序。
p.161
As humans, we have a natural desire for more. We are driven to survive at all costs. Evolution reflects this. With our unique minds, we build systems to aid in the survival of physical and mental forms. This may sound
作为人类，我们对“更多”有一种自然的渴望。我们被驱动着不惜一切代价去生存。演化反映了这一点。用我们独特的心智，我们构建系统去帮助物理与心智形式的存活。这听起来可能
p.162
repetitive, and it is, because it's important. Entropy never sleeps and we must constantly work to protect the order we create in our lives.
很重复，而它确实重复，因为它很重要。熵从不睡觉，我们必须不断努力去保护我们在生活中创造出的秩序。
p.162
Systems layer on top of each other to make our mind more efficient. We get better at 'investing' our mental energy. If we don't maintain these systems, they fall apart. Now, what does entropy have to do with focused work and productivity? If you don't systemize your path to success, with time and focused effort, you won't achieve it. And if you don't maintain order in the productivity system you create, you allow room for procrastination. Your productivity system is one out of many that will be messy at the start. Even if you copy it from your favorite productivity teacher. Your lifestyle and work have many nuances that can only be accounted for in your direct experience. Through experimentation, failure, and problem-solving, your routine will become more enjoyable and efficient the longer you stick to the path.
系统层层堆叠，让我们的心智更高效。我们变得更擅长“投资”我们的心智能量。如果我们不维护这些系统，它们就会土崩瓦解。那么，熵与专注工作和生产力有什么关系？如果你不把你的成功路径系统化，带着时间和专注的努力，你无法实现它。而如果你不维护你创造出的生产力系统里的秩序，你就给拖延留出了空间。你的生产力系统是众多系统中、开头必定会很乱的那一个。即便你是从你最爱的生产力老师那里复制来的。你的生活方式和工作有许多细微之处，只有在你的直接经验里才能被考虑到。通过实验、失败和问题解决，只要你坚持在这条路上，你的惯例就会变得越享受、越高效。
p.162
Productivity is about getting from point A to point B as fast as possible. Productivity is not about seeing who can work the longest so you can brag to your friends, family, and coworkers. Like your home bookshelf, if you don't have a system for your work, you will get overwhelmed with the tasks that continue to scatter in front of you.
生产力在于尽快从 A 点到达 B 点。生产力不在于看谁能工作最久，好让你能向朋友、家人和同事炫耀。就像你家里的书架一样，如果你没有一套用于工作的系统，你会被那些继续在你眼前散落的任务压垮。
p.162
When you are overwhelmed, if you don't have a system, routine, or plan to focus your mind, the intensity of that overwhelm will increase. Now that when entropy has its grasp on your productivity, it may lead to a week-long downward spiral of emotions and laziness. Nobody wants that.
当你被压垮时，如果你没有一套系统、惯例或计划来聚焦你的心智，那份不堪重负的强度会增加。而当熵抓住了你的生产力，它可能导致一场持续一周的情绪与懒散的下行螺旋。没人想要那样。
p.162
If you were to loosely identify with a positive version of success and the projects that will take you there, you will have the desire to refine a path to aid in the survival of those concepts. If you create a vision for your future that holds meaning, you will subconsciously work to survive that vision. If you create an identity that makes the automatic decision to build your future for 4 hours every day, you will work to survive that identity. Even if you can only spend thirty minutes on that vision at this point in your life.
如果你松散地把自己认同为一个正面版本的“成功”以及那些将带你抵达那里的项目，你就会拥有渴望去精炼一条路径，以帮助那些概念的存活。如果你为自己的未来创造出一个持有意义的愿景，你就会潜意识地努力去让那个愿景存活。如果你创造出一个“每天自动决定用 4 小时构建未来”的身份，你就会努力去让那个身份存活。即便在你现在的人生阶段，你只能把三十分钟花在那个愿景上。
p.163
Why? Because if you don't survive the things that make you, you, then you experience the concept of death. The thought of death fills us with fear because it is the embodiment of the absolute unknown. If we don't live at our edge, a chaotic state of mind is the default.
为什么？因为如果你不去让那些“造就你之所以为你”的东西存活，你就会体验“死亡”这个概念。对死亡的念头让我们充满恐惧，因为它是绝对未知的化身。如果我们不在自己的边缘上活着，一种混乱的心之状态就是默认。
p.163
We can either transmute that fear toward beneficial outcomes or become slaves to it. So, let's take a meta-approach to productivity. I am not going to give you exact steps. A prescriptive "how" is not as powerful as you think, even when that's what your mind craves. Instead, I will give you a few helpful starting points so you can begin to create your own "how" with time, experimentation, and iteration.
我们要么能把那份恐惧炼化成有益的结果，要么成为它的奴隶。所以，让我们对生产力采取一个元层面的方法。我不会给你确切的步骤。一个处方式的“怎么做”没有你以为的那么强大，即便那正是你心智所渴望的。相反，我会给你几个有用的起点，让你能随时间、实验和迭代开始创造出你自己的“怎么做”。
p.163
First, why 4 hours? Conceptual systems need mental energy to thrive. From personal experience, scientific studies, and anecdotes from the world's most respected creatives, 3-5 hours is the sweet spot for mental energy expenditure. Focus is a muscle that fatigues with time. At the start, you will notice the difficulty of pure unbroken focus for even thirty minutes. As you train your focus through conscious repetition, you will be able to do more quality work in 4 hours than the average individual can in a week.
第一，为什么是 4 小时？概念性系统需要心智能量才能繁荣。从个人经验、科学研究，以及世上最受尊敬的创作者们的轶事来看，3 到 5 小时是心智能量消耗的最佳点。专注是一块随时间而疲劳的肌肉。开头，你会注意到纯粹不间断地专注哪怕三十分钟都有多难。当你通过有意识的重复训练你的专注，你就能在 4 小时内做出比普通人一周还多的优质工作。
p.163
Second, 4 hours creates the frame of a game that you can play to win. If you play the character of someone that only works 4 hours, and you've internalized that trait, then you will feel the pressure to complete your work within that time. Even better, when you chunk that work session up into smaller time blocks, you create a powerful environment to narrow your focus into a productive state of good stress.
第二，4 小时创造出一个你能玩来取胜的游戏框架。如果你扮演一个只工作 4 小时的角色，而你已经把这个特质内化了，那你就会感到压力要在那个时间内完成工作。更好的是，当你把那个工作时块切成更小的时间块，你就创造出一个强大的环境，把你的焦点收窄进一种“好的压力”的生产性状态。
p.163
I would encourage you to train your focus on your current work. Start by setting a timer for fifteen minutes of pure focus on a high-priority task, no distractions. After a few days, increase that time to thirty minutes, then forty-five, then an hour. Like building a muscle. You won't be able to focus for a metaphorical 495-pound bench press on your first try.
我会鼓励你把专注训练在你当前的工作上。先设一个十五分钟纯粹专注的计时器，投入一件高优先级任务，不被打扰。几天之后，把时间增到三十分钟，然后四十五分钟，然后一小时。就像练肌肉。你不可能第一次尝试就做一次比喻意义上的 495 磅卧推。
p.163
Most people don't have 4 hours to work on their own thing. So don't feel like you have to work this long if you have other responsibilities right now. Don't let the expectations I set in this book prevent you from facing the
大多数人没有 4 小时来做自己的事。所以如果你现在有其他责任，不要觉得你也必须工作这么久。不要让我在这本书里设下的期待妨碍你面对
p.164
reality of your situation. Do what you can, start small, and work your way up the challenge ladder in all areas of life. Anybody can set aside thirty to sixty minutes every morning to build out their dreams. Sure, it may take a week to get used to waking up earlier, and you may need to sacrifice nightly bad habits that you don't want to break to get to bed on time, but the fact remains that anybody can do it.
自己处境的现实。做你能做的，从小处开始，并在生活的所有领域里沿着挑战阶梯往上走。任何人都能每天早上腾出三十到六十分钟来构建自己的梦想。当然，习惯早起可能要一周，而你可能需要牺牲那些你不想打破的夜间坏习惯才能按时上床，但事实仍然是：任何人都能做到。
p.164
If you can spend 8 hours building someone else's dreams, you can spend 1 hour building your own. Every individual that wants more out of life needs a dedicated vision building session. Your vision isn't going to build itself. You must carve out time no matter how small at the start. During this dedicated vision-building session, the choice of tasks you perform are crucial.
如果你能花 8 小时构建别人的梦想，你就能花 1 小时构建自己的。每个想从生活中获得更多的个体，都需要一场专门的愿景构建会。你的愿景不会自己建起来。你必须在开头凿出时间，无论多小。在这场专门的愿景构建会里，你选择执行哪些任务至关重要。
p.164
First, identify where you are in relation to your goals. Do you have the clarity to execute on the tasks that will bring meaningful results? Or do you need to use that time for self-education and study? Remember that you are creating a playable game here. Nobody starts out as an expert. They graduate from novice to intermediate to advanced, with a balance of education and practice to match that progression.
第一，识别你相对于目标所处的位置。你是否有清晰去执行那些会带来有意义结果的任务？还是你需要把那个时间用于自学和研究？记住，你在这里创造的是一个可玩的游戏。没人一开始就是专家。他们从新手毕业到中级到高级，用与那个进程相匹配的教育与练习的平衡。
p.164
Every morning, be sure that you are performing tasks that move levers. Lever-moving tasks are the actions that generate results. If you aren't getting results, that is feedback to change what you are doing. Without positive feedback, there is a growing potential for rogue thoughts, emotions, and external stimuli to grab at your attention.
每天早上，确保你在执行那些撬动杠杆的任务。撬动杠杆的任务是能产生结果的行为。如果你没拿到结果，那就是改变你正在做什么的反馈。没有正面反馈，那些“野生的念头、情绪和外部刺激抓住你注意力”的可能性就会增长。
p.164
Distractions are the catalyst of entropy in your productivity system. The more distractions you give the chance to penetrate your awareness, the more likely you will be to go into a downward spiral of procrastination. The most effective advice I can give is to condition your internal and external environment to be distraction-free. Set your alarm an hour earlier to wake up before the distractions. Stick to a routine that makes work sessions seamless and efficient with practice. Hold the idea of your holistic, ideal lifestyle in your mind as you go about your creative endeavors. None
干扰是你生产力系统里熵的催化剂。你给越多干扰机会去穿透你的觉察，你就越可能进入一场拖延的下行螺旋。我能给出的最有效建议，是把你的内在与外在环境条件化成无干扰的。把闹钟设早一小时，在干扰之前醒来。坚持一套让工作时段随练习变得无缝且高效的惯例。在你进行创造性努力时，把那个整体性的理想生活方式放在心里。以上
p.165
of this is immediate, but with a vision-aligned intent to build, you will surprise yourself on even a 6-month timescale. Focused work is how you change your life in record time.
没有一样是即时的，但带着一个与愿景一致的构建意图，即便在 6 个月的时间尺度上，你也会让自己吃惊。专注工作是你以创纪录速度改变人生的方式。
THE SKILL STACK
技能组合
p.166
p.166
The state of work is changing. Specialists are out, but so are generalists. We live in a time of specialized generalism. You must pursue your curiosity, become obsessed with one crevice of reality, stack skills to solve burning problems within that domain, and let the base of your skill tree spread its roots into other connected domains.
工作的状态正在变化。专才是过时的，通才也是。我们生活在一个专业化的通才时代。你必须追求好奇心、痴迷于现实的一个裂缝、堆叠技能去解决那个领域内燃烧的问题，并让你技能树的根基蔓延到其他相连的领域。
p.166
Learning one skill isn't enough, especially if that skill is compartmentalized, predictable, and lacks the need for creativity. If you can be trained into it, so can everyone else, and so can a robot. The difference between a human and a robot is consciousness. Consciousness is the clay of reality in which we create through order, routine, and minimizing states of chaos.
只学一项技能是不够的，尤其当那项技能是被隔离开的、可预测的、且不需要创造力的时候。如果你能被训练掌握它，那其他人也能，机器人也能。人与机器人的区别是意识。意识是现实的黏土，我们通过秩序、惯例以及最小化混乱状态，在其中进行创造。
p.166
The Renaissance Era came after the famine, pandemics, and ignorance of the Dark Ages. It was a cultural, political, and economic rebirth that housed many of the thinkers, artists, and scientists we know today. One could say it was the creative emergence that went on to transcend and include the lessons from a period of struggle.
文艺复兴时代跟在黑暗时代的饥荒、瘟疫与无知之后到来。它是一场文化、政治和经济的重生，容纳了我们今天所知的许多思想家、艺术家和科学家。可以说它是那场创造性的涌现：它去超越并包含了来自一段挣扎时期的教训。
p.166
During these times, there was what we know as a "Renaissance man," a person who had a range of skills across multiple domains like art, science, literature, music, and politics. Their critical thinking and creativity only helped with the application of their knowledge.
在那个时代，存在我们所说的“文艺复兴人”——一个在艺术、科学、文学、音乐和政治等多个领域都有广泛技能的人。他们的批判性思维和创造力，只会有助于他们知识的应用。
p.167
In this Digital Renaissance of the 3rd millennium, we can notice similar patterns. Technological advancements have made it possible to learn new skills that were previously reserved for specialists, usually the ones that have the cash to afford specialized education.
在第三个千年的这场数字文艺复兴里，我们能注意到类似的模式。技术进步使学习那些此前只留给专才（通常是那些有钱负担专业教育的人）的新技能成为可能。
p.167
As an example, anyone with a few hours to spare can watch a tutorial on web design, purchase website software for less than a nice dinner, and build a what-looks-to-be professionally designed site. Or you can just talk to an artificial intelligence engine and have it build one for you. That way, you can focus your education on creating, selling, and iterating on a product or service that actually gets you paid.
举个例子，任何一个有几小时空闲的人，都能看一段网页设计的教程、用不到一顿好晚餐的钱购买网站软件、并建出一个看起来由专业人士设计的网站。或者你可以直接跟一个人工智能引擎说话，让它给你建一个。那样，你就能把教育集中在创造、销售、以及迭代一个真能让你赚到钱的产品或服务上。
p.167
There are no limits, aside from pleasurable distractions, to what you can learn and apply as one person. Individuals can learn design, marketing, writing, and video to run a multimillion-dollar business selling a solution to the problem they've solved in their lives. I purchased a pair of blue light glasses yesterday from an individual that did just this. They struggled with eye strain and sleep, studied potential solutions, experimented with them, and created a stylish pair of glasses that solves the problem. Since this was a personal endeavor, and since they built a readership online, they have very little competition with the big brands selling the same product with little soul behind it.
除开那些令人愉快的干扰，作为一个人，你能学并应用的东西没有极限。个体可以学习设计、营销、写作和视频，去运营一门价值数百万美元的生意，卖一个“解决他们自己生活中已解决问题”的解法。我昨天从一个正是这么做的个体那里买了一副蓝光眼镜。他们曾受眼疲劳和睡眠问题困扰、研究了潜在解法、实验了它们，并创造出一副时髦的眼镜来解决这个问题。由于这是一项个人的努力，且由于他们在网上建立了一批读者，他们与那些卖同样产品、背后却没什么灵魂的大品牌之间几乎没有竞争。
p.167
For that to be a possibility for you, you not only need value to offer, which comes from your personal development and skill acquisition. But you need to pair that specialty with a general understanding of the modern skills that allow you to put your payment-worthy value in front of a fraction of the billions of people you can reach on the internet. Now that you have awareness of this, try to notice it when you are exploring the digital world. View brands, content, and products from the lens of a researcher, not a consumer, and you will pick up lessons that can aid in the actualization of your goals.
要让那成为你的可能，你不仅需要提供价值——那来自你的个人发展和技能习得。你还必须把那份专长与对现代技能的通用理解配对，好让你能把你值得付费的价值，放到你在互联网上能触及的数十亿人中的一小部分面前。既然你已觉察到这一点，就试着在你探索数字世界时注意到它。以研究者的透镜、而不是消费者的透镜去看品牌、内容和产品，你就会拾起能帮助实现你目标的教训。
p.167
In my teens and early twenties, I had a general obsession for learning and building. I have always had a potentially monetizable side project to work on to shine a light on the skills I needed to acquire through self-education.
在我的青少年和二十岁出头时期，我对学习和构建有一种普遍的痴迷。我一直有一个潜在可变现的副项目要做，以此照亮我需要通过自学获得的技能。
p.168
In the course of 10 years, I obsessed over fitness, nutrition, search engine optimization, web design and development, graphic design, digital art, social media, content writing, marketing and sales, copywriting, neuroscience, philosophy, spirituality, self-development, and a few more, but I'll spare you my self-aggrandizing list of polymathic study.
在 10 年过程中，我痴迷于健身、营养、搜索引擎优化、网页设计与开发、平面设计、数字艺术、社交媒体、内容写作、营销与销售、文案、神经科学、哲学、灵性、自我发展，以及另外几样，但我会省去我这份自我夸耀式的博学清单。
p.168
What were the results after a decade? The one thing that people tell you is impossible: doing what I love for a living. And even if they don't verbally say it's impossible, they imply it through their attempts to impregnate your mind with their limiting worldview.
十年之后的结果是什么？那件人们告诉你不可能是的事：靠做自己热爱的事谋生。而即便他们嘴上不说它不可能，他们也通过试图用自己那限制性的世界观给你洗脑，来暗示这一点。
p.168
So, let's take a big-picture approach to modern skill acquisition. I will not give you exact steps, as this isn't a course or classroom. But I will give you the principles. From those, you must start, encounter a real-world problem, and self-educate in a manner that teaches you the subjective technical details of any domain through experience. You may not understand the teachings below for months or years depending on your current experience level. Lessons you pick up along the way will compound into one big "aha!" moment. From there, you can make your dreams real.
所以，让我们对现代技能习得采取一个大局的方法。我不会给你确切步骤，因为这不是课程或教室。但我会给你原则。从那些原则出发，你必须开始、遇到一个真实世界的问题、并以一种通过经验教你任何领域主观技术细节的方式自学。取决于你当前的经验层级，你可能要数月或数年才理解下面的教导。你沿途拾起的教训会复利成一个巨大的“啊哈！”时刻。从那里，你就能让你的梦想成真。
p.168
I'm assuming you want to acquire skills so that you can create an independent income source. Even if you only want to learn skills for the sake of advancing your career, you are doing it because your psyche craves challenge. Eventually that challenge will cease to exist in a corporate hierarchy. It would make sense to cut to the chase and go straight into building your own thing. To do that, you will be exchanging value with other humans for value in the form of time, money, leverage, information, and expertise.
我假设你获取技能，是为了能创造一份独立的收入来源。即便你只想为了推进职业而学技能，你这么做也是因为你的心灵渴望挑战。最终那个挑战会在公司层级里停止存在。直接切入正题、一路走进构建自己的东西，会是合理的。要做到那一点，你将与他人交换价值，换取时间、金钱、杠杆、信息和专长形式的价值。
p.168
Every single skill you learn should be approached from the perspective of human nature and psychology. That's all modern skills are, a modality for capturing attention, holding attention, and delivering value on attention. Business is about transferring consciousness into your customer and framing focus toward a shared desired outcome for mutual benefit.
你学到的每一项技能，都应该从人性与心理学的视角去接近。现代技能的全部，就是一种捕获注意力、保持注意力、并在这份注意力上交付价值的模态。商业就是把意识转移进你的客户、并把焦点框向一个共享的理想结果，以实现互利。
p.169
So, we need 3 things. A valuable message, a medium for distribution, and a results-oriented skill for delivering a transformation. Then, we can eliminate competition through individuality and compound results with our increasing ability to solve creative problems.
所以，我们需要三样东西。一个有价值的讯息、一个分发媒介，以及一项以结果为导向的、用于交付转变的技能。然后，我们就能通过个体性消除竞争，并用我们不断增长的解决创造性问题的能力去复利结果。
THE MESSAGE
讯息
p.169
p.169
A valuable message is a way to communicate with others that is relatable, understandable, or actionable. If it isn't perceived as valuable, it won't capture attention. If it doesn't capture attention, how are they going to see the true value you provide? This is the first limiting belief that many must dissolve: you have to learn how to capture attention if you want anything (including money) from someone else. Attention-capture techniques are neutral until put into evil hands.
一个有价值的讯息，是一种与他人沟通的方式，它是可共鸣的、可理解的，或可行动的。如果它不被感知为有价值，它就不会捕获注意力。如果它不捕获注意力，他们怎么会看见你所提供的真正价值？这是许多人必须消解的第一个限制性信念：如果你想从别人那里得到任何东西（包括钱），你必须学会如何捕获注意力。捕获注意力的技术在被放进邪恶之手前是中性的。
p.169
Value is determined by perception. And as we've learned, perception is influenced by an individual's worldview. A young person may see the value in riches, while an old person may see the value in peace. To understand this, learn marketing and sales. These skills pull from psychological principles and apply them to the transactional nature of business. Marketing and sales give you a practical approach to learning about the human psyche in the real world.
价值由感知决定。而如我们所学，感知受个体的世界观影响。一个年轻人可能在财富中看到价值，而一个老人可能在平静中看到价值。为理解这一点，去学营销和销售。这些技能从心理学原则中取材，并应用到商业的交易本性上。营销和销售给你一条实用的路径，去在真实世界里学习人类心灵。
p.169
Now, some may have certain beliefs and ideas that come to mind at the talk of these potentially unethical skills. Used car salesmen and experiences with pushy scammers stick out to you more than how 100% of the population unconsciously manipulates one another with the same methods.
