The world's most successful people are those that use unethical skills in an ethical manner. Everyone has a dark side, and if you don't integrate that dark side through skills like marketing and sales, you will go on to manipulate others in a way that contributes to collective regress. Rid yourself of your illusory beliefs and channel the skills you acquire toward your ideal future.
现在，有些人一听到这些潜在不道德的技能，脑中就会浮现某些信念和想法。二手车销售员、以及跟强推销骗子的经历，比“100% 的人口都用同样方法无意识地互相操纵”这件事更让你印象深刻。世上最成功的人，是那些以合乎伦理的方式使用不道德技能的人。每个人都有黑暗面，而如果你不通过营销和销售这样的技能去整合那个黑暗面，你就会以一种为集体退步做贡献的方式去操纵他人。摆脱你那虚幻的信念，把你获得的技能引向你的理想未来。
p.170
Marketing is how you craft a message that is attention-grabbing, relevant, and valuable for a specific person or identity. Identity houses their goalcentric perspective, houses the perception of their problems. Sales is a process for making people aware of their problems, showing them how that problem is impacting their lives, and presenting a solution to achieve their goals.
营销，是你如何打造一个能抓注意力、相关、且对某个特定人或身份有价值的讯息。身份容纳着他们以目标为中心的视角，容纳着他们对自己问题的感知。销售，是一个让人觉察到自己的问题、向他们展示那个问题如何影响他们的生活、并呈现一个达成他们目标的解法的过程。
p.170
The best way to understand these evergreen skills is through a transformation. That's what people want. Humans have a desire for more, and to accomplish that, they must evolve. On the Universal scale, a story is a transformation. Music is an audible story. A sculpture is frozen music. Humans find meaning in transformations, and if you want to gather people that find value in what you have to offer, base the message you put out around an implied "before and after" with a clear path in between.
理解这些常青技能的最好方式，是通过一次“转变”。那正是人们想要的。人类有一种对“更多”的渴望，而要达成它，他们必须演化。在宇宙尺度上，一个故事就是一次转变。音乐是一个可听见的故事。雕塑是被冻结的音乐。人类在转变中找到意义；而如果你想聚集那些在你所提供之物中找到价值的人，就把你发出的讯息建立在一种隐含的“之前与之后”，中间有一条清晰路径。
p.170
All good stories start with a problem that opens a curiosity loop to capture attention. Once they've hooked the reader, they agitate the problem, relate with them through personal experience, and provide a potential solution that proves it can help them achieve the transformation they desire. You can notice this pattern by observing any form of media with a conscious mind. Look for implied problems, pains, solutions, and benefits that form a soft story structure. Look beyond the literal.
所有好故事都从一个问题开始，它打开一个好奇回路来捕获注意力。一旦钩住了读者，他们就搅动那个问题，通过个人经验与他们共鸣，并提供一个潜在解法，证明它能帮他们达成所渴望的转变。你可以用一颗有意识的心去观察任何形式的媒体，就能注意到这个模式。去寻找那些隐含的问题、痛、解法和益处，它们构成一个柔和的故事结构。看透字面。
p.170
Now, we don't want people to see your valuable message and not change their behavior in a positive manner. If your message does not influence another's actions, it falls short of impact. But don't think that you must push them toward action. Your ideas can help form their worldview in a way that influences their positive decision-making over weeks, months, and years. This is where gamification comes into play, as games are just guided stories. You don't push your worldview, you illustrate it with a wellarticulated message and let people make their own decisions.
现在，我们不想让人看见你那条有价值的讯息、却不以正面方式改变自己的行为。如果你的讯息不影响他人的行动，它就没达到影响力。但别以为你必须把他们推向行动。你的想法可以帮助形成他们的世界观，从而在数周、数月、数年里影响他们正面的决策。这就是游戏化的用武之地，因为游戏不过是受引导的故事。你不去强推销你的世界观，而是用一个表达良好的讯息去阐明它，并让人们自己做决定。
p.170
When we dissect the concept of a game, we uncover the structure of a valuable message. Every player is at their own experience level. They each have their unique strengths, weaknesses, likes, and dislikes. And they
当我们解剖“游戏”这个概念，我们就揭开了有价值讯息的结构。每个玩家都处在自己的经验层级上。他们各自有独特的长处、短处、喜好和厌恶。而他们
p.171
oscillate between unawareness and awareness of the problems and solutions available to them for their current situation.
在“对自己当前处境可用的那些问题与解法”的无觉察与觉察之间振荡。
p.171
There are other aspects of games, like incentives to progress, but the point is that people want to win the game. If you can position your value in a way that helps them do that, they will help you win the game you are playing in return.
游戏还有其他面向，比如“进步激励”，但要点是：人们想赢下这场游戏。如果你能把你的价值定位成帮他们做到那一点，他们也会反过来帮你赢下你正在玩的游戏。
p.171
Now, understand that there is more than one player at any given level of the game. A majority of them are in the beginner stage, less in the intermediate, and few in the advanced. A natural hierarchy.
现在要明白，在游戏的任何一个层级上都不止一个玩家。他们中大多数处在初学阶段，中级较少，高级更少。一个自然的层级。
p.171
Not only that, but you must consider the hierarchy of goals that you are guiding people through. Your message will need to be carefully crafted depending on where people can view it. If more people can find your message, like on social media, it will start broad and at a beginner level. Then, it is your job to guide those that want to be guided toward the intermediate and advanced levels.
不仅如此，你还必须考虑你正在引导人们走过的那套目标层级。你的讯息需要根据人们能在哪里看见它而被精心打造。如果更多人能找到你的讯息，比如在社交媒体上，它就会从宽广、初学层级开始。然后，你的工作就是引导那些想被引导的人走向中级和高级层级。
p.171
Your job is to understand a specific group of people, study their problems, reflect on your experience from solving your own, and create a solution in the form of a product to help them reach the next stage. As you create and execute on the purpose, path, and priority framework from earlier, you will have the perfect marketing strategy laid out for you. The purpose is the specific result you are marketing toward people. Your path is the solution for getting there (which took trial, error, and experience to create). The priority is the burning problem your potential customer must solve in their life. When you build, market, and sell to yourself, you create a niche of one that others struggle to compete with.
你的工作是理解一个特定人群、研究他们的问题、反思你自己解决同类问题时的经验，并以一个产品的形式创造出解法，帮他们抵达下一阶段。当你创造并执行之前讲过的“目的、路径、优先级”框架时，你就会被摆出一套完美的营销策略。那个目的，就是你正在向人们营销的那个具体结果。你的路径，就是抵达那里的解法（它需要试错和经验才能创造出来）。那个优先级，就是你的潜在客户必须在生活中解决的燃烧问题。当你向自己构建、营销并销售时，你就创造出一个别人难以与之竞争的“只有一个人的利基”。
p.171
With a shared goal, clarity on how to reach it, and guided action, you create a frame that both you and your potential customer can operate within. You have already experienced the lows and highs; now you must guide others through them.
带着一个共享目标、关于如何抵达它的清晰、以及被引导的行动，你创造出一个你与潜在客户都能在其中运作的框架。你已经体验过那些低点和高点；现在你必须引导他人穿过它们。
p.171
The valuable message you craft should educate, entertain, and inspire others to solve their problems and actualize their potential. But you need a way to
你所打造的有价值讯息，应当教育、娱乐并启发他人去解决自己的问题、实现自己的潜能。但你需要一种方式去
p.172
get this message in front of people.
把这条讯息送到人们面前。
THE MEDIUM
媒介
p.172
p.172
In life, discipline equals freedom. In business, distribution equals freedom. Distribution is the process of sending and receiving value, free or paid. In the digital age, distribution is no longer limited to a physical location with limited customers and high overhead. Nor is it limited to where you can ship a physical product. Both of those still work, of course, but they strip the power away from the individual.
在生活中，自律等于自由。在商业中，分发等于自由。分发就是发送与接收价值的过程，免费的或付费的。在数字时代，分发不再局限于一个顾客有限、开销高昂的实体位置。也不再局限于你能把实体产品寄到哪里。那两种当然仍然可行，但它们把权力从个体手里剥走了。
p.172
Today, individuals can publish anything for the world to see, build an audience small or large, and monetize their skills, beginner or advanced. But this is only possible if you zoom out to observe, study, and understand the great online game.
今天，个体可以发布任何东西供世界观看、建立或大或小的受众、并把自己的技能变现，无论初学还是高级。但只有当你拉远镜头去观察、研究并理解那场宏大的线上游戏时，这才有可能。
p.172
The back end of the internet is code, and the front end is media. Coding is a great high-value skill to learn, especially when paired with marketing know-how, but we will be focusing on the creative aspect of business. Distribution comes from the combination of media and code. Technical know-how, paired with the ability to articulate your value, is how anyone can earn an independent income.
互联网的后端是代码，前端是媒体。编程是一项很值得学的高价值技能，尤其与营销知识配对时，但我们会聚焦于商业的创造性面向。分发来自媒体与代码的结合。技术知识，配上表达你价值的能力，是任何人赚取独立收入的方式。
p.172
Social media is the most accessible form of distribution of a message at zero cost. Beyond that, there are website builders, blog and membership platforms, and organizational tools that can be used as digital real estate for a message that holds more depth. I often think about how this technology would have been used by our favorite ancients, masters, artists, and thinkers. They would have been ecstatic about the creative potential it offers. There are thousands of public figures and thought leaders we love today, and that only makes me sad for the voices of the past that were stifled because they lacked distribution.
社交媒体是以零成本分发讯息的最可获取的形式。除此之外，还有建站工具、博客与会员平台，以及组织工具，可以用作承载更有深度讯息的数字地产。我常想，这项技术若被我们最爱的古人、大师、艺术家和思想家所用会如何。他们会为它所提供的创造性潜能欣喜若狂。我们今天喜爱的公众人物和思想领袖有成千上万，而这只让我为那些因缺乏分发而被压抑的过去之声感到悲伤。
p.173
The mediums for distributing your message are writing and speaking.
分发你讯息的媒介是写作和口说。
p.173
Writing is the vehicle for articulated thought and communication. It is the medium for putting your message in front of those that can adopt the perspective it presents and operate within that shared reality. Marketing and sales allow you to craft a valuable message. Writing and speaking allow you to distribute that message. Study them all and you won't need to worry about money, replacement, or your career.
写作是被表达清楚的思想与沟通的载体。它是把你的讯息放到那些能采纳它所呈现的视角、并在那个共享现实中运作的人面前的媒介。营销和销售让你打造一条有价值的讯息。写作和口说让你分发那条讯息。把它们全都研究一遍，你就不必再担心钱、被替换，或你的职业。
p.173
From that writing, or without it, you can speak in public or on video to bring a new dimension to your message. Speaking brings a new dimension to writing, but I will spare you the technical details. Start with writing, as it will only enhance your ability to speak in the future. With the right message and a tactical strategy for the platform you are using, attracting readers, customers, or like-minded individuals isn't too far out of reach.
从那些写作出发，或者不用它，你可以在公开场合或视频里讲话，为你讯息带来一个新的维度。口说为写作带来新的维度，但我会省去技术细节。从写作开始，因为它只会增强你未来说话的能力。有了正确的讯息和针对你所使用平台的战术策略，吸引读者、客户或同频的人，并非遥不可及。
p.173
If you don't have the ability to get your message, in any form, in front of a specific group of people, how are you going to make an income for yourself?
如果你没有能力把你的讯息——无论以何种形式——送到一个特定人群面前，你打算怎么为自己挣一份收入？
p.173
No matter the size of your business, and whether or not you want to frame the value you have to offer as a business, you need people and a product. Your message and chosen medium - multiplied by the power of the internet- bridge the gap between people and product.
不论你生意的大小，也不论你是否想把所提供的价值框为“一门生意”，你都需要人和产品。你的讯息和你选定的媒介——乘以互联网的力量——搭起了人与产品之间的桥。
p.173
This alone is what led to the destruction of my past businesses. I was too focused on perfecting my product but didn't prioritize getting that product in front of people that cared about the product. Even further, I didn't realize that I could attract and nurture a community of people to the point of becoming customers through my writing.
仅这一点就是我过去那些生意被毁的原因。我太专注于完善我的产品，却没把“把那个产品送到在意它的人面前”排到优先。更进一步，我甚至没意识到自己可以通过写作吸引并培育一个社群，直到他们成为客户。
p.173
"Business" holds a lot of negative connotations that manifest as limiting beliefs for most people. Business is just getting paid for your contribution to the future, hopefully a better one, by whatever means you have available to you. The internet is available to almost everyone.
“商业”带有许多负面含义，对大多数人来说，那些含义显现为限制性信念。商业不过是为你对未来的贡献——但愿是更好的未来——而获得报酬，用你手上可用的任何手段。互联网几乎对所有人可用。
p.173
These principles reflect on more planes than business. When trying to find an ideal partner, or just trying to make friends, you need people and a
这些原则在商业之外的更多层面上成立。在试图寻找理想伴侣，或只是想交朋友时，你需要人和一个
p.174
product. If you, the product, are valuable but not putting yourself in front of people, you won't make any "sales." If you aren't valuable, but are putting yourself in front of people, it's the same story.
产品。如果你这个人——那个产品——很有价值，却没把自己放到人们面前，你就做不成任何“销售”。如果你没价值，却把自己放到人们面前，故事也一样。
p.174
In social situations, your value is communicated as a message through the medium of speaking. You must capture, hold, and deliver on the attention you receive from them. If the message is not framed under a shared perspective that houses a hierarchy of goals, it will be difficult for the conversation to lead to mutual benefit. If your selves don't have commonalities to gain interest in, the conversation will die out.
在社交情境里，你的价值以讯息的形式、通过口说这个媒介被传达。你必须捕获、保持、并兑付你从他们那里获得的注意力。如果那条讯息不被框在一个容纳着目标层级的共享视角之下，这场对话就很难引向互利。如果你们两人的自我之间没有可以激发兴趣的共同点，这场对话就会消亡。
p.174
The same is true for business but writing reigns supreme as the medium to articulate your message at the start. From that increasing level of articulation, your thoughts will become less jumbled, and the power of your speaking will increase with it.
商业也是如此，但写作在开头作为表达你讯息的媒介居首。随着表达层级的提升，你的想法会变得不那么杂乱，而你口说的力量也会随之增长。
p.174
If you can think, write, and speak to solve a problem for a specific individual, you become powerful. Use that power as you wish, but I would encourage you to use it for the good of humanity. That seems to be the only logical reasoning for earning an ethical independent income.
如果你能思考、写作、并口说去解决某个特定个体的问题，你就变得强大。你可以随心使用那股力量，但我会鼓励你把它用在人类之善上。那似乎是“赚取一份合乎伦理的独立收入”唯一合乎逻辑的理由。
RESULTS-ORIENTED SKILLS
以结果为导向的技能
p.174
p.174
In this ever-evolving world I, value exchange will never go out of style. If you can write, speak, market, and sell, you can adapt to the current landscape by learning results-oriented skills.
在这个不断演化的世界里，价值交换永远不会过时。如果你能写、能说、能营销、能销售，你就能通过学习以结果为导向的技能，适应当前的景观。
p.174
Results-oriented skills are how you apply your message and medium of choice. They are the vessel for distributing your value. The message and medium are evergreen, while results-oriented skills change with the landscape. You must keep your finger on the pulse of advancements in your interests so that you don't fade out as time progresses.
以结果为导向的技能，是你如何应用你的讯息和选定的媒介。它们是分发你价值的容器。讯息和媒介是常青的，而以结果为导向的技能随景观变化。你必须把手指按在你所感兴趣领域进展的脉搏上，这样你才不会被时间淘汰。
p.174
Before the Industrial Revolution, we used our hands to create tools, products, and services to exchange with others within our community. The
工业革命之前，我们用手创造工具、产品与服务，在社群里与他人交换。
p.175
ones that understood their nature - human nature - were the ones that could turn dirt into gold. After the Industrial Revolution, technology saw an exponential leap in production capacity. We spotted problems, created solutions, and distributed those solutions to the specific groups of people that needed them. If they had perceived value to exchange in return, like money, even better.
那些理解他们本性——人性——的人，是那些能把泥土变成金子的人。工业革命之后，技术在生产能力上实现了指数级飞跃。我们发现问题、创造解法、并把那些解法分发到需要它们的特定人群那里。如果他们感知到什么价值可以回换，比如钱，那就更好了。
p.175
As time went on, distribution systems became more efficient. Companies, individuals, and businesses of all sizes began advertising their message on billboards, in direct mail, and vehicle graphics. Some opted for general marketing in television commercials, while others aspired to be on the front page of magazines.
随着时间推移，分发系统变得更高效。公司、个体和各类规模的企业开始用广告牌、直邮和车体图形来宣传它们的讯息。有些人选择在电视广告里做泛营销，另一些人则渴望登上杂志封面。
p.175
In the Digital Revolution, things have drastically changed and less than 1% of the internet population has caught on. Instead of physical letters, we send emails and instant messages. Instead of large meetings, we have video calls. Instead of serving our physical communities, we attract and serve those that we can serve best through a compelling message.
在数字革命中，事情发生了剧烈变化，而互联网人口中不到 1% 的人跟上了。我们不发纸质信，而发邮件和即时消息。我们不办大型会议，而用视频通话。我们不服务自己的实体社群，而是通过一条有说服力的讯息去吸引并服务那些我们最能服务的人。
p.175
As with every unit of mind, the digital plane of business transcends and includes its predecessors. We still utilize past business principles, but they have been made more effective with the creative emergence of the internet. You no longer have to jump through hoops and ladders with a mountain of cash as leverage. Deep thinkers can write a book without a publisher. Musicians can spin tracks without a record label. Fitness specialists can market their coaching packages without being one of a few hundred people that have made the cover of Sports Illustrated.
如同每一个心智单元一样，商业的数字层面超越并包含它的前辈。我们仍在使用过去的商业原则，但它们因互联网的创造性涌现而变得更有效。你不再需要用堆积如山的现金当杠杆去钻过圈套与阶梯。深度思考者不需要出版社就能写书。音乐人不需要唱片公司就能做曲。健身专家不需要成为那几百个登上《体育画报》封面的人之一，就能营销自己的教练套餐。
p.175
Instead, you stack skills, build digital leverage, and adopt the mindset of radical self-reliance. Business principles (marketing, sales, writing, and speaking) should be mandatory education for every individual, because in the future of work, they will determine your success.
相反，你堆叠技能、建立数字杠杆、并采纳彻底自立的思维。商业原则（营销、销售、写作和口说）应当成为每个人的必修教育，因为在工作的未来，它们将决定你的成功。
p.175
These results-oriented skills are subject to change, but email marketing, graphic design, videography, photography, editing, animation, automation,
这些以结果为导向的技能会变化，但邮件营销、平面设计、视频拍摄、摄影、剪辑、动画、自动化，
p.176
and social media are but a few results-oriented skills that allow us to apply our message to the current landscape with our medium of choice.
以及社交媒体，只是少数几项能让我们用所选媒介把讯息应用到当前景观上的、以结果为导向的技能。
p.176
These not only apply to your own business or life's work, but to others. All brands, creators, and students have problems that they want solved in their personal and professional lives. When you stack results-oriented skills with the evergreen skills, you can practice on your own business and create a product or service for another.
这些不仅适用于你自己的生意或人生事业，也适用于他人的。所有品牌、创作者和学生，都有他们在个人与职业生活中想要解决的问题。当你把以结果为导向的技能与常青技能堆叠起来，你就能在自己的生意上练习，并为他人创造产品或服务。
p.176
If you invest the time it would take to get a degree in building an email list of 50,000 like-minded readers, that's twice the capacity of what a professional football stadium can hold. Now, if you craft a persuasive message, write a few emails, and promote a product that you've created as a solution to your own problems, I would not be surprised if you made the average United States salary in a month, minimum.
如果你把“拿一个学位”所需的时间用来建立一份五万名同频读者的邮件名单，那相当于一个职业足球场容量的两倍。现在，如果你打造一条有说服力的讯息、写几封邮件、并推广一个你作为“自己问题之解法”而创造出的产品，如果你一个月至少赚到美国平均薪资，我不会感到惊讶。
p.176
Of course, this does not prevent you from generating a creative income from the start. You don't need a massive readership, but I would encourage you to prioritize building one that can sustain your lifestyle without timeconsuming labor. You will need to start small and manual. Get your name, message, and products in front of as many eyes as possible. I can give you tactics all day long, or you can learn the lessons through experience. Trial and error will teach you the same lesson as the masters because that is how they learned it.
当然，这并不妨碍你从一开始就生成一份创造性收入。你不需要庞大的读者群，但我会鼓励你优先建立一个无需耗时劳动、就能维持你生活方式的读者群。你需要从小而手工的方式开始。把你的名字、讯息和产品放到尽可能多的眼睛面前。我可以整天给你战术，或者你可以通过经验学会那些教训。试错会教你与大师相同的教训，因为他们就是这样学会的。
p.176
If you have value to offer, you can use your knowledge to craft a persuasive message and send it directly to anybody on the internet, even celebrities. I wouldn't recommend targeting celebrities, because there has to be an equal exchange of perceived value for them to even consider responding to you. But it may be worthwhile targeting someone whose business presents a challenging problem that matches your skill.
如果你有价值可提供，你就可以用自己的知识打造一条有说服力的讯息、并把它直接发给互联网上的任何人，甚至名人。我不会建议瞄准名人，因为必须有对等的、可感知的价值交换，他们才会考虑回复你。但瞄准某个人的生意呈现出与你技能相匹配的挑战性问题，可能是值得的。
p.176
"Luck" is a percentage that increases with the amount of people that know your value. Your value reflects the level of challenge you can take on. The level of challenge determines your profitability. Start small, help the few
“运气”是一个百分比，它随“知道你价值的人数”而增加。你的价值反映你能接下的挑战层级。挑战层级决定你的盈利性。从小处开始，帮你能帮的
p.177
people that you can, and with a far time horizon you can impact more people than you thought was possible.
少数人，带着一个远大的时间视野，你就能影响比你想象中更多的人。
CREATIVE PROBLEM-SOLVING
创造性问题解决
p.177
p.177
One percent of fifty years is 6 months, and most people can't commit to the uncertain path for more than 2 weeks. All of this takes time, a lot of time, and anyone that says otherwise isn't looking out for your best interest. Only you can do that.
五十年的 1% 是 6 个月，而大多数人在这条不确定的路上连 2 周都坚持不了。这一切都需要时间，很多时间，任何说不是这样的人都不是在为你最大利益着想。只有你能为它着想。
p.177
As you are pushing the boundaries of the known, finding fulfillment in the challenging problems that present themselves, and shining the light of awareness in the unknown, you increase the volume of your domain of mastery.
当你推动已知的边界、在那些显现出来的挑战性问题中找到圆满、并在未知中照出觉察之光时，你就扩大了你精通领域的容积。
p.177
Here's a thought experiment. There are 4 small circles that form the outline of a square, each of them in 4 corners. These circles represent health, wealth, relationships, and happiness; the 4 eternal markets. These are where all burning, and profitable, problems exist.
这里有个思想实验。有 4 个小圆，构成一个正方形轮廓，各占 4 个角。这些圆代表健康、财富、关系与幸福；那 4 个永恒市场。所有燃烧的、且能获利的问题都存在于此。
p.177
As you develop yourself within these domains, the circles increase in diameter until they begin to overlap like a Venn diagram. Each of these circles can be considered a field of awareness. You are knowledgeable of each domain and able to piece together a creative solution to common problems. Let's set those aside for a minute and create a new set of circles. This time, they represent the evergreen skills: writing, speaking, marketing, and sales. The same thing happens. As you cultivate these skills, awareness overlaps and you can solve problems at the intersections while specialists are focused on one small circle.
当你在这些领域中发展自己，这些圆的直径会增加，直到它们像韦恩图那样开始重叠。这些圆中的每一个都可以被看作一个觉察场域。你对每个领域都有知识，并能拼出一个针对常见问题的创造性解法。让我们把它们先放一边，造一组新的圆。这次，它们代表常青技能：写作、口说、营销和销售。同样的事发生。当你培育这些技能，觉察重叠起来，你就能在交叉处解决问题，而专才们正聚焦于一个小圆。
p.177
Next, apply the same thing to results-oriented skills. As you learn 1, 2, 3, 4 applicable skills, because improvement never ends since entropy never sleeps, you begin to compound your creative problem-solving abilities.
接下来，把同样的事应用到以结果为导向的技能上。当你学了 1、2、3、4 项可应用的技能——因为提升永不结束，因为熵从不睡觉——你就开始复利你的创造性问题解决能力。
p.178
The last piece of this puzzle is personal interests. Most people never have the thought of making a living doing what they love because they are missing awareness of the eternal markets, evergreen skills, and resultsoriented skills that allow them to navigate the business landscape.
这块拼图的最后一片是个人兴趣。大多数人从没有过“靠做自己热爱之事谋生”这个念头，因为他们缺少对永恒市场、常青技能、以及那些让他们能导航商业景观的以结果为导向技能的觉察。
p.178
Now, any of the above can be considered personal interests of yours. Curiosity is powerful, and I would be disappointed if those skills did not excite you for a potential future. But we can create one last square of growing circles that represent your personal interests.
现在，上面任何一样都可以被视为你的个人兴趣。好奇心很强大，如果那些技能不能让你对潜在未来感到兴奋，我会失望。但我们可以造最后一组代表你个人兴趣的、不断增长的圆。
p.178
In my case, I gravitated toward spirituality, philosophy, metaphysics, and human potential. When I connect this last piece to the other 3 sets of squares we've created, it forms 4 walls in the shape of a cube. We can place a problem in the middle of that cube, navigate the outer edges for creative firepower, and piece together a unique solution that may one day be worth millions of dollars.
在我的情况里，我被灵性、哲学、形而上学和人类潜能吸引。当我把这最后一片与我们创造的另外 3 组正方形连起来，它就形成一个立方体的 4 面墙。我们可以把一个问题放到那个立方体中央，到外沿去寻取创造火力，并拼出一个有朝一日可能值数百万美元的独特解法。
p.178
Money, of course, is a byproduct of your life's work. Money matters, especially in this day and age, but there is a way to find meaning in this fabricated resource. Your personal interests can be anything. Do not outsource your curiosity to me. The interests you choose will begin to form a philosophy behind your work as you trek on the path of mastery.
金钱，当然是你人生事业的一个副产品。金钱很重要，尤其在当今这个时代，但有一种在这个被造出来的资源里找到意义的方式。你的个人兴趣可以是任何东西。不要把你的好奇心外包给我。当你跋涉在精通之路上，你选择的兴趣会开始形成你工作背后的一个哲学。
p.178
Nothing happens, then everything happens. When the outer edges of your multidimensional fields of awareness touch, it's like the missing piece of an infinite puzzle. At first, you can't tell what the image is, but once the right piece clicks into place, you solidify a leap in understanding. Too many people quit before this phenomenon occurs. They believe that understanding is linear when it's exponential. One day you have zero dollars, clients, or confidence and the next you have an abundance of them all.
什么都没发生，然后一切都发生了。当你那些多维觉察场域的外沿相触，它就像一块无限拼图中缺失的那一片。起初，你分辨不出那图像是什么，但一旦正确的那片咔哒归位，你就固化了理解上的一次飞跃。太多人在这个现象发生之前就退出了。他们相信理解是线性的，而它其实是指数的。某一天你有零美元、零客户、零自信，第二天你就全都多得用不完。
p.178
When the image of the puzzle is clear, you can observe the story of others, identify their missing piece, and help them fill the gap. All of this sounds great, I'm sure, but let's make it even more practical.
当拼图的图像清晰了，你就能观察他人的故事、识别他们缺失的那一片、并帮他们补上缺口。这一切听起来很棒，我相信。但让我们把它变得更实际一点。
p.179
You need a real-world project to act as a vessel for your exploration of the unknown. A project helps narrow your focus on one achievable goal, brings clarity to your actions, and encourages true learning through struggle.
你需要一个真实世界的项目，充当你在未知中探索的容器。一个项目帮你把焦点收窄到一个可实现的目标上、给你的行动带来清晰，并通过挣扎鼓励真正的学习。
THE PROJECT
项目
p.180
p.180
One pattern I've noticed in my life is that I've always carved out time to build something of my own. Things like schoolwork, client work, and even projects assigned to me on a job were necessary, but they didn't bring me the fulfillment I was looking for. Having a perpetual stream of evolving personal projects to work on first thing brought novelty to my days. The discoveries, insight, and progress that I made across multiple domains was the source of my zest for life.
我在自己生活中注意到的一个模式是：我总是凿出时间来构建某种自己的东西。像学业、客户工作，甚至岗位上分配给我的项目都是必要的，但它们没给我带来我所寻找的圆满。拥有一串永续的、不断演化的个人项目，让我每天第一件事就有新鲜感。我在多个领域里取得的新发现、洞见和进步，是我对生活之热情的来源。
p.180
To find the fulfillment that assigned projects can't provide, you must go inward, because someone can't give you what is meant to be a conscious personal creation. You need to know what you want because if you don't, someone will tell you what you want, and you will believe it.
要找到“被分配的项目”无法提供的圆满，你必须向内走，因为别人给不了你本应是“有意识个人创造”的东西。你需要知道自己想要什么，因为如果你不知道，就会有人来告诉你你想要什么，而你会相信。
p.180
From that meaningful goal, we can perceive our problems from a higher perspective. This is where most people go wrong. They want the problem to go away in an instant. So, they fail to gain clarity on the path to achievement, become overwhelmed, and get stuck in a negative thought 100p.
从那个有意义的目标出发，我们能从一个更高视角感知自己的问题。这正是大多数人出错的地方。他们想让问题在一瞬间消失。于是，他们没能获得关于达成路径的清晰、变得不堪重负，并卡在一个负面念头循环里。
p.180
Instead, we want to approach our hierarchy of goals like we would a grade school science project. The essence of the scientific method is to form a hypothesis, identify a problem, research how to solve it, document your discoveries, refine your system, and publish the solution.
相反，我们要像对待一个小学科学项目那样对待我们的目标层级。科学方法的精髓是：形成一个假设、识别一个问题、研究如何解决它、记录你的发现、精炼你的系统，并发布那个解法。
p.181
The solutions that you create for any area of your life can be used in 2 useful ways. The first is to free up mental energy in your life so you can build something deeper. The second is to pass along your solutions to those that want to be helped. Either to raise the collective consciousness, make an income, or both.
你为你生活中任何领域创造出的解法，可以有两种有用的用法。第一，是腾出你生活中的心智能量，好让你能构建更深的东西。第二，是把你的解法传给那些想被帮助的人。要么为了提升集体意识，要么为了挣一份收入，或者两者兼有。
p.181
Through structured self-experimentation, your dreams become inevitable, and you create more serendipity in your life. Now, we don't have to stop at one-off projects. A project is a unit of mind, and we can layer them for even more impact.
通过结构化的自我实验，你的梦想变得不可避免，你在生活中创造出更多机缘（serendipity）。现在，我们不必止步于一次性项目。一个项目是一个心智单元，而我们能把它们层层叠加，去获得更大的影响力。
p.181
You are the infinite project. You are your life's work. You improve yourself by pursuing a hierarchy of goals, each of those goals being a project in and of itself that can be used, shared, or monetized.
你就是那个无限项目。你就是你的人生事业。你通过追求一套目标层级来改进自己，而其中每一个目标本身就是一个可被使用、分享或变现的项目。
p.181
If you are the project, and each subsequent project presents a certain level of challenge that can be met with lifelong learning, your life is structured for maximum and sustained enjoyment. You will be forced to step into the unknown, where your nervous system signals that you are experiencing a meaningful event. When your life becomes a process rather than an outcome, the perception of your daily life reflects that, and your suffering decreases. Each level of challenge that you surpass allows you to educate those under you that are facing the same. Projects only live on as long as their impact is spread Note that this introduces a similar phenomenon as designing our ideal lifestyle. When our string of projects and who we want to become align, our attention narrows on the survival of each project, and the power of the unconscious mind sends resources to help.
如果你就是那个项目，而每一个后续项目都呈现出某个能被终身学习满足的挑战层级，那你的人生就被结构化成了最大且可持续的享受。你会被迫踏进未知，在那里你的神经系统会发出信号：你正在经历一件有意义的事。当你的生活变成一个过程而不是一个结果，你对自己日常生活的感知就反映了这一点，你的痛苦就减少了。你超越的每一个挑战层级，都让你能去教育那些正面临同样挑战的下属者。项目只有在其影响被扩散出去时才继续存活。注意，这引入了与我们设计理想生活方式时相似的现象。当我们那串项目与“我们想成为谁”对齐时，我们的注意力就收窄到每个项目的存活上，而潜意识心智的力量会送出资源来帮忙。
p.181
As we complete, publish, and iterate on our projects, we increase the complexity of the self. At each level of mind, your perspective expands to match, and you can relate to reality in a less-selfish manner.
当我们完成、发布并迭代我们的项目时，我们增加了自我的复杂度。在心智的每一个层级上，你的视角相应扩展，你能以一种不那么自私的方式与现实建立关系。
p.181
From this higher perspective, our goals evolve, and the host of problems that accompany them become more meaningful to solve. Once you've mastered your survival to the point where it consumes a marginal amount of
从这个更高视角出发，我们的目标演化，而伴随它们的那些问题，在解决时变得更有意义。一旦你精通了自己的生存，精通到它只消耗一点边际的
p.182
mental energy, you can focus your attention on the creative impact of your mind.
心智能量，你就能把注意力聚焦到你心智的创造性影响上。
HOW TO LEARN
如何学习
p.182
p.182
The source of learning is struggle, not memorization. Learning is the process of turning knowledge into understanding, and the lowest points of your life are those where a stackable lesson presents itself, but only if you apply it in reality.
学习的来源是挣扎，不是记忆。学习是把知识转化为理解的过程，而你人生中的最低点，正是那些呈现出一堂可堆叠课程的时刻——但只有你在现实中应用它才算。
p.182
Knowledge compounds, and without quality ideas, struggle, and time, you will fail to reach new levels of understanding. Again, this process is not immediate, and for most, genuine knowledge creation is an impossibility until they wake up. The problem is the attitude that schools approach learning with. At a young age, the act of obedience without question is tattooed into our psyche. It makes sense why there has been a silent education revolution on the internet.
知识会复利，而没有高质量的想法、挣扎和时间，你就无法抵达新的理解层级。再次地，这个过程不是即时的；对大多数人来说，直到他们醒来之前，真正的知识创造都是不可能的。问题在于学校对待学习的那种态度。在年幼时，“不加质疑地服从”这个行为被纹进我们的心灵。这就是为什么互联网上发生了一场无声的教育革命。
p.182
The neurotransmitter that most influences our behavior is dopamine.
最能影响我们行为的神经递质是多巴胺。
p.182
Dopamine plays an important role in our learning process, and when we seek to understand it, we can leverage it. From here on, we are assuming that you have an intention. Intention is the invisible bridge between goal and action. With a mind that is open to our desired future, we expand our field of awareness to notice things that will aid in the survival of that future. What are you aiming toward? Hold that at the top of your mind so you can recognize and apply lessons directly to that goal.
多巴胺在我们的学习过程中扮演重要角色，而当我们寻求理解它，我们就能利用它。从这里开始，我们假设你有一个意图。意图是目标与行动之间那座看不见的桥。带着一颗对我们渴望的未来敞开的心，我们扩展觉察场域，去注意到那些有助于那个未来存活的东西。你正瞄准什么？把它放在心智最顶端，这样你就能识别教训、并直接应用到那个目标上。
p.182
Novelty, pattern recognition, and the dopamine involved with both are the next step in our learning endeavors. The easiest way to notice this is to reread your favorite book. Or reflect on your experience with this book. When you revisit information from a new level of mind, you notice resources that didn't originally catch your attention through novelty. If your goal, conscious or unconscious, is to buy a new car, certain aspects of this book will stick out to you more than others. Your mind is a magnet
新奇、模式识别，以及两者所涉及的多巴胺，是我们学习努力中的下一步。注意到这一点的最简单方式，是重读你最爱的书。或者反思你与这本书的经验。当你从一个新的心智层级重访信息时，你会通过新奇注意到那些最初没有抓住你注意力的资源。如果你的目标——有意识的或无意识的——是买一辆新车，这本书的某些面向会比别的更让你注意。你的心智是一块
p.183
for novel ideas. By design, you collect knowledge that will aid in buying that new car. If your intention is to misinterpret everything I write so that you have an excuse to stay the same, that can be dangerous.
吸引新奇想法的磁铁。按设计，你会收集有助于买那辆新车的知识。如果你的意图是曲解我写的每一件事，好让你有借口保持不变，那可能是危险的。
p.183
For someone that has a different goal, like getting out of the state of emotional turmoil they are in, they will interpret this book from a completely different perspective. The same is true for someone that wants to make more money, get fit, or just entertain themselves out of boredom. Pattern recognition comes into play with this as well. Once you set your mind on that new car, or better mental health, you will notice that specific car, or happy individuals, as you are out and about in the world. Or how when you learn a new word, you start hearing it more often.
对一个持有不同目标的人，比如“脱离他们所处的那种情绪动荡状态”，他们会从一个完全不同的视角解读这本书。对想赚更多钱、想变健康、或只是想从无聊中自娱的人，也一样。模式识别在这里同样起作用。一旦你把心思放到那辆新车上，或者更好的心理健康上，当你在世界里出门走动时，你就会注意到那辆特定的车，或那些快乐的人。或者就像当你学了一个新词，你就开始更频繁地听到它。
p.183
By having a simple intention to act, your signal-to-noise ratio improves through dopamine. We can see why those that choose the unconscious modality of living look so miserable. It's because their attention is being manhandled by the goals that have been projected on them.
带着一个简单的“行动意图”，你的信噪比会通过多巴胺提升。我们能看见为什么那些选择无意识活法的人看起来那么悲惨。因为他们的注意力正在被那些投射到他们身上的目标粗暴操控。
p.183
Next, I want to introduce a few universal laws. The Law of Use and the Law of Inspired Action. These play together in unison and synthesize well with novelty and pattern recognition.
接下来，我想介绍几条普遍法则。使用法则与受启发行动法则。它们协同运作，并与新奇和模式识别很好地合成。
p.183
The Law of Use is simple. If you don't use it, you lose it. Meaning, if you do not apply the information you process with your conscious mind, especially if on an inconsistent basis, then it has less of a chance of becoming a habitual thought process.
使用法则很简单。你不用它，就会失去它。意思是，如果你不应用你用有意识心智处理过的信息——尤其当这种应用是不一致的时候——那么它变成习惯性思维过程的机会就更小。
p.183
The Law of Inspired Action adds firepower to the information we intend to apply toward our goals. The novelty and patterns we noticed are more than likely to inspire us to act, but that inspiration has a short fuse.
受启发行动法则为我们打算朝目标应用的信息增添火力。我们注意到的新奇和模式，极有可能启发我们去行动，但那份灵感引线很短。
p.183
So, it makes absolute sense to have some form of idea-capture system for your projects. Like the notebook you took out to strategize your lifestyle or a dedicated app in your phone. You won't be able to execute on any and all ideas right away. The next best thing is to write it down so you don't waste that potential. And no, you won't remember it without writing it down.
所以，为你的项目建立某种形式的想法捕获系统是绝对合理的。就像你抽出来为生活方式做策略的那本笔记本，或手机里一个专门的应用。你无法立刻执行任何和每一个想法。次好的事就是把它们写下来，好让你不浪费那份潜能。而不，你不写下来是记不住的。
p.184
To round out our ability to learn, the Protegé Effect is our final piece. In short, it's "learning by teaching." When you teach what you know, and struggle to articulate certain concepts, you reveal gaps in your knowledge. Those knowledge gaps are filled through intentional education, novelty, and pattern recognition. Not only will you spot information that aids in the pursuit of your goals, but also for the missing pieces you've identified in the pursuit of helping others reach theirs. Teaching what you know, regardless of how much of an imposter you think you are, is how you supercharge your understanding of ideas.
为圆满我们的学习能力，“门徒效应”是我们的最后一片。简言之，它是“通过教学来学习”。当你教你所知的东西、并挣扎于表达某些概念时，你就揭示了自己知识中的缺口。那些知识缺口通过有意识的教育、新奇和模式识别被填上。你不仅会辨认出有助于追求你目标的信息，也会辨认出你在帮助他人抵达他们目标的过程中所识别出的那些缺失碎片。教你所知的东西，无论你觉得自己多么像个骗子，都是你超级充能自己对想法之理解的方式。
p.184
Humans learn best when they pursue a goal, encounter a problem, remain conscious of that problem, notice information that can solve that problem, rapidly act on that information, and go on to teach what they learn to others. Whether this was an intentional design by a higher power or not, we can see how self-development, paired with a sense of mastery, is the path to a life of meaning, money, and impact.
人类学得最好的时候，是当他们追求一个目标、遇到一个问题、保持对那个问题的觉察、注意到能解决那个问题的信息、迅速在那个信息上行动，然后继续把所学教给别人。不论这是不是一个更高力量的刻意设计，我们都能看见：自我发展，配上一种精通感，是通往一种充满意义、金钱与影响的人生的路径。
BECOME A BUILDER
成为一个构建者
p.184
p.184
Overabundance of information is like pouring a gallon of murky water down a small drain. We love to horde theory, orthodoxy, and conceptual understanding of things without direct experience. Because that means we would have to do something we perceive as uncomfortable, when we've been conditioned into perceived comfort. Life doesn't work that way, and nobody wants to be "that" guy. You know, the one that gives a book's worth of advice without understanding your goals and not having done it themselves.
信息过剩，就像把一加仑浑浊的水倒进一个小排水口。我们喜欢囤积理论、正统教条、以及对事物的概念性理解，而不去直接体验。因为那意味着我们得去做一件我们感知为不舒服的事，而我们已经被条件化成感知中的舒适。生活不是那样运作的，而没人想做“那种人”。你知道的，就是那个给你一整本书的建议、却不理解你的目标、自己也没做过的人。
p.184
What you'll find in most domains is that true experts rarely need guidance. They used science, theory, and advice to get to the intermediate stage, but they learned that intuition and direct experience trump all once you get into the advanced stage. The reason that people don't realize this is that they are too attached to the identity they built along the way. The helpful concepts
你在大多数领域会发现的是：真正的专家很少需要指导。他们用科学、理论和建议抵达了中级阶段，但一旦进入高级阶段，他们就学到直觉和直接经验压倒一切。人们没意识到这一点的原因，是他们太依附于自己沿途建立的那个身份。那些有帮助的概念
p.185
they gathered with time gain a shred of sentience and become their puppet master.
随时间被他们收集起来，获得了一丝知觉，并成了他们的傀儡师。
p.185
You balance practice and theory by becoming a builder. That is, always having a project to build in alignment with the theory you are learning about.
你通过成为一个构建者来平衡练习与理论。也就是说，永远有一个与你正在学的理论一致的项目要构建。
p.185
When I was learning design, I started by watching endless tutorials on how to use a specific software instead of any of the other options available. This only led to getting stuck in tutorial hell. Learning the principles of design would have been the traditional route, but even that may leave you with an endless thirst for information collection without application.
当我学设计时，我从看无尽的教程开始——怎么用某个特定软件，而不是其他可用的选项。这只会导致卡在教程地狱里。学习设计原则本会是传统的路线，但即便那个也可能让你留下无尽的、只收集信息却不应用的渴望。
p.185
When it came time to put my skills to the test in the real world, I knew nothing. I was forced to supplement what I was building with specific tutorials if I wanted to see any meaningful progress. I had wasted weeks of time "learning" just to end up at ground zero.
当到了要在真实世界里测试我技能的时候，我什么都不懂。如果我想看到任何有意义的进步，我就被迫用具体的教程来补充我正在构建的东西。我浪费了数周时间“学习”，最后落在地面零点。
p.185
Once I realized how much I retained from learning in accordance with a real-world project, I switched to this method exclusively. If I wanted to learn how to build a website, I wouldn't start learning first. I would outline a project, pull inspiration from a project that I admire, and seek specific knowledge from beginner to advanced in a way that allowed me to apply the information immediately. That way, I was forced to encounter struggle from the very start. I prime my brain to receive an immediate lesson through my specific research. Once I find the solution to the problem, I get a "quick win" and start to build momentum into the rest of the project. Most people learn and learn and learn just to start over when it comes time to build, because they realize that everything they've learned has no direct use in the project they began. They don't have a goal-specific lens to interpret their learnings from.
一旦我意识到“与一个真实世界项目一致地学习”让我记住了多少东西，我就专门改用这个方法。如果我想学怎么建一个网站，我不会先学。我会先勾勒出一个项目、从一个我欣赏的项目中取灵感，并寻求从初学到高级的特定知识，以一种让我能立刻应用信息的方式。那样，我就被迫从一开始就遇到挣扎。我用我的具体研究给大脑预热，以接收一堂即时的课。一旦找到问题的解法，我就获得一次“快速胜利”，并开始在项目余下部分积累动量。大多数人学了又学、学了又学，到了要构建时却要重新开始，因为他们意识到自己所学的一切在他们开始的那个项目里没有直接用处。他们没有一面“目标特定的透镜”去解读自己的所学。
p.185
Success is a game of intelligent imitation, and that's exactly what this process allows us to do. If you want to truly learn, theory must brush up against reality. Start, then learn.
成功是一场“聪明模仿”的游戏，而这个流程恰恰让我们能这么做。如果你想真正学习，理论就必须与现实践擦。先开始，再学习。
SELF-EXPERIMENTATION
自我实验
p.186
p.186
The only way to solve your own problems for good is through selfexperimentation.
永远解决你自己问题的唯一方式，是通过自我实验。
p.186
People forget that their minds are infinitely unique. Yes, our genetic code is rather similar, but the billions of bits of information you've processed in your lifetime are radically different from others. Every bit was processed in a microscopic crevice of reality, at a different time, and with prior bits processed that influence how the next situation will be perceived.
人们忘了，他们的心智是无限独特的。没错，我们的遗传密码相当相似，但你在自己一生中处理过的数十亿比特信息，与别人截然不同。每一比特都在现实的一个微观裂缝里被处理，在不同的时间，并带着此前已处理过、会影响下一个处境如何被感知的那些比特。
p.186
Most people can't leverage this fact because they aren't conscious of the often-prolonged cause and effect of their choices. Instead, they mimic the latest haircut because it may help attract a tasteful mate. Or they chase after what's hot, flashy, or new because everyone else is.
大多数人无法利用这个事实，因为他们对自己选择那种常常很漫长的因果没有觉察。相反，他们模仿最新的发型，因为那或许有助于吸引一个有品位的伴侣。或者他们追逐热门、浮华或新潮的东西，因为别人都在追。
p.186
In business, relationships, career development, and anywhere else you need to stand out, the minor distinctions are what give you an advantage. Solving problems in your own way is how you stand out in a world of copycats. Self-experimentation is the opposite of blind trust in a theory, guru, or belief system. It is the only way to discover what truly works for you and your infinitely unique needs. For any given problem, there are dozens of options available to you to solve it. Internalize this, because people are naturally indecisive. They have difficulty opening their focus beyond their problems to find a solution that when they do, they get overwhelmed to the point of doing nothing.
在商业、关系、职业发展，以及任何你需要脱颖而出的地方，那些细微的差别正是给你优势的东西。以自己的方式解决问题，是你在一个模仿者世界里脱颖而出的方式。自我实验是对某个理论、大师或信念体系的盲目信任的反面。它是发现“什么真正适合你和你那无限独特需求”的唯一方式。对任何给定问题，都有几十个可用选项供你解决。把这个内化，因为人天生犹豫不决。他们很难把自己的焦点打开到问题之外去寻找一个解法，以至于当他们真这么做时，会被压垮到什么都不做的程度。
p.186
If you have relationship problems, you can go on a retreat to contemplate, hire a therapist, or try to work it out directly with your partner. No single option is the best until you piece together a solution that works, but even that can't be preached as law to others with a similar problem. Most of the time, you won't choose just one of the techniques, but a combination of parts from trying them all. That is how you create a novel solution to your own problems that advances progress within that industry.
如果你有关系问题，你可以去一场静修营沉思、雇一位治疗师，或尝试直接与伴侣一起把它解决。在你拼出一个有效的解法之前，没有哪个单一选项是最好的；但即便那个解法，也不能被当作法则去向有类似问题的他人说教。大多数时候，你不会只选其中一种技术，而是从把所有都试一遍中取一部分组合起来。这就是你如何为自己问题创造出一个推进该行业进步的新奇解法。
p.187
If you have money problems, you can try creating a budget, starting a side business, or improving your skillset to get a higher-paying job. As you explore different options, you may find that all of them help. Rather than seeing your money problems as something that can be solved in one go, you realize that the solution is in changing minor facets of your lifestyle. If you have health issues, you can try fad diets like veganism, carnivore, or keto just to learn that the big-picture principles of nutrition are all the same. From that enlightened state, you can create the perfectly unique diet plan that you can adhere to for life (while most regain their weight immediately after stopping the diet).
如果你有金钱问题，你可以尝试做一份预算、开始一门副业，或提升你的技能组合去拿一份更高薪的工作。当你探索不同选项时，你可能会发现它们全都有用。与其把你的金钱问题看作能被一次搞定的东西，你会意识到解法在于改变你生活方式的次要面向。如果你有健康问题，你可以试试纯素、肉食或生酮这类流行饮食法，最后学到营养的大局原则其实都一样。从那个开悟状态出发，你可以创造出那份你能够终身坚持的、完美独特的饮食计划（而大多数人停了那套饮食法后立刻就把体重涨回去了）。
p.187
If you have self-esteem issues, you can start running, bicycling, or lifting weights. The danger is in getting trapped in one ideology rather than pulling truth from all.
如果你有自尊问题，你可以开始跑步、骑车或举重。危险在于被困在一种意识形态里，而不是从所有里面提取真相。
p.187
With self-experimentation, you are aiming to create a sustainable system that is conducive to your vision for the future. As your system becomes more efficient with time and mental energy, that problem ceases to bother you, and you can invest your focus in problems that require a higher degree of creativity.
通过自我实验，你的目标是创造一套可持续的、有益于你未来愿景的系统。随时间和心智能量的投入，你的系统变得更高效，那个问题就不再困扰你，而你就能把你的专注投入那些需要更高创造力程度的问题上。
p.187
To understand this process of systemization, let's look at a bodybuilder. Their goal is to build and retain the most muscle mass possible. To do so, they go through "bulking" and "cutting" cycles. When they bulk, they slightly overconsume calories to put the body in a muscle-building environment. They will inevitably gain some unwanted body fat. We can think of this as the self-experimentation process. During the bulk, they reach a threshold. They gain enough body fat to the point of not liking how they look, feeling slow and sluggish, and having trouble eating the right amount of food When they cut, they slightly underconsume calories to put the body in a fat loss environment, hopefully one that retains the muscle they've built underneath. They may lose some muscle, but they should achieve a new
为理解这个系统化过程，让我们看一位健美者。他们的目标是建立并保留尽可能多的肌肉量。为做到那一点，他们要经历“增肌”和“减脂”循环。增肌时，他们略微过量摄入热量，把身体置于一个适合增肌的环境。他们不可避免地会获得一些不想要的体脂。我们可以把这想成自我实验过程。在增肌期间，他们到达一个阈值。他们获得的体脂多到自己不喜欢自己的样子、感到迟钝笨重、吃对量的食物都变得困难。减脂时，他们略微摄入不足的热量，把身体置于一个减脂的环境，但愿是那种能保住底下已建肌肉的环境。他们也许会掉一些肌肉，但到减脂结束时，他们应该抵达一个新的
p.188
"peak" physique by the time the cut is over. We can think of this as systemization.
“巅峰”体型。我们可以把这想成系统化。
p.188
When you pursue a new goal and a problem presents itself, you try multiple options to find a solution. You may not find the exact solution immediately, but you will pick up a lot of useful information. At some point, you bite off more than you can chew. You start to feel overwhelmed because of the mental fat you've gained. Many are familiar with the cyclical period in their lives where they feel lost or anxious.
当你追求一个新目标、一个问题显现出来时，你会尝试多个选项去找一个解法。你可能不会立刻找到确切的解法，但你会拾起许多有用的信息。到某个时刻，你会贪多嚼不烂。你开始感到不堪重负，因为你获得了那些“心智脂肪”。许多人都熟悉自己人生中那种感觉迷失或焦虑的周期性阶段。
p.188
Soon enough, you will need to cut back and rid your life of the things that aren't working to solve your problems. Try everything, see what sticks, and give yourself permission to drop the things that don't. We want muscle, not fat, and that muscle is there to stay without much additional effort. This pattern reflects across all domains. When I was pushing for business growth and hitting new monthly highs in revenue, I would work longer hours, try new tactics, create new products, and move as many levers as I could. I put my business in an environment conducive to growth through my season of intensity.
很快，你就需要削减、把你生活里那些“对解决你的问题没起作用”的东西清除掉。把什么都试一遍，看看什么会留下来，并给自己许可去放下那些不会的。我们要的是肌肉，不是脂肪，而那肌肉在那里是为了不太费额外力气就能保住。这个模式在所有领域都成立。当我为生意增长冲刺、月收入创下新高时，我会工作更长时间、尝试新战术、创造新产品，并尽可能多地去撬动杠杆。我通过我那段强度季，把我的生意置于一个有利于增长的环境里。
p.188
I knew there would come a time when I had to cut back to 4-hour workdays and my ideal lifestyle. When I did, the business muscle that was built in my endeavors revealed a new monthly baseline revenue.
我知道会有一个时刻，我必须削减回四小时工作日和我理想的生活方式。当我这么做时，我那些努力中建立起的商业肌肉，揭示出一个新的月度基线收入。
p.188
This is how you solve all the problems in your life. Identify a problem, experiment with different solutions, and drop everything that isn't sustainable. If you can't see yourself doing it every single month, week, or day, it doesn't belong as a habitual part of your life.
这就是你如何解决生活中的所有问题。识别一个问题、实验不同的解法，并放下一切不可持续的。如果你看不到自己能每个月、每一周、每一天都做它，那它就不该成为你生活中习惯性的一部分。
PROJECT TO PRODUCT
从项目到产品
p.188
p.188
Everyone is an entrepreneur; some just choose to get paid for the problems they solve in their personal life. Problems are best solved with a personal project and self-experimentation. You become an entrepreneur when you
每个人都是创业者；有些人只是选择为自己在个人生活中解决的那些问题获得报酬。问题最好通过一个个人项目和自我实验来解决。当你把你的项目
p.189
take your projects public. And remember, you are the ultimate project. The exchange of goods is the foundation of human connection regardless of generation, gender, race, or type of good being exchanged.
公开化时，你就成为一个创业者。而记住，你是那个终极项目。货物交换是人类连接的基础，无论哪一代、哪种性别、哪个种族，或交换的是何种货物。
p.189
In modern times, money is an important resource for the proper function of our everyday lives. It is the lifeblood of society, and it is your job to earn and spend in areas that you want to bring to life. As problems continue to be solved, the emergence and development of a more advanced digital currency is unfolding before our eyes. Money is a valuable resource for everyone who does not have it, and those that want it only need the skills to exchange for it. Unless you want to disconnect from any social interaction and attempt to survive in the woods, you need money. No amount of selfrighteous preaching about how money is "evil" is going to change that. If you want to participate in the incredible advancements of our times, you will have to contribute to humanity through business and value exchange. All profitable products start as a project whether the intention to sell is there or not. If you want to generate a creative income, you will need to sell a valuable product. And what's a better starting point than a personal project that solves a burning problem that all living beings encounter?
在现代，金钱是我们日常生活正常运转的一项重要资源。它是社会的血液，而你的职责是在你希望带到生命中去的领域里赚取和花费。随着问题持续被解决，一种更先进的数字货币的涌现与发展正在我们眼前展开。金钱对每个没有它的人来说都是宝贵资源，而那些想要它的人只需要交换它的技能。除非你想与任何社会互动断开、尝试在树林里求生，你就需要钱。无论多少关于“金钱是邪恶的”的自以为正直的说教，都改变不了这一点。如果你想参与我们这个时代的不可思议进步，你将必须通过商业和价值交换为人类做贡献。所有能获利的产品都始于一个项目，无论是否有出售的意图。如果你想生成一份创造性收入，你就需要卖一个有价值的产品。而比“一个解决所有生命都会遇到的燃烧问题的个人项目”更好的起点是什么？
p.189
Now, I want to make it clear that I am using "product" as a blanket term for "what you sell." This can be a physical or digital product or service. It makes sense to start off as a freelancer, consultant, or tutor with the systems you've developed. Once you have distribution and leverage under your own name, you can turn that proven system into a product that sells while you sleep Most people wait to start a business until they have the perfect plan that holds no meaning to them. Others have an unconscious relationship with money that leads them to believe that "selling" is bad. Yet, they go on to work for a massive corporation that exploits their employees to sell a product. Or they don't realize that they are selling their ideas, beliefs, and worldview during every single interaction. If you don't sell your own product, you will be forced to sell someone else's.
现在，我想说明，我用“产品”作为一个泛指“你所卖的东西”的术语。这可以是实体或数字的产品或服务。以你已经发展出的系统，从自由职业者、顾问或家教开始是合理的。一旦你在自己名下建立了分发和杠杆，你就能把那套已被验证的系统变成一个在你睡觉时也能卖的产品。大多数人等到有了一个完美计划才开始创业，而那个计划对他们自己毫无意义。另一些人与金钱有一种无意识的关系，让他们相信“销售”是坏的。然而，他们接着去为一家剥削员工、卖产品的大公司工作。或者他们没意识到，他们在每一次互动中都在卖自己的想法、信念和世界观。如果你不卖自己的产品，你就会被迫去卖别人的。
p.190
Success is counterintuitive, and if you want out of the societal dominator hierarchies, you will have to create a product. There isn't any other way. This method of turning your personal projects into a product is one method of many but is an incredible starting point for those that want to discover, pursue, and evolve their life's work without venture capital or investing their life savings.
成功是反直觉的，而如果你想脱离社会性的支配型层级，你就必须创造一个产品。没有别的办法。这种“把你的个人项目变成产品”的方法，是众多方法中的一种，但对那些想在没有风险投资、也不必押上全部积蓄的情况下发现、追求并演化自己人生事业的人来说，它是一个不可思议的起点。
p.190
Not to mention, people get wrapped up in worrying about saturation, competition, and product market fit. This method bypasses all of them by leveraging the most unique thing on this planet: you.
更何况，人们会陷进对饱和、竞争和产品市场契合度的担忧里。这个方法通过利用这地球上最独特的东西——你——绕开了所有那些。
p.190
After a plethora of freelancing and e-commerce business failures, wasting tens of thousands of dollars on sample products, paid advertisements, and business courses with an ever-growing student debt, I saw my first success in web design. I'll spare you the details of the journey. The notable aspect was that I started out of curiosity. I had always wanted to do something creative, and my field of awareness at the time allowed me to register and research web design.
在一连串自由职业与电商生意的失败、在样品产品、付费广告和商业课程上浪费数万美元、以及不断增长的学生贷款之后，我在网页设计上看到了我的第一次成功。旅程的细节我就省了。值得注意的一点是，我出于好奇而开始。我一直想做点有创造性的事，而我当时的觉察场域让我能登记并研究网页设计。
p.190
I built projects for my previous business attempts, like freelance photography, and offered to build projects for my family and friends. Of course, if I could go back, I would change the way I did things, but that's why I'm writing this book. To pass on my lessons.
我为我之前的生意尝试——比如自由摄影——做过一些项目，并主动提出为我的家人和朋友做项目。当然，如果我能回去，我会改变我做事的方式，但那正是我写这本书的原因。把我的教训传下去。
p.190
The logical transition for those web design projects was to become a freelance web designer, so that's what I did, and I solved the problems that presented themselves until I made a sustainable full-time income. First, I had no idea how to land clients, so I studied and experimented with multiple techniques I could find on the internet. Second, I realized that a single skill wasn't enough to get the results that would allow me to charge higher prices, so I started learning marketing, sales, and writing. Third, I knew that I couldn't increase my income beyond a certain point with manual client acquisition, so I started building distribution by posting content in public to attract a following. By solving those 3 problems over the course of a year, I gained more specific knowledge (and made more money) than my 4 years at college would ever allow me to.
那些网页设计项目的合理转变，是成为一名自由网页设计师，所以我就那么做了，而我一直解决显现出来的问题，直到我赚到一份可持续的全职收入。第一，我完全不知道怎么拿下客户，所以我研究并实验了我在网上能找到的多种技术。第二，我意识到单一项技能不足以取得那些能让我收更高价格的结果，所以我开始学营销、销售和写作。第三，我知道靠手工获客，我的收入无法超过某个点，所以我开始通过公开发布内容来建立分发、吸引追随者。用一年时间解决这三个问题，我获得的特定知识（以及赚到的钱）比我大学四年能给我的更多。
p.191
If I had known at the time, I could have gone straight into consulting or tutoring. Specific people prefer to do things themselves; others prefer to have it done for them. I prefer to teach, so my business endeavors evolved to reflect that. I gained experience by solving my own problems and eventually went on to teach what I'd learned in my freelance web design business.
如果我当时就知道，我本可以径直进入咨询或家教。有些人偏爱自己动手做事；另一些人偏爱让别人替他们做。我偏爱教学，所以我的商业努力演化成了反映这点的样子。我通过解决自己的问题获得经验，并最终去教我在自由网页设计生意中学到的东西。
p.191
Notice how I didn't close my mind off to something less limited than a singular skill like web design. Many new entrepreneurs identify with a skill or interest rather than the problem they are solving. A skill is a tool that solves a problem that births passion. Be open to improving your skill stack or accept that the path is going to be more difficult than it needs to be. As I acquired new skills and reflected on the problems in my business, marketing consulting was my next purpose. I despised doing manual work for local business owners, targeted individuals who were more like me, and used my skill stack to create a service that would benefit their professional lives.
注意，我没有把心智封闭在比“网页设计”这样的单一技能更不局限的东西之外。许多新创业者认同的是一项技能或兴趣，而不是他们正在解决的问题。技能是一个用来解决“催生热情之问题”的工具。要开放地去改进你的技能组合，或者接受那条路会比它需要的更难走。随着我获得新技能、并反思我生意里的问题，营销咨询成了我的下一个目的。我厌恶为本地企业主做手工活，于是瞄准那些更像我的个体，并用我的技能组合创造出一项能助益他们职业生活的服务。
p.191
This is when I began to understand the raw power of the internet. I started my creator journey, began attracting an audience with my interests and expertise, and had clients coming to me. I had escaped the feast-or-famine cycle that a majority of freelancers get trapped in.
这就是我开始理解互联网原始力量的时候。我开始了我的创作者旅程、开始用我的兴趣和专长吸引受众，并开始有客户主动来找我。我逃脱了大多数自由职业者被困住的“盛宴或饥荒”循环。
p.191
Soon enough, I had the distribution necessary to decrease the amount of client work I took on. I was solving the problem of productivity in my life and decided to create my own planner.
很快，我就拥有了减少客户工作所需的足够分发。我当时正在解决自己生活中“生产力”这个问题，并决定创造我自己的日程本。
p.191
Through self-experimentation, I purchased 3 different planners, obsessed over the latest productivity advice, and tested them all in my daily routine. Some things worked well, some didn't. The things that did, I added to the planner design.
通过自我实验，我买了 3 种不同的日程本、痴迷于最新的生产力建议，并在我自己的日常惯例里把它们全试了一遍。有些东西效果很好，有些不行。有效的那些，我把它们加进了日程本设计里。
p.191
I had no idea what stood ahead in the unknown domain of print manufacturing, but I figured it out one step at a time. Weeks later, I had the first sample planner in my hand. The feeling of building your own thing is incredible. I hope you experience it one day.
我对印刷制造那个未知领域前方有什么一无所知，但我一步一步弄明白了。几周后，我手里有了第一本样品日程本。构建自己东西的那种感觉不可思议。我希望你有一天能体验到它。
p.192
After 3 years of evolution, I had built multiple digital products, trashed them, created new ones, trashed them again, and before I knew it, I had a multimillion follower distribution network and a hyper-profitable product stack that would sustain creative endeavors like writing this book.
经过 3 年的演化，我建成了多个数字产品、把它们废弃、创造新的、又再次废弃，而在我不经意间，我就拥有了一个数百万追随者的分发网络，以及一套超高利润的产品组合，足以支撑像写这本书这样的创造性努力。
p.192
The first lesson of this brief story is that there is always a better problem to solve. Most people solve a grueling problem in their life, settle for the solution that was created, and remain isolated in that bubble of grueling effort. More is better, but only when backed by a sense of mastery. The second lesson is that my products started as projects in my life. I wanted to improve my productivity, so I experimented with different solutions, created my own, and distributed it with my marketing, sales, writing, and speaking skills.
这个简短故事的第一个教训是：永远存在一个更好的问题可解决。大多数人解决了生活中一个折磨人的问题、接受创造出来的那个解法，并仍然孤立在那个“折磨人的努力”的气泡里。更多更好，但只有在一种精通感支撑下才是如此。第二个教训是：我的产品都始于我生活中的项目。我想改进我的生产力，所以我实验了不同解法、创造了我自己的，并用我的营销、销售、写作和口说技能把它分发出去。
p.192
The path to the good life is simple: actively pursue your ideal lifestyle, create solutions to problems along the way, and get paid for sharing that solution with others.
通往好生活的路很简单：积极地追求你理想的生活方式、沿途为问题创造解法，并通过与人分享那个解法而获得报酬。
THE VESSEL
容器
p.193
p.193
In an ideal world, everyone would be able to sustain their desired lifestyle doing what they enjoy. But we do not live in that world yet, and human nature favors the distribution of power through evolving hierarchies. You can rest assured that a majority of the population has not been exposed to this information, and information is the primary resource of modern success. If you wish to do so, you can leverage this opportunity into a fulfilling life before it becomes the only way of life. That is, everyone leaning into their entrepreneurial nature to both earn a living and contribute to the world, from local to Universal.
在一个理想世界里，每个人都能靠做自己喜欢的事来维持自己想要的生活方式。但我们还不住在那个世界里，而人性偏向于让权力通过不断演化的层级来分发。你可以放心，人口中的大多数还没有暴露于这些信息，而信息是现代成功的主要资源。如果你愿意，你可以把这份机会利用成一种有圆满感的生活，趁它还没有变成唯一的活法之前。也就是说，趁“每个人都向自己的创业本性倾斜，既谋生又为世界做贡献，从本地到宇宙”还没成为唯一道路之前。
p.193
Human nature reflects that many will choose to stay at the bottom of any given power hierarchy just because they were conditioned to. But we know that destiny can be influenced through our daily choices.
人性反映出，许多人会选择留在任何给定权力层级的底部，只是因为被条件化成那样。但我们知道，命运可以通过我们的日常选择被影响。
p.193
With the desire to change, anyone reading this book can leverage modern technology to not only create an independent income source, but have an abundance of money, time, and control of attention to focus on the other important aspects of life.
带着改变的渴望，任何读这本书的人都能利用现代技术，不仅创造一份独立收入来源，还能拥有充裕的金钱、时间和对注意力的控制，去聚焦生活中其他重要的面向。
p.193
Everyone should have an understanding of business principles for a few reasons. One, so that they are not limited in the amount of money they make. Two, so that they can experience the microcosm of life that business
每个人都应该理解商业原则，有几个原因。第一，这样他们就不会被自己所能赚的金钱数额所限制。第二，这样他们就能体验商业
p.194
is. As with all pursuits that seem shallow on the surface, there is a depth of wisdom waiting to be discovered. It is a deeply spiritual endeavor.
作为生活微缩宇宙的那一面。如同所有表面上看似浅薄的追求一样，那里有一份等待被发现的智慧深度。它是一项深层灵性的努力。
p.194
Money is the barrier to improvement in many areas of life. The cliché advice that "money doesn't buy happiness" is a half-truth that influences people to neglect the modern resource that they go on to become a slave to. Cashflow is often the first problem that should be prioritized, because a lack of it places a limit on how far any other area of life can be developed. Long, exhausting hours spent on work that does not align with your values does not need to be a permanent sentence. It can act as a stepping stone to acquire skills, build a community, and earn enough to meet your basic needs. Entrepreneurship is the only logical option for long-term thinkers. Yes, even to those that love the structure that a job provides.
金钱是生活许多领域中改进的障碍。“金钱买不到幸福”这句陈词滥调是一个半真，它影响人们去忽视那个他们后来会变成奴隶的现代资源。现金流往往是最该被优先解决的第一个问题，因为缺钱会给生活的任何其他领域能被发展到多远设一个上限。花在与你价值观不一致的工作上的漫长的、耗尽人的时间，不必是一项永久判决。它可以充当一块垫脚石，用来获得技能、建立一个社群，并赚到足以满足你基本需要的钱。创业是长期思考者唯一合乎逻辑的选项。没错，即便对那热爱工作所提供之结构的人也是如此。
p.194
Entrepreneurship does not eliminate structure but allows you to take a lifestyle-first approach to creating your own.
创业不消除结构，而是让你以“生活方式优先”的方式去创造你自己的结构。
p.194
People climb corporate ladders because their psyche craves challenge. But you can only climb so high. The challenge will cease to exist, and unless you find another source, preferably intrinsic, it would be wise to cut to the chase and start building your own thing. Entrepreneurship is a processfocused endeavor with an infinite bucket of challenges that you can pick and choose.
人们攀爬公司阶梯，因为他们的心灵渴望挑战。但你只能爬到那么高。那个挑战会停止存在，而除非你找到另一个来源（最好是内在的），那还不如直接切入正题、开始构建你自己的东西。创业是一项聚焦过程的努力，拥有一桶无限的、你能挑选的挑战。
p.194
In a long-winded attempt to prime your mind to receive this lesson, the internet now demands that you display your value in public. Employers are hiring based on social media portfolios. Freelancers are working with large corporations across the globe. Entrepreneurs are leveraging the close-toinfinite reach of the internet to distribute their creations.
在一次冗长的、旨在给你的心智预热以接收这堂课的尝试之后：互联网如今要求你在公开场合展示你的价值。雇主正根据社交媒体作品集招聘。自由职业者正与全球的大公司合作。创业者正利用互联网近乎无限的触及范围去分发他们的创造。
p.194
Education is the first step on your journey and there are 3 modalities for distributing the value you have to offer in the form of a product or service. This is how you package up your skills, interests, and expertise to join in on the emergence of the new economy.
教育是你旅程的第一步，而以产品或服务的形式分发你所提供之价值，有三种模态。这就是你如何把你的技能、兴趣和专长打包，以加入新经济的涌现。
p.194
To form a foundation, we will be discussing all of this under the lens of creative, knowledge, and online work. We will not be discussing the
为建立一个基础，我们将在创造性的、知识的、以及线上的工作这一透镜下讨论所有这些。我们不会讨论
p.195
information you can learn and be trained into by the school system. We want scale, autonomy, and fulfillment from the systems we are creating through self-development.
那些你能从学校系统学到、并被训练掌握的信息。我们想从我们通过自我发展所创造出的系统中，获得规模化、自主和圆满。
p.195
If you'd like to build a massive company, that's a worthy endeavor. But, unless you have business leverage in the form of a network or capital, you shouldn't be thinking about taking a huge jump into the depths of the business unknown. All that we talk about can be done as one person. Once you have leverage, you can start a company from a place of low risk and high reputation.
如果你想建一家巨型公司，那是一项值得的努力。但除非你拥有网络或资本形式的商业杠杆，你不该想着往商业未知的深处做巨大一跃。我们所谈的一切都能以一个人的方式完成。一旦你有了杠杆，你就能从一个低风险、高声誉的位置去创办一家公司。
p.195
First, there is "done for you" work. This includes the realm of freelancing, consulting, and specialized services, where you are doing the manual labor for another business, brand, or individual. With the proper strategy, you can generate a sizeable income. But, if you are a one-man operation, you have a ceiling on how much you can earn.
第一，是“替你完成”型的工作。这包括自由职业、咨询和专业服务领域，你在为另一门生意、品牌或个人做手工劳动。有了恰当的策略，你能生成一份可观的收入。但如果你是单人运作，你能赚多少就有个天花板。
p.195
Second, there is "done with you" work. This is a similar service-style offer that includes consulting, coaching, and tutoring. This is where we begin to earn with the creative ability of our mind, not manual labor. You can reach new heights as one person, but there is but a slightly higher cap than "done for you" work.
第二，是“与你一起做”型的工作。这是一种类似服务式的供给，包括咨询、教练和家教。这是我们开始用自己心智的创造能力、而不是手工劳动去赚取的地方。作为一个人，你能到达新的高度，但那里的上限只比“替你完成”型略高一点。
p.195
Third is "do it yourself," where digital and physical products come into play. These include courses, subscriptions, software, tools, guides, books, templates, and programs that distribute, teach, and get results for your customers with minimal work on your end. The goal is to be able to earn an income while you sleep. That is the new luxury for the individual of the 3rd millennium.
第三，是“你自己做”型，数字和物理产品在此登场。这包括课程、订阅、软件、工具、指南、书籍、模板和项目，它们以你这一端最小的工作量去分发、教学并为客户取得结果。目标是在你睡觉时也能赚取一份收入。那是第三个千年里，个体新的奢侈品。
p.195
You are to experiment with each one according to your experience level, pivot into the next, and structure your work in alignment with your ideal lifestyle. Understand that entrepreneurship places everything within your control. Everything. You can change any aspect of your lifestyle, product offerings, or the work you choose to do if you perceive it from an evolving level of mind.
你要根据自己的经验层级去实验每一种、转向下一种，并以与你理想生活方式一致的方式去结构化你的工作。要明白，创业把你的一切都置于你的控制之内。一切。如果你从一个不断演化的心智层级去感知，你能改变你生活方式、产品供给，或你所选择去做的任何工作的任何面向。
p.196
"Done for you," "done with you," and "do it yourself" style offers can increase in value and profitability with a developed system that gets results a strong reputation behind the person selling it, and the previous results you've gotten past clients and customers.
“替你完成”“与你一起做”“你自己做”这三种风格的供给，都能随着一套取得结果的成熟系统、售卖者背后的强声誉、以及你此前从过往客户和顾客那里取得的结果，而在价值与盈利性上增长。
THE ONE-PERSON BUSINESS
一人公司
p.196
p.196
How to start a billion-dollar company: Don't. Instead, start as one person. If you can't turn your interests into income, you don't have the skill to start a business that requires 10 times the resources.
如何创办一家数十亿美元的公司：别办。相反，从一个人开始。如果你不能把自己的兴趣变成收入，你也没有技能去创办一家需要 10 倍资源的公司。
p.196
Most people have dreams of being the CEO of a successful business but haven't managed to be the CEO of their own life. And when they do manage to run a large business, their finances flourish, but their relationships, health, and happiness are nowhere to be found.
大多数人梦想成为一家成功企业的 CEO，却还没能成为自己人生的 CEO。而当他们真经营起一家大企业时，他们的财务繁荣了，但他们的关系、健康和幸福却无处可寻。
p.196
With 5 years of focused effort, I was able to leverage my self- development into $10,000, $100,000, $150,000, $800,000, and $3,500,000 in business revenue year after year with the infinite reach of the internet. These are rounded numbers. Five years may seem like a long time but remember that 4-year-degrees don't even guarantee job placement for the disappointing average US salary. As one person, this is more than enough to sustain any lifestyle you'd like, no matter the damage inflation creates by the time you read this book.
用 5 年专注的努力，借助互联网无限的触及范围，我得以把我自我发展转化为逐年 $10,000、$100,000、$150,000、$800,000 和 $3,500,000 的商业收入。这些是取整后的数字。五年也许看起来很长，但记住，4 年制学位甚至都不能确保你被安排上岗，换来那个令人失望的美国平均薪资。作为一个人，这已经够维持你想要的任何生活方式，无论到你读这本书时通货膨胀造成了多大破坏。
p.196
I'm not a fan of get-rich-quick schemes, but success is counterintuitive, and the quickest fix is the longest path. Think about it: if you solve a burning problem in your life, one that every single person has, and your income is a direct reflection of the quality of problems you solve, why not start there? It is the most profitable and meaningful route by all measures and calculations. There is no use trying to land on Mars when we can't even live on this Earth. By solving your own problems and helping others solve their own, you raise the collective consciousness to the point of everyone solving problems they are passionate about.
我不是快速致富骗局的粉丝，但成功是反直觉的，而最快的解法是最长的路。想一下：如果你解决了自己生活中一个燃烧的问题，一个每个人都有的问题，而你的收入是你所解决问题质量的直接反映，那为什么不从那里开始？从所有衡量与计算看，它都是最有利可图、最有意义的路线。当我们甚至无法在这地球上活好时，试图登陆火星是没有用的。通过解决你自己的问题并帮别人解决他们自己的，你把集体意识提升到每个人都去解决自己所热爱之问题的程度。
p.197
You, as an individual, have the ability to attract an audience to your work and put a valuable product or service in front of them. This product or service should complement your skill set ranging from consulting, freelancing, and information in various forms like a course or book, physical tools or crafts, creative systems, and the rest.
你作为一个个体，有能力把受众吸引到你的工作上来，并把一个有价值的产品或服务放到他们面前。这个产品或服务应当与你从咨询、自由职业、到课程或书籍等各种形式的信息、物理工具或手作、创造性系统等等的技能组合互补。
p.197
There is a reason you have the interests, skills, and experience that you do. It would be silly to think that others' lives wouldn't benefit from them. You aren't special, and that's the point: there are people just like you that can benefit from your conscious development.
你拥有你现有的兴趣、技能和经验，是有一个原因的。认为别人的生活不会从中受益，那是愚蠢的。你并不特别，而这正是要点：有与你一样的人，能从你有意识的发展中受益。
p.197
A modern business can be broken down into 3 core components: brand, content, and product. Your brand is your story. Your content is a map. Your product is a game. Even business reflects Universal patterns.
一门现代生意可以拆成 3 个核心组件：品牌、内容与产品。你的品牌是你的故事。你的内容是地图。你的产品是游戏。连商业也反映着宇宙的模式。
p.197
To attract people to your business, your brand will be the first touchpoint. It must clearly illustrate a desirable goal that others want to achieve specifically a goal that you are working toward or have achieved. The skills and interests you acquire are what make the story toward this goal unique. Realize that you do not need results to start. People find value in those documenting their journey to achieve a goal that they have. Not only that, but you can create a profitable product right now. You can research a product that you use, create your own, and put a price tag on it. knowing that you are sticking your hand into a stream that is already flowing. Most people have the same big goals in life. They want more money, sex, happiness, and energy. They want a higher-quality experience. But there are infinite ways to achieve these goals, and you have taken a unique path of education and action to achieve them. I would encourage you to forge and distribute a meaningful philosophy behind the surface-level pursuits that people want.
要把人吸引到你生意上来，你的品牌会是第一个接触点。它必须清楚地展示一个别人想要达成的、值得追求的目标，具体地说，是一个你正在朝其努力、或已经达成的目标。你所获得的技能和兴趣，正是让通向这个目标的故事变得独特的东西。要意识到你起步并不需要结果。人们会在那些“记录自己达成某个目标之过程”的人身上找到价值。不仅如此，你现在就能创造一个有利润的产品。你可以研究一个你正在使用的产品、创造你自己的版本，并给它贴上价格标签——知道你是把一只手伸进一条本就在流动的溪流里。大多数人在生活里有着同样的宏大目标。他们想要更多金钱、性、幸福和能量。他们想要更高质量的体验。但达成这些目标的方式是无限的，而你走了一条独特的教育与行动之路去达成它们。我会鼓励你在人们想要的表层追求背后，锻造并分发一个有意义的人生哲学。
p.197
Content, in the form of media, is how you attract people to your brand Content can be anything that registers in the awareness of people in real life, or in our case the internet. Emails, articles, videos, writing, designs, and the rest distributed to a crevice of digital reality by free or paid means.
内容，以媒体的形式，是你如何把人吸引到你的品牌上来。内容可以是任何在真实生活里——或在我们这种情况里，在互联网上——登记进人们觉察的东西。邮件、文章、视频、文字、设计，以及其余一切通过免费或付费手段分发到数字现实某个裂缝的东西。
p.198
When crafting the message you wish to distribute with content, you must take into account the level of mind of your potential audience. Some people are at the beginning of their story with a plethora of surface-level problems to solve, so create for them. Some people are one step behind you and need that final piece to the puzzle, so create for them.
当你打造你想用内容分发的讯息时，你必须考虑潜在受众的心智层级。有些人处在自己故事的开始，有大量表层问题要解决，那就为他们创作。有些人比你落后一步、需要那块最终拼图，那就为他们创作。
p.198
Most of your audience will be beginner level. This isn't by your design, but because most of the world doesn't believe they have the capacity to improve themselves. Encourage them the most but be sure not to neglect the others that need a more advanced message.
你的受众大多数会是初学层级。这不是你所设计的，而是因为这世上大多数人不相信自己有改进自己的能力。给他们最多的鼓励，但也务必不要忽视那些需要更高级讯息的其他人。
p.198
Most people are mindless consumers of the media that crosses their eyes. But the silent observers, they reverse engineer, dissect, and research why that message is so impactful. From the lesson they receive, they can develop the message they are putting out.
大多数人都是从他们眼前滑过的媒体的无脑消费者。但那些沉默的观察者，他们会逆向工程、解剖并研究为什么那条讯息如此有影响力。从他们收到的这一课中，他们能发展出自己正在发出的讯息。
p.198
By attracting an audience to your brand, creating a message that shines awareness on the problems they face and the solutions to solve them, you set yourself up to generate a creative income with the product you create. Using what we learned about "done for you," "done with you," and "do it yourself' products and services in the last section, let's walk through a business path that allows your life's work to bloom. The only startup cost is a commitment to the path The easiest way to generate an income is to help people increase their own. This may seem shallow, but remember, money is the main resource holding individuals back from personal evolution. By prioritizing your education around the evergreen skills - marketing, sales, writing, and speaking - you set yourself up for your first hunt in the wild, wild internet.
通过把受众吸引到你的品牌上来、创造一条照亮他们所面临问题及其解法讯息，你就为自己铺好了用你创造的产品生成一份创造性收入的路。用我们在上一节学到的“替你完成”“与你一起做”和“你自己做”的产品与服务，让我们走一遍一条能让你人生事业绽放的商业路径。唯一的创业成本是对这条路的承诺。生成收入最容易的方式是帮人们增加他们自己的收入。这也许看起来浅薄，但记住，金钱是阻止个体个人演化的主要资源。通过把你的教育优先安排在常青技能上——营销、销售、写作和口说——你就为你在狂野互联网上的第一次狩猎做好了准备。
p.198
This path follows the "learn a skill, teach the skill, sell the skill" progression. You can either stick with the evergreen skills or learn a resultsoriented skill that is specific to the state of the internet as you are reading this.
这条路径遵循“学一项技能、教这项技能、卖这项技能”的递进。你要么坚持常青技能，要么在你读到此处时学一项针对互联网当前状态的、以结果为导向的技能。
p.199
You start by learning the skills with methods previously discussed, teach the skills as the message you use to attract an audience, and lastly, you sell the skill to those that understand your newly developed expertise. If this doesn't make sense, it's because you haven't built a project that requires the evergreen skills.
你先用此前讨论过的方法学这些技能，再把这些技能作为你用来吸引受众的讯息去教，最后把这项技能卖给那些理解你新形成专长的人。如果这讲不通，那是因为你还没有构建过一个需要这些常青技能的项目。
p.199
That is the first option to generating a creative income. From my experience in consulting, teaching, and working with nearly 10 thousand brands, this is the fastest path to cash, no gimmicks.
那是生成一份创造性收入的第一个选项。根据我在咨询、教学、以及与近 1 万个品牌合作中的经验，这是通向现金最快的一条路，没有花招。
p.199
The second option is an evolution of the first. I would recommend that you start building your independent income source immediately, but some people want to learn the ropes before they press play. That's understandable.
第二个选项是第一个的演化。我会建议你立刻开始建立你的独立收入来源，但有些人想在按下播放键之前先了解门道。那是可以理解的。
p.199
You will need a complete skill stack to progress into this second stage. All evergreen skills and a few results-oriented skills that you learn as you build are necessary for this to work.
你需要一套完整的技能组合才能进阶到第二阶段。所有常青技能，以及你在构建过程中学到的一些以结果为导向的技能，都是让这个生效的必要条件。
p.199
This style of one-person business is where you quite literally pursue your goals in public (brand), solve your problems as you are pursuing those goals (content), and create a system to help others do the same (product). You are not limited to profitable skills. Instead, you can use those skills to make your interests profitable. The interests that you became obsessed with on your path to a big, meaningful goal. Don't be surprised if your life's work becomes more and more clear.
这种一人公司的风格，就是你字面意义上地在公开场合追求你的目标（品牌）、在追求那些目标时解决你的问题（内容）、并创造一套系统去帮别人做同样的事（产品）。你不局限于“能获利的技能”。相反，你可以用那些技能让你的兴趣变得能获利。那些你在通往一个宏大、有意义目标的路上变得痴迷的兴趣。如果你的生命事业变得越来越清晰，不要惊讶。
p.199
This path does not require mastery in every skill associated with the skill stack previously discussed. Instead, mastery is developed when you start building, identify problems, and supplement your building with specific self-education.
这条路径不要求你在此前讨论的技能组合里的每一项技能上都精通。相反，精通是在你开始构建、识别问题、并用具体的自我教育补充你的构建时发展出来的。
p.199
You can create, test, and iterate a freelancing, coaching, or consulting offer at a low price point. You do not have the experience required to develop and market an expensive service, so start small as you would anything else worth improving.
你可以以一个低价格点创造、测试并迭代一份自由职业、教练或咨询供给。你还没有开发并营销一项昂贵服务所需的经验，所以像对待任何其他值得改进的事一样从小处开始。
p.200
The reason we are starting with a service, not a product, is because generating an income from a low-priced product would be near impossible from the start without ample money invested in paid distribution, like advertisements.
我们从服务、而不是产品开始的原因是：没有投入大量金钱去做付费分发（比如广告），从低价格产品生成收入在开头几乎不可能。
p.200
With a problem-oriented service and sales know-how, you can generate a full-time income with 2-4 clients a month, rather than one hundred to five hundred product sales. As we will learn in the next section, all you need to do is get the service in front of eyeballs and your name in people's mouths. As you work with others, generate results, and attract an audience, you are well on your way to removing the cap on your income. In most cases, if you do not grow stagnant, you can outearn most of the "best jobs" you will find after twelve years of formal education. Considering everything goes right, which it won't, you can expect belief-shattering results within 6-12 months of focus.
带着一项问题导向的服务和销售知识，你能靠每月 2 到 4 个客户生成一份全职收入，而不是靠一百到五百次产品销售。如同我们会在下一节学到的，你只需要把这项服务放到眼球面前、把你的名字放进人们嘴里。当你与他人合作、取得结果、并吸引受众时，你就已经走在了摘掉收入上限的路上。在大多数情况下，如果你不变得停滞，你能赚得比你在 12 年正规教育后能找到的大多数“最好的工作”更多。考虑到一切顺利——而它不会——你可以期待在专注 6 到 12 个月内取得足以击碎信念的结果。
p.200
With leverage built and an audience unable to invest in a high-cost service, you can use your previous results to create a product from that service. When you put it in front of the audience you've been nurturing for months to years, it will sell.
杠杆建立起来、而受众又无法投资一项高成本服务之后，你就可以用它此前的成果，把那项服务做成一个产品。当你把它放到你已培育了数月到数年的受众面前时，它会卖出去。
p.200
You can choose to stay as one person, or you can use the leverage you've built to start a "real" business. Although, I don't see why you'd want to unless you develop a love for building and monetizing impactful projects. YOU ARE THE NICHE You have $100,000 trapped in your head. Starting a business is how you begin to order that information to display its perceived value.
你可以选择继续做一个人，也可以选择用你建立起的杠杆去创办一家“真正的”企业。不过，除非你发展出对“构建并变现影响力项目”的热爱，我看不出你为什么要那么做。你 就 是 那 个 利 基：你有 $100,000 被困在你脑袋里。创业是你开始整理那些信息、以展示其可感知价值的方式。
p.200
The most profitable niche is you. Your unique skills, interests, and experience overlap in a way that allow you to solve profitable problems for people you enjoy working with. The authentic don't have to compete with anyone but themselves.
最有利可图的利基就是你。你独特的技能、兴趣和经验，以一种让你能为你乐于与之合作的人解决有利可图问题的方式重叠。本真的人不必与任何人竞争，除了他们自己。
p.201
In every business course, video, or article I consume, the most apparent advice is to "niche down." It makes sense, but pushes people toward working with people they hate, with a skill they feel locked into, and don't have any room to pivot without exhausting the money they use to survive. Which would sell more? A journal? Or a journal with structured prompts and bonus accountability sheet for those that struggle with habit formation? This illustrates the importance of not only having a niche but creating a system for that niche to improve results. And, you can imagine that the price point, design, and marketing strategy can be tailored to that niche, making it easier to find and sell to those people.
在我消费的每一门商业课程、视频或文章里，最显眼的建议是“收窄利基”。这合理，但它把人推向与他们讨厌的人合作、用一项他们觉得被锁死的技能、并且毫无在不耗尽自己生存资金的情况下转向的空间。哪一个会卖得更多？一本日志本？还是一本带结构化提示、以及给那些难以养成习惯之人的附加问责表的日志本？这说明，不仅拥有一个利基很重要，为那个利基创造一套提升结果的系统也很重要。而且你能想象，价格点、设计和营销策略都能针对那个利基定制，让人更容易找到并卖给那些人。
p.201
The problem is that most people start a full or side business for the sake of money and money alone. It's understandable, but we can incorporate meaning and fulfillment into your pursuit of money without any setbacks. Keep in mind that I am proposing that you start as a one-person business, monetize your self-development, and once you are generating a creative income for yourself, you can choose to start a company and fuel it with the leverage you've built.
问题在于，大多数人创办一门全职或副业生意，只是为钱、且只为钱。这可以理解，但我们能在你对金钱的追求中纳入意义与圆满，且毫无损失。请记住，我提议的是：你从一人公司开始、把你的自我发展变现，而一旦你为自己生成了一份创造性收入，你就可以选择创办一家公司、用你建立的杠杆为它供能。
p.201
The mistake of many is to niche down on solving a problem within a market. This is great, but a problem is difficult to identify without a goal. Instead, niche down on a desirable goal that someone else wants to achieve, create a system for them to get there, and introduce new challenges as you help them improve their skill set.
许多人的错误，是在一个市场里收窄到“解决某个问题”上。这很棒，但没有目标，一个问题很难被识别。相反，收窄到一个别人想要达成的、值得追求的目标上，为他们创造一套抵达那里的系统，并在你帮他们提升技能组合时引入新的挑战。
p.201
This is how you order the minds of your customers, by gamifying your product or service. In a world where results mean more than credentials, you must do everything in your power to make your product easy to use, effective, and transformative. Results are determined by behavior change. If your customers don't use your information to better move within the world, you did not do your job.
这就是你如何给你的客户的心智建立秩序，通过把你的产品或服务游戏化。在一个结果比资历更有意义的世界里，你必须竭尽所能让你的产品易用、有效、并具转化力。结果由行为改变决定。如果你的客户不用你的信息去更好地在世界中行动，你就没做好你的工作。
p.201
If we are meant to provide value to a specific person, or identity, because it will register best in their current level of mind, why not use the value we've cultivated through our self-development and distribute it from a more
如果我们注定要为某个特定的人、或身份提供价值，因为它会在他们当前的心智层级上登记得最好，那为什么不使用我们通过自我发展所培育的价值、并从一个更
p.202
